summary: Calegari and Geraghty extend the Taylor–Wiles method to situations where the relevant automorphic forms contribute to l0 + 1 degrees of cohomology (defect l0 > 0). Part 1 (l0 = 1) patches balanced modules (Definition 2.2, Proposition 2.3) and proves, unconditionally, minimal R = T and freeness for weight-one Katz forms over Q (Theorems 1.4, 3.26, 3.30, with local–global compatibility at p for torsion weight-one Hecke algebras, Theorem 3.11, and the vexing-prime bundles L_σ), consequences for Boston's conjecture (Corollaries 1.5–1.6) and multiplicity two in J₁(N*) exactly in the unramified scalar case (Theorem 4.8); and, assuming Conjecture A, minimal R = T for PGL₂ over imaginary quadratic fields (Theorems 1.2, 1.3, 5.11). Part 2 patches perfect complexes of length l0 (Lemma 6.2, Theorems 6.3–6.4, Proposition 6.6), builds them in Betti and coherent cohomology (§7), computes the Galois side for GL_n over any number field (§8) and, assuming Conjecture B (§9), proves near faithfulness (Theorem 9.19) and conditional automorphy lifting for GL_n (Theorem 5.16), hence potential modularity and Sato–Tate for elliptic curves over every number field (Theorem 1.1). The atlas already plans the patching algebra (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5, P7–P9, R03.6, whose reviewed nodes take §§2 and 6 from this paper), the deformation theory (GlobalGaloisDeformations, LocalGaloisDeformationRings), locally symmetric spaces and Hecke complexes (ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces, IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) and modular curves, but no R = T in defect one, no weight-one R = T, no conditional GL_n lifting over arbitrary fields and no integral coherent Hecke complexes. Routes: a Part II of GL2ModularityLifting (minimal R = T in defect one: weight one over Q and Bianchi forms); a Part II of PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure (conditional GL_n automorphy lifting over arbitrary number fields); a Part II of AutomorphicBundles (integral coherent cohomology and Hecke complexes); and source routes to DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra, LocalGaloisDeformationRings, AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights, SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions (Theorem 1.1 as a conditional endpoint) and fourteen others. 217 mistakes are recorded: the 12 items of the authors' 2022 bracket Correction, and 205 new ones, among them false or incomplete statements of Lemmas 4.2, 4.4, 6.2 and 7.4 and of Lemma 3.15(4), missing hypotheses in Theorems 1.3, 1.4, Corollary 1.5 and Theorem 6.3, the local–global compatibility at Taylor–Wiles primes missing from Conjecture B, and a wrong bound N₂ in the proof of Theorem 1.1.

items.name: Standing coefficient conventions (p, K, O, ϖ, k)
items.statement: Throughout the paper a prime p ≥ 3 is fixed; K is a finite extension of Q_p with ring of integers O, ϖ is a uniformizer of O and k = O/ϖ is the residue field.
items.note: A convention, not a result. Mathlib supplies the objects for any nonarchimedean local field K: the ring 𝒪[K] (a DVR), a uniformizer and the finite residue field 𝓀[K]. The class is more general than 'finite extension of Q_p'. Characteristic 0 and finiteness over ℚ_[p] are hypotheses the consumer adds; the instance for finite extensions of ℚ_p is Tau Ceti LocalFieldsRamification layer 0 work. p ≥ 3 is a standing hypothesis.

items.name: The category C_O
items.statement: C_O denotes the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k; the morphisms in C_O are the continuous O-algebra homomorphisms.
items.note: R03.1 plans exactly this category, with Λ = O. Between complete Noetherian local rings, CG's continuous O-algebra maps are the local maps. Mathlib has the ingredients (IsLocalRing, IsNoetherianRing, IsAdicComplete) but no such category, and neither library has deformation-theoretic coefficient categories.

items.name: Teichmüller lift ⟨χ⟩ of a character
items.statement: If G is a group and χ : G → k^× is a character, ⟨χ⟩ : G → O^× denotes the Teichmüller lift of χ, i.e. the composite of χ with the multiplicative Teichmüller section k^× → O^×.
items.note: Tau Ceti has the Teichmüller section k^× → O^× for the ring of integers of a nonarchimedean local field. ⟨χ⟩ is its composite with χ : G → k^× (MonoidHom.comp), so no further declaration is needed. Mathlib's Perfection.teichmuller and WittVector.teichmuller are the perfectoid/Witt-vector versions and are near misses for this use.

items.name: Galois-theoretic and adelic conventions
items.statement: For a field F, G_F = Gal(F̄/F) for a chosen algebraic closure; ε : G_F → Z_p^× is the p-adic cyclotomic character. For a number field F and a prime v: O_v is the ring of integers of F_v, π_v a uniformizer of O_v, G_v := G_{F_v}, I_v ⊂ G_v the inertia group, Frob_v ∈ G_v/I_v the arithmetic Frobenius, D_v (sometimes) the decomposition group at v; Art : F_v^× → W_{F_v}^{ab} is the local Artin map normalized to send uniformizers to geometric Frobenius lifts. A_F and A_F^∞ are the adeles and finite adeles of F (A, A^∞ when F = Q).
items.note: A composite convention. G_F, ε, inertia, Frobenius elements, F_v with O_v, and the adeles are in the libraries. The local Artin map Art : F_v^× → W_{F_v}^{ab} with the geometric normalization is planned by Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory layers 7 and 9, and G_v/I_v ≅ Ẑ with Frobenius lifts by LocalFieldsRamification layer 4. The decomposition group D_v as restriction along a chosen place is planned in R01.2.

items.name: Unramified character λ(α)
items.statement: If R is a topological ring and α ∈ R^×, λ(α) : G_v → R^× denotes the continuous unramified character sending Frob_v to α, when such a character exists.
items.note: No layer constructs λ(α), the continuous unramified character G_v → R^× with Frob_v ↦ α. It also needs the criterion for when λ(α) exists: n ↦ α^n must extend continuously from Z to Ẑ, which holds for instance when R is a complete local ring with finite residue field. The pieces are planned: G_v ↠ Ẑ with Frobenius lifts (LocalFieldsRamification layer 4) and rank-one continuous representations with twists (R01.1). Layer 4 leaves 'profinite exponentiation' to a ProfiniteArithmetic roadmap, which is not in the atlas; the ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations README only lists 'an unramified character' among its test examples.

items.name: Total cohomology H^*(P) and degree-preserving convention
items.statement: If P is a bounded complex of S-modules for some ring S, H^*(P) := ⊕_i H^i(P); any map H^*(P) → H^*(P) is assumed to be degree preserving. If R is a local ring its maximal ideal is sometimes denoted m_R.
items.note: A notational convention. H^*(P) is the one-line abbreviation ⨁ i, P.homology i. A 'degree-preserving' map is a family of maps H^i → H^i, and m_R is IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R. Neither library has a bundled 'total cohomology' declaration, and none is needed.

items.name: The invariant l0 and the Betti/Coherent contexts
items.statement: Case Betti: Galois representations conjecturally arising from tempered π of cohomological type associated to a reductive group G (over Q), where K is a maximal compact subgroup of G(R), A is the maximal Q-split torus in the centre of G, and l0 := rank G(R) − rank K − rank A (ranks of the real groups, as in §8.4) is arbitrary ⟦printed: 'maximal compact K, maximal Q-split torus A, and l0 = rank(G) − rank(K) − rank(A)'; see sourceIssues E2⟧. Case Coherent: Galois representations conjecturally arising from tempered π associated to G, where (G, X) is a Shimura datum ('Shimura variety' in the paper) over a totally real field F, such that π_v is a non-degenerate limit of discrete series at l0 infinite places (printed ℓ0) and a discrete series at all other infinite places. In the coherent case the value of l0 depends on the infinity components allowed. What the method needs is that, after localizing at a suitable maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra T, the cohomology is concentrated in l0 + 1 consecutive degrees. The case l0 = 0 recovers exactly the usual Taylor–Wiles method.
items.note: No layer defines the invariant ℓ0 = rank G − rank K − rank A, where A is the split component of the centre (see sourceIssues E2), with its partner q0. No layer defines the Coherent variant (the number of infinite places where π_v is a non-degenerate limit of discrete series), or the hypothesis that the localized cohomology is concentrated in ℓ0 + 1 consecutive degrees. ALS.0 plans maximal compact subgroups, symmetric spaces and 'the reductive center correction', but not these numerical invariants. P9 treats ℓ0 only algebraically, as dim S∞ − dim R∞. PAPER-VENKATESH-19/1 treated the analogous δ as planned in ALS.0, but no layer states it.

items.name: Semi-stable representation ρ : G_F → GL2(O)
items.statement: For a number field F, a representation ρ : G_F → GL2(O) is semi-stable if ρ|_{I_v} is unipotent for all finite v not dividing p, and ρ|_{G_v} is semi-stable in the sense of Fontaine [12] for v | p.
items.note: Fontaine semistability at v | p is B_st-admissibility, which R06.2 plans through D_st. Away from p, unipotent inertia is the Weil–Deligne condition of R01.2 (Frobenius-semisimplification with only monodromy on inertia). Neither library has period rings or semistable representations. External input: Fontaine, Représentations p-adiques semi-stables, Astérisque 223 (1994) [12] (for the notion at v | p)

items.name: Level N(ρ̄) and 'modular of level N(ρ̄)' (imaginary quadratic case)
items.statement: For F imaginary quadratic and ρ̄ : G_F → GL2(k), N(ρ̄) is the product of the usual prime-to-p Artin conductor (of ρ̄) and the primes v | p where ρ̄ (i.e. ρ̄|_{D_v}) is not finite flat. The introduction does not define 'ρ̄ is modular of level N(ρ̄)' formally. It says that this condition is only a statement about the existence of a mod-p cohomology class of level N(ρ̄), not the existence of a characteristic-zero lift, and that it is the natural generalization of Serre's conjecture. (In the proof, §5.4, pp. 378–379, it is used in this form: the ideal m_∅ of T_∅ generated by ϖ and T_λ − Trace ρ̄(Frob_λ), for λ ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v | p}, is a proper ideal. Here T_∅ is the Hecke algebra of Definition 5.4 acting on H_1 of the arithmetic quotient Y = Y_0(∅) of §5.2, whose level at x ∈ S(ρ̄) and at v | p depends on the local type of ρ̄.)
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.2(3) and following remark, p. 301 (made precise in §5.4, pp. 378–379)
items.note: Only the prime-to-p Artin conductor is planned (R01.3); finite-flatness at v | p is in R07.1/R08.4. The notion 'ρ̄ is modular of level N(ρ̄)' is planned nowhere. It means a mod-p Hecke eigenclass in H_1(Y_0(N), k) for GL_2 over an imaginary quadratic F whose eigenvalues match ρ̄. AF.4 mentions torsion Hecke eigenclasses and ALS.0/ALS.3 give the manifolds and Hecke correspondences. Residual modularity is defined only for classical forms over Q (R15.6).

items.name: Theorem 1.2: modularity lifting over imaginary quadratic fields (conditional on Conjecture A)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A. Let F/Q be an imaginary quadratic field and let p ≥ 3 be unramified in F. Let ρ : G_F → GL2(O) be a continuous semi-stable Galois representation with cyclotomic determinant, unramified outside finitely many primes, and let ρ̄ : G_F → GL2(k) be its mod-ϖ reduction. Suppose that (1) for v | p, ρ|_{D_v} is either finite flat or ordinary; (2) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible; (3) ρ̄ is modular of level N(ρ̄), where N(ρ̄) is the product of the usual prime-to-p Artin conductor and the primes v | p where ρ̄ is not finite flat; (4) ρ is minimally ramified ⟦the paper does not define this term; it means that ρ is a minimal deformation of ρ̄ in the sense of §5.1, p. 369 (Q = ∅), including the condition at v | p⟧. Then ρ is modular: there exists a regular algebraic cusp form π for GL(2)/F such that L(ρ, s) = L(π, s).
items.note: Modularity lifting over imaginary quadratic F in defect ℓ0 = 1 is planned nowhere. GL2ModularityLifting follows KW II with ℓ0 = 0 over totally real fields, and no stage mentions Bianchi or imaginary-quadratic modularity lifting. The 'regular algebraic cusp form π with L(ρ,s) = L(π,s)' conclusion would use the HLTT/Scholze Galois representations of AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.4. Conjecture A is an open hypothesis (§9.3).

items.name: Theorem 1.3: R^min = T_m and freeness over imaginary quadratic fields (conditional on Conjecture A)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A. Let F/Q be an imaginary quadratic field and p ≥ 3 unramified in F. Let ρ̄ : G_F → GL2(k) be a continuous representation with cyclotomic determinant such that (1) for v | p, ρ̄|_{D_v} is either finite flat or ordinary; (2) ρ̄ is modular of level N = N(ρ̄); (3) ρ̄|_{G_{F(ζ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible; (4) if ρ̄ is ramified at x with N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ −1 mod p, then either ρ̄|_{D_x} is reducible or ρ̄|_{I_x} is absolutely irreducible; ⟦(5), missing from the printed statement and required by the proof via §5.1(3), p. 369 (see sourceIssues E5): for every prime x ∤ p at which ρ̄ is ramified, ρ̄|_{I_x} is irreducible, or unipotent, or semisimple (then ≅ ψ ⊕ ψ^{−1}). Equivalently, ρ̄|_{I_x} is not of the form ψ ⊗ (non-trivial unipotent) with ψ a non-trivial quadratic character of I_x⟧. Let R^min be the minimal finite flat (respectively ordinary) deformation ring of ρ̄ with cyclotomic determinant, and T_m the algebra of Hecke operators acting on H_1(Y_0(N), O) localized at the maximal ideal m corresponding to ρ̄. Then there is an isomorphism R^min ≅ T_m, and there is an integer μ ≥ 1 such that H_1(Y_0(N), O)_m is free of rank μ as a T_m-module.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.3, p. 302; deduced from Theorem 5.11 and multiplicity one for PGL(2)/F, §5.4, p. 380; proved p. 380
items.note: R^min ≅ T_m and the freeness of H_1(Y_0(N), O)_m over imaginary quadratic fields are planned nowhere. The abstract algebra (Proposition 2.3) is planned in R03.5. The arithmetic inputs are not: the ℓ0 = 1 Taylor–Wiles system for Bianchi manifolds, the deformation-to-Hecke map from Conjecture A, and the minimal finite-flat/ordinary deformation ring over F. See sourceIssues E5 (missing local hypothesis at ramified primes).

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (addendum): μ = 1 in characteristic zero
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.3, if H_1(Y_0(N), O)_m ⊗ Q ≠ 0, then μ = 1.
items.note: This part of Theorem 1.3 (μ = 1 when H_1(Y_0(N), O)_m ⊗ Q ≠ 0) is planned nowhere. It follows from freeness plus a characteristic-zero rank computation, which needs the Bianchi Hecke module of the missing Theorem 1.3. See sourceIssues E121 (μ = 1 fails at type P, M, H primes).

items.name: Theorem 1.3 (addendum): complete intersection when T_m is finite
items.statement: In the situation of Theorem 1.3, if dim(T_m) = 0, then T_m is a complete intersection.
items.note: This part of Theorem 1.3 (T_m is a complete intersection when dim T_m = 0) is planned nowhere as an arithmetic statement. The complete-intersection predicate and criteria are planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.3; Mathlib has no complete-intersection predicate (AUDIT-17). The algebraic mechanism is the byproduct R ≅ R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞ of Proposition 2.3, which is planned in R03.5.

items.name: Theorem 1.4: R^min = T_m for weight-one Katz forms
items.statement: Suppose that p ≥ 3. Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(k) be an odd continuous irreducible Galois representation of Serre level N, unramified at p. Let R^min denote the universal minimal unramified-at-p deformation ring of ρ̄. Then there exist a quotient X_U of X_1(N) and a vector bundle L_σ on X_U such that, if T denotes the Hecke algebra of H^1(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ), there is an isomorphism R^min ≅ T_m, where m is the maximal ideal of T corresponding to ρ̄. Moreover H^1(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_m is free as a T_m-module.
items.note: Minimal R = T for Katz weight-one forms on X_U, with the vexing-prime bundle L_σ and freeness of H^1(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_m, is planned nowhere. The pieces are planned: the Hodge bundle ω and Katz forms (R15.1/R15.2), modular curves (tauceti ModularCurves), the Deligne–Serre weight-one representation (R19.1). ML.1 only registers 'weight-one modularity in proved cases', from sources NEWTON-THORNE/ARTHUR-MOK/EXISTING. IKM's related item calegari-wt1 was likewise marked missing. See sourceIssues E6 (needs the §3.1 hypothesis ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0).

items.name: Corollary 1.5: minimal unramified-at-p lifts are weight-one modular
items.statement: Suppose p ≥ 3 and ρ : G_Q → GL2(O) is a continuous representation such that (1) for all primes v, either ρ(I_v) → ρ̄(I_v) is an isomorphism or dim(ρ^{I_v}) = dim(ρ̄^{I_v}) = 1; (2) ρ̄ is odd and irreducible; (3) ρ is unramified at p. Then ρ is modular of weight one. ⟦As printed, (1) does not force minimality; the statement proved by the paper needs (1′): some twist of ρ by a finite-order character is a minimal deformation (Definition 3.1, Q = ∅) of the correspondingly twisted ρ̄ — see sourceIssues E9.⟧
items.note: Weight-one modularity of minimal lifts unramified at p is planned nowhere as a theorem. ML.1 is only a registry of weight-one modularity 'in proved cases' and names no such source. Use the corrected hypothesis (1′) recorded in sourceIssues E9.

items.name: Corollary 1.6: minimal deformations unramified at p have finite image
items.statement: Suppose p ≥ 3. Let ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(k) be odd, continuous, irreducible and unramified at p. Let (A, m) be a complete local Noetherian O-algebra with residue field k and ρ : G_Q → GL2(A) a minimal deformation of ρ̄. Then ρ has finite image.
items.note: Finite image of minimal deformations unramified at p (towards Boston's strengthening of Fontaine–Mazur) is planned nowhere. It combines Theorem 1.4 with the finiteness criterion of R03.4 (node finiteness-of-deformation-rings-criteria: 'R_F is finite (as a set) iff η_F(G) is finite') and the Deligne–Serre weight-one representation of R19.1.

items.name: Multiplicity one or two in J_1(N*) (announced in §1, proved as Theorem 4.8)
items.statement: (Introduction, p. 305.) For p odd and ρ̄ an irreducible modular representation, let N* be the minimal level at which ρ̄ arises in weight two and m the corresponding maximal ideal. The paper states: if ρ̄ is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is a scalar, then the multiplicity of ρ̄ in J_1(N*)[m] is two; in all other cases the multiplicity was already known to be one, and in the exceptional case it was already known to be ≥ 2. (Theorem 4.8, §4.1, p. 361, as proved.) Let p ≥ 3 and let ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(k) be an absolutely irreducible modular (= odd) representation of Serre conductor N = N(ρ̄) and Serre weight k(ρ̄) with p + 1 ≥ k(ρ̄) ≥ 2, which has minimal conductor amongst all its twists (at all primes other than p). Let N* = N if k(ρ̄) = 2 and N* = Np otherwise. Let T be the ring of endomorphisms of J_1(N*)/Q generated by the Hecke operators T_l for all primes l (including p), and m the maximal ideal of T corresponding to ρ̄. If ρ̄ is ramified at p, or unramified at p with ρ̄(Frob_p) non-scalar, then J_1(N*)[m] ≃ ρ̄ (multiplicity one). If ρ̄ is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar, then J_1(N*)[m] ≃ ρ̄ ⊕ ρ̄ (multiplicity two).
items.note: The multiplicity of ρ̄ in J_1(N*)[m] (two exactly when ρ̄ is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar, one otherwise) is planned nowhere. No stage mentions multiplicity one or two for Jacobians. SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 plans integral Hecke modules and old/new sequences, and R20.3 plans weight optimisation, but neither states this. CG prove it in §4 from the weight-one freeness of Theorem 1.4. See sourceIssues E1 (introduction's claim needs twist-minimal ρ̄).

items.name: Defect d_S(M) (Definition 2.1)
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring with residue field k (= S/m_S) and M a finitely generated S-module. The defect of M is d_S(M) := dim_k Tor_0^S(M, k) − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, k) = dim_k M/m_S M − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, k).
items.note: Planned verbatim in the accepted R03.5 node. The node already cites this paper (§2.1 Definitions 2.1–2.2, 'PDF pp. 11–14' = pp. 307–310). Mathlib has the Tor functor CategoryTheory.Tor for monoidal abelian categories with projective resolutions (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean:44), but neither library defines the defect.

items.name: Minimal free resolutions and Betti numbers
items.statement: For S, M as in Definition 2.1 there is a (possibly infinite) resolution ⋯ → P_i → ⋯ → P_1 → P_0 → M → 0 by finite free S-modules with the image of P_i in P_{i−1} contained in m_S P_{i−1} for every i ≥ 1 (a 'minimal' resolution). If r_i = rank P_i then P_i/m_S P_i ≅ Tor_i^S(M, k), hence r_i = dim_k Tor_i^S(M, k); in particular d_S(M) = r_0 − r_1.
items.note: A finite module over a Noetherian local ring is pseudo-coherent, so its possibly infinite minimal free resolution with r_i = dim_k Tor_i(M, k) is P7's minimal complex. Neither library has minimal resolutions. Tau Ceti's IsMinimalProjectivePresentation is a two-term presentation, a near miss (as IKM's minimal-complexes item noted).

items.name: Balanced module (Definition 2.2)
items.statement: A finitely generated module M over a Noetherian local ring S is balanced if d_S(M) ≥ 0.
items.note: Planned verbatim in the accepted R03.5 node, whose source is this paper. Absent from both libraries.

items.name: Balanced modules have square presentations
items.statement: If M is balanced (over the Noetherian local ring S), then M admits a presentation S^d → S^d → M → 0 with d = dim_k M/m_S M.
items.note: Planned verbatim in the R03.5 node. It follows from a minimal resolution (P7) by enlarging the relation module to rank d. Absent from both libraries.

items.name: Rings and ideals of the l0 = 1 patching argument: Δ_N, S_N, S∞, R∞, 𝔞, 𝔞_N, 𝔟_N
items.statement: Fix an integer q ≥ 1. For N ≥ 1 let Δ_N := (Z/p^N Z)^q and S_N := O[Δ_N] (group ring of a finite p-group; a local ring). Let S∞ := O⟦(Z_p)^q⟧ = lim_N O[Δ_N] be the completed group ring; choosing a Z_p-basis γ_1,…,γ_q of Z_p^q, S∞ ≅ O⟦y_1,…,y_q⟧ via y_j ↦ γ_j − 1, so S∞ ∈ C_O is regular of dimension q + 1 and formally smooth over O. Let R∞ := O⟦x_1,…,x_{q−1}⟧ (dimension q). Let 𝔞 ⊂ S∞ be the augmentation ideal, the kernel of S∞ ↠ O sending each element of (Z_p)^q to 1 (so 𝔞 = (γ_1 − 1,…,γ_q − 1)); let 𝔞_N := ker(S∞ ↠ S_N); and let 𝔟_N be the open ideal of S∞ generated by ϖ^N and 𝔞_N (so S∞/𝔟_N = (O/ϖ^N)[Δ_N]).
items.locator: §2, p. 306; §2.2, Proposition 2.3(2)–(3), p. 307; proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 308
items.note: The rings and ideals are named in the R03.5 node. The completed group ring O⟦Z_p^q⟧, its augmentation and the identification O⟦Z_p^q⟧ ≅ O⟦y_1..y_q⟧ come from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 (and L2 for Z_p^d). Mathlib has group algebras (MonoidAlgebra), power series (MvPowerSeries) and the IsRegularLocalRing class. It has no completed group ring, and no proof that O⟦y_1..y_q⟧ is regular of dimension q + 1: AUDIT-17 records only dim R + 1 ≤ dim R⟦X⟧. See sourceIssues E14 (S_N is reduced, not 'non-reduced').

items.name: Proposition 2.3: abstract patching for l0 = 1 (balanced modules)
items.statement: Suppose that (1) R is an object of C_O and H is a finite R-module which is also finite over O; (2) q ≥ 1 is an integer, and for each integer N ≥ 1, S_N := O[Δ_N] with Δ_N := (Z/p^N Z)^q; (3) R∞ := O⟦x_1, …, x_{q−1}⟧; (4) for each N ≥ 1, φ_N : R∞ ↠ R is a surjection in C_O and H_N is an R∞ ⊗_O S_N-module; (5) for each N ≥ 1: (a) the image of S_N in End_O(H_N) is contained in the image of R∞, and moreover the image of the augmentation ideal of S_N in End_O(H_N) is contained in the image of ker(φ_N); (b) there is an isomorphism ψ_N : (H_N)_{Δ_N} ≅ H of R∞-modules (Δ_N-coinvariants; R∞ acts on H via φ_N); (c) H_N is finite and balanced over S_N (Definition 2.2). Then H is a free R-module.
items.note: Planned verbatim: the accepted R03.5 node transcribes Proposition 2.3 from this paper. It notes that the conclusion is only freeness, with no complete-intersection claim. No library has patching.

items.name: Auxiliary open ideals 𝔡_N of R
items.statement: In the setting of Proposition 2.3 put d := dim_k(H/ϖH); if d = 0 then H = 0 and the result is trivial, so assume d > 0. There is a sequence (𝔡_N)_{N≥1} of open ideals of R with 𝔡_N ⊃ 𝔡_{N+1} for all N, ∩_{N≥1} 𝔡_N = (0), and ϖ^N R ⊂ 𝔡_N ⊂ ϖ^N R + Ann_R(H) for all N; for example 𝔡_N = (ϖ^N) + Ann_R(H)^N, which is open because R/Ann_R(H) ⊂ End_O(H) is finite over O.
items.note: A proof-internal construction, planned in the R03.5 node's proof steps. Openness uses that R/Ann_R(H) ⊂ End_O(H) is finite over O. Hence R/𝔡_N is Artinian with finite residue field, and so finite, which the finiteness of patching data also needs.

items.name: Patching datum of level N, isomorphism, and reduction D mod N′
items.statement: In the proof of Proposition 2.3 (with d = dim_k H/ϖH), a patching datum of level N is a 4-tuple (φ, X, ψ, P) where: φ : R∞ ↠ R/𝔡_N is a surjection in C_O; X is an R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞-module such that the action of S∞ on X factors through S∞/𝔟_N and X is finite over S∞; ψ : X/𝔞X ≅ H/ϖ^N H is an isomorphism of R∞-modules (R∞ acting on H/ϖ^N H via φ); P is a presentation (S∞/𝔟_N)^d → (S∞/𝔟_N)^d → X → 0. Two data (φ, X, ψ, P), (φ′, X′, ψ′, P′) are isomorphic if φ = φ′ and there is an isomorphism X ≅ X′ of R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞-modules compatible with ψ, ψ′ and with the presentations P, P′. For 1 ≤ N′ ≤ N, a datum D of level N gives a datum D mod N′ of level N′ (reduce φ modulo 𝔡_{N′}, X to X/𝔟_{N′}X, ψ modulo ϖ^{N′}, P modulo 𝔟_{N′}).
items.note: Planned in the R03.5 node. The node does not spell out the isomorphism relation or the reduction 'D mod N′', but the layer's 'compatible transition data' covers them.

items.name: Finitely many patching data of each level
items.statement: For each N ≥ 1 there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of patching data of level N.
items.note: Planned in R03.5. The paper's justification ('R∞ and S∞ are topologically finitely generated') also silently uses two finiteness facts: R/𝔡_N is finite, and X is a quotient of the finite set (S∞/𝔟_N)^d. The R03.5 blueprint should state both.

items.name: The patching data D_{M,N}
items.statement: For integers M ≥ N ≥ 1 define a patching datum D_{M,N} = (φ, X, ψ, P) of level N from φ_M : R∞ ↠ R and the R∞ ⊗_O S_M-module H_M: φ is the composite R∞ ↠ R ↠ R/𝔡_N; X := H_M/𝔟_N H_M; ψ : X/𝔞X ≅ H/ϖ^N H is the reduction modulo ϖ^N of ψ_M : H_M/𝔞H_M ≅ H; P is any presentation (S∞/𝔟_N)^d → (S∞/𝔟_N)^d → X → 0, which exists because H_M/𝔞H_M ≅ H and d_{S_M}(H_M) ≥ 0.
items.note: Planned in R03.5. The item writes the target as H/ϖ^N H; p. 309 prints 'ψ : X/𝔞X → H/𝔟_N', shorthand for H/𝔟_N H = H/ϖ^N H.

items.name: The patched module X∞ and the maps φ∞, ψ∞, P∞, ı
items.statement: There is a sequence of pairs (M_i, N_i)_{i≥1} with M_i ≥ N_i, M_{i+1} > M_i, N_{i+1} > N_i and D_{M_{i+1},N_{i+1}} mod N_i ≅ D_{M_i,N_i} for all i. Write D_{M_i,N_i} = (φ_i, X_i, ψ_i, P_i) and fix isomorphisms X_{i+1}/𝔟_{N_i}X_{i+1} ≅ X_i realising these. Define φ∞ : R∞ ↠ R as the inverse limit of the φ_i; X∞ := lim_i X_i (transition maps X_{i+1} ↠ X_{i+1}/𝔟_{N_i} ≅ X_i); ψ∞ : X∞/𝔞X∞ ≅ H the isomorphism of R∞-modules (R∞ acting on H via φ∞) induced by the ψ_i; and P∞ : S∞^d → S∞^d → X∞ → 0 the presentation obtained from the P_i (exact by the Mittag-Leffler condition). Then X∞ is an R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞-module, and the image of S∞ in End_O(X∞) is contained in the image of R∞ (by (5a), as End_O(X∞) = lim_i Hom_O(X∞, X_i)). X∞ is a finite R∞-module. Since S∞ is formally smooth over O, there is a homomorphism ı : S∞ → R∞ in C_O compatible with the actions of S∞ and R∞ on X∞.
items.note: Planned in the R03.5 node. The exactness step uses the Mittag-Leffler lemma (item ext-mittag-leffler, planned in P7). The lift ı uses formal smoothness of S∞ ≅ O⟦y⟧ over O, i.e. power-series maps sending the y_j to elements of the maximal ideal (R03.1: 'continuous maps from power-series rings').

items.name: The patched module is free over R∞
items.statement: With X∞, P∞, ı as above: dim_{S∞}(X∞) = dim_{R∞}(X∞) ≤ dim R∞ < dim S∞, hence the first map S∞^d → S∞^d of P∞ is injective (its kernel K is torsion-free, and K ≠ 0 would force X∞ ⊗_{S∞} Frac(S∞) ≠ 0), so P∞ is a minimal free resolution of X∞ and depth_{S∞}(X∞) = dim(S∞) − 1; since depth_{R∞}(X∞) = depth_{S∞}(X∞), depth_{R∞}(X∞) = dim(R∞) and X∞ is free over R∞. Moreover ı(𝔞) ⊂ ker(φ∞).
items.note: Planned in R03.5, using R03.3's Auslander–Buchsbaum and its depth/dimension comparison under finite local maps. pd_{S∞}(X∞) = 1 exactly holds because X∞ ≠ 0 (d > 0) and dim X∞ < dim S∞, so X∞ is not S∞-free.

items.name: Byproduct of Proposition 2.3: R ≅ R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞
items.statement: In the situation of Proposition 2.3 with H ≠ 0, there are a surjection φ∞ : R∞ ↠ R in C_O and a homomorphism ı : S∞ → R∞ in C_O with ker(φ∞) = ı(𝔞)R∞; thus R ≅ R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞ is the quotient of O⟦x_1, …, x_{q−1}⟧ by the q elements ı(γ_1 − 1), …, ı(γ_q − 1), and H ≅ X∞/𝔞X∞ is free over R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞ = R.
items.note: Planned in the R03.5 node (and in the R03.6 node for the ℓ0-general version). The equality ker φ∞ = ı(𝔞)R∞ uses H ≠ 0: a nonzero free R∞/ı(𝔞)R∞-module on which ker φ∞ acts by zero forces ker φ∞ ⊂ ı(𝔞)R∞.

items.name: Depth and dimension are insensitive to finite local base change
items.statement: Let A → B be a local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings and M a finitely generated B-module that is finitely generated as an A-module. Then dim_A(M) = dim_B(M) and depth_A(M) = depth_B(M).
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 310 (used without comment)
items.note: Covered by R03.3's layer description, though the accepted R03.3 node does not state it separately; the paper uses it without proof. Mathlib has Module.supportDim. Tau Ceti's ringKrullDim_eq_of_isIntegral_of_faithfulSMul (dimension is preserved along an injective integral extension) gives the dimension half via annihilators. Both are near misses; no depth invariant exists. External input: Standard (e.g. Bruns–Herzog, Cohen–Macaulay Rings, §1.2 exercises on depth under finite local homomorphisms); not cited by the paper

items.name: Exactness of inverse limits under Mittag-Leffler
items.statement: If (0 → A_i → B_i → C_i → 0)_{i≥1} is an inverse system of short exact sequences of abelian groups (or modules) and (A_i) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition (e.g. all A_i are finite), then 0 → lim A_i → lim B_i → lim C_i → 0 is exact.
items.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 309 ('Exactness follows from the Mittag–Leffler condition')
items.note: Planned in several layers; P7 is the one inside the patching roadmap. Mathlib has the Mittag-Leffler condition for functors to Type (CofilteredSystem.lean:137) and surjectivity of ℕ-indexed limits of surjections (Limits/Types/Images.lean:110). It has no lim¹ and no exactness of inverse limits of modules. In CG's use all the terms are finite sets, so Mittag-Leffler is automatic. External input: Standard (e.g. the Stacks Project, Algebra chapter, section on Mittag-Leffler systems); not cited by the paper

items.name: Serre's modularity conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger)
items.statement: Every continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(F̄_p) is modular, i.e. arises from a cuspidal eigenform (of Serre's weight and level).
items.note: Khare–Wintenberger's theorem is planned by ClassicalSerreModularity (the KW route in R26/R27, the Dieulefait–Pacetti route in R33). CG use it only to drop Buzzard–Taylor's residual modularity hypothesis. Neither library has it. External input: Khare–Wintenberger, Serre's modularity conjecture. I, Invent. Math. 178 (2009) 485–504 [24] (with part II and Kisin for the full proof)

items.name: Borel–Wallach range of tempered cohomology
items.statement: For G = Res_{F/Q} PGL(n) (more generally a reductive group with invariants q0, l0), cuspidal automorphic π that are tempered at ∞ contribute to cuspidal cohomology exactly in the degrees [q0, q0 + l0], a range of l0 + 1 consecutive degrees.
items.locator: §1, p. 300 (cited as [9]); precise reference given in §8.4, p. 406
items.note: Planned nowhere: tempered cohomological π contribute to (𝔤, K)-cohomology exactly in degrees [q0, q0 + ℓ0] (Borel–Wallach III.5.1 and VII.6.7, cited on p. 406). AF.1a pins Borel–Wallach only for van Est and continuous cohomology (Corollary IX.5.6(ii)). AF.4 defines 'cohomological representations' but not their (𝔤, K)-cohomology range. PAPER-VENKATESH-19/2 ('The shape of the tempered cohomology', the same theorem) was marked missing and routed to a proposed ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces Part II. External input: Borel–Wallach, Continuous cohomology, discrete subgroups, and representations of reductive groups, 2nd ed., AMS (2000) [9], Theorem VII.6.7, p. 226 (as cited on p. 406)

items.name: Weight-one residual set-up: ρ̄, S(ρ̄), vexing primes T(ρ̄), standing hypotheses, Q
items.statement: ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(k) is a continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible representation with ρ̄|_{G_p} unramified. S(ρ̄) is the set of primes of Q at which ρ̄ is ramified; T(ρ̄) ⊂ S(ρ̄) is the set of primes x with x ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|_{G_x} irreducible and ρ̄|_{I_x} reducible (the vexing primes, following Diamond). It is further assumed that if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|_{G_x} is reducible then ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ (0) (the paper notes this always holds for a twist of ρ̄ by a character unramified outside S(ρ̄)). Q denotes a finite set of primes of Q disjoint from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p} (by abuse also the product of its primes).
items.note: The standing data are an instance of planned notions, as with IKM's global-deformation-functors item (planned in R04.1/R04.3/R08.2). These are the residual representation (R01.1/R01.4), the ramification set S(ρ̄) and the local case distinctions of the minimally ramified conditions (R08.2). Diamond's term 'vexing' and the set T(ρ̄) are not named in any layer. The R08.2 blueprint should define them, and CG §3.1 is a good source. The twist remark is a small R01.1 lemma.

items.name: Unramified at p implies absolutely irreducible over Q(ζ_p)
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and let ρ̄ : G_Q → GL2(k) be continuous, odd and absolutely irreducible, with ρ̄|_{G_p} unramified. Then ρ̄|_{G_{Q(ζ_p)}} is absolutely irreducible. (Stated without proof in the paper; oddness is not needed for the implication.)
items.note: Covered by R01.4's restriction-to-cyclotomic-fields scope; its node supplies the key reduction to Q(√p*). The remaining step is not named. If ρ̄ ≅ Ind from K = Q(√p*), then ρ̄ ≅ ρ̄ ⊗ ε_K, which contradicts ρ̄|I_p = 1 because ε_K|I_p is nontrivial and p is odd. The R01.4 blueprint should add it, with CG §3.1 as the source.

items.name: Deformation of ρ̄
items.statement: For R in C_O, a deformation of ρ̄ to R is a ker(GL2(R) → GL2(k))-conjugacy class of continuous lifts ρ : G_Q → GL2(R) of ρ̄; the deformation containing a lift ρ is often referred to simply as ρ.
items.note: Strict-equivalence classes of lifts (conjugacy by ker(GL_2(R) → GL_2(k))) are R04.1. The extension from Artinian rings to all of C_O goes through pro-representability (R04.2, R03.2). No deformation theory in either library.

items.name: Definition 3.1: deformations minimal outside Q; minimal deformations
items.statement: A deformation ρ : G_Q → GL2(R) of ρ̄ is minimal outside Q if (1) det(ρ) = ⟨det(ρ̄)⟩, the Teichmüller lift of det(ρ̄); (2) if x ∉ Q ∪ S(ρ̄) is a prime of Q, then ρ|_{G_x} is unramified; (3) if x ∈ T(ρ̄), then ρ(I_x) → ρ̄(I_x) is an isomorphism; (4) if x ∈ S(ρ̄) − T(ρ̄) and ρ̄|_{G_x} is reducible, then ρ^{I_x} is a rank one direct summand of ρ as an R-module. If Q = ∅ such deformations are called minimal.
items.note: Conditions (2)-(4) are the unramified and DDT-minimal local conditions of R08.2: ρ(I_x) ≅ ρ̄(I_x) at vexing x, and ρ^{I_x} a rank-one direct summand. Condition (1) is R04.1's fixed-determinant variant. The global functor 'minimal outside Q' is an instance of R04.3. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/global-deformation-functors was classified the same way.

items.name: Representability of the minimal-outside-Q deformation functor
items.statement: The functor on C_O sending R to the set of deformations of ρ̄ to R that are minimal outside Q is represented by a complete Noetherian local O-algebra R_Q. When Q = ∅, R_∅ is also written R^min.
items.note: Representability of the unframed functor under absolute irreducibility is R04.2, with Schlessinger in R03.2. Representability of the minimal local subfunctors is R08.2, and the global quotient is R04.3. The paper only cites DDT Thm 2.41; nothing is in the libraries. External input: H. Darmon, F. Diamond, R. Taylor, 'Fermat's Last Theorem', in Elliptic curves, modular forms & Fermat's last theorem (Hong Kong 1993), Int. Press 1997 [27], proof of Theorem 2.41

items.name: Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄) and dual Selmer group H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄) is the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0ρ̄) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄)/L_{Q,x}, where x runs over all primes of Q and L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad^0ρ̄)^{I_x}) if x ∉ Q, and L_{Q,x} = H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄) if x ∈ Q. H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) denotes the corresponding dual Selmer group, i.e. the kernel of H^1(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) → ⊕_x H^1(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1))/L_{Q,x}^⊥, where L_{Q,x}^⊥ is the annihilator of L_{Q,x} under local Tate duality.
items.note: The Selmer and dual Selmer groups for the local conditions L_{Q,x} are planned at R02.5, on top of SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2's local-condition construction. The annihilator under local Tate duality comes from Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 5, which is not built.

items.name: Greenberg–Wiles Euler characteristic formula for Selmer groups
items.statement: (Used input: [27, Thm 2.18].) Let {L_x} be local conditions on ad^0ρ̄, unramified at almost all x; for p odd the archimedean condition is L_∞ = H^1(R, ad^0ρ̄) = 0. Then dim_k H^1_{L}(Q, ad^0ρ̄) = dim_k H^1_{L^⊥}(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) + dim_k H^0(Q, ad^0ρ̄) − dim_k H^0(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) + Σ_{x finite}(dim_k L_x − dim_k H^0(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄)) + (dim_k L_∞ − dim_k H^0(R, ad^0ρ̄)). Applied in the proof of Prop 3.2 to L = {L_{Q,x}}: the archimedean term is −1 (the paper just calls it 'the contribution at the infinite place'; it is −1 because p is odd and ρ̄ is odd); H^0(Q, ad^0ρ̄) = H^0(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0 by absolute irreducibility of ρ̄ and unramifiedness of ρ̄|G_p. As in the proof of [27, Cor. 2.43], the local term at a finite prime x vanishes if x ∉ Q (including x = p) and equals dim_k H^0(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1)) if x ∈ Q.
items.note: The formula (DDT Thm 2.18) is R02.5's dimension formula, resting on R02.3 (global Euler characteristic) and R02.4 (Poitou-Tate). The infinite-place −1 for odd ρ̄ and p odd belongs to R02.6's 'infinity ... contributions visible'. So do the vanishing of local terms for unramified conditions, including at x = p. External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], Theorem 2.18, and the local computations in the proof of Corollary 2.43

items.name: Dimension of the reduced tangent space of R_Q (Proposition 3.2)
items.statement: The reduced tangent space Hom(R_Q/m_O, k[ε]/(ε²)) of R_Q (here m_O = ϖO) has dimension dim_k H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) − 1 + Σ_{x∈Q} dim_k H^0(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1)).
items.note: This is an instance of the planned tangent-space and Selmer-dimension computations. Those layers are written against KW II, where the determinant is fixed and p may be 2. Their blueprint should record this instance: over Q, unramified at p, with the net −1 coming from the infinite place (defect ℓ₀ = 1). PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/prop-15-2 makes the same remark.

items.name: Tangent space of R_Q at Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Suppose that for each x ∈ Q, x ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues. Then H^0(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1)) is one-dimensional for each x ∈ Q, and the reduced tangent space of R_Q has dimension dim_k H^1_Q(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) − 1 + #Q.
items.note: The local computation dim H^0(Q_x, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 1 for x ≡ 1 mod p with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, and the resulting tangent dimension, are the dual-Selmer calculations R04.5 and R02.6 plan.

items.name: Existence of primes killing the dual Selmer group (argument of DDT Thm 2.49)
items.statement: Used input: suppose p is odd and ρ̄|G_{Q(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible. For every N ≥ 1 there is a set Q_N of q = dim_k H^1_∅(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) primes x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {p} with x ≡ 1 mod p^N and ρ̄(Frob_x) having distinct eigenvalues, such that H^1_{Q_N}(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0. The proof is Chebotarev: each nonzero dual Selmer class is detected by the restriction to G_x of such a prime x.
items.note: Killing the dual Selmer group by Chebotarev primes x ≡ 1 mod p^N with distinct eigenvalues, under cyclotomic absolute irreducibility, is exactly R04.5 and R02.6. Chebotarev is Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10, which is not built. External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], Theorem 2.49 (and its proof)

items.name: Taylor–Wiles primes for weight one (Proposition 3.3)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H^1_∅(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)). Then q ≥ 1, and for any integer N ≥ 1 there is a set Q_N of primes of Q such that: (1) #Q_N = q; (2) x ≡ 1 mod p^N for each x ∈ Q_N; (3) for each x ∈ Q_N, ρ̄ is unramified at x and ρ̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues; (4) H^1_{Q_N}(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = (0). In particular the reduced tangent space of R_{Q_N} has dimension q − 1, and R_{Q_N} is a quotient of a power series ring over O in q − 1 variables.
items.note: The Taylor-Wiles prime sets Q_N with #Q_N = q and H^1_{Q_N}(Q, ad^0ρ̄(1)) = 0 are R04.5. The presentation of R_{Q_N} as a quotient of O⟦x_1,…,x_{q−1}⟧ is R04.6. As in PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/prop-15-2 (which cites CG Prop 5.2), the KW II-based blueprint must record the 'one less' count (q−1 variables, ℓ₀ = 1).

items.name: Modular curves X_1(N), X_1(N;Q), X_1(NQ) over O and their moduli interpretations
items.statement: Fix an integer N ≥ 5 with (N, p) = 1 and a squarefree integer Q with (Q, Np) = 1. X_1(N), X_1(N;Q), X_1(NQ) are the modular curves of level Γ_1(N), Γ_1(N) ∩ Γ_0(Q), Γ_1(N) ∩ Γ_1(Q), as smooth proper schemes over Spec O. X_1(N) and X_1(NQ) are the base changes to O of the curves of Gross [28, Prop. 2.1]. Thus X_1(NQ) represents the functor sending an O-scheme S to the set of isomorphism classes of pairs (E, α_NQ), where E/S is a generalized elliptic curve and α_NQ : μ_NQ ↪ E[NQ] is an embedding of group schemes whose image meets every irreducible component of each geometric fibre. Write α_NQ = α_N × α_Q. The group (Z/NQZ)^× acts by ⟨a⟩(E, α_NQ) := (E, a∘α_NQ). X_1(N;Q) is the smooth proper O-curve classifying triples (E, α_N, C_Q): α_N : μ_N ↪ E[N] an embedding, and C_Q ⊂ E[Q] a subgroup étale-locally isomorphic to Z/QZ such that C_Q + α_N(μ_N) meets every irreducible component of every geometric fibre. X_1(N;Q) is the quotient of X_1(NQ) by (Z/QZ)^× ⊂ (Z/NQZ)^×, and X_1(NQ) → X_1(N;Q), (E, α_NQ) ↦ (E, α_N, α_Q(μ_Q)), is étale.
items.note: Tau Ceti ModularCurves compactifies only Y₁(N)/H for prime N ≥ 5 over Z[1/N], by normalisation, and excludes generalised elliptic curves. The curves X_1(N), X_1(NQ) and X_1(N;Q) over O (N invertible in O) with their moduli interpretation therefore belong to ModularCurvesPartII R13.1-R13.4a, whose source list includes CONRAD07. The μ_N-embedding (Gross) formulation, the mixed Γ₁(N)∩Γ₀(Q) problem and the étaleness of X_1(NQ) → X_1(N;Q) are not named and must be recorded when R13.2 is decomposed. External input: B. H. Gross, 'A tameness criterion for Galois representations associated to modular forms (mod p)', Duke Math. J. 61 (1990) [28], Proposition 2.1 (the models X_1(N), X_1(NQ))

items.name: The Hodge bundle ω on a modular curve
items.statement: For a modular curve X over O, Y ⊂ X is the open modular curve parametrizing genuine elliptic curves. π : E → X is the universal generalized elliptic curve and ω := π_*ω_{E/X}, where ω_{E/X} is the relative dualizing sheaf. ∞ denotes the reduced divisor supported on the cusps, and ω^{⊗n}(−∞) means ω^{⊗n} ⊗ O_X(−∞) (notation used but not spelled out in the paper). By Remark 3.10 (p. 325), H^0(X_R, ω^{⊗k}) is identified with Katz modular forms of weight k over R. The paper does not explicitly identify H^0(X, ω^{⊗n}(−∞)) with cusp forms.
items.locator: §3.2.1, p. 313 (Katz forms: Remark 3.10, p. 325); §1, p. 303 (introduced on X_1(N))
items.note: ω = π_*ω_{E/X}, ω(−∞) and forms as sections are R15.1, with the Tate-curve normalisation in its reviewed node 'hodge-bundle-with-tate-curve-normalization'. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism
items.statement: The Kodaira–Spencer map induces an isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1_{Y/O} over the open modular curve Y, which extends to an isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1_{X/O}(∞) on X. Equivalently Ω^1_{X/O} ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−∞).
items.note: The reviewed node records the Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism at full level n ≥ 3 over Z[1/n]. CG's Γ₁(N) and Γ_H versions over O follow by the descent R15.1 plans. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 also reads R15.1 as covering Kodaira-Spencer on modular curves. Neither library has Kodaira-Spencer, and the paper's citation '[29], A1.3.17' should point to Katz's 1973 LNM 350 paper. External input: N. M. Katz, 'p-adic properties of modular schemes and modular forms', Modular Functions of One Variable III, LNM 350 (1973), A1.3.17. The paper cites '[29], A1.3.17', but [29] is Katz's 1977 note; sourceIssues E19.

items.name: Curves X, X_1(Q), X_0(Q) of level Γ_H(N)
items.statement: Fix a subgroup H ⊂ (Z/NZ)^×. X (resp. X_1(Q), resp. X_0(Q)) denotes the quotient of X_1(N) (resp. X_1(NQ), resp. X_1(N;Q)) by the action of H. Each carries an action of (Z/NZ)^×/H. Assume H is chosen so that X is the fine moduli space (not merely the coarse one) of generalized elliptic curves with Γ_H(N)-level structure, where Γ_H(N) := {(a b; c d) ∈ Γ_0(N) : d mod N ∈ H}.
items.note: Γ_H(N)-quotients of the open curves are Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 9, which the atlas cites and does not re-plan. Compactified quotients at composite N, and the representability range CG assumes (X a fine moduli space), are ModularCurvesPartII R13.2 and R13.4a.

items.name: Coefficients: X_R, L_M, and torsion modular forms
items.statement: For an O-algebra R, X_R := X ×_{Spec O} Spec R. For an O-module M and a coherent sheaf L on X, L_M := L ⊗_O M. The closed immersion j : X_{O/ϖ^m} → X identifies H^0(X_{O/ϖ^m}, j^*L) with H^0(X, L_{O/ϖ^m}) for any O-flat sheaf of O_X-modules L, and L_{K/O} = lim→_m L_{O/ϖ^m}.
items.note: Forms with coefficients in an O-module are planned in R15.1. The identification H^0(X_{O/ϖ^m}, j^*L) = H^0(X, L_{O/ϖ^m}) and the colimit description L_{K/O} = lim L_{O/ϖ^m} are basic coherent-cohomology facts: the colimit uses commutation of cohomology with filtered colimits on a Noetherian scheme (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 scope).

items.name: Universal Hecke algebra T^univ
items.statement: T^univ is the commutative polynomial algebra over the group ring O[(Z/NQZ)^×] in indeterminates T_x (x prime, x ∤ pNQ) and U_y (y prime, y | Q). For a ∈ (Z/NQZ)^×, ⟨a⟩ denotes the corresponding element of T^univ.
items.note: T^univ is literally MvPolynomial ι (MonoidAlgebra O (ZMod (N*Q))ˣ), where ι indexes the primes x ∤ pNQ together with the primes y | Q. ⟨a⟩ is MonoidAlgebra.of a. The item defines only the abstract algebra; its action on cohomology is the separate (missing) Hecke-operator items.

items.name: Covers X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) and cusps C_Δ(Q)
items.statement: X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) is an étale Galois covering with group Δ_Q := (Z/QZ)^×. For a quotient Δ of Δ_Q, X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) is the corresponding intermediate cover (the quotient of X_1(Q) by ker(Δ_Q → Δ)). C_Δ(Q) ⊂ X_Δ(Q) is the divisor of cusps.
items.note: Free-quotient étale torsors on the open curves are Tau Ceti Layer 9A. Their extension over the cusps, and the cusp divisor C_Δ(Q), are ModularCurvesPartII R13.2-R13.4a together with R15.1's 'cusp ideal/divisor'. Étaleness of X_1(Q) → X_0(Q) at the cusps, which comes from the μ-type level structure, is not named and should be recorded in R13.3's blueprint.

items.name: Diamond operators on coherent cohomology
items.statement: For a ∈ (Z/NQZ)^× and L = ω^{⊗n} or ω^{⊗n}(−∞) on X_Δ(Q), there is a natural isomorphism ⟨a⟩^*L ≅ L. For an O-module A and i = 0, 1, ⟨a⟩ acts on H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A) as the pullback H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A) → H^i(X_Δ(Q), ⟨a⟩^*L_A) = H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A). The same recipe defines ⟨a⟩ on H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}), since ⟨a⟩ preserves C_Δ(Q). For i = 0 this is the usual diamond action (Gross [28, §3]).
items.note: The automorphisms ⟨a⟩ and ⟨a⟩^*ω ≅ ω are R14.1. Their action on forms is R15.2. The action on H^1 and on cusp sections is plain functoriality of coherent cohomology under an automorphism with a sheaf isomorphism (no trace), but no layer names it.

items.name: Γ_0(x)-level curves X_Δ(Q;x) and degeneracy maps π_1, π_2 (x ∤ pNQ)
items.statement: For a prime x ∤ pNQ, X_Δ(Q;x) is the O-curve obtained by adding Γ_0(x)-level structure to X_Δ(Q), equivalently the quotient of X_1(NQ;x) by the appropriate subgroup of (Z/NQZ)^×. There are two finite flat maps π_1, π_2 : X_Δ(Q;x) → X_Δ(Q). π_1 is the forgetful map on open curves, extended by contraction. π_2 sends (E, α_NQ, C_x) to (E' := E/C_x, α'_NQ), where α'_NQ is α_NQ composed with the natural isomorphism E[NQ] ≅ E'[NQ]. Both extend to the compactifications.
items.note: π_1 and π_2 on the Γ₀(x)-level curve and their extension to compactifications (Conrad Prop 4.4.3) are R14.1 and R13.4b, with the Γ₀(x)-refined moduli problem in R13.2. External input: B. Conrad, 'Arithmetic moduli of generalized elliptic curves', J. Inst. Math. Jussieu 6 (2007) [30], Proposition 4.4.3 (extension of π_i and φ_12 to compactifications)

items.name: Fricke-type map w_x
items.statement: w_x : X_Δ(Q;x) → X_Δ(Q;x) is defined on the open curve by (E, α_NQ, C_x) ↦ (E/C_x, α'_NQ, E[x]/C_x). It satisfies w_x²(E, α_NQ, C_x) = (E, x∘α_NQ, C_x) = ⟨x⟩(E, α_NQ, C_x), so it is not an involution. Also π_2 = π_1 ∘ w_x, hence π_2^*ω = w_x^*π_1^*ω = w_x^*ω.
items.note: On the open curve w_x is the Katz-Mazur [x-Isog] transposition (Tau Ceti Layer 8), carried along with the Γ₁(NQ) structure. Its extension to X_Δ(Q;x), and the identities w_x² = ⟨x⟩ and π_2 = π_1∘w_x, fall under R14.1's moduli-theoretic correspondences, although R14.1 does not name Atkin-Lehner maps.

items.name: The map φ_12 : π_2^*ω → π_1^*ω
items.statement: Let E be the universal elliptic curve over Y_Δ(Q;x), C_x ⊂ E the universal subgroup of order x, and φ : E → E/C_x the quotient isogeny. Pullback of differentials along φ defines φ_12 : π_2^*ω → π_1^*ω over Y_Δ(Q;x). It extends over X_Δ(Q;x) by [30, Prop. 4.4.3]. The same construction for x | Q on X_Δ(Q;x) (as in the U_x item) gives φ_12 there.
items.note: Pulling differentials back along the universal isogeny, and extending the resulting sheaf map π_2^*ω → π_1^*ω over the compactification (Conrad Prop 4.4.3), is part of R14.1's correspondence construction. Tau Ceti ModularCurves Layer 2 supplies isogenies over a base. External input: Conrad [30], Proposition 4.4.3

items.name: Operator W_x on forms of level Γ_0(x)
items.statement: W_x on H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), ω_A^{⊗n}) is the composite H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), ω_A^{⊗n}) → (w_x^*) H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), π_2^*ω_A^{⊗n}) → (φ_12^{⊗n}) H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), π_1^*ω_A^{⊗n}) = H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), ω_A^{⊗n}). Explicitly, W_x f(E, α_NQ, C_x) = φ^* f(E/C_x, α'_NQ, E[x]/C_x).
items.note: No layer names a geometric Atkin-Lehner-type operator W_x on H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), ω^n_A) for an arbitrary O-module A. R14.1 supplies the maps w_x and φ_12, and R15.2 defines Hecke actions only on forms. See sourceIssues E21 (printed display has target H^i, not H^0).

items.name: W_x² = x^n⟨x⟩ (W_x² = x⟨x⟩ in weight one)
items.statement: On H^0(X_Δ(Q;x), ω_A^{⊗n}), W_x² = x^n⟨x⟩. This is corrected: the paper prints 'W_x² = x⟨x⟩' for general n, which is right only for n = 1, the only case used (Lemmas 3.5, 3.6). In particular W_x² = x⟨x⟩ in weight one.
items.note: The identity is a composition formula for the operator W_x, which is itself not planned. The corrected form W_x² = x^n⟨x⟩ holds because the composite isogeny E → E/E[x] ≅ E is [x], which acts on ω^{⊗n} by x^n. The paper's W_x² = x⟨x⟩ is right for n = 1, the only case it uses. See sourceIssues E21 (W_x² = x^n⟨x⟩ in weight n).

items.name: Hecke operators T_x on H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n}_A), on cusp forms and on the cusps
items.statement: For a prime x ∤ pNQ, an O-module A, i = 0, 1 and L = ω^{⊗n}, define T_x by requiring x·T_x to be the composite H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A) → (π_2^*) H^i(X_Δ(Q;x), π_2^*L_A) → (φ_12^{⊗n}) H^i(X_Δ(Q;x), π_1^*L_A) → (tr(π_1)) H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A). x is a unit in O. For L = ω^{⊗n}(−∞) use the same composite, via π_2^*(ω^{⊗n}(−∞)) ⊂ (π_2^*ω^{⊗n})(−∞) and the fact that the trace preserves sections vanishing at the cusps. On H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}), x·T_x is the analogous composite through H^0(C_Δ(Q;x), π_j^*ω_A^{⊗n}), with φ_12 and the trace induced on the quotients (C_Δ(Q;x) ⊂ X_Δ(Q;x) the cuspidal divisor).
items.note: R14.1 plans the correspondences and 'the correct coherent/étale formulation' of traces, and R15.2 plans Hecke actions on forms. R15.2's reviewed node, however, defines T_l on forms with coefficients only for k ≥ 2 or (k = 1, 3 ≤ n ≤ 11), where base change holds. The weight-one, arbitrary-coefficient case and the actions on H^1 and on the cusp divisor are planned nowhere. Edixhoven's H^1 operators (the same definition, [31, p. 586]) appear inside R15.3's weight-reduction node over F̄_p, but not as a construction. External input: B. Edixhoven, 'The weight in Serre's conjectures on modular forms', Invent. Math. 109 (1992) [31], p. 586 (same definition)

items.name: Hecke-equivariance of the cuspidal long exact sequence
items.statement: The long exact sequence ⋯ → H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n}(−∞)_A) → H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}) → H^i(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}) → ⋯, coming from 0 → ω^{⊗n}(−∞) → ω^{⊗n} → ω^{⊗n}|_{C_Δ(Q)} → 0, is T_x-equivariant (x ∤ pNQ) for the operators T_x defined above. Equivariance for the diamond operators ⟨a⟩ and for U_x (x | Q), which are defined by the same recipes, is implicit in the paper rather than stated.
items.note: Equivariance of the cuspidal long exact sequence for T_x, U_x and ⟨a⟩ depends on the unplanned coherent Hecke actions. (The extraction's 'equivalent for U_x' should read 'equivariant'.)

items.name: Operators U_x for x | Q
items.statement: For a prime x | Q, X_1(NQ;x) is the smooth O-curve parametrizing tuples (E, α_NQ, C_x): E a generalized elliptic curve, α_NQ : μ_NQ ↪ E[NQ] an embedding, and C_x ⊂ E[x] a subgroup étale-locally ≅ Z/xZ such that α_NQ(μ_NQ) + C_x meets every irreducible component of every geometric fibre and α_NQ(μ_x) + C_x = E^sm[x]. X_Δ(Q;x) is its quotient by the subgroup used to form X_Δ(Q) from X_1(NQ). π_1 : X_Δ(Q;x) → X_Δ(Q) is the forgetful map, and π_2(E, α_NQ, C_x) = (E/C_x, α'_NQ). With φ_12 : π_2^*ω → π_1^*ω from [30, Prop. 4.4.3], U_x is defined on H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A) (L = ω^{⊗n} or ω^{⊗n}(−∞)) and on H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}) by the same formula x·U_x = tr(π_1)∘φ_12^{⊗n}∘π_2^*.
items.note: U_x at x | Q needs the curve X_1(NQ;x), whose level structure requires α_NQ(μ_x)+C_x = E^sm[x]. That curve is within R13.2's scope but unnamed. U_x then needs the same trace formula as T_x, which is unplanned. External input: Conrad [30], Proposition 4.4.3

items.name: Hecke action on the cusps is Eisenstein (Remark 3.4, corrected)
items.statement: (Remark 3.4, corrected.) The paper describes the action of T_x on H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}) as specializing q = 0 in the usual q-expansion formula for T_x ([28, §3]), with q a local parameter at the cusp ∞. This correctly computes T_x at the (Z/NQZ)^×-orbit of ∞, but that group does not act transitively on the cusps. Correct statement: if f ∈ H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_k^{⊗n}) is a nonzero eigenform for all T_x (x ∤ pNQ) with character χ : (Z/NQZ)^× → k^× (⟨a⟩f = χ(a)f), then its eigensystem is Eisenstein. The associated semisimple representation (unramified at x ∤ pNQ, with Frob_x characteristic polynomial X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩x^{n−1}) is ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2ε^{n−1} with ψ_1ψ_2 = χ, hence reducible. For f supported on the orbit of ∞, T_x f = (1 + χ(x)x^{n−1})f and the representation is 1 ⊕ χε^{n−1}; the paper asserts this for every f. Consequently, and this is all Lemma 3.7(2) uses (there with n = 1, A = K/O), H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n})_m = 0 for every maximal ideal m of T^univ coming from a non-Eisenstein m_∅.
items.note: The Hecke action on H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω^n_k) as the q = 0 specialisation of the q-expansion formula, and the conclusion that its eigensystems are Eisenstein, are planned nowhere. It is the input to Lemma 3.7(2). The correction of sourceIssues E23 applies: the paper's T_x f = (1+χ(x)x^{n−1})f holds on the orbit of ∞, and in general one gets ψ_1 ⊕ ψ_2ε^{n−1}. External input: Gross [28], §3 and formula (3.5) (q-expansion of T_x)

items.name: Anaemic and full Hecke algebras T^an, T, T_∅
items.statement: T^an ⊂ End_O H^0(X_1(Q), ω_{K/O}) is the O-subalgebra generated by the Hecke operators T_n with (n, pNQ) = 1 and all diamond operators ⟨a⟩ with (a, NQ) = 1 ('an' = anaemic). T is the O-algebra generated by the same operators together with U_x for all primes x | Q. For Q = 1, T_∅ = T^an_∅ denotes T. T^an is a finite O-algebra, hence T^an = ∏_m T^an_m over its maximal ideals. There are natural homomorphisms T^an → T^an_∅ = T_∅, induced by H^0(X, ω_{K/O}) ↪ H^0(X_1(Q), ω_{K/O}), and T^an ↪ T.
items.note: ModularCurvesPartII R14.2 plans integral Hecke algebras through faithful action on Jacobian or Tate-module objects. R15.2's node covers Hecke operators on forms only where base change holds. The anaemic and full weight-one Hecke algebras on H^0(X_1(Q), ω_{K/O}), whose modules can have torsion that does not lift, and their product decomposition are planned nowhere.

items.name: Residual Galois representation attached to a maximal ideal of T_∅
items.statement: For each maximal ideal m_∅ of T_∅ there are a finite extension k' of T_∅/m_∅ and a continuous semisimple representation G_Q → GL_2(k'). It is characterized by: for each prime x ∤ Np it is unramified at x and Frob_x has characteristic polynomial X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩ (mod m_∅). It can be defined over T_∅/m_∅.
items.note: Gross Prop 11.1 multiplies a mod p Katz weight-one eigenform by the Hasse invariant (R15.3) to reach weight p. It then lifts via Deligne-Serre with a weight change (R15.5) and applies Deligne's representations (R19.1); R15.5 explicitly flags the Katz weight-one case. The representation is not claimed unramified at p here. External input: Gross [28], Proposition 11.1 (applied to a normalized eigenform f ∈ H^0(X, ω_{k'}) on which T_∅ acts through m_∅)

items.name: Eisenstein and non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: A maximal ideal m_∅ of T_∅ is Eisenstein if the associated residual Galois representation (above) is reducible, and non-Eisenstein otherwise. For m_∅ non-Eisenstein, its preimage in T^an, again written m_∅, is a maximal ideal of T^an.
items.note: The notion of an (non-)Eisenstein maximal ideal, meaning one whose residual representation is reducible or irreducible, is used and planned by R14.3 and R19.6. Here it is applied to the weight-one algebra T_∅, which is itself unplanned (hecke-algebras-Tan-T-Tempty).

items.name: Galois representations valued in localized weight-one Hecke algebras
items.statement: If m_∅ is non-Eisenstein, there is a continuous representation G_Q → GL_2(T_{∅,m_∅}), unramified away from pN, such that for x ∤ pN the characteristic polynomial of Frob_x is X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩. Likewise there is a continuous representation G_Q → GL_2(T^an_{m_∅}), unramified away from pNQ, with the same characteristic polynomials for x ∤ pNQ.
items.note: R19.6 plans representations over localised Hecke algebras in its cohomological settings. IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.4 plans 'compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems'. The weight-one input is not planned: a Hecke-equivariant embedding of H^0(X, ω_{O/ϖ^m}) into higher weight by powers of Hasse-invariant lifts, which yields a representation over the possibly non-flat T_{∅,m∅} and T^an_{m∅}. This matches PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/thm-14-5, which is missing.

items.name: Localizations T^an_{m_∅} and T_{m_∅}
items.statement: For m_∅ non-Eisenstein, viewed also as a maximal ideal of T^an, the localization T_{m_∅} := T ⊗_{T^an} T^an_{m_∅} is a direct factor of T. After possibly extending O, its maximal ideals correspond to the systems of U_x-eigenvalues (x | Q) on H^0(X_1(Q), ω_k)[m_∅].
items.note: The claim that T_{m∅} = T ⊗ T^an_{m∅} is a direct factor whose maximal ideals match the U_x-eigenvalue systems on H^0(X_1(Q), ω_k)[m∅] concerns the unplanned weight-one Hecke algebras. The underlying algebra (a finite algebra over a complete local ring is a product of its localisations) is not cited from either library here.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles level raising in weight one (Lemma 3.5)
items.statement: Setting of §3.2 (N ≥ 5, (N,p) = 1, H with X a fine moduli space, Q squarefree with (Q, Np) = 1), with m_∅ a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_∅. Suppose that for each prime x | Q, x ≡ 1 mod p and X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩ ∈ T_∅[X] has distinct roots modulo m_∅. Let m be the maximal ideal of T containing m_∅ and U_x − α_x, for a choice of root α_x of X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩ mod m_∅ for each x | Q. Then there is a T^an_{m_∅}-module isomorphism H^0(X, ω_{K/O})_{m_∅} ≅ H^0(X_0(Q), ω_{K/O})_m.
items.note: GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2 plans the analogous control statement at Taylor-Wiles level ('prove the required freeness/control statement ... specialisation back to the original level') only for its KW II defect-0 Hecke modules. Nothing plans it for weight-one coherent H^0 with K/O coefficients. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 records that GL2ModularityLifting 'has none for weight-one coherent cohomology'. See sourceIssues E26 (length argument needs ϖ^m-torsion submodules) and E27 (full faithfulness of π_1^* does not suffice).

items.name: T^an_{m_∅} → T_{∅,m_∅} is surjective
items.statement: For m_∅ non-Eisenstein, the natural map T^an_{m_∅} → T_{∅,m_∅} is surjective. Hence the localization H^0(X, ω_{K/O})_{m_∅} is the same whether m_∅ is regarded as an ideal of T_∅ or of T^an.
items.note: The argument is that the T_{∅,m∅}-valued representation descends to the image of T^an, and that T_x and ⟨x⟩ are the trace and determinant of Frobenius. The generic tools are planned (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.5 coefficient descent, IHG.1 reconstruction), but they are applied here to the unplanned weight-one representation.

items.name: Degeneracy maps ψ, ψ^∨ and V_x at a prime x ∤ Np
items.statement: For a prime x ∤ Np let π_1, π_2 : X_0(x) → X be the projections and φ_12 : π_2^*ω → π_1^*ω as in §3.2.3. Define V_x := φ_12∘π_2^* : H^0(X, ω_{K/O}) → H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O}). Define ψ := (π_1^*, V_x) : H^0(X, ω_{K/O})² → H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O}) and ψ^∨ := x^{−1}(tr(π_1), tr(π_1)∘W_x)^T : H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O}) → H^0(X, ω_{K/O})², with W_x the operator of §3.2.3 (NQ there playing the role of N). Both are T^an-linear.
items.note: The degeneracy maps π_1^* and V_x = φ_12∘π_2^* come from maps that R14.1 plans. ψ^∨, however, uses the weight-one coherent trace and W_x on K/O-coefficient forms (both unplanned). ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.1 plan degeneracy and old/new statements only in their étale, Betti and Jacobian settings.

items.name: The composite ψ^∨∘ψ and its determinant
items.statement: ψ^∨∘ψ is given by the matrix [[x^{−1}tr(π_1)∘π_1^*, x^{−1}tr(π_1)∘φ_12∘π_2^*], [x^{−1}tr(π_1)∘W_x∘π_1^*, x^{−1}tr(π_1)∘W_x∘φ_12∘π_2^*]] = [[x^{−1}(x+1), T_x], [T_x, ⟨x⟩(x+1)]]. Hence det(ψ^∨∘ψ) = x^{−1}(x+1)²⟨x⟩ − T_x². If α_x, β_x are the roots of X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩ mod m_∅, then det ≡ x^{−1}(α_x − xβ_x)(β_x − xα_x) mod m_∅. When x ≡ 1 mod p this is ≡ 4⟨x⟩ − T_x² ≡ −(α_x − β_x)² mod m_∅.
items.locator: §3.2.4, proof of Lemma 3.5 (p. 318) and of Lemma 3.6 (p. 321)
items.note: This is the matrix of ψ^∨∘ψ and its determinant mod m∅, a step in the proofs of Lemmas 3.5 and 3.6 that depends on the unplanned weight-one operators.

items.name: Relations between U_x, T_x, π_1^* and V_x; the matrix of U_x on old forms
items.statement: As maps H^0(X, ω_{K/O}) → H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O}) (weight one, x prime, x ∤ Np): π_1^*∘T_x = U_x∘π_1^* + x^{−1}V_x, and U_x∘V_x = x·π_1^*∘⟨x⟩. The second identity is corrected: the paper prints U_x∘V_x = π_1^*∘⟨x⟩. Consequently U_x preserves Im ψ. In the coordinates (f, g) ↦ π_1^*f + V_x g on H^0(X, ω_{K/O})²_{m∅} ≅ (Im ψ)_{m∅}, it acts by A = [[T_x, x⟨x⟩], [−x^{−1}, 0]], whose characteristic polynomial is X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩. Hence (A − α_x)(A − β_x) ≡ 0 mod m_∅ in M_2(T_{∅,m∅}).
items.note: These are the relations π_1^*∘T_x = U_x∘π_1^* + x^{−1}V_x and (corrected) U_x∘V_x = x·π_1^*∘⟨x⟩, and the oldform matrix of U_x in weight one. They are composition formulas of the kind R14.1 plans ('Prove composition, double-coset and adjoint formulas'), but for unplanned coherent operators. The correction is consistent with the paper's own matrix A = [[T_x, x⟨x⟩], [−x^{−1}, 0]].

items.name: Identity x^{−1}π_1^*∘tr(π_1)∘W_x = U_x + x^{−1}W_x
items.note: The identity x^{−1}π_1^*∘tr(π_1)∘W_x = U_x + x^{−1}W_x on H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O}) is a step of Lemma 3.5 using the unplanned W_x and coherent trace. See sourceIssues E27 (proof needs a direct moduli computation).

items.name: Lemma 3.6, distinct-roots case (auxiliary prime without x ≡ 1 mod p)
items.statement: Suppose Q = x is a prime not dividing Np and the roots α_x, β_x of X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩ ∈ (T_∅/m_∅)[X] do not have ratio x or x^{−1} (m_∅ non-Eisenstein). Let m be the maximal ideal of T containing m_∅ and U_x − α_x. If α_x ≠ β_x, there is a T^an_{m_∅}-isomorphism H^0(X, ω_{K/O})_{m_∅} ≅ H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O})_m.
items.note: This is level raising at an auxiliary non-Taylor-Wiles prime, with eigenvalue ratio ≠ x^{±1}, in weight-one coherent H^0. Level-change results in R14.4 and R20.1 are planned only in étale and Jacobian (weight ≥ 2) settings.

items.name: Lemma 3.6, equal-roots case (multiplicity doubles)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Lemma 3.6 (Q = x prime, x ∤ Np, root ratio ≠ x^{±1}, m_∅ non-Eisenstein), if α_x = β_x then there is a T^an_{m_∅}-isomorphism H^0(X, ω_{K/O})²_{m_∅} ≅ H^0(X_0(x), ω_{K/O})_m, induced by ψ.
items.note: This is the doubling-multiplicity case (α_x = β_x) of Lemma 3.6. It is unplanned for the same reason as the distinct-root case.

items.name: The maximal ideal m of T^univ
items.statement: Let Δ be a quotient of Δ_Q = (Z/QZ)^×. The non-Eisenstein ideal m_∅, together with a choice of eigenvalue α_x mod m_∅ for U_x for each prime x | Q, gives rise to a maximal ideal m of T^univ. After extending O if necessary, T^univ/m ≅ k. Implicitly, not spelled out in the paper, m is the kernel of T^univ → T_∅/m_∅ sending T_x ↦ T_x (x ∤ pNQ), ⟨a⟩ ↦ ⟨a mod N⟩ (a ∈ (Z/NQZ)^×) and U_x ↦ α_x (x | Q). Localizations at m of the T^univ-modules H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A), H^0(C_Δ(Q), ω_A^{⊗n}), and later H_i(X_Δ(Q), L), are written (·)_m.
items.note: T^univ is in the library (MvPolynomial over MonoidAlgebra). The maximal ideal m built from m∅ and the chosen U_x-eigenvalues, and the localised modules H^i(X_Δ(Q), L_A)_m, depend on the unplanned weight-one Hecke algebras and actions.

items.name: Pontryagin duality
items.statement: For an O-module M, M^∨ := Hom_O(M, K/O). M ↦ M^∨ is the Pontryagin duality functor.
items.note: M^∨ = Hom_O(M, K/O) is the O-linear Pontryagin dual that CC.3 plans 'with ... correct coefficient targets'. Mathlib has only the ℤ-linear character module and the topological Pontryagin dual.

items.name: Lemma 3.7(1): H^1 with K/O coefficients is divisible
items.statement: Let Δ be a quotient of Δ_Q and L a vector bundle on X_Δ(Q). Then H^1(X_Δ(Q), L_{K/O})^∨ is p-torsion free; equivalently H^1(X_Δ(Q), L_{K/O}) is divisible.
items.note: Divisibility of H^1(X, L_{K/O}) for a vector bundle on a flat proper O-curve follows from H^2 = 0 on curves. That input is planned in Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B over a field and StableReduction Layer 2 over locally Noetherian bases. The lemma itself is planned nowhere, and the libraries have no vanishing theorem.

items.name: Lemma 3.7(2): cusp forms = all forms after localizing at non-Eisenstein m
items.statement: Let Δ be a quotient of Δ_Q and m the maximal ideal of T^univ attached to a non-Eisenstein m_∅ and choices of α_x (x | Q). For i = 0, 1 the natural map H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω(−∞)_{K/O})_m → H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω_{K/O})_m is an isomorphism.
items.note: The statement that cusp forms and all forms agree on H^0 and H^1 after localising at a non-Eisenstein m follows from Remark 3.4 and the unplanned coherent Hecke actions. See sourceIssues E23 (Remark 3.4's transitivity claim is false).

items.name: Homology groups H_i(X_Δ(Q), L) and the maps π_*
items.statement: For a vector bundle L on X_Δ(Q) and i = 0, 1, H_i(X_Δ(Q), L) := H^i(X_Δ(Q), (Ω^1 ⊗ L^*)_{K/O})^∨. Here L^* is the dual bundle and Ω^1 = Ω^1_{X_Δ(Q)/O} ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−∞) via Kodaira–Spencer. If Δ ↠ Δ' are quotients of (Z/QZ)^× giving a Galois cover π : X_Δ(Q) → X_{Δ'}(Q) and L is a vector bundle on X_{Δ'}(Q), then π_* : H_i(X_Δ(Q), π^*L) → H_i(X_{Δ'}(Q), L) is the Pontryagin dual of the pullback π^* on cohomology.
items.note: The coherent homology H_i(X, L) := H^i(X, (Ω^1⊗L^*)_{K/O})^∨ and the maps π_* are planned nowhere. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/weight-one-sheaf, the Shimura-curve analogue, is likewise missing. The O-linear Pontryagin dual is planned at CompletedCohomologyPartII:CC.3.

items.name: Verdier (Grothendieck–Serre) duality D : H_i ≅ H^{1−i}
items.statement: For a vector bundle L on X_Δ(Q) there is an isomorphism D : H_i(X_Δ(Q), L) ≅ H^{1−i}(X_Δ(Q), L) (O-coefficient coherent cohomology), i = 0, 1. Under D the map π_* corresponds to the trace tr(π) : H^{1−i}(X_Δ(Q), π^*L) → H^{1−i}(X_{Δ'}(Q), L).
items.note: Serre duality is planned over a field (Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B) and in SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3. StableReduction Layer 2 plans the relative dualizing sheaf of proper flat curves over a base. The integral form H_i(X, L) ≅ H^{1−i}(X, L) over O, obtained from duality over O/ϖ^m and passage to the limit, and its compatibility of π_* with the trace are planned nowhere. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24's serre-duality-14 item for Shimura curves is also missing. External input: R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, LNM 20 (1966) [32], Corollary 11.2(f)

items.name: Hecke action on H_i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n})
items.statement: T^univ acts on H_i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n}) as follows: identify Ω^1 with ω^{⊗2}(−∞), so H_i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n}) = H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{2−n}(−∞)_{K/O})^∨, and take the Pontryagin dual (transpose) of the T^univ-action on H^i(X_Δ(Q), ω^{2−n}(−∞)_{K/O}).
items.note: The Hecke action on H_i is the transpose of the (unplanned) action on H^i(X, ω^{2−n}(−∞)_{K/O}), through Kodaira-Spencer.

items.name: Atkin–Lehner-type operator w^* attached to ζ
items.statement: Extend O so that it contains a primitive NQ-th root of unity ζ. w^* is the operator on H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^{⊗n}) (also with K/O coefficients) attached to ζ as in Edixhoven [31, §7.1].
items.note: Edixhoven's operator w_ζ on geometric forms on X_Δ(Q) over O[ζ_NQ] is planned nowhere. Edixhoven §7, its source, is already a source of R15.3's reviewed weight-reduction node. External input: Edixhoven [31], §7.1

items.name: The duality isomorphism Φ and its Hecke compatibility
items.statement: Let Φ be the composite of isomorphisms H^1(X_Δ(Q), ω^{2−n}(−∞)_{K/O}) →(D) H^0(X_Δ(Q), Ω ⊗ ω^{n−2}(∞))^∨ →(KS^∨) H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^n)^∨ →((w^*)^∨) H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^n)^∨. Here D is Verdier duality and KS the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism. Then Φ∘T_x = x^{1−n}T_x^∨∘Φ for primes x ∤ pNQ, the same relation holds for U_x (x | Q), and Φ∘⟨x⟩ = ⟨x⟩∘Φ, where on the right the operators act by the duals of their actions on H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^n).
items.note: R15.3's reviewed node 'weight-reduction-to-at-most-p-plus-one' lists Edixhoven Prop. 7.3 among its proof inputs: 'Hecke compatibility of the boundary map ... obtained from Serre duality and Kodaira-Spencer'. That is the same Hecke-twisted duality, over F̄_p at level N ≥ 5. The O and K/O version on X_Δ(Q), Φ∘T_x = x^{1−n}T_x^∨∘Φ, is not planned. External input: Edixhoven [31], proof of Proposition 7.3

items.name: Ψ : H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^n) ≅ H_1(X_Δ(Q), ω^n); Hecke-linear in weight one
items.statement: Ψ := Φ^∨ : H^0(X_Δ(Q), ω^n) → H_1(X_Δ(Q), ω^n) is an isomorphism of O-modules. When n = 1, Ψ is T-linear, i.e. it commutes with all T_x, U_x and ⟨a⟩.
items.note: Ψ = Φ^∨ : H^0(X, ω^n) ≅ H_1(X, ω^n), which is T-linear when n = 1 because x^{1−n} = 1. It depends on the unplanned Φ and H_1.

items.name: Defect over O[Δ] via coinvariants
items.statement: Let Δ be a finite p-group, S = O[Δ] (a local ring), M a finitely generated S-module, and r the O-rank of the coinvariants M_Δ = M ⊗_S O. Tensoring 0 → O →(ϖ) O → k → 0 (trivial Δ-action) with M gives an exact sequence 0 → Tor_1^S(M, O)/ϖ → Tor_1^S(M, k) → M_Δ →(ϖ) M_Δ → M ⊗_S k → 0. Hence d_S(M) := dim_k M ⊗_S k − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, k) = r − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, O)/ϖ.
items.note: The defect d_S(M) and balanced modules are in the reviewed DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 node 'balanced-modules-and-module-patching' (CG Defs 2.1-2.2). The coinvariant formula d_S(M) = r − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, O)/ϖ for S = O[Δ] is not in it.

items.name: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q), and its Hecke equivariance
items.statement: For a finite étale Galois cover π : X → Y with group G and a sheaf F on Y, there is a spectral sequence H^i(G, H^j(X, π^*F)) ⇒ H^{i+j}(Y, F), functorial in F. Applied to X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) with group Δ and F = (Ω^1 ⊗ ω^{−1} ⊗ L^*)_{K/O}, and Pontryagin-dualized, it gives a spectral sequence H_i(Δ, H_j(X_Δ(Q), ω⊗L)) = Tor_i^{O[Δ]}(H_j(X_Δ(Q), ω⊗L), O) ⇒ H_{i+j}(X_0(Q), ω⊗L). Its differentials commute with the action of T^univ. After localizing at m this gives M_Δ ≅ H_0(X_0(Q), ω⊗L)_m (with M = H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω⊗L)_m) and an exact sequence (H_1(X_Δ(Q), ω⊗L)_m)_Δ → H_1(X_0(Q), ω⊗L)_m → Tor_1^{O[Δ]}(M, O) → 0.
items.note: The general spectral sequence H^i(G, H^j(X, π^*F)) ⇒ H^{i+j}(Y, F) for a finite étale Galois cover (Milne III.2.20, with III.3.8 for quasi-coherent sheaves) falls within SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 ('Own Zariski, etale ... site comparisons; construct sheaf cohomology'). PAPER-HARPAZ-WITTENBERG-16/30 already placed the field case there. Not planned anywhere: the T^univ-equivariance of its differentials (functoriality along the Hecke correspondences), its Pontryagin-dualised Tor form, and the localised consequences M_Δ ≅ H_0(X_0(Q))_m with the Tor_1 exact sequence. External input: J. S. Milne, Étale Cohomology (1980) [33], Theorem III.2.20 and Remark III.3.8

items.name: Balancedness of weight-one homology at Taylor–Wiles level (Proposition 3.8)
items.statement: Setting of §3.2 (N ≥ 5, (N,p) = 1, H with X a fine moduli space, Q squarefree with (Q, Np) = 1), with m the maximal ideal of T^univ attached to a non-Eisenstein m_∅ and choices of U_x-eigenvalues. Let Δ be a quotient of (Z/QZ)^× of p-power order. Then the O[Δ]-module H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω)_m is balanced (Definition 2.2), i.e. d_{O[Δ]}(H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω)_m) ≥ 0.
items.note: Balancedness of H_0(X_Δ(Q), ω)_m over O[Δ] replaces GL2ModularityLifting:R22.2's freeness in defect ℓ₀ = 1. No layer plans it. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 plans the patching that consumes it (CG Prop 2.3), and P9 the balanced-dimension conclusions for complexes.

items.name: Remark 3.10: representability, stacks, and Katz forms
items.statement: Several of the modular curves considered do not represent their moduli problems (because of automorphisms). In such cases X_H(N) is still a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Spec O, ω descends to it (though not always to the associated scheme), and H^0(X, ω) makes sense with many of the required properties. If Y → X is a finite étale morphism of modular stacks with Galois group G and L = ω^k, then H^0(X, L) ≅ H^0(Y, L)^G. Taking Y representable (always possible for the X considered), H^0(X_R, ω^k) is identified, for an O-algebra R, with the Katz modular forms of weight k over R as defined in [29]. Footnote 3: for H ⊂ (Z/13Z)^× the squares, X_1(13) → X_H(13) is finite étale with group Z/3Z, and the scheme underlying X_H(13) is P^1 over O (p ≠ 13). Serre [34, 35] has ρ̄ : G_Q → GL_2(F_3) with N(ρ̄) = 13, k(ρ̄) = 2, ε(ρ̄) quadratic, induced from Q(√−3); Serre's conjecture (3.2.4?) of [36] predicts a mod-3 form on X_H(13). As a stack, for p = 3, H^0(X_H(13)_{F_3}, ω²) = H^0(X_1(13)_{F_3}, ω²)^{Z/3Z} ≠ 0, in accordance with [31, Conj. 4.2]. As printed with ω²; the genus-zero point is really about cusp forms ω²(−∞), and H^0(X_1(13)_{F_3}, ω²(−∞))^{Z/3Z} ≠ 0. p. 326: the paper avoids stacks by choosing a prime q ≢ 1 mod p, q ≥ 5, with ρ̄ unramified at q (implicitly q ∤ Np) and the eigenvalue ratio of ρ̄(Frob_q) neither q nor q^{−1} (equal eigenvalues allowed). Infinitely many such q exist by Chebotarev: take q split completely in the fixed field of ker ρ̄ with q ≢ 1 mod p. It then adds Γ_1(q)-level structure. Every deformation of ρ̄ with fixed determinant is unramified at q, and by Lemma 3.6 the Hecke-module multiplicities are the same or doubled according as ρ̄(Frob_q) has distinct or equal eigenvalues.
items.note: Planned elsewhere: modular curves as DM stacks, descent of ω, H^0(X, L) ≅ H^0(Y, L)^G, and the identification with Katz forms (R15.1 and its level-one/level-two descent node). Not planned: the p. 326 device, an auxiliary prime q ≢ 1 mod p with eigenvalue ratio ≠ q^{±1} chosen by Chebotarev, then Γ₁(q) structure and Lemma 3.6. That device resembles PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/rmk-12-2 (missing) and should be split out. Footnote 3 is a worked example. External input: N. M. Katz [29] (definition of Katz modular forms)

items.name: Serre level N, the subgroup H and the base modular curve X (weight-one setting of §3.3)
items.statement: Standing setting of §3 (p ≥ 3; O the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Q_p, uniformiser ϖ, residue field k; C_O the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k). ρ̄: G_Q → GL₂(k) is continuous, odd and absolutely irreducible, ρ̄|G_p is unramified, and ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0 whenever x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible (§3.1). Set N = N(ρ̄), the Serre level of ρ̄, and let H be the p-part of (Z/N(ρ̄)Z)^×. With N and H fixed, X denotes the modular curve of §3.2.1, i.e. the quotient of X₁(N) by H (the curve X_H(N) over O of generalized elliptic curves with Γ_H(N)-level structure, Γ_H(N) = {(a b; c d) ∈ Γ₀(N) : d mod N ∈ H}); likewise X₁(Q), X₀(Q) are the H-quotients of X₁(NQ), X₁(N;Q). The paper notes that N ≥ 5 by Serre's conjecture and that ρ̄ is modular of this level by Edixhoven [31, Theorem 4.5].
items.note: This item is a choice of data, and each piece is planned. N(ρ̄) is R01.3. The compactified Γ_H(N)-curve over O ⊃ Z[1/N] and its H-quotients X₁(Q), X₀(Q) are R13.2/R13.4a, with Tau Ceti Layer 9 for the open part; Tau Ceti Layer 10 compactifies only prime N ≥ 5 and uses no generalised elliptic curves. ω on the curve is R15.1. The asides 'N ≥ 5' and 'ρ̄ is modular of level N(ρ̄)' rest on ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6 and SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3. K2's setup-3-3-serre-level covers the same data and is also planned.

items.name: Assumption 3.9: no vexing primes
items.statement: Assumption 3.9: the set T(ρ̄) is empty, where T(ρ̄) ⊂ S(ρ̄) is the set of (vexing) primes x at which ρ̄ is ramified with x ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|G_x irreducible and ρ̄|I_x reducible (§3.1).
items.note: This is a Prop-valued hypothesis, T(ρ̄) = ∅, on the vexing primes defined in §3.1; it adds no new mathematics. The vexing case belongs with R08.2's minimally ramified conditions. AutomorphicCongruences L5w pins the identical non-vexing condition (H3) for BCS/Fujiwara, so the predicate should be defined once in R08.2 and imported by L5w and the Part II. CG removes the assumption in §3.9.

items.name: Cohomology of ω^k on modular stacks and Katz modular forms (Remark 3.10)
