items.statement: If X = X_H(N) does not represent its moduli problem, it is still a smooth proper Deligne–Mumford stack over Spec(O) and ω descends to X. For a finite étale morphism Y → X of modular stacks with Galois group G and L = ω^k, there is an isomorphism H⁰(X, L) ≃ H⁰(Y, L)^G. Taking Y representable, for an O-algebra R, H⁰(X_R, ω^k) is identified with the Katz modular forms of weight k over R (as in [29]).
items.note: Four parts are planned. R09.4/SF.1 give X_H(N) as a smooth proper DM stack over O. R15.1 gives the descent of ω, the isomorphism H⁰(X, L) ≅ H⁰(Y, L)^G for a representable finite étale Galois cover Y → X, and the identification of H⁰(X_R, ω^k) with Katz forms over R. Footnote 3 makes a good R15.1 acceptance test: the coarse space of X_H(13) has genus 0, yet H⁰(X_H(13)_{F₃}, ω²) ≠ 0.

items.name: Auxiliary prime q to make the modular curves representable
items.statement: Choose a prime q with q ≠ p [implicit in the paper], q ≢ 1 mod p and q ≥ 5, such that ρ̄ is unramified at q and the ratio of the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_q) is neither q nor q^{-1} (equal eigenvalues allowed). Infinitely many such primes exist. The fixed field L of ker(ρ̄) does not contain Q(ζ_p) (p ≠ 2 and ρ̄ is unramified at p, which is the corrected justification). So by Chebotarev there are infinitely many q that split completely in L with q ≢ 1 mod p, and these satisfy the conditions. For such q, the ratio condition means ρ̄ has no deformations that are ramified and Steinberg (unipotent on inertia) at q, and q ≢ 1 mod p rules out any other deformations ramified at q. So every deformation of ρ̄ with fixed determinant is unramified at q. One adds Γ₁(q)-level structure and the arguments go through almost unchanged. The only difference is that the multiplicity of the corresponding Hecke modules is either the same as expected or twice it, according as ρ̄(Frob_q) has distinct or equal eigenvalues (Lemma 3.6).
items.note: Three pieces are planned. Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10 gives the 'infinitude of every Frobenius class'. AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry R09.5 plans to 'Construct removal or addition of auxiliary prime-to-characteristic level and show how it rigidifies automorphisms'. R08.2 plans the local conditions away from p. Three pieces are not planned. (i) The local lemma: if ρ̄ is unramified at q, q ≢ 1 mod p and the eigenvalue ratio is not q^{±1}, every fixed-determinant lift of ρ̄|G_q is unramified. (ii) The existence of such q ≥ 5, split completely in the kernel field of ρ̄ with q ≢ 1 mod p, using ζ_p ∉ that field. (iii) The multiplicity statement, which rests on Lemma 3.6.

items.name: The maximal ideal m_∅ of T_∅ attached to ρ̄
items.statement: There exists a maximal ideal m_∅ of T_∅ (the Hecke algebra of §3.2.4 with Q = 1, acting on H⁰(X, ω_{K/O})) corresponding to ρ̄: m_∅ is generated by ϖ, T_x − Trace(ρ̄(Frob_x)) for all primes x with (x, Np) = 1, and ⟨x⟩ − det(ρ̄(Frob_x)) for all x with (x, N) = 1 (lifts to O of the traces and determinants being understood). Extending O if necessary, T_∅/m_∅ = k.
items.note: When ρ̄(Frob_p) has distinct eigenvalues, m_∅ exists by planned layers: Serre's conjecture at level N(ρ̄) (ClassicalSerreModularity R27.6) and Edixhoven's Theorem 4.5 with k(ρ̄) = 1, whose proof the reviewed R15.4 node assigns to SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3. The exceptional case, equal eigenvalues, needs Coleman–Voloch [37], which no layer plans; R20.5 says 'Do not claim this layer proves the general Katz weight-one refinement'. The algebra T_∅ is itself unplanned (K2: hecke-algebras-Tan-T-Tempty). This matches K2's serre-conjecture-weight-one-modularity and IKM's companion-forms, both missing. External input: Serre's conjecture (Khare–Wintenberger [24], Invent. Math. 178 (2009)); companion forms: Gross [28] (Duke Math. J. 61 (1990)) and Coleman–Voloch [37] (Invent. Math. 110 (1992)); level: Edixhoven [31, Theorem 4.5]

items.name: The maximal ideal m of T at level Q
items.statement: Let Q be a squarefree integer with (Q, Np) = 1 (as in §3.2). For each prime x | Q assume that X² − T_x X + ⟨x⟩ has distinct roots in T_∅/m_∅ = k, and choose a root α_x ∈ k. T denotes the O-subalgebra of End_O H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{K/O}) generated by T_n ((n, pNQ) = 1), the diamond operators ⟨a⟩ ((a, NQ) = 1) and U_x (x | Q) (§3.2.4). m is the maximal ideal of T generated by (the preimage of) m_∅ and U_x − α_x for x ∈ Q.
items.note: R14.1 and R15.2 plan Hecke correspondences and actions. However, the reviewed R15.2 node gives Katz's T_ℓ on weight-one forms with module coefficients only for levels 3 ≤ n ≤ 11. GL2ModularityLifting R22.2 plans Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebras only in the KW II Betti/étale setting. So no layer plans the weight-one torsion Hecke algebra T at level Q with the operators U_x, or the ideal m generated by m_∅ and U_x − α_x. K2's maximal-ideal-m-of-Tuniv is the same kind of object and is also missing.

items.name: Theorem 3.11 (Local–Global Compatibility), part 1: Galois representation over T_m, unramified at p
items.statement: Setting: p ≥ 3; ρ̄, N, H, X as in §3.3 (with the auxiliary Γ₁(q)-level of Remark 3.10 if needed); Assumption 3.9; Q squarefree with (Q, Np) = 1; T_∅, m_∅ with T_∅/m_∅ = k; for each prime x | Q, X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩ has distinct roots in k and α_x is a chosen root; T and m ⊂ T as in max-ideal-m-level-Q. Then there exists a deformation ρ_Q: G_Q → GL₂(T_m) of ρ̄ which is unramified outside NQ (in particular unramified at p) and is determined (up to conjugation) by the property that Trace(ρ_Q(Frob_x)) = T_x for all primes x with (x, pNQ) = 1.
items.note: The ingredients are planned elsewhere: weight-n representations over Hecke algebras (R19.1, R19.6), their ordinary local structure (R21.3), the Hasse invariant (R15.3), and determinant interpolation through finite quotients (IHG.4). The theorem itself is planned nowhere: a deformation of ρ̄ over the torsion weight-one algebra T_m, unramified at p, determined by its traces. IKM's Shimura-curve analogue thm-14-5 and K2's hecke-valued-galois-reps are also missing, and ML.1's 'weight-one modularity in proved cases' is only a registry.

items.name: Theorem 3.11, part 2: the twist ρ'_Q is minimal outside Q
items.statement: In the setting of thm-3-11-existence, let η be the unique character of p-power order with η² = ⟨det(ρ̄)⟩·det(ρ_Q)^{-1} (⟨·⟩ the Teichmüller lift), and ρ'_Q := ρ_Q ⊗ η. Then ρ'_Q is a deformation of ρ̄ minimal outside Q (Definition 3.1): det ρ'_Q = ⟨det ρ̄⟩; ρ'_Q|G_x is unramified for primes x ∉ Q ∪ S(ρ̄) (including x = p); condition (3) at T(ρ̄) is vacuous under Assumption 3.9; and for x ∈ S(ρ̄) − T(ρ̄) with ρ̄|G_x reducible, (ρ'_Q)^{I_x} is a rank-one direct summand.
items.note: Twisting and changing the determinant are planned generically in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.4 ('twisting by characters', 'changing determinant'). The minimal conditions at S(ρ̄) come from thm-3-14, which is planned. Not planned: the p-power-order square root η (p > 2) and the proof that ρ_Q ⊗ η over the weight-one algebra T_m is minimal outside Q, which needs thm-3-11-existence.

items.name: Theorem 3.11, part 3: local structure of ρ'_Q at primes x | Q
items.statement: In the setting of thm-3-11-existence, and [hypothesis added, see sourceIssues E35] assuming each prime x | Q satisfies x ≡ 1 mod p (or at least α_x/β_x ≢ x^{±1} in k, where β_x is the other root), as for the Taylor–Wiles primes of Proposition 3.3: for a prime x | Q, the restriction of ρ'_Q to D_x is conjugate to a direct sum ξ ⊕ ⟨det(ρ̄)⟩|_{D_x}·ξ^{-1} of residually unramified characters, where ξ̄(Frob_x) ≡ α_x mod m, and the restriction of ξ to I_x, hence via local class field theory to Z_x^× ⊗ Z_p = Δ_x (the p-part of (Z/xZ)^×), is compatible in the usual way with the diamond operators in T_m.
items.note: In weight ≥ 2 the local structure at the Taylor–Wiles primes is planned: GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5, GL2ModularityLifting R22.2 ('construct the auxiliary Hecke modules and the finite group actions') and R19.4. Remark 3.12 transfers it to weight one by Hasse-invariant congruences. The weight-one torsion statement over T_m is not planned. The item's added hypothesis at x | Q (x ≡ 1 mod p, or α_x/β_x ≢ x^{±1}) is recorded as sourceIssues E35.

items.name: The weight-one T_p lies in T_m and equals the trace of Frob_p
items.statement: Consequence of the proof of Theorem 3.11 (all three cases). Let T_p be the weight-one Hecke operator at p (Gross [28, §4]) acting on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m. Then T_p ∈ T_m/I_m for every m > 0, hence T_p ∈ T_m, and Trace(ρ_Q(Frob_p)) = T_p. If α ≠ β (the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_p)), moreover ρ_Q|G_p ≅ λ(α̃) ⊕ λ(β̃), where α̃, β̃ ∈ T_m are the roots of X² − T_pX + ⟨p⟩ lifting α, β.
items.note: This is a consequence of the three cases of the proof. It depends on Gross's weight-one T_p (gross-weight-one-Tp, missing) and on the Galois representations of thm-3-11-existence. No layer plans the weight-one operator T_p or its membership in T_m.

items.name: The quotients T_m/I_m and the reduction to finite level
items.statement: For each m > 0, H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m ≅ H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{K/O})_m[ϖ^m]; let I_m be the annihilator of this module in T_m. Then T_m = lim←_m T_m/I_m, so it suffices to construct, for each m > 0, a representation ρ_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m) satisfying the conditions of Theorem 3.11.
items.note: This is an elementary reduction: T_m is finite over O and acts faithfully on the union of the ϖ^m-torsion submodules, so T_m ≅ lim T_m/I_m. It concerns the unplanned weight-one torsion Hecke algebras. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7's 'finite coefficient quotients before inverse limits' concerns complexes, not this.

items.name: Multiplication φ by a lift A of a power of the Hasse invariant
items.statement: Fix m > 0. Let A be a lift of (some power of) the Hasse invariant whose q-expansion satisfies A ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m, of weight n − 1, where n − 1 is divisible by (p − 1) and by a large enough power of p that ε^{n−1} ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m. Multiplication by A defines φ: H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{K/O}) → H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_{K/O}). Both sides embed by q-expansion into K/O⟦q⟧, and the square formed with the identity of K/O⟦q⟧ commutes only modulo ϖ^m (on ϖ^m-torsion, φ is the identity on q-expansions). φ is Hecke-equivariant away from p on ϖ^m-torsion.
items.note: This is planned as a weight-change statement. R15.3 constructs A and its characteristic-zero lifts, and R15.2 supplies the q-expansion principle and the Hecke q-expansion formulas. The mod-ϖ^m refinement used here should be written into R15.3 with CG as source. It needs three things: A ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m, e.g. a p^{m−1}-th power of a lift; n − 1 divisible by (p−1)p^{m−1}, so that ℓ^{n−1} ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m; and equivariance for T_ℓ, ⟨a⟩ and U_x on ϖ^m-torsion.

items.name: Gross: the Hecke operator T_p on weight-one Katz forms mod ϖ^m
items.statement: For level prime to p, the Hecke operator T_p acts on weight-one Katz forms with coefficients in O/ϖ^m, i.e. on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m}), commuting with the other Hecke operators; on q-expansions T_p = U + ⟨p⟩V, where U(Σa_jq^j) = Σa_{jp}q^j and V(Σa_jq^j) = Σa_jq^{jp}. (Used in the form: on q-expansions mod ϖ^m, φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ = ⟨p⟩V_p.)
items.note: R15.2's reviewed node defines T_ℓ only for ℓ invertible on the base (Katz 1.11). R15.3 plans Frobenius/Verschiebung but not Gross's operator. That operator is T_p on weight-one Katz forms over O/ϖ^m, equal to U + ⟨p⟩V on q-expansions, commuting with the other Hecke operators (Gross [28] §4, Prop. 4.1, (4.7)). Gross [28] was not read; the statement follows CG's use of it. External input: B. H. Gross, A tameness criterion for Galois representations associated to modular forms (mod p), Duke Math. J. 61 (1990), 445–517: §4 (Prop. 4.1 and formula (4.7))

items.name: The map ψ = (φ, φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ) from two copies of weight one to weight n
items.statement: ψ: H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})² = H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{K/O})²[ϖ^m] → H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_{K/O})[ϖ^m] = H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_{O/ϖ^m}) is ψ = (φ, φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ), i.e. ψ(f, g) = φ(f) + (φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ)(g), with T_p the weight-one operator (Gross) and U_p the weight-n Hecke operator at p. On q-expansions modulo ϖ^m, ψ = (φ, ⟨p⟩V_p), V_p(Σa_jq^j) = Σa_jq^{jp}.
items.note: The doubling map is ψ = (φ, φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ) from two copies of weight one to weight n. It uses φ (planned at R15.3) and Gross's T_p (missing). No layer plans it, for modular curves or for Shimura curves; IKM's doubling-injectivity and thm-14-5 are also missing.

items.name: Katz: θ is injective on mod p forms of small weight
items.statement: The theta operator θ = q d/dq on mod p Katz modular forms (level prime to p) has no kernel on forms of weight k with 1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2 (the paper: 'no kernel in weight ≤ p − 2'); in particular, for p ≥ 3, θ is injective on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_k).
items.note: Injectivity in weight 1 for p ≥ 3 follows from the planned filtration rule, since a nonzero weight-one form has filtration 1. The rule gives injectivity in weights 1 ≤ k ≤ p − 2; in weight p − 1, θ(A) = 0. R15.3's reviewed decomposition records the construction of θ from Katz, LNM 601 ('A result on modular forms in characteristic p'), as an unread import. That paper is exactly CG's [29]. External input: N. M. Katz, A result on modular forms in characteristic p, Modular functions of one variable V, LNM 601 (1977), 53–61 ([29])

items.name: ψ is injective
items.statement: The map ψ: H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})² → H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_{O/ϖ^m}) is injective.
items.note: The proof reduces to the ϖ-socle and uses the q-expansion principle (R15.2), the identity ψ = (φ, ⟨p⟩V) on q-expansions, and Katz's θ-injectivity (R15.3). The injectivity of ψ itself is not planned. IKM's Shimura-curve version, which uses the supersingular locus, is also missing.

items.name: Action of U_p on the image of ψ
items.statement: U_p (weight n) preserves ψ(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²) and, transported by ψ^{-1}, acts on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})² by the matrix (T_p ⟨p⟩; −1 0) in the coordinates ψ(f, g) = φ(f) + (φ∘T_p − U_p∘φ)(g) [corrected; the paper prints (T_p 1; −⟨p⟩ 0), which is the conjugate matrix for the coordinates (f, ⟨p⟩g); see sourceIssues E37], with T_p the weight-one operator (cf. Gross [28, Prop. 4.1]). Hence U_p satisfies U_p² − T_pU_p + ⟨p⟩ = 0 on the image of ψ, acts invertibly there (determinant ⟨p⟩), and U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{-1} acts on the image of ψ by diag(T_p, T_p).
items.note: This depends on ψ and Gross's T_p, both missing. I checked the corrected matrix. With T_p = U + ⟨p⟩V in weight one, U_p ≡ U mod ϖ^m in weight n, and UV = id, one gets U_pψ(f,0) = ψ(T_pf, −f) and U_pψ(0,g) = ψ(⟨p⟩g, 0). In the coordinates (f, g) the matrix is (T_p ⟨p⟩; −1 0), as the item states. Its characteristic polynomial X² − T_pX + ⟨p⟩ agrees with the printed matrix, so the paper's argument is unaffected.

items.name: Eigenvalues of U_p on the m-part of Im ψ
items.statement: Let α, β be the (possibly equal) eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_p) and α̃, β̃ ∈ O any lifts. Then ⟨p⟩ ≡ αβ mod m, and (U_p − α̃)(U_p − β̃) acts nilpotently on ψ(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²_m). The only possible eigenvalues of U_p modulo m in higher weight are determined by ρ̄ and are α, β or 0; since U_p acts invertibly on ψ(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²_m), only α and β occur there.
items.note: Gross [28] was not read, so this describes the input as CG uses it. The facts ⟨p⟩ ≡ αβ mod m and that the residual U_p-eigenvalues lie in {α, β, 0} come from the Galois representations of weight-n forms (R19.1, R21.3). They also use Gross's Proposition 12.1: the representation of a mod-p weight-one eigenform is unramified at p, with the expected Frobenius polynomial. No layer plans Proposition 12.1; R20.5 disclaims the Katz weight-one refinement, and K2's residual-galois-rep-m-empty is planned only without unramifiedness at p. The nilpotence of (U_p − α̃)(U_p − β̃) on the m-part of Im ψ is not planned either. External input: Gross [28, Proposition 12.1 and the remark before equation (4.7)]

items.name: Weight-n Hecke algebras T_n^an ⊂ T_n ⊂ T̃_n and the ideals m, m̃_α, m̃_β
items.statement: For the weight n ≥ 2 of hasse-multiplication-phi: T_n^an ⊂ End_O(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_O)) is the O-subalgebra generated by T_x for primes (x, NQp) = 1 and diamond operators ⟨a⟩ for (a, NQ) = 1; T_n is the subalgebra generated by T_n^an and U_x for x | Q; T̃_n is the subalgebra generated by T_n and U_p (U_p denoting the weight-n Hecke operator T_p). m_∅ also denotes the maximal ideal of T_n^an corresponding to ρ̄; m ⊂ T_n is generated by m_∅ and U_x − α_x (x ∈ Q); m̃_α, m̃_β ⊂ T̃_n are the ideals containing m and U_p − α, resp. U_p − β; if α = β one writes m̃ = m̃_α = m̃_β. Since n > 1, H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_O) ⊗ O/ϖ^m ≅ H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_{O/ϖ^m}), so the latter is a module for T̃_n (and T_n, T_n^an).
items.note: The weight-n (n ≥ 2) Hecke algebras over O on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω^n_O) are planned: R14.1 supplies the correspondences and R15.2 the actions. They include U_x for x | Q and U_p, which is T_p at level prime to p. The base change H⁰(ω^n_O) ⊗ O/ϖ^m ≅ H⁰(ω^n_{O/ϖ^m}) for n ≥ 2 is the reviewed R15.2 node (Katz 1.7.1). The ideals m, m̃_α, m̃_β are elementary.

items.name: The ordinary image T_{n,m_α} and its embedding in a product of fields
items.statement: There is a natural map T_{n,m} → T̃_{n,m̃_α}. T_{n,m_α} denotes its image [corrected: in all cases; the paper says the map is injective when α = β, which fails in general; see sourceIssues E38]. There are inclusions T_{n,m_α} ↪ T̃_{n,m̃_α} ↪ ∏_i E_i. Here E_i runs over a finite collection of finite extensions of K corresponding to the ordinary eigenforms of weight n and level Γ₁(NQ) (the paper's wording; implicitly the eigenforms on X₁(Q) whose Hecke eigensystem is congruent to m̃_α, i.e. T_x ≡ Trace ρ̄(Frob_x) for (x, NQp) = 1, U_x ≡ α_x for x | Q, and U_p ≡ α).
items.note: The image algebra T_{n,m_α} is a definition. The embedding T̃_{n,m̃_α} ↪ ∏E_i is reducedness of the O-flat weight-n Hecke algebra after localisation: U_x is semisimple on oldforms there because X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩ has distinct roots mod m. That lies in R15.2/R19.6's scope. The correction of the paper's injectivity claim is sourceIssues E38.

items.name: Galois representations ρ_{n,α}, ρ̃_{n,α} of the weight-n ordinary Hecke algebras (§3.4 (a), (b))
items.statement: There are continuous representations ρ_{n,α}: G_Q → GL₂(T_{n,m_α}) and ρ̃_{n,α}: G_Q → GL₂(T̃_{n,m̃_α}) such that: (a) ρ̃_{n,α} is ρ_{n,α} composed with the natural inclusion T_{n,m_α} → T̃_{n,m̃_α}; (b) ρ_{n,α} and ρ̃_{n,α} are unramified at all primes x with (x, pNQ) = 1, and the characteristic polynomial of ρ_{n,α}(Frob_x) for such x is X² − T_xX + x^{n−1}⟨x⟩.
items.note: Parts (a) and (b) are planned. The char-0 eigenform representations with polynomial X² − a_xX + x^{n−1}⟨x⟩ are R19.1, whose reviewed node follows Deligne–Serre Theorem 6.1. They are glued over the localised Hecke algebra in R19.6. Part (a) is composition with an inclusion. The weight-one analogue (K2's hecke-valued-galois-reps) is missing. External input: Standard facts on Galois representations attached to classical modular forms (Deligne), glued over the Hecke algebra via Carayol [39] since ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible; the paper gives no specific citation

items.name: Ordinary local structure at p of ρ̃_{n,α} (§3.4 (c))
items.statement: (c) If E is a field of characteristic zero and φ: T̃_{n,m̃_α} → E is a homomorphism [printed T̃_{n,m̃}; see sourceIssues E39], then φ∘ρ̃_{n,α}|G_p is equivalent to a representation of the form (ε^{n−1}λ(φ(⟨p⟩)/φ(U_p)) ∗; 0 λ(φ(U_p))), where λ(z) is the unramified character sending Frob_p to z.
items.note: The ordinary shape of φ∘ρ̃_{n,α}|G_p at characteristic-zero points, (ε^{n−1}λ(φ(⟨p⟩)/φ(U_p)) ∗; 0 λ(φ(U_p))), is the local structure of p-ordinary eigenforms (Wiles 1988, Mazur–Wiles), planned in R21.3 and R19.5. The printed T̃_{n,m̃} for T̃_{n,m̃_α} is sourceIssues E39. External input: Local structure of p-ordinary eigenforms (e.g. A. Wiles, On ordinary λ-adic representations associated to modular forms, Invent. Math. 94 (1988), §2; Mazur–Wiles); the paper cites only 'standard facts'

items.name: Theorem 3.14: ρ_{n,α} is minimal away from p
items.statement: Under Assumption 3.9, ρ_{n,α} is a deformation of ρ̄ satisfying conditions (2) and (4) of Definition 3.1, except for the condition of being unramified at p. That is: ρ_{n,α}|G_x is unramified for every prime x ∉ Q ∪ S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}; and for x ∈ S(ρ̄) − T(ρ̄) with ρ̄|G_x reducible, ρ_{n,α}^{I_x} is a rank-one direct summand of ρ_{n,α} as a T_{n,m_α}-module. The paper justifies this by the choice of N and H, the local Langlands correspondence, and results of Diamond–Taylor and Carayol ([15, Lemma 5.1.1]). Moreover, by the choice of H, det(ρ_{n,α})|I_x has order prime to p for each prime x | N. [The paper prints 'for each prime x ≠ p', which fails for x | Q; see sourceIssues E40.] Without Assumption 3.9, condition (2) still holds.
items.note: This is CDT Lemma 5.1.1: local–global compatibility away from p at each point, via local Langlands, Diamond–Taylor and Carayol, transferred to the O-flat reduced Hecke algebra. Unramifiedness of det ρ_{n,α}|I_x up to prime-to-p order comes from the choice of H. R22.1 is written for KW II's Hilbert/quaternionic setting, so CDT §5 and CG should be added as sources for the modular-curve Γ₁(N)/H case. See sourceIssues E40 (determinant claim must exclude x | Q). External input: Conrad–Diamond–Taylor [15, Lemma 5.1.1] (via the local Langlands correspondence and results of Diamond–Taylor and Carayol)

items.name: The T̃_{n,m̃}[G_Q]-module B
items.statement: Fix one eigenvalue α of ρ̄(Frob_p) and write m̃ = m̃_α. Via ρ̃_{n,α}, B := T̃²_{n,m̃} is a T̃_{n,m̃}[G_Q]-module, free of rank two over T̃_{n,m̃}, with B/m̃ ≅ ρ̄ as a G_Q-representation; G_p denotes the decomposition group of G_Q at p.
items.note: B is the free rank-two module underlying ρ̃_{n,α}. It is planned with that representation, and B/m̃ ≅ ρ̄ is its residual property.

items.name: Lemma 3.15 (1)–(2): the ordinary filtration of B
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄(Frob_p) is not a scalar. Then there is an exact sequence of T̃_{n,m̃}[G_p]-modules 0 → A → B → C → 0 such that (1) A and C are free T̃_{n,m̃}-modules of rank one, and (2) the sequence splits, B ≃ A ⊕ C, as a sequence of T̃_{n,m̃}-modules.
items.note: The ordinary filtration 0 → A → B → C → 0, free of rank one and T̃-split, is the ordinary local structure over the Hecke algebra that R21.3 plans. The standard sources prove it when ρ̄ is p-distinguished. CG's case, ρ̄(Frob_p) non-scalar with α = β allowed, rests on dim C/m = 1, Nakayama's lemma and O-flatness. It should be added to R21.3 with CG as source.

items.name: Lemma 3.15 (3): the quotient C is unramified with Frobenius U_p
items.statement: In Lemma 3.15, the action of G_p on C factors through G_{F_p} = G_p/I_p, and Frobenius acts via the operator U_p ∈ T̃_{n,m̃}.
items.note: The unramified quotient C, on which Frobenius acts through U_p, is part of the ordinary local structure over the Hecke algebra planned in R21.3.

items.name: Lemma 3.15 (4): the character on the sub A
items.statement: In Lemma 3.15, G_p acts on A via the character ε^{n−1}λ(⟨p⟩U_p^{-1}) [corrected: the paper also says 'is unramified', which is false since ε^{n−1} is ramified for n ≥ 2; the character is unramified modulo ϖ^m because ε^{n−1} ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m; see sourceIssues E41].
items.note: The character ε^{n−1}λ(⟨p⟩U_p^{−1}) on A is part of R21.3's ordinary local structure. The printed claim that A is 'unramified' is false for n ≥ 2 and is corrected in the item. The character is unramified only modulo ϖ^m, because ε^{n−1} ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m. This is sourceIssues E41.

items.name: Case α ≠ β: Hensel lifting of U_p-eigenvalues and the projection isomorphism
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ β. (i) Since U_p acts invertibly on Im ψ and T_p = U_p^{-1}⟨p⟩ + U_p there, T_p − α − β lies in m̃_α and in m̃_β, so T_p − α̃ − β̃ acts nilpotently on H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m, and T_m/I_m[T_p] ⊂ End(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m) is a local ring (maximal ideal m̃ generated by m and T_p − α − β). (ii) U_p satisfies X² − T_pX + ⟨p⟩ = 0 over T_m/I_m[T_p], so by Hensel's lemma there are α̃, β̃ ∈ T_m/I_m[T_p], lifting α and β, with (U_p − α̃)(U_p − β̃) = 0 on the m-part of the image of ψ. (iii) Composing φ with the T̃_n-equivariant projection onto (ψH⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²)_{m̃_α} gives an isomorphism of T^univ-modules H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})_m ≃ (ψH⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²)_{m̃_α}.
items.note: The whole argument is weight-one specific: T_p − α − β nilpotent on the m-part, the locality of T_m/I_m[T_p], the lifts α̃, β̃, and the projection isomorphism onto the m̃_α-part of Im ψ. It depends on ψ and Gross's T_p (missing) and on the Lemma 3.5 argument (K2: missing).

items.name: Case α ≠ β: T_m/I_m as a quotient of the ordinary weight-n Hecke algebra; T_p ∈ T_m/I_m
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ β. Then T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] ⊂ End(Im(ψ)_{m̃_α}) is a quotient of T̃_{n,m̃_α}, and T_m/I_m is the corresponding quotient of T_{n,m_α}. The trace of any lift of Frobenius at p on the corresponding quotient of ρ_{n,α} equals U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{-1} (as ε^{n−1} ≡ 1 mod ϖ^m), which equals T_p in End(Im(ψ)_{m̃_α}); hence T_p ∈ T_m/I_m. Since U_p = α̃ in T_m/I_m[U_p], the corresponding quotients of T_{n,m_α} and T̃_{n,m̃_α} coincide.
items.note: This realises T_m/I_m as a quotient of the ordinary weight-n algebra, with T_p = U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{−1} ∈ T_m/I_m. It depends on the missing doubling material and on the planned weight-n algebras (R15.2, R19.6).

items.name: The representations ρ_{Q,m}, ρ̃_{Q,m} and the twist ρ'_{Q,m}
items.statement: ρ_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m) is ρ_{n,α} composed with the surjection T_{n,m_α} ↠ T_m/I_m, and ρ̃_{Q,m} is ρ̃_{n,α} on the corresponding quotient T_m/I_m[U_p] of T̃_{n,m̃_α} (in §§3.6–3.7 on the quotient T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] of T̃_{n,m̃}, and ρ̃_{Q,m} = ρ_{Q,m} ⊗_{T_{n,m}} T̃_{n,m̃}). The character ν := ⟨det ρ̄⟩·det(ρ_{Q,m})^{-1} is unramified outside Q and of p-power order; since p > 2, ν has a square root η, also unramified outside Q; ρ'_{Q,m} := ρ_{Q,m} ⊗ η satisfies all conditions of Definition 3.1 except possibly unramifiedness at p, and it suffices to show that ρ̃_{Q,m} (equivalently ρ_{Q,m}) is unramified at p.
items.note: This constructs ρ_{Q,m} and ρ̃_{Q,m} as quotients of ρ_{n,α} (planned) through the missing doubling quotients, together with the twist by η = √ν. Twisting in general is planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.4. The reduction to 'ρ_{Q,m} unramified at p' is weight-one specific.

items.name: Chebotarev + Carayol: ρ_{Q,m} is determined by its traces
items.statement: Let R be a complete Noetherian local ring with residue field k and ρ₁, ρ₂: G_Q → GL₂(R) continuous representations whose residual representation ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible. If Trace ρ₁ = Trace ρ₂, then ρ₁ and ρ₂ are conjugate. Together with the Chebotarev density theorem: ρ_{Q,m} is uniquely determined by Trace ρ_{Q,m}(Frob_x) = T_x for all primes (x, pNQ) = 1.
items.note: Uniqueness up to conjugation from traces is planned, with residual absolute irreducibility over a complete local ring (IHG.1, R19.6, R01.5), and so is Chebotarev density (Tau Ceti Layer 10). For p > 2 the traces determine the rank-two determinant law. R19.6's reviewed node records a gap: Chenevier's Theorem B needs an algebraically closed residue field, and 'That descent is not supplied by this source'. Carayol [39], Théorème 1, is stated for a finite residue field and closes that gap. External input: H. Carayol, Formes modulaires et représentations galoisiennes à valeurs dans un anneau local complet, Contemp. Math. 165 (1994), 213–237, Théorème 1 ([39])

items.name: Case α ≠ β: ρ_{Q,m}|G_p ≅ λ(α̃) ⊕ λ(β̃)
items.statement: Suppose α ≠ β. By Lemma 3.15 for m̃_α, ρ̃_{Q,m}|G_p ≅ (λ(β̃) ∗; 0 λ(α̃)); by symmetry (defining ρ_{Q,m} via T_{n,m_β}, legitimate by carayol-trace-uniqueness) also ρ̃_{Q,m}|G_p ≅ (λ(α̃) ∗; 0 λ(β̃)). Since α ≠ β, ρ_{Q,m}|G_p splits as λ(α̃) ⊕ λ(β̃); in particular ρ_{Q,m} is unramified at p, and T_p = U_p^{-1}⟨p⟩ + U_p = α̃ + β̃ = Trace(ρ_{Q,m}(Frob_p)).
items.note: The argument combines the two ordinary filtrations, obtained from m̃_α and m̃_β, with α ≠ β to split ρ_{Q,m}|G_p. It uses Lemma 3.15 (planned in R21.3) and Carayol uniqueness (planned). The weight-one conclusion is not planned.

items.name: Lemma 3.16 (Doubling)
items.statement: Suppose α = β, so m̃ = m̃_α = m̃_β [the paper states the lemma 'without any assumption on ρ̄(Frob_p)'; it is correct, and only used, when α = β; see sourceIssues E43]. Then the action of T̃_{n,m̃} on ψ(H⁰(X₁(Q), ω_{O/ϖ^m})²_m) factors through a quotient isomorphic to T_m/I_m[T_p][X]/(X² − T_pX + ⟨p⟩), where U_p acts by X. In particular this quotient T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] is free of rank two over T_m/I_m[T_p], with basis 1, U_p.
items.note: The key step is that U_p satisfies no relation AU_p + B = 0 over T_m/I_m[T_p] on the m-part of Im ψ; this is the injectivity of ψ. That step is not planned. The item correctly restricts the lemma to α = β.

items.name: Doubled quotients (after Wiese)
items.statement: Following Wiese [38], a quotient of T̃_{n,m̃} is called doubled if it is free of rank 2 as a module for the image of T_{n,m} in it ('the corresponding quotient of T̃_{n,m̃} contains two copies of the image of T_{n,m}'). By Lemma 3.16 (α = β), the quotient T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] of T̃_{n,m̃} is doubled over T_m/I_m = T_m/I_m[T_p].
items.note: Wiese's notion of a doubled quotient [38] (free of rank 2 over the image of T_{n,m}) appears in no layer. The atlas's other 'doubling' matches (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4, and others) are the unrelated Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis doubling method.

items.name: Case α = β: ρ_{Q,m} over T_m/I_m and ρ̃_{Q,m} ≃ ρ_{Q,m} ⊕ ρ_{Q,m}
items.statement: Suppose α = β. The trace under ρ_{n,α} of any lift of Frobenius at p is sent to U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{-1} = T_p in T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p], so T_p ∈ T_m/I_m; the image of T_{n,m} under T_{n,m} → T̃_{n,m̃} ↠ T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] is T_m/I_m = T_m/I_m[T_p], which gives ρ_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m). Let ρ̃_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m[U_p]) be obtained by tensoring over T_{n,m} with T̃_{n,m̃}. By Lemma 3.16, T_m/I_m[U_p] ≃ T_m/I_m ⊕ T_m/I_m as T_m/I_m-modules, and hence ρ̃_{Q,m} ≃ ρ_{Q,m} ⊕ ρ_{Q,m} as T_m/I_m[G_Q]-modules (in particular as T_m/I_m[G_p]-modules). As in §3.5 it suffices to prove that ρ_{Q,m} is unramified at p.
items.note: This depends on Lemma 3.16. The steps are: T_p ∈ T_m/I_m, the representation ρ_{Q,m} over T_m/I_m, and ρ̃_{Q,m} ≅ ρ_{Q,m} ⊕ ρ_{Q,m} as a T_m/I_m[G_Q]-module. None is planned.

items.name: Lemma 3.17 (Wiese): R-split sequences 0 → N → M ⊕ M → L → 0
items.statement: Let (R, m) be a local ring, and let N, M and L be R[G_p]-modules which are free R-modules of rank two. Suppose there is an exact sequence of R[G_p]-modules 0 → N → M ⊕ M → L → 0 which is split as a sequence of R-modules, and that L/m is indecomposable as an R[G_p]-module. Then N ≃ M ≃ L as R[G_p]-modules.
items.note: This is general algebra over a local ring R with a group G_p: an R-split exact sequence 0 → N → M ⊕ M → L → 0 of rank-two free R-modules with L/m indecomposable forces N ≃ M ≃ L. Wiese's Proposition 4.4 is stated for F_p-algebras, with the condition on N. Neither library has it, and no layer plans it; IHG.1's 'extension modules and the lattice constructions' is the nearest scope. External input: G. Wiese, On Galois representations of weight one, Doc. Math. 19 (2014), 689–707, Proposition 4.4 ([38]); stated there for F_p-algebras R and with the condition on the submodule N; the paper says the proof is the same

items.name: Case α = β, ρ̄(Frob_p) non-scalar: ρ_{Q,m} is unramified at p
items.statement: Suppose α = β and ρ̄(Frob_p) is non-scalar. Tensor the sequence 0 → A → B → C → 0 of Lemma 3.15 with the doubled quotient T_m/I_m[U_p] = T_m/I_m ⊕ T_m/I_m of T̃_{n,m̃}: the quotient of B is ρ̃_{Q,m}, free of rank 4 over T_m/I_m and ≅ ρ_{Q,m} ⊕ ρ_{Q,m} as a T_m/I_m[G_p]-module; the quotients of A and C (call the latter L) are free of rank 2 over T_m/I_m, and the sequence is T_m/I_m-split. Frob_p acts on L/m by U_p, and L/m is free of rank one over k[U_p]/(U_p − α)², so U_p − α acts nilpotently but non-trivially and L/m is indecomposable. By Lemma 3.17, L ≃ ρ_{Q,m} as G_p-modules; L is a quotient of C, hence unramified; so ρ_{Q,m} is unramified at p, and T_p = U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{-1} = Trace(ρ_{Q,m}(Frob_p)).
items.note: The argument tensors the planned Lemma 3.15 filtration with the doubled quotient and applies Lemma 3.17 to get L ≃ ρ_{Q,m}. Since L is unramified, so is ρ_{Q,m}. Both Lemma 3.16 and Lemma 3.17 are missing.

items.name: Case 3 local setting: trivial ρ̄|G_p, Frobenius lift φ_p, and χ = εω^{-1}
items.statement: Case α = β with ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar: after twisting, ρ̄: G_p → GL₂(k) is trivial. Fix a lift φ_p ∈ G_p of Frob_p. ε is the p-adic cyclotomic character, ω the Teichmüller lift of the mod-p reduction of ε, and χ := εω^{-1}, so χ ≡ 1 mod ϖ; φ_p is chosen (modified if necessary) so that χ(φ_p) = 1. An eigenvalue of a linear operator means a root of its characteristic polynomial.
items.note: This is notation for the local problem at p: trivial ρ̄|G_p after twisting, a lift φ_p of Frob_p, and χ = εω^{−1}. Normalising χ(φ_p) = 1 is possible because χ(I_p) = 1 + pZ_p. Decomposition and inertia groups with their characters are R01.2; the framed setting is R08.1. See sourceIssues E44 (ρ̃_{n,α}|G_p must be twisted as well).

items.name: Definition 3.18: framed deformation rings R^univ and R̃^univ (with an eigenvalue of φ_p)
items.statement: For A in C_O, D(A) is the set of framed deformations (lifts) of the trivial ρ̄: G_p → GL₂(k) to A, and D̃(A) is the set of framed deformations together with an eigenvalue α of (the image of) φ_p. These functors are represented by rings R^univ and R̃^univ respectively. There is a natural inclusion R^univ → R̃^univ, and R̃^univ is the quadratic extension of R^univ given by the characteristic polynomial of φ_p: R̃^univ ≅ R^univ[X]/(X² − tr ρ^univ(φ_p)·X + det ρ^univ(φ_p)).
items.note: R^univ, the framed deformation ring of the trivial ρ̄: G_p → GL₂(k), is planned in R08.1. R̃^univ ≅ R^univ[X]/(X² − tr ρ^univ(φ_p)X + det ρ^univ(φ_p)) represents the pairs (framed lift, eigenvalue of φ_p). It follows formally from R^univ and is free of rank 2 over it, so it needs no separate construction. Its ordinary quotients are L7 (thm-3-19-1-kisin).

items.name: Fixed-determinant quotients R^{univ,χ^{n−1}}, R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}}
items.statement: R^{univ,χ^{n−1}} and R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}} are the quotients of R^univ and R̃^univ corresponding to deformations with determinant χ^{n−1}.
items.note: The fixed-determinant quotients R^{univ,χ^{n−1}} and R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}} are planned in R08.1.

items.name: Theorem 3.19 (1): the ordinary quotient R̃^† (Kisin)
items.statement: Fix an integer n ≥ 2. There exists a unique reduced O-flat quotient R̃^† of R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}} such that the points on the generic fibre of R̃^† correspond to (ρ, α) with ρ: G_p → GL₂(E) (E/K finite) such that ρ ∼ (χ^{n−1}λ(α^{-1}) ∗; 0 λ(α)).
items.note: R̃^† is the reduced O-flat ordinary quotient with a chosen unramified-quotient eigenvalue α, characterised by its generic-fibre points. This is Kisin's construction in the ordinary rank-2 case with varying α, as in Geraghty [40] §3.4, and falls within L7's ordinary functors and their reduced/flat quotients. CG gives no reference for Kisin. External input: Attributed to Kisin, with no reference given in the paper (Kisin's construction of ordinary / potentially semistable deformation rings; cf. Geraghty [40, §3.4] for ordinary rings with a choice of eigenvalue)

items.name: Theorem 3.19 (2): R̃^† is a normal Cohen–Macaulay domain of relative dimension 4
items.statement: The ring R̃^† is an integral domain which is normal, Cohen–Macaulay, and of relative dimension 4 over O. More precisely R̃^† ⊗ k is an integral normal Cohen–Macaulay ring of dimension four, which is not Gorenstein, and is identified (in Snowden's notation) with the completion of B₁ at b = (1, 1; 0).
items.locator: §3.7, Theorem 3.19 (2), p. 335; restated as the first sentence of Theorem 4.3, §4.1, p. 356
items.note: L7 plans 'representability, dimension and component maps', which covers the relative dimension 4 and, at most, irreducibility. The rest is Snowden's theorem [41] and is not planned: R̃^† is a normal Cohen–Macaulay domain, and R̃^† ⊗ k is a normal CM domain of dimension 4 that is not Gorenstein, identified with the completion of B₁ at b = (1, 1; 0). The domain property is from Geraghty [40, proof of Lemma 3.4.3]. The CM notions themselves are planned in DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3. External input: Integral domain: proof of Lemma 3.4.3 of D. Geraghty, Modularity lifting theorems for ordinary Galois representations ([40]); the rest: A. Snowden, Singularities of ordinary deformation rings ([41], Math. Z.)

items.name: The ring R^† (image of R^univ in R̃^†)
items.statement: R^† denotes the image of R^univ in R̃^†.
items.note: R^† is the image of R^univ in R̃^†, that is, the ordinary ring after forgetting the eigenvalue α (the flag datum). This is exactly the 'image after forgetting the flag' that L7 and L8 plan.

items.name: Definition 3.20: R^unr and R̃^unr
items.statement: R^unr is the largest quotient of R^† corresponding to unramified deformations of ρ̄ (i.e. R^† modulo the entries of ρ(g) − 1 for g ∈ I_p), and R̃^unr is the corresponding quotient R̃^† ⊗_{R^†} R^unr of R̃^†.
items.note: R^unr is the largest unramified quotient of R^†, i.e. R^† modulo the entries of ρ(g) − 1 for g ∈ I_p, and R̃^unr is its base change to R̃^†. Unramified conditions are planned only away from p (R08.2), so these quotients of the ordinary rings are CG-specific and not planned.

items.name: Definition 3.21: the unramified ideal I
items.statement: The unramified ideal I ⊂ R^univ is the kernel of the map R^univ → R^unr.
items.note: The unramified ideal I = ker(R^univ → R^unr) is not planned in any layer.

items.name: Definition 3.21: the doubling ideal J
items.statement: The doubling ideal J ⊂ R^univ is the annihilator of R̃^†/R^† as an R^univ-module.
items.note: The doubling ideal J = Ann_{R^univ}(R̃^†/R^†) measures how far the ring with eigenvalue exceeds its image after forgetting the eigenvalue. That is the difference L7/L8 separate, but no layer defines J.

items.name: Snowden's equations for R̃^† and its generators
items.statement: (As in Snowden) R̃^† represents the functor of framed deformations ρ of the trivial ρ̄ to A with determinant χ^{n−1}, together with α ∈ A, writing φ := ρ(φ_p) and g := ρ(g), satisfying: (1) φ ∈ M₂(A) has determinant 1; (2) α is a root of the characteristic polynomial of φ; (3) Trace(g) = χ^{n−1}(g) + 1 for g ∈ I_p; (4) (g − 1)(g′ − 1) = (χ^{n−1}(g) − 1)(g′ − 1) for g, g′ ∈ I_p; (5) (g − 1)(φ − α) = (χ^{n−1}(g) − 1)(φ − α) for g ∈ I_p; (6) (φ − α)(g − 1) = (α^{-1} − α)(g − 1) for g ∈ I_p. Consequently R̃^† is (topologically) generated over O by elements of its maximal ideal: φ₁, …, φ₄ (the entries of ρ(φ_p) − 1 = (φ₁ φ₂; φ₃ φ₄)), x_{ij} (i = 1, …, 4, finitely many j: the entries of m_j = ρ(g_j) − 1, g_j ∈ I_p), and β, where α = 1 + β; R^† is generated by the φ_i and x_{ij}; β² − (φ₁ + φ₄)β − (φ₁ + φ₄) = 0 and α + α^{-1} = 2 + φ₁ + φ₄.
items.note: Equations (4)–(6) are rank-2 instances of L8's determinant-ordinary 'ordered products (ρ(g₁)−χ₁(g₁))⋯(ρ(g_n)−χ_n(g_n))=0'. L8, however, proves its comparison 'only under the published hypotheses' of ACC+. Snowden's theorem is not planned: for trivial ρ̄ and determinant χ^{n−1}, the reduced O-flat R̃^† is the ring cut out by equations (1)–(6). Nor are the resulting generators φ_i, x_ij, β with β² − (φ₁+φ₄)β − (φ₁+φ₄) = 0. External input: A. Snowden, Singularities of ordinary deformation rings ([41])

items.name: Explicit presentations of R^unr and R̃^unr
items.statement: Let ϖ^m be the greatest power of ϖ dividing (χ^{n−1}(g) − 1)O for all g in the decomposition group at p; by considering determinants, R^unr and R̃^unr are annihilated by ϖ^m. Then R^unr ≅ O/ϖ^m⟦φ₁, φ₂, φ₃, φ₄⟧/(φ₁ + φ₄ + φ₁φ₄ − φ₂φ₃), the ring representing matrices φ = (1 + φ₁ φ₂; φ₃ 1 + φ₄) over O/ϖ^m, trivial modulo the maximal ideal, with determinant one; and R̃^unr (such matrices with an eigenvalue α = 1 + β) is R̃^unr ≃ R^unr[β]/(β² − (φ₁ + φ₄)β − (φ₁ + φ₄)) ≃ R^unr ⊕ R^unr as an R^unr-module. In particular R^unr → R̃^unr is injective and R^unr acts faithfully on R̃^unr/R^unr ≃ R^unr.
items.note: The explicit rings are R^unr ≅ O/ϖ^m⟦φ₁,…,φ₄⟧/(φ₁+φ₄+φ₁φ₄−φ₂φ₃) and R̃^unr ≅ R^unr[β]/(β² − (φ₁+φ₄)β − (φ₁+φ₄)). Here ϖ^m is fixed by χ^{n−1}(g) ≡ 1 on the decomposition group. The computation is CG's and not planned.

items.name: Lemma 3.22: J = I
items.statement: The doubling ideal equals the unramified ideal: J = I (as ideals of R^univ).
items.note: The equality J = I is a new local deformation-theoretic result of CG. J ⊆ I comes from the faithfulness of R^unr on R̃^unr/R^unr; I ⊆ J comes from Snowden's relation (6). No layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 3.24: T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R̃^† ↠ T̃_{n,m̃}
items.statement: Case 3: α = β and ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar. Write m̃ = m̃_α, and let T_{n,m} denote the image T_{n,m_α} of T_{n,m} in T̃_{n,m̃}. Then there is a surjection T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R̃^† ↠ T̃_{n,m̃}. Here T̃_{n,m̃} = T_{n,m}[U_p]. [Normalisation not stated in the paper; see sourceIssues E44:] T̃_{n,m̃} becomes an R̃^univ-algebra through a framing of ρ̃_{n,α}|G_p ⊗ λ(c^{-1}). Here c ∈ T_{n,m}^× is the square root of ⟨p⟩ with c ≡ α mod m (Hensel, p odd). The twisted representation has trivial reduction and determinant χ^{n−1}, and c^{-1}U_p serves as the eigenvalue of φ_p. The map R̃^univ → T̃_{n,m̃} factors through R̃^†, because T̃_{n,m̃} ↪ ∏E_i (ordinary eigenforms of weight n and level Γ₁(NQ)) and each factor gives a point of the form in Theorem 3.19(1). Likewise R^univ → T_{n,m} factors through R^†. The resulting map T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R̃^† → T̃_{n,m̃} sends α ∈ R̃^† to c^{-1}U_p (the paper prints 'to U_p'). Its image contains T_{n,m} and U_p, so it is surjective.
items.note: The surjection T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R̃^† ↠ T̃_{n,m̃} relates the planned weight-n Hecke algebras (R15.2, R19.6, R21.3) to the local rings. It needs the factorisation R^univ → T_{n,m} through R^†, obtained from the embedding into ∏E_i. This is weight-one-argument specific. See sourceIssues E38 (read T_{n,m} as its image) and E44 (twist by λ(c^{−1}) before framing).

items.name: Definition 3.25: the global doubling ideal J^glob
items.statement: The global doubling ideal J^glob ⊂ R^† is the annihilator of T̃_{n,m̃}/T_{n,m} as an R^†-module (R^† acting through R^† → T_{n,m}).
items.note: J^glob = Ann_{R^†}(T̃_{n,m̃}/T_{n,m}) is not planned in any layer. See sourceIssues E38 (read T_{n,m} as its image in T̃_{n,m̃}).

items.name: J ⊂ J^glob, I ⊂ J^glob: doubled quotients are unramified at p
items.statement: T̃_{n,m̃}/T_{n,m} is a quotient of (T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R̃^†)/(T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} R^†) ≃ T_{n,m} ⊗_{R^†} (R̃^†/R^†) as an R^†-module; hence (the image of) J is contained in J^glob, and by Lemma 3.22, I ⊂ J^glob. Equivalently: on any quotient of T_{n,m} over which the corresponding quotient of T̃_{n,m̃} is doubled (free of rank 2 as a module for the image of T_{n,m}), the action of the Galois group at p is unramified.
items.note: The chain is J ⊂ J^glob, so I ⊂ J^glob by Lemma 3.22, so doubled quotients are unramified at p. It combines Lemma 3.24 with Lemma 3.22, and both are missing.

items.name: Case α = β, ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar: conclusion of the proof of Theorem 3.11
items.statement: Suppose α = β and ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar. By Lemma 3.16 the quotient T_m/I_m[T_p][U_p] of T̃_{n,m̃} is doubled over T_m/I_m, so by doubled-quotients-unramified the representations ρ_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m) and ρ̃_{Q,m}: G_Q → GL₂(T_m/I_m[U_p]) are unramified at p; the trace of any lift of Frobenius on this quotient is U_p + ⟨p⟩U_p^{-1} = T_p, so T_p ∈ T_m/I_m and Trace(ρ_{Q,m}(Frob_p)) = T_p. The rest of the argument follows as in §3.5, completing the proof of Theorem 3.11.
items.note: This is the conclusion of Theorem 3.11 when ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar. It uses Lemma 3.16 and doubled-quotients-unramified, both missing.

items.name: Theorem 3.26: minimal R = T and freeness in weight one
items.statement: Setting of §3.3: p ≥ 3; ρ̄: G_Q → GL₂(k) continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible and unramified at p, with ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0 for x ∈ S(ρ̄) with ρ̄|G_x reducible; N = N(ρ̄); H the p-part of (Z/NZ)^×; X = X₁(N)/H, with the auxiliary level of Remark 3.10 if needed. Assume Assumption 3.9. Then the map ϕ: R^min ↠ T_{∅,m_∅} is an isomorphism, and T_{∅,m_∅} acts freely on H₀(X, ω)_{m_∅}. Here H₀(X, ω) := H⁰(X, (Ω¹_{X/O} ⊗ ω^{-1})_{K/O})^∨ (Pontryagin dual), and Ω¹ ⊗ ω^{-1} ≅ ω(−∞) by Kodaira–Spencer (§3.2.4).
items.note: This is minimal weight-one R = T with T_{∅,m_∅} acting freely on H₀(X, ω)_{m_∅}, the ℓ₀ = 1 case of CG's method. No layer plans it: GL2ModularityLifting has defect 0, and ML.1 is a registry. K1's thm-1-4 and IKM's calegari-wt1 are missing and go to the same place.

items.name: Minimal deformation over T_{∅,m∅} and the surjection φ: R^min ↠ T_{∅,m∅}
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §3.1 and §3.3: p ≥ 3; ρ̄: G_Q → GL2(k) continuous, odd, absolutely irreducible and unramified at p; if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|G_x is reducible then ρ̄^{I_x} ≠ 0; N = N(ρ̄) is the Serre level, H is the p-Sylow subgroup of (Z/NZ)^×, and X = X_1(N)/H over O (with auxiliary Γ1(q)-level added if needed for representability, §3.3); T_∅ ⊂ End_O H^0(X, ω_{K/O}) is generated by the T_n with (n, pN) = 1 and the ⟨a⟩ with (a, N) = 1; m∅ is the (non-Eisenstein) maximal ideal of T_∅ attached to ρ̄, with T_∅/m∅ = k. Assume also Assumption 3.9 (T(ρ̄) = ∅). Taking Q = ∅ (written 'Q = 1', since Q also denotes the product of its primes) in Theorem 3.11 gives ρ_∅: G_Q → GL2(T_{∅,m∅}) lifting ρ̄, unramified outside N, with tr ρ_∅(Frob_x) = T_x for all primes x ∤ pN. Its twist ρ′ := ρ_∅ ⊗ η, where η is the unique p-power-order character with η² = det(ρ̄)·det(ρ_∅)^{-1} (det ρ̄ read via its Teichmüller lift), is a minimal deformation of ρ̄ (Definition 3.1 with Q = ∅). By the universal property of R^min = R_∅ it induces a local O-algebra homomorphism φ: R^min → T_{∅,m∅}, and φ is surjective.
items.note: R^min and its universal property are planned (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3), and so is twisting by the p-power character η (R04.4). What is not planned is the weight-one Hecke-valued deformation ρ_∅ over T_{∅,m∅}, which is CG Theorem 3.11 with Q = ∅. K3 marked it missing (thm-3-11-*, min-hecke-surjection-phi). GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 plans deformation-to-Hecke surjections only in KW II's weight ≥ 2 Betti/étale setting. Neither library has Galois deformation rings or Hecke algebras over O acting on coherent cohomology.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles patching datum for Theorem 3.26
items.note: The abstract patching theorem (CG Prop. 2.3) is planned in the accepted DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.5 node. The Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N (Prop. 3.3) are planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5/R04.6. The group rings S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q] and R∞ = O⟦x_1,…,x_{q−1}⟧ are library carriers: mathlib:MonoidAlgebra and mathlib:MvPowerSeries. The instantiation is not planned: H_N = H_0(X_{Δ_N}(Q_N), ω)_m as an R∞ ⊗ S_N-module, through the weight-one Hecke algebra T_{Q_N} and Theorem 3.11. K3 gives its overlapping patching-data-weight-one the same status. See sourceIssues E48 (surjectivity onto T_{Q_N,m} is not justified).

items.name: Splitting at Taylor–Wiles primes; R_{Q_N} modulo the augmentation ideal is R^min (condition (5a))
items.statement: In the setting of patching-datum-weight-one, fix x ∈ Q_N. The restriction to G_x of the universal deformation G_Q → GL2(R_{Q_N}) has the form χ_{α_x} ⊕ χ_{β_x}. Each summand has rank one over R_{Q_N}, and χ_{α_x} lifts λ(α_x); λ(α_x) is not defined in the paper, and presumably means the unramified character with Frob_x ↦ α_x. Restrict the χ_{α_x} (x ∈ Q_N) to I_x and apply local class field theory: this gives a map O[Δ_{Q_N}] → R_{Q_N}. The quotient of R_{Q_N} by the image of the augmentation ideal of O[Δ_{Q_N}] is R^min. This gives the second part of condition (5a) of Proposition 2.3: the image of the augmentation ideal of S_N in End_O(H_N) is contained in the image of ker(φ_N). The first part of (5a) holds 'by construction (see Theorem 3.11)': the image of S_N in End_O(H_N) is contained in the image of R∞. This uses Theorem 3.11's statement that, for x | Q, the restriction of ξ to I_x (hence, via local class field theory, to Δ_x) is compatible with the diamond operators in T_m.
items.note:
This item has two halves with different statuses.
- The Galois half is planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5/R04.6: the splitting ρ^univ|G_x ≅ χ_α ⊕ χ_β, the map O[Δ_Q] → R_Q through χ_α|I_x and the local Artin map (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7), and R_Q/a_Q ≅ R^min. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/prop-12-3, the same statement, is marked planned in R04.5/R04.6.
- The conclusion (5a) on H_N is not planned. It identifies the diamond action of S_N on H_N with the image of R∞ and of ker φ_N, which needs the weight-one local-at-Q compatibility of Theorem 3.11. K3 marked that compatibility (thm-3-11-local-at-Q) missing.

items.name: The Δ_N-coinvariants of H_N recover H (condition (5b))
items.statement: In the setting of patching-datum-weight-one, there is a Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence Tor_i^{S_N}(H_j(X_{Δ_N}(Q_N), ω)_m, O) ⇒ H_{i+j}(X_0(Q_N), ω)_m. It gives (H_N)_{Δ_N} ≅ H_0(X_0(Q_N), ω)_m. By Lemmas 3.5 and 3.7 this yields an isomorphism (H_N)_{Δ_N} ≅ H_0(X, ω)_{m∅} = H of R∞-modules, where R∞ acts on H via φ_N.
items.note: This is the Hecke-equivariant Hochschild–Serre computation (H_N)_{Δ_N} ≅ H_0(X_0(Q_N), ω)_m, followed by CG Lemmas 3.5 and 3.7. K2 marked all three missing (hochschild-serre-coherent, lemma-3-5, lemma-3-7-*). Mathlib has Representation.Coinvariants (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Coinvariants.lean:57), but no Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for coherent cohomology of Galois covers.

items.name: H_N is balanced over S_N (condition (5c))
items.statement: In the setting of patching-datum-weight-one, H_N is finite over O, hence finite over S_N, and d_{S_N}(H_N) ≥ 0. In other words, H_N is balanced over S_N in the sense of Definition 2.2.
items.note: Balancedness (Definition 2.2) is planned in the R03.5 node. The claim d_{S_N}(H_N) ≥ 0 for the weight-one module is CG Proposition 3.8, which K2 marked missing (prop-3-8-balanced).

items.name: Hecke-equivariant duality H_0(X, ω) ≅ H^1(X, ω), giving T_{∅,m∅} ≅ T_m
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of thm-3-26, there is a Hecke-equivariant isomorphism H_0(X, ω) ⥲ H^1(X, ω). It is built as in the discussion preceding Proposition 3.8 (§3.2.4) from Verdier duality D, the Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism and the operator w_ζ^*, which together give a T-linear isomorphism in weight n = 1. Hence T_{∅,m∅} ≅ T_m, where T is the O-algebra of endomorphisms of H^1(X, ω) generated by the Hecke operators prime to Np, and m is the maximal ideal of T corresponding to ρ̄.
items.note:
The ingredients are planned:
- Serre duality over a field: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B and SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3.
- Kodaira–Spencer: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.1 node.

Not planned: the integral, K/O-coefficient Hecke-twisted isomorphism H_0(X, ω) ≅ H^1(X, ω) on the coherent weight-one modules and the induced T_{∅,m∅} ≅ T_m. K2 marked the analogues Phi-duality-twisted-hecke and Psi-weight-one-hecke-iso missing. Neither library has Serre duality.

items.name: Theorem 1.4 when there are no vexing primes
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §3.1 and §3.3 and Assumption 3.9 (T(ρ̄) = ∅). Take X_U := X = X_1(N)/H and L_σ := O_X. Let T be the Hecke algebra of H^1(X, ω), generated by the prime-to-Np Hecke operators, and m its maximal ideal corresponding to ρ̄. Then R^min ≅ T_m, and H^1(X, ω)_m is a free T_m-module.
items.note: This is Theorem 1.4 when T(ρ̄) = ∅, deduced from Theorem 3.26 and the duality H_0 ≅ H^1. Both inputs are missing, and so is K1's thm-1-4.

items.name: H_0(X, ω)_{m∅} is free of rank one over T_{∅,m∅}
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of thm-3-26, the free T_{∅,m∅}-module H_0(X, ω)_{m∅} has rank one. Argument:
• If H_0(X, ω_K)_{m∅} ≠ 0, this is multiplicity one for GL(2)/Q.
• In general, by Nakayama's lemma it suffices that dim_k H^0(X, ω_k(−∞))[m∅] = 1. By the q-expansion principle this follows once T_p ∈ T_{∅,m∅} (shown in §§3.5–3.7) and U_x ∈ T_{∅,m∅} for every x | N.
• U_x ∈ T_{∅,m∅} for x | N comes from N(ρ̄) = N (statement corrected). If ρ̄^{I_x} is a line (in particular whenever x ‖ N, and whenever ρ̄|G_x is reducible), the minimal deformation over T_m has a unique I_x-invariant T_m-line, and Frob_x acts on it through U_x; so U_x ∈ T_m. If ρ̄^{I_x} = 0, then U_x = 0 ∈ T_m.
items.locator: §3.8, paragraph after the deduction of Theorem 1.4, p. 340
items.note:
Some inputs are planned or in the library:
- Nakayama's lemma: mathlib:Submodule.eq_bot_of_le_smul_of_le_jacobson_bot (Nakayama.lean:118).
- The q-expansion principle: AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights R15.2 node.
- Multiplicity one in characteristic zero: see multiplicity-one-GL2.

Not planned: T_p ∈ T_{∅,m∅} (the §§3.5–3.7 doubling argument) and U_x ∈ T_m from the local structure of the minimal deformation over the torsion weight-one Hecke algebra. See sourceIssues E49 (case split must use ρ̄^{I_x}) and E50 (local–global compatibility for U_x at x‖N).

items.name: Vexing prime; the set T(ρ̄)
items.statement: A prime x ≠ p is vexing for ρ̄ if (1) ρ̄|D_x is absolutely irreducible; (2) ρ̄|I_x ≃ ξ ⊕ ξ^c is reducible; and (3) x ≡ −1 mod p. The paper does not define ξ, ξ^c; implicitly ξ is a character of I_x and ξ^c its conjugate under Frobenius. T(ρ̄) is the set of vexing primes. In §3.1 it is defined as the set of x ∈ S(ρ̄) with x ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|G_x irreducible and ρ̄|I_x reducible.
items.locator: §3.9, pp. 340–341 (the definition begins at the foot of p. 340); §3.1, p. 310
items.note: This is a residual local predicate, and it adds no new mathematics. The atlas states its negation as a hypothesis (L5w's (H3), over totally real F). R08.2 plans the minimally ramified local conditions, which split exactly on this case. The word 'vexing' and the set T(ρ̄) are not named in any layer; K1, K2 and K3 give the same status and ask that R08.2's blueprint define them, with CG §3.1/§3.9 as a source.

items.name: The set P(ρ̄) of ramified reducible primes
items.statement: P(ρ̄) is the set of x ∈ S(ρ̄) − T(ρ̄) at which ρ̄ is ramified and ρ̄|G_x is reducible.
items.note: This is a named subset built from planned local predicates: S(ρ̄), T(ρ̄), ramification and reducibility of ρ̄|G_x. It is exactly the set of ramified primes where Definition 3.1(2) (ρ^{I_x} a rank-one summand) applies, which is R08.2's minimally ramified case. The name P(ρ̄) is new, and its only use in the paper is to choose the level groups U_x.

items.name: Conductor exponents c_x
items.statement: For x ∈ S(ρ̄), c_x is the exponent of the Artin conductor of ρ̄|G_x, so that N(ρ̄) = ∏_{x∈S(ρ̄)} x^{c_x}. If x ∈ T(ρ̄), then c_x is even.
items.note: c_x = n(x, ρ̄) is the Artin conductor exponent, planned in R01.3 and its reviewed node artin-conductor-with-its-wild-part. Evenness at vexing primes follows from R01.3's planned induction formula: ρ̄|G_x is induced from the unramified quadratic extension, so c_x = 2·a(ξ).

items.name: Local level groups V_x ⊂ U_x ⊂ GL2(Z_x) (corrected)
items.statement:
For each prime x, compact open subgroups V_x ⊂ U_x ⊂ GL2(Z_x), with V_x normal in U_x, are defined as follows.
• x ∈ P(ρ̄): U_x = V_x = {g ∈ GL2(Z_x) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 d) mod x^{c_x}, with d ∈ (Z/x^{c_x})^× of p-power order}.
• x ∈ T(ρ̄): U_x = GL2(Z_x) and V_x = ker(GL2(Z_x) → GL2(Z/x^{c_x/2})).
• x ∈ S(ρ̄) − (T(ρ̄) ∪ P(ρ̄)): U_x = V_x = {g ∈ GL2(Z_x) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 d) mod x^{c_x}, with d of p-power order} (corrected; see sourceIssues E51).
• x ∉ S(ρ̄): U_x = V_x = GL2(Z_x).
items.note: These are the minimal-level choices that are specific to the paper: at P(ρ̄) and at the other primes of S(ρ̄), d of p-power order modulo x^{c_x}; at T(ρ̄), full level x^{c_x/2}. No layer defines them. R22.1 ('construct the localised finite-level Hecke module and algebra with the required local type') is the weight ≥ 2 KW II analogue. Mathlib's CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0/Gamma1 (CongruenceSubgroups.lean:79/131) are subgroups of SL(2,ℤ), not compact opens of GL2(Z_x), so they are a near miss. See sourceIssues E51 (third bullet needs d of p-power order).

items.name: Auxiliary local groups U_{1,x} ⊂ U_{0,x}
items.statement: For every rational prime x: U_{0,x} := {g ∈ GL2(Z_x) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 ∗) mod x} and U_{1,x} := {g ∈ GL2(Z_x) : g ≡ (∗ ∗; 0 1) mod x}.
items.note: These are the standard Γ₀(x) and Γ₁(x) local level groups. Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9B names the corresponding subgroups of GL₂(Z/NZ): the Borel, and the subgroup {[[1,b],[0,d]]} in its row-vector convention, which is transpose to CG's (∗ ∗; 0 1). R13.2 plans the Γ₀/Γ₁ level problems. Mathlib's Gamma0/Gamma1 ⊂ SL(2,ℤ) are a near miss. The blueprint must fix the row/column convention.

items.name: Global level groups U, V, U_i(Q), V_i(Q)
items.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes disjoint from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}. Set U := ∏_x U_x and V := ∏_x V_x, subgroups of GL2(A^∞). For i = 0, 1 set U_i(Q) := ∏_{x∉Q} U_x × ∏_{x∈Q} U_{i,x} and V_i(Q) := ∏_{x∉Q} V_x × ∏_{x∈Q} U_{i,x}. Then V ◁ U and V_i(Q) ◁ U_i(Q), each with quotient ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL2(Z/x^{c_x/2}).
items.note: U, V, U_i(Q) and V_i(Q), with V ◁ U and quotient ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL₂(Z/x^{c_x/2}), are built from the missing local groups U_x, V_x. AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.4 plans nested compact opens only generically.

items.name: Modular curves X_W and their standard sheaves
items.note:
The plan covers the following:
- The curves: compactified moduli of generalised elliptic curves with full, Γ₁ and Γ₀ level (R13.1/R13.2), coarse compactified curves with finite-inertia quotients (R13.4a), and Γ_H quotients (Tau Ceti Layer 9).
- Auxiliary-level rigidification: R09.5.
- ω and the cusp divisor ∞: R15.1.

The mixed levels W (full level x^{c_x/2} at vexing primes, a p-power-order condition on d elsewhere) are not literally listed. They are products and quotients of the listed problems. The curves X_V are not geometrically connected (§3.9.2). K2 and K3 gave the §3.2 curves the same status.

items.name: X_V → X_U is a tame Galois quotient by U/V
items.statement: The moduli description gives a natural right action of U/V on X_V, and X_V/(U/V) ≅ X_U. Away from the cusps, Y_V → Y_U is étale and Galois with group U/V, and X_V → X_U is tamely ramified. The same holds for X_{V_i(Q)} → X_{U_i(Q)} (i = 0, 1).
items.note: The open part is Tau Ceti 9A/9D: free actions give étale torsors, and M(P)/H ≅ M(P/H) (KM 8.1.5). The compactified quotient and the ramification at cusps are ModularCurvesPartII R13.3/R13.4a. Tameness at cusps also uses cusp-inertia-prime-to-p. The item cites Deligne–Rapoport IV 3.10, which should be a source for R13.4a. External input: [42] P. Deligne, M. Rapoport, Les schémas de modules de courbes elliptiques, LNM 349 (1973), §IV and IV 3.10

items.name: The Δ_Q-covers X_{U_1(Q)} → X_{U_Δ(Q)} → X_{U_0(Q)}
items.statement: For Q a finite set of primes disjoint from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}, the natural map X_{U_1(Q)} → X_{U_0(Q)} is étale and Galois with group Δ_Q := ∏_{x∈Q} U_{0,x}/U_{1,x} ≅ ∏_{x∈Q} (Z/x)^×. For a quotient Δ of Δ_Q, X_{U_Δ(Q)} → X_{U_0(Q)} denotes the intermediate Galois cover with group Δ; that is, U_Δ(Q) is the preimage in U_0(Q) of ker(Δ_Q → Δ). X_{V_Δ(Q)} is defined in the same way.
items.note: X_{U_1(Q)} → X_{U_0(Q)} is the Γ₁ → Γ₀ quotient at the primes of Q, with group Δ_Q. Its intermediate covers are quotients by subgroups of Δ_Q. K2 gave its X-Delta-Q-cover the same status. Étaleness at the cusps is R13.3's cusp computation.

items.name: The group G = U/V and the representation σ
items.statement: G := U/V = ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL2(Z/x^{c_x/2}). σ is a representation of G on a finite free O-module W_σ. W_σ^* := Hom_O(W_σ, O) is its O-dual, and σ^* := Hom_O(σ, O) is the dual representation, on W_{σ^*} = W_σ^*.
items.note: The explicit product ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL(Fin 2)(ZMod (x^{c_x/2})), a representation σ of it on a finite free O-module (Representation O G W with Module.Free and Module.Finite), and the dual representation on W_σ^* = Module.Dual O W_σ are all Mathlib objects. The identification G = U/V is the content of global-level-groups (missing), not of this item.

items.name: The vector bundles L_σ ⊃ L_σ^sub on X_U
items.statement: Let f: X_V → X_U be the natural map. On X_U define L_σ := (f_*(O_{X_V} ⊗_O W_σ))^G and L_σ^sub := (f_*(O_{X_V}(−∞) ⊗_O W_σ))^G, where G acts diagonally: on X_V by its right action and on W_σ through σ. By the projection formula, L_σ = (f_*f^*(O_{X_U} ⊗_O W_σ))^G = ((f_*O_{X_V}) ⊗_O W_σ)^G. Arguing locally, L_σ^sub = (f_*(O_{X_V}(−∞)) ⊗_O W_σ)^G, and L_σ^sub ⊂ L_σ. The bundles are built so that H^0(X_U, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ) ≅ (H^0(X_V, ω^{⊗n}) ⊗_O W_σ)^G = Hom_{O[G]}(W_σ^*, H^0(X_V, ω^{⊗n})), and H^0(X_U, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ^sub) ≅ Hom_{O[G]}(W_σ^*, H^0(X_V, ω^{⊗n}(−∞))) (lemma-3-27-2).
items.note: The vector bundles L_σ = (f_*(O_{X_V} ⊗ W_σ))^G and L_σ^sub on X_U, which extract σ-typed forms, are planned nowhere. AutomorphicBundles B0 is the nearest ('Prove exactly when a coefficient descends through … a finite coarse quotient. A coherent pushforward to a coarse space is not assumed locally free'). But B0 works with algebraic representations over canonical models, not with representations of a finite level quotient U/V over O, where p may divide |G|. R15.1's descent from a rigidified cover is the trivial-σ case. The identity (H^0 ⊗ W_σ)^G = Hom_{O[G]}(W_σ^*, H^0) uses mathlib:Representation.linHom.invariantsEquivRepHom.

items.name: L_σ and L_σ^sub on X_{U_i(Q)}
items.statement: For i = 0, 1, L_σ also denotes the pullback of L_σ along X_{U_i(Q)} → X_U. Since this map is flat, the pullback is isomorphic to (f_*(O_{X_{V_i(Q)}} ⊗_O W_σ))^G, where f: X_{V_i(Q)} → X_{U_i(Q)}. On X_{U_i(Q)}, L_σ^sub denotes (f_*(O_{X_{V_i(Q)}}(−∞)) ⊗_O W_σ)^G. The pullback of L_σ^sub from X_U is a subsheaf of it, and the quotient is supported at ramified cusps.
items.note: This depends on L-sigma (missing). Flat pullback along X_{U_i(Q)} → X_U, and the comparison of sub-sheaves at ramified cusps, are specific to L_σ.

items.name: Hecke operators on cohomology with coefficients in L_σ, L_σ^sub
items.statement:
Let X := X_{U_i(Q)} (i ∈ {0, 1}; Q = ∅ gives X_U), X(V) := X_{V_i(Q)}, and f: X(V) → X. For a prime x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}:
• X_0(x) = X_0(U; x) is X with an added level structure at x as in §3.2.3 (its type depends on whether x ∈ Q), with degeneracy maps π_1, π_2: X_0(x) → X. X_0(V; x) is defined in the same way from X(V), with f: X_0(V; x) → X_0(x).
• π_i is flat and X_0(x) ×_{π_i, X} X(V) ≅ X_0(V; x) over X_0(x). Hence π_i^*L_σ ≅ (f_*(O_{X_0(V;x)} ⊗_O W_σ))^G canonically for i = 1, 2. This gives a canonical isomorphism φ(σ)_{12}: π_2^*L_σ ⥲ π_1^*L_σ.
• For a ∈ Z prime to S(ρ̄) ∪ Q, the automorphism ⟨a⟩ of X (multiplication by a on the level structure) satisfies ⟨a⟩^*L_σ ≅ L_σ canonically.
• For an O-module M and n ∈ Z, xT_x on H^i(X, ω^n ⊗ L_σ ⊗_O M) is the composite (shown for M = O): H^i(X, ω^n ⊗ L_σ) →(π_2^*) H^i(X_0(x), π_2^*ω^n ⊗ L_σ) →(φ_{12}^{⊗n} ⊗ φ(σ)_{12}) H^i(X_0(x), π_1^*ω^n ⊗ L_σ) →(tr(π_1)) H^i(X, ω^n ⊗ L_σ).
• On X_0(x) put L_σ^sub := (f_*(O_{X_0(V;x)}(−∞)) ⊗_O W_σ)^G. Then π_1^*(L_σ^sub) and π_2^*(L_σ^sub) lie in L_σ^sub, and π_{1,*}(L_σ^sub) ↪ π_{1,*}(π_1^*L_σ) →(tr(π_1)) L_σ factors through L_σ^sub. This defines T_x on the cohomology of ω^n ⊗ L_σ^sub ⊗_O M.
• U_y (y ∈ Q) is defined in the same way.
The result is: operators T_x (x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}) and ⟨a⟩ (a prime to S(ρ̄)) on H^j(X_U, ω^n ⊗ L_σ ⊗_O M) and H^j(X_U, ω^n ⊗ L_σ^sub ⊗_O M); and operators T_x (x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {p}), U_y (y ∈ Q) and ⟨a⟩ (a prime to S(ρ̄) ∪ Q) on the corresponding groups for X_{U_i(Q)}.
items.note: The correspondences X_0(x), π_1, π_2, ⟨a⟩ and φ_12 are planned in ModularCurvesPartII R14.1 (K2: degeneracy-maps and phi12 planned). Hecke operators on coherent cohomology with arbitrary coefficients in weight one are missing (K2: hecke-T-x-coherent, source route to R15.2). The twisted operators on ω^n ⊗ L_σ and ω^n ⊗ L_σ^sub are planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.27(1): L_σ and L_σ^sub are locally free
items.statement: Let X be X_U (resp. X_{U_i(Q)} for i = 0 or 1), let X(V) be X_V (resp. X_{V_i(Q)}), and let f: X(V) → X be the natural map. Then the sheaves L_σ^sub and L_σ are locally free of finite rank on X.
items.note: This is local freeness of G-invariant pushforwards along a finite cover that is étale Galois away from the cusps and tame at the cusps, where p may divide |G|. Its inputs are planned (Mumford descent in SF.1/R09.3, cusp inertia in R13.3). The lemma itself is not planned; see L-sigma for why AutomorphicBundles B0 does not cover it. See sourceIssues E58 (compute after completion, not on Zariski stalks).

items.name: Lemma 3.27(2): L_σ and L_σ^sub extract W_σ^*-isotypic forms
items.statement: With X, X(V) and f as in lemma-3-27-1, let A be an O-algebra and 𝒱 a coherent locally free sheaf of O_{X_A}-modules. Then there are isomorphisms H^0(X_A, 𝒱 ⊗_{O_{X_A}} (L_σ)_A) ⥲ (H^0(X(V)_A, f^*𝒱) ⊗_O W_σ)^G and H^0(X_A, 𝒱 ⊗_{O_{X_A}} (L_σ^sub)_A) ⥲ (H^0(X(V)_A, (f^*𝒱)(−∞)) ⊗_O W_σ)^G. The proof also gives (L_σ)_A ≅ (f_*(O_{X(V)_A} ⊗_O W_σ))^G.
items.note: Sections of 𝒱 ⊗ L_σ over any O-algebra A are identified with G-invariants at level V. This depends on L-sigma and on quotient-by-G-base-change (planned). The final Hom_{O[G]} reformulation is a Mathlib-level identity (Representation.linHom.invariantsEquivRepHom).

items.name: Descent of coherent sheaves along a free finite group quotient
items.statement: As used here: let a finite group G act freely on a scheme Y′ with quotient π: Y′ → Y = Y′/G, so π is finite étale Galois. Then F ↦ π^*F is an equivalence between coherent O_Y-modules and G-equivariant coherent O_{Y′}-modules, with quasi-inverse F′ ↦ (π_*F′)^G. Locally free sheaves correspond to locally free sheaves of the same rank, and the equivalence is compatible with taking duals.
items.locator: cited in §3.9.1, proof of Lemma 3.27, p. 346, and before Lemma 3.28, p. 348
items.note: The equivalence between coherent sheaves on Y′/G and G-equivariant coherent sheaves on Y′, for a free action, is effective descent of quasi-coherent sheaves along the finite étale Galois cover. Y′ ×_Y Y′ ≅ G × Y′ turns descent data into equivariant structures. Neither library has it: the audit marks SF.1's 'Effective fpqc/fppf descent of objects (quasi-coherent modules, affine schemes)' as partial. Mathlib's FaithfullyFlat/Descent.lean descends only properties of ring maps, and Tau Ceti ModularCurves 0E covers affine and finite locally free schemes, not sheaves. External input: [43] D. Mumford, Abelian Varieties, §III.12, Theorem 1(B) (and its proof)

items.name: Inertia at cusps of X(V) → X is prime to p; local form at cusps
items.statement: For the covers f: X(V) → X of lemma-3-27-1 and a cusp x′ of X(V) over a cusp x of X, the inertia group I(x′/x) ⊂ G is abelian of order prime to p. After enlarging O (all cusps defined over O, O containing the e-th roots of unity with e := #I(x′/x)), there is a uniformizer q at x′ such that Ô_{X,x} → Ô_{X(V),x′} is isomorphic to O⟦q^e⟧ → O⟦q⟧. Moreover I(x′/x) ≅ μ_e ⊂ O^× via σ ↦ σ(q)/q, and for the character χ_i: I(x′/x) ≅ μ_e → O^×, ζ ↦ ζ^i, the χ_i-part of Ô_{X(V),x′} is q^i O⟦q^e⟧ (0 ≤ i ≤ e − 1).
items.locator: §3.9.1, proof of Lemma 3.27, p. 346 (citation); proof of Lemma 3.28, pp. 348–349 (local form)
items.note: Completed local rings at cusps, cusp widths, ramification and stabilisers (through the Tate curve) are R13.3. The inertia at a cusp is a unipotent group of x-power order times ±1, so it has order prime to p. The χ_i-eigenspace decomposition of O⟦q⟧ under μ_e is elementary algebra that R13.3's blueprint should state. Deligne–Rapoport VI.5 is the cited source. External input: [42] Deligne–Rapoport, §VI.5 (abelian of order prime to p)

items.name: X(V)_A/G ≅ X_A for every O-algebra A
items.statement: Let X, X(V) and f be as in lemma-3-27-1. For every O-algebra A there is an isomorphism X(V)_A/G ⥲ X_A; in particular O_{X_A} ⥲ f_*(O_{X(V)_A})^G. Moreover (L_σ)_A ≅ (f_*(O_{X(V)_A} ⊗_O W_σ))^G ≅ (f_*(O_{X(V)_A}) ⊗_O W_σ)^G as sheaves on X_A.
items.note: Base change of coarse quotients for the finite-inertia presentations used here is within R09.5's and R13.4a's stated scope. The needed case is that X(V)_A/G ≅ X_A for every O-algebra A, even though p may divide |G| and the action is not free at the cusps. That is the tame-inertia case (Katz–Mazur A7.1.4). Tau Ceti ModularCurves 9A (KM 7.1.4) and 9D (KM 8.1.6) give the isomorphism only for flat base change, |H| invertible or free actions, so R09.5's blueprint must include the tame criterion explicitly. External input: [42] Deligne–Rapoport, §IV Prop. 3.10 (A = O; the same argument for A = k); [44] N. Katz, B. Mazur, Arithmetic Moduli of Elliptic Curves, Prop. A7.1.4 (general A)

items.name: The injection L_{σ^*} ↪ L_σ^*
items.statement: Let L_σ^* := Hom_{O_X}(L_σ, O_X). For every O-algebra A, (L_{σ^*})_A ≅ (f_*(O_{X(V)_A}) ⊗_O Hom_O(W_σ, O))^G ≅ (Hom_{f_*(O_{X(V)_A})}(f_*(O_{X(V)_A}) ⊗_O W_σ, f_*(O_{X(V)_A})))^G. Restriction to G-invariants, using O_{X_A} ≅ f_*(O_{X(V)_A})^G, gives a map (L_{σ^*})_A → Hom_{O_{X_A}}((L_σ)_A, O_{X_A}) = (L_σ^*)_A. This map is the base change of a map L_{σ^*} → L_σ^* over Spec O and is an isomorphism over Y_A. In particular L_{σ^*} → L_σ^* is injective and stays injective after base change to Spec A, for every A.
items.note: The injection L_{σ^*} ↪ L_σ^* depends on L-sigma (missing).

items.name: Lemma 3.28, first statement: L^sub_{σ^*} ≅ (L_σ^*)(−∞)
items.statement: With X and X(V) as in lemma-3-27-1, the injection L_{σ^*} ↪ L_σ^* restricts to an isomorphism L^sub_{σ^*} ⥲ (L_σ^*)(−∞). That is, it maps the subsheaf L^sub_{σ^*} ⊂ L_{σ^*} isomorphically onto (L_σ^*)(−∞) ⊂ L_σ^*.
items.note: The cusp-local duality computation L^sub_{σ^*} ≅ L_σ^*(−∞) uses the χ_i-decomposition at tame cusps. It depends on L-sigma (missing).

items.name: Lemma 3.28, second statement: (L_σ^sub)^*(−∞) ≅ L_{σ^*}
items.statement: With X and X(V) as in lemma-3-27-1, (L_σ^sub)^*(−∞) ≅ L_{σ^*}; equivalently (L^sub_{σ})^* ≅ L_{σ^*}(∞).
items.note: The companion duality (L_σ^sub)^* ≅ L_{σ^*}(∞) depends on L-sigma (missing).

items.name: Corollary 3.29 for L_σ (weight n > 1)
items.statement: Let X, X(V) be as in lemma-3-27-1. If n > 1, then H^1(X, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ) = {0}, and hence, for every m ≥ 1, H^0(X, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ ⊗_O O/ϖ^m) = (H^0(X(V), ω^{⊗n}) ⊗_O W_σ)^G ⊗_O O/ϖ^m.
items.note:
The vanishing H^1(X, ω^n ⊗ L_σ) = 0 for n > 1, and base change of H^0, are specific to L_σ. The inputs are planned:
- Serre duality over k: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B / SF.3.
- Cohomology and base change: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer C / StableReduction Layer 2.

items.name: Corollary 3.29 for L_σ^sub (weight n > 2)
items.statement: Let X, X(V) be as in lemma-3-27-1. If n > 2, then H^1(X, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ^sub) = {0}, and hence, for every m ≥ 1, H^0(X, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ^sub ⊗_O O/ϖ^m) = (H^0(X(V), ω^{⊗n}(−∞)) ⊗_O W_σ)^G ⊗_O O/ϖ^m.
items.locator: §3.9.1, Corollary 3.29 ('the analogous result holds for n > 2 if we replace L_σ by L_σ^sub'), p. 349
items.note: This is the analogue of cor-3-29-L-sigma for L_σ^sub with n > 2, and it has the same dependencies.

items.name: Serre duality on the special fibre X_k
items.statement: For X as in lemma-3-27-1 and a locally free sheaf F on the smooth proper curve X_k, H^1(X_k, F) is k-dual to H^0(X_k, Ω^1_{X_k} ⊗ F^∨), and Ω^1 ≅ ω^{⊗2}(−∞) by Kodaira–Spencer. In particular H^1(X_k, ω^{⊗n} ⊗ L_σ)^∨ ≅ H^0(X_k, ω^{⊗(2−n)} ⊗ L_σ^*(−∞)).
items.locator: used in §3.9.1, proof of Corollary 3.29, p. 350
items.note: Serre duality on a smooth proper curve over k is planned in Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B, which states it for line bundles, and in SF.3. The Kodaira–Spencer isomorphism ω^{⊗2} ≅ Ω^1(log ∞) is in the reviewed R15.1 node. The locally free (vector-bundle) form needed here is a routine extension that Layer B's blueprint should cover. Neither library has Serre duality or a dualizing sheaf. External input: Serre (Grothendieck) duality for smooth proper curves over a field; not cited at this point (cf. Verdier duality [32] R. Hartshorne, Residues and Duality, Cor. 11.2(f), used in §3.2.4)

items.name: The Conrad–Diamond–Taylor types σ_x at vexing primes and σ = (σ_x)
items.statement: For each vexing prime x ∈ T(ρ̄), with c_x the (even) conductor exponent of ρ̄|G_x, W_{σ_x} is the O-representation σ_x of GL2(Z/x^{c_x/2}Z) defined in [15, §5]. The collection σ = (σ_x)_{x∈T(ρ̄)}, that is, the representation ⊗_x σ_x of G = ∏_{x∈T(ρ̄)} GL2(Z/x^{c_x/2}), gives rise to the vector bundle L_σ on X_U (item L-sigma).
items.note: This is the Conrad–Diamond–Taylor type σ_x of GL₂(Z/x^{c_x/2}) at a vexing prime (CDT §5, after Henniart). It is local representation theory of GL₂(Q_x) away from p. R16.2 plans the explicit GL₂ classification with 'dimensions of congruence-invariants', R16.3 the explicit local Langlands with conductors, and ET.6 generic 'supercuspidal/type' theory. None of them names types that detect an inertial type, or σ_x. External input: [15] B. Conrad, F. Diamond, R. Taylor, Modularity of certain potentially Barsotti–Tate Galois representations, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999), §5

items.name: [15, Lemma 5.1.1]: W_σ cuts out the minimal automorphic representations at T(ρ̄)
items.statement: As used: for n large, the eigensystems occurring in (H^0(X_{V_1(Q)}, ω^n)_m ⊗_O W_σ)^G, the W_σ^*-isotypic part of the level-V_1(Q) forms, come from automorphic representations whose Galois representations are minimal at every x ∈ T(ρ̄). Consequently the associated deformation of ρ̄ over the Hecke algebra of this space satisfies Definition 3.1(3): ρ(I_x) ⥲ ρ̄(I_x) for x ∈ T(ρ̄).
items.locator: cited in §3.9.2, proof of Theorem 3.30, step (4), p. 354
items.note: This is global minimality at T(ρ̄) of eigensystems in the W_σ^*-isotypic part at level V. It combines local–global compatibility away from p, planned in AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4, with the type theory of cdt-sigma-x, which is missing. K3 marked the no-types analogue (thm-3-14) planned, via R19.4/R08.2/R22.1. What is new here is the type at vexing primes. External input: [15] Conrad–Diamond–Taylor, JAMS 12 (1999), Lemma 5.1.1

items.name: The Hecke algebra T_∅ acting on H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)
items.statement: T_∅ is the ring of Hecke operators acting on H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ) generated by the Hecke operators away from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}. That is, it is the O-subalgebra of End_O(H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)) generated by the T_x (x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}) and the ⟨a⟩ (a prime to S(ρ̄)) of hecke-operators-L-sigma. They act through H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ) = H^0(X_U, (ω ⊗ L^sub_{σ^*})_{K/O})^∨ with the Pontryagin-dual action (step (3) with n = 1, p. 351). m∅ is the maximal ideal of T_∅ corresponding to ρ̄ (as in §3.3). The paper does not say how the map φ: R^min → T_{∅,m∅} of Theorem 3.30 is obtained. By analogy with §3.8 it should come from a minimal deformation of ρ̄ over T_{∅,m∅}. Step (4) as printed produces such a deformation only over the Hecke algebra of H^0(X_{U_1(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O}) (for Q = ∅, of H^0(X_U, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O})), and that algebra is not T_∅; see sourceIssues E61 on σ versus σ^*.
items.note: This is the Hecke algebra of H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ) and the map φ. It depends on the missing L_σ, its Hecke operators and the weight-one Galois representations. See sourceIssues E61 (σ versus σ^* mismatch with step (4)).

items.name: Theorem 3.30 (minimal R = T in weight one, vexing primes allowed)
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §3.1 and §3.3 without Assumption 3.9, so T(ρ̄) may be non-empty. Let U, V be as in global-level-groups (with the corrected local-level-groups-Ux-Vx), let σ = (σ_x)_{x∈T(ρ̄)} be as in cdt-sigma-x with bundle L_σ on X_U, and let T_∅ and m∅ be as in T-empty-with-L-sigma. Then the map φ: R^min ↠ T_{∅,m∅} is an isomorphism, and T_{∅,m∅} acts freely on H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m∅}.
items.note: This is minimal weight-one R = T with vexing primes allowed, and no layer plans it. The reasons are those given for thm-3-26, and it also needs the missing L_σ machinery. See sourceIssues E61 (σ versus σ^* mismatch in the statement).

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (1): analogue of Lemma 3.5 with L_σ
items.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes disjoint from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p} such that, for each x ∈ Q, x ≡ 1 mod p and X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩ has distinct roots mod m∅. Choose a root α_x for each x ∈ Q, and let m be the maximal ideal generated by m∅ and the U_x − α_x. Then there is an isomorphism of Hecke modules H^0(X_U, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O})_{m∅} ⥲ H^0(X_{U_0(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O})_m. The key input, for Q = {x}, is an operator W_x on H^0(X_{U_0(x)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O}) with W_x² = x⟨x⟩ and (1/x)·π_1^* ∘ tr(π_1) ∘ W_x = U_x + (1/x)·W_x. It is induced by the operator W_x of §3.2.3 on H^0(X_{V_0(x)}, ω_{K/O}), which commutes with G = U/V, through H^0(X_{U_0(x)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O}) = (H^0(X_{V_0(x)}, ω_{K/O}) ⊗_O W_σ)^G.
items.note: This is the L_σ analogue of CG Lemma 3.5, which K2 marked missing, including the operator W_x induced from level V. The underlying w_x is planned in ModularCurvesPartII R14.1 (K2: fricke-w-x). W_x on coherent cohomology is missing (K2: W-x-operator, source route to R15.2). See sourceIssues E27 (the W_x identity needs a direct proof).

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (2): cusp forms and all forms agree after non-Eisenstein localisation
items.statement: Let Q be as above, Δ a quotient of Δ_Q and m a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal. Then, for i = 0, 1, the natural map H^i(X_{U_Δ(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ^sub)_{K/O})_m → H^i(X_{U_Δ(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O})_m is an isomorphism. Proof: let C_{V_Δ(Q)} ⊂ X_{V_Δ(Q)} be the cuspidal subscheme. There is an exact sequence of sheaves 0 → ω ⊗ L_σ^sub → ω ⊗ L_σ → (f_*((ω ⊗_O W_σ)|_{C_{V_Δ(Q)}}))^G on X_{U_Δ(Q)}. The cohomology of the last term is concentrated in degree 0 and equals (H^0(C_{V_Δ(Q)}, ω) ⊗_O W_σ)^G, on which the Hecke action is Eisenstein.
items.note: This is the L_σ analogue of Prop. 3.7(2) and Remark 3.4: boundary cohomology is Eisenstein. K2 marked both missing (lemma-3-7-2, rem-3-4-boundary-eisenstein). See sourceIssues E66 (cusps are not one orbit; argue type by type).

items.name: H_i with coefficients in L_σ; the duality maps Φ and Ψ; transposed Hecke operators
items.note: This covers H_i with L_σ coefficients, the Hecke-twisted duality isomorphisms Φ and Ψ, and the relation T_x^t = ⟨x^{-1}⟩T_x. The inputs are planned: Verdier/Serre duality (SF.3, Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge B, StableReduction Layer 2) and Kodaira–Spencer (R15.1). K2 marked homology-H-i and Phi-duality-twisted-hecke missing, and the L_σ version also depends on the missing Lemma 3.28.

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (3): analogue of Proposition 3.8 (balancedness with L_σ)
items.statement: Let Q satisfy the hypotheses of thm-3-30-step1-level-raising, with m as there, and let Δ be a quotient of Δ_Q = (Z/QZ)^× of p-power order. Then the O[Δ]-module M := H_0(X_{U_Δ(Q)}, ω ⊗ L_σ)_m is balanced (Definition 2.2): d_{O[Δ]}(M) ≥ 0.
items.note: This is the L_σ analogue of Prop. 3.8 (K2: prop-3-8-balanced, missing). Balancedness itself is planned in the R03.5 node.

items.name: Dimension equality H^0(…L_σ)_{m^*} vs H^0(…L_{σ^*})_m via contragredients
items.statement: Let Q and m be as in thm-3-30-step3-balanced (level U_0(Q)). Let R be the polynomial ring over O in the operators T_x, U_y^t and ⟨a⟩ (x ∤ pNQ prime, y | Q, a prime to NQ). Let α: T → T/m = k be the reduction map, and m^* := ker(β: R → k), where β(T_x) = α(⟨x^{-1}⟩T_x), β(U_y^t) = α(U_y) and β(⟨a⟩) = α(⟨a^{-1}⟩).
