The paper prints β(T_x) = α(⟨x⟩T_x); that value is inconsistent with the Ψ-relations and with the contragredient. Via Ψ, dim_K H_1(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_σ)_m = dim_K H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m^*}. Moreover dim_K H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m^*} = dim_K H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_{σ^*})_m. Justification given: after fixing K ↪ C, both sides are described by automorphic representations π of GL2/Q that are limits of discrete series at ∞, unramified outside S(ρ̄) ∪ Q, with appropriate local conditions at S(ρ̄) ∪ Q. The map π ↦ π^∨ (contragredient) interchanges H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m^*} ⊗_K C and H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_{σ^*})_m ⊗_K C.
items.note: The inputs are planned: contragredients (R16.2, via SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3) and the identification of holomorphic forms with automorphic representations (R16.6). Not planned: the specific comparison of the m^*- and m-parts of H^0(X_{U_0(Q),K}, ω ⊗ L_σ) and H^0(…, ω ⊗ L_{σ^*}). It needs weight-one (limit of discrete series) forms with L_σ and the types of cdt-sigma-x (missing).

items.name: Theorem 3.30, step (4): analogue of Theorem 3.11 (Galois representations with L_σ), corrected
items.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes disjoint from S(ρ̄) ∪ {p}. Let T be the O-subalgebra of endomorphisms of H^0(X_{U_1(Q)}, (ω ⊗ L_σ)_{K/O}) generated by the T_x (x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {p}), the U_y (y ∈ Q) and the ⟨a⟩. For each x ∈ Q assume that X² − T_xX + ⟨x⟩ has distinct roots in T_∅/m∅, and let α_x be one of them. Let m be the ideal of T generated by m∅ and the U_x − α_x (x ∈ Q). Then there is a Galois representation ρ_Q: G_Q → GL2(T_m) deforming ρ̄, unramified outside S(ρ̄) ∪ Q, with tr ρ_Q(Frob_x) = T_x for all x ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {p}. Moreover ρ′_Q := ρ_Q ⊗ η, with η as in Theorem 3.11, is a deformation of ρ̄ minimal outside Q.
items.note: This is the L_σ analogue of Theorem 3.11, whose parts K3 marked missing, together with minimality at T(ρ̄) through cdt-lemma-5-1-1 (missing) and Hasse-invariant multiplication (planned in R15.3).

items.name: Hecke operators and duality ([31, Prop. 7.3]); transposed operators
items.statement: As used: under Serre–Verdier duality between H^1(X, ω^{2−n}(−∞)_{K/O}) (with coefficients) and H^0(X, ω^n) (with coefficients), T_x (resp. U_y) corresponds to x^{1−n} (resp. y^{1−n}) times the dual of the transposed operator T_x^t (resp. U_y^t), with the transposed operators as defined in [31].
items.locator: cited in §3.9.2, proof of Theorem 3.30, step (3), p. 351
items.note: The reviewed R15.3 node weight-reduction-to-at-most-p-plus-one already plans Edixhoven Prop. 7.3, but only over F̄_p for S(N,k) → M^0(N,p+1−k)^dual. The form used here is not planned: K/O and O/ϖ^m coefficients, arbitrary weight n, transposed operators T_x^t, U_y^t, and L_σ. K2 routed its analogue Phi-duality-twisted-hecke to R15.3. External input: [31] B. Edixhoven, The weight in Serre's conjectures on modular forms, Invent. Math. 109 (1992), Prop. 7.3 (and its proof), §7.1

items.name: Rank one of H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m∅} in characteristic-zero-nonvanishing cases
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of thm-3-30, if H_0(X_U, ω_K ⊗ L_σ)_{m∅} is non-zero, then H_0(X_U, ω ⊗ L_σ)_{m∅} is free of rank one over T_{∅,m∅}.
items.note: Rank one with L_σ follows from characteristic-zero multiplicity one (planned; see multiplicity-one-GL2) and CDT Lemma 4.2.4(3) (missing). It sits on the missing Theorem 3.30. See sourceIssues E61 (same σ versus σ^* change needed).

items.name: [15, Lemma 4.2.4(3)] (local multiplicity one of the type)
items.statement: As used: for the representations σ_x of [15] at vexing primes, each relevant automorphic representation contributes a one-dimensional space to the W_σ^*-isotypic part, so that with multiplicity one for GL(2) each characteristic-zero eigensystem occurs once in H_0(X_U, ω_K ⊗ L_σ)_{m∅}.
items.note: This is the local multiplicity-one statement for the type: dim Hom_{GL₂(Z_x)}(σ_x, π_x) ≤ 1, with the relevant π_x contributing a line. It is local representation theory of GL₂ that no layer names (see cdt-sigma-x). External input: [15] Conrad–Diamond–Taylor, JAMS 12 (1999), Lemma 4.2.4(3)

items.name: Multiplicity one for GL(2)/Q
items.statement: As used, with no reference given: cuspidal automorphic representations of GL2(A_Q) occur with multiplicity one and are determined by their Hecke eigenvalues at almost all primes (strong multiplicity one). Together with newform theory (for X_1(N)/H with N = N(ρ̄)) or the local multiplicity-one statement for the type σ (with L_σ), each characteristic-zero Hecke eigensystem in the m∅-part occurs with multiplicity one.
items.note:
Adelic multiplicity one and strong multiplicity one for GL₂ are R16.4. The classical forms (newform theory with the conductor, new-part multiplicity one, cross-level strong multiplicity one) are Tau Ceti ModularForms Layers 4–5. Tau Ceti already proves two classical fixed-level statements, valid for every k ∈ ℤ including weight one:
- tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.finrank_cuspFormsNewEigenspace_eq_one: each joint good-Hecke eigenspace in S_k(N,χ)^new is a line.
- tauceti:HeckeRing.GL2.Newform.eq_of_forall_notMem_eigenvalue_eq: strong multiplicity one with a finite exceptional set.

These are near misses. They are not the adelic statement, not cross-level, and not the fact that the m∅-part consists of newforms of level N(ρ̄). External input: Standard: strong multiplicity one (Jacquet–Langlands, Piatetski-Shapiro) and newform theory (Atkin–Lehner, Li, Casselman); not cited in the paper

items.name: Canonical modules of complete local Cohen–Macaulay rings under quotients by regular sequences
items.statement: Let (A, m, k) be a complete local Cohen–Macaulay ring of dimension n. Then A has a canonical module ω_A. If (x_1, …, x_r) is an A-regular sequence and B = A/(x_1, …, x_r), then ω_B := ω_A ⊗_A B is a canonical module for B, and ω_A ⊗_A A/m = ω_B ⊗_B B/m. If r = n, so that dim B = 0, then Hom_B(−, ω_B) is a dualizing functor and dim_k B[m] = dim_k ω_B ⊗ B/m = dim_k ω_A ⊗ A/m.
items.note: Regular sequences are in Mathlib: RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular (RegularSequence.lean:146), with depth via Ext in RingTheory/Depth/Rees.lean. Cohen–Macaulay rings are planned in R03.3, but R03.3 does not name canonical modules. Neither library has canonical modules, Cohen–Macaulay rings or Matlis duality. K5 and PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 (cm-module-dual, dualizing-facts-11-1) treat these as missing and route them to R03.3. External input: [45] D. Eisenbud, Commutative Algebra, GTM 150, §21.3; [46] J. Herzog, E. Kunz (eds.), Der kanonische Modul eines Cohen–Macaulay-Rings, LNM 238

items.name: Canonical (dualizing) module of a Cohen–Macaulay local ring; its number of generators
items.statement: For a Noetherian local Cohen–Macaulay ring (A, m, k) of dimension n, a canonical module ω_A is a finitely generated maximal Cohen–Macaulay A-module of type 1 and finite injective dimension (equivalently Ext^i_A(k, ω_A) = 0 for i ≠ n and dim_k Ext^n_A(k, ω_A) = 1). It is unique up to isomorphism when it exists, and every complete local Cohen–Macaulay ring has one. For dim A = 0, ω_A is the injective hull E_A(k), and Hom_A(−, ω_A) is a dualizing (Matlis) functor. μ(ω_A) := dim_k ω_A ⊗_A A/m is the number of generators of ω_A (this equals the Cohen–Macaulay type of A, and A is Gorenstein iff μ(ω_A) = 1). The paper uses 'canonical module' and 'dualizing module' as synonyms.
items.note: Neither library has depth, Cohen–Macaulay rings, canonical/dualizing modules, injective hulls or Matlis duality: grep of Mathlib and Tau Ceti for Macaulay/Gorenstein/canonical module/dualizing/injective hull/Matlis finds nothing relevant, and Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/Depth.lean is an empty deprecated module. Mathlib can express 'finite injective dimension' (CategoryTheory.HasInjectiveDimensionLE, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/Injective/Dimension.lean) and has regular sequences (RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular), but it has no canonical module and no type or μ(ω). R03.3 plans Cohen–Macaulay rings but not canonical modules. FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration:LI.1 only lists 'dualizing modules' in an inventory. tauceti StableReduction layer 2 plans the relative dualizing sheaf of Cohen–Macaulay curves, which is geometric. PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6 plans only the O-dual of Gorenstein O-orders. External input: Eisenbud, Commutative Algebra [45], §21.3; Herzog–Kunz [46]

items.name: Canonical module of a quotient by a regular sequence
items.statement: Let (A, m, k) be a complete local Cohen–Macaulay ring of dimension n with canonical module ω_A. If (x_1, …, x_m) is a regular sequence for A and B = A/(x_1, …, x_m), then ω_B := ω_A ⊗_A B is a canonical module for B. Consequently ω_A ⊗_A A/m = ω_A ⊗_A (B ⊗_B B/m) = ω_B ⊗_B B/m, so μ(ω_A) = μ(ω_B).
items.note: Absent from both libraries (no canonical modules). Mathlib has regular sequences and ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular (Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Regular.lean: dim(R/(rs)) + length = dim R). These are ingredients, not the statement. No atlas layer plans base change of canonical modules along a regular sequence (Bruns–Herzog 3.3.5). External input: Eisenbud [45] §21.3 (see also Herzog–Kunz [46]; Bruns–Herzog, Thm 3.3.5)

items.name: Socle of an Artinian quotient by a maximal regular sequence computes μ(ω)
items.statement: In the situation of canonical-module-mod-regular-sequence, if m = n (so B = A/(x_1,…,x_n) has dimension 0), then Hom_B(−, ω_B) is a dualizing functor and dim_k B[m] = dim_k ω_B ⊗ B/m = dim_k ω_A ⊗ A/m, where B[m] = Hom_B(k, B) is the socle of B.
items.note: No Matlis duality or injective hull exists in either library. Tau Ceti's TauCeti.socle (TauCeti/RingTheory/SimpleModule/Socle.lean:42, the sum of the simple submodules) is a near miss: it equals B[m] = Hom_B(k,B) for local Artinian B only after a comparison, and nothing relates it to ω_B ⊗ k. No layer plans this identity. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/socle-artinian-gorenstein is the analogous missing item. External input: Eisenbud [45] §21.3 (Matlis duality)

items.name: Lemma 4.1 (Hom_{Z_p}(A, Z_p) is the canonical module)
items.statement: Let A be a finite flat local Z_p-algebra, and suppose that A is Cohen–Macaulay. Then Hom_{Z_p}(A, Z_p) is a canonical module for A.
items.note: Not in either library. The near miss is PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L6, which plans 'the O-dual Hom_O(R,O) as an R-module' and the equivalence 'Gorenstein-order condition ⟺ invertibility/local rank-one freeness'. That is the Gorenstein (μ = 1) shadow of Lemma 4.1 for O-orders. It does not identify Hom_{Z_p}(A,Z_p) with the canonical module of a Cohen–Macaulay finite flat local Z_p-algebra, which §4.1 needs with μ = 3.

items.name: Canonical module of a module-finite extension of a Gorenstein local ring
items.statement: If A is a Cohen–Macaulay local ring that is a module-finite extension of a regular (or Gorenstein) local ring R, then Hom_R(A, R) is a canonical module for A.
items.note: Eisenbud Theorem 21.15 (for S Cohen–Macaulay and module-finite over R with canonical module ω_R, Ext^{dim R−dim S}_R(S, ω_R) is a canonical module for S, so Hom_R(S,R) when R is regular or Gorenstein and the dimensions agree) is in neither library. No layer plans canonical modules. External input: Eisenbud [45], Theorem 21.15

items.name: Complete intersection (complete local O-algebra)
items.statement: A complete local Noetherian O-algebra C with residue field k is a complete intersection if C ≅ O⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧/(f_1, …, f_r) for some regular sequence f_1, …, f_r of O⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧. Since the complete-intersection property does not depend on the presentation, the kernel of any surjection O⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧ ↠ C is then generated by a regular sequence.
items.note: Neither library has a complete-intersection predicate. Mathlib has presentations and regular sequences only, and the audit of tauceti StableReduction layer 1 notes that no local complete intersection notion exists. R03.3 plans the notion and 'the exact complete-intersection criteria used in patching'. Independence of the presentation (Bruns–Herzog 2.3.4-type) is one of those criteria. R03.3's reviewed decomposition has coverage 'partial', with 'complete-intersection criteria … not read'. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/complete-intersection is likewise planned in R03.3. External input: standard; e.g. Bruns–Herzog, Thm 2.3.4

items.name: Lemma 4.2, first part (power series rings)
items.statement: If B is a complete local Cohen–Macaulay O-algebra that admits a dualizing module ω_B with μ generators, then the same is true for the power series ring A = B⟦T_1, …, T_n⟧: A is a complete local Cohen–Macaulay ring and admits a dualizing module with μ generators.
items.note: The Cohen–Macaulay half (B CM ⇒ B⟦T⟧ CM) lies within R03.3's scope ('depth and dimension formulas under the local maps actually used'). The canonical module with μ generators is not planned anywhere and is in neither library, so the item as stated is missing.

items.name: Lemma 4.2, second part (completed tensor with a complete intersection), corrected
items.statement: Let B be a complete local Cohen–Macaulay O-algebra admitting a dualizing module with μ generators, and let C be a complete local O-algebra which is a complete intersection. [Correction: assume in addition that B is flat over O.] Then B ⊗̂_O C is a complete local Cohen–Macaulay ring admitting a dualizing module with μ generators. Proof: write C = O⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧/(f_1,…,f_r) with (f_i) regular. Since B is O-flat, B⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧ is flat over O⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧, so the images of the f_i form a regular sequence in B⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧ and B ⊗̂_O C = B⟦T_1,…,T_n⟧/(f_1,…,f_r). Now apply canonical-module-mod-regular-sequence to B⟦T⟧ → B and B⟦T⟧ → B ⊗̂_O C.
items.note: Missing: canonical modules are absent from both libraries and all layers. Ingredients exist or are planned. Mathlib's RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular.of_flat_of_isBaseChange (Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/Flat.lean:34) gives flat base change of weakly regular sequences, the step 'B⟦T⟧ flat over O⟦T⟧ ⇒ images of f_i regular' (after completion). DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.1 plans completed tensor products over O. The O-flatness hypothesis on B (sourceIssues E72) must be kept.

items.name: O[Δ] is a complete intersection; the example B[Δ]
items.statement: For any finite abelian group Δ of p-power order, O[Δ] is a complete intersection whose generic fibre O[Δ][1/p] is formally smooth (étale) over K. Hence Lemma 4.2 applies to B[Δ] = B ⊗_O O[Δ]: if B is a complete local Cohen–Macaulay O-algebra with a dualizing module with μ generators, then so is B[Δ].
items.locator: §4.1, p. 356; also proof of Lemma 4.11, p. 364
items.note: Mathlib has group algebras (MonoidAlgebra) but no complete-intersection notion, so 'O[Δ] is a complete intersection with étale generic fibre' is in neither library. DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P8 and the R03.5 node use S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q] as a quotient of S_∞ = O⟦(Z_p)^q⟧. They do not state that the kernel ((1+z_i)^{p^N}−1) is a regular sequence, nor that K[Δ] is étale. The same fact is used again in Lemma 4.11, cases (1)–(2).

items.name: The ordinary framed deformation ring with Frobenius eigenvalue, R̃† (and R†)
items.statement: Let ρ̄: G_{Q_p} → GL_2(k) be unramified with ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar (after twisting, trivial). Fix n ≥ 2, a lift φ_p of Frob_p, ε the cyclotomic character, ω the Teichmüller lift of ε mod p, and χ = εω^{-1} (so χ ≡ 1 mod ϖ), with φ_p chosen so that χ(φ_p) = 1. R̃^univ represents framed deformations of ρ̄ together with an eigenvalue α of φ_p, and R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}} is its quotient with determinant χ^{n−1}. R̃† is the unique reduced O-flat quotient of R̃^{univ,χ^{n−1}} whose generic-fibre points are the ρ: G_{Q_p} → GL_2(E) with ρ ∼ (χ^{n−1}λ(α^{-1}) ∗; 0 λ(α)), where λ(α) is the unramified character sending Frob_p to α. R† denotes the image of R^univ (framed deformations without α) in R̃†. §4.1 describes R̃† as the framed deformation ring of ordinary representations of weight n with fixed determinant, together with a Frobenius eigenvalue α acting on an unramified quotient.
items.locator: §4.1, p. 356, recalling §3.7, Definition 3.18 and Theorem 3.19, pp. 334–335
items.note: Not in either library, since neither has Galois deformation rings (audit: 'No deformation functors or deformation rings exist in either library'). The definition is planned in LocalGaloisDeformationRings: L7 owns ordinary deformation functors and the flag-bearing versus flag-forgotten pair (R̃† versus its image R†), and R08.3 owns Kisin's reduced/O-flat quotients with prescribed characteristic-zero points (CG credit part (1) of Theorem 3.19 to Kisin). Caveat: L7 proves representability and dimension only 'under the source genericity/distinguishedness assumptions', and ρ̄ trivial is the non-distinguished case. The structure theorems for R̃† (items thm-4-3-a, snowden-special-fibre-presentation, thm-4-3-b-type-three) are not planned. The primary extraction of Definition 3.18/Theorem 3.19 belongs to the §3.7 cluster.

items.name: Snowden's presentation of the special fibre R̃† ⊗ k
items.statement: R̃† ⊗_O k is isomorphic to the completion of Snowden's variety B_1 at b = (1,1;0): writing m = (a b; c −a), n = φ − id = (φ_1 φ_2; φ_3 φ_4), β = α − 1, the relations are mn = βm, P_φ(α) = 0, m² = 0, det(φ) = 1. Explicitly R̃† ⊗ k ≅ A := k⟦a, b, c, φ_1, φ_2, φ_3, φ_4, β⟧ / (φ_1 + φ_4 + φ_1φ_4 − φ_2φ_3, β² − (φ_1+φ_4)β − (φ_1+φ_4), aφ_1 + bφ_3 − aβ, aφ_2 + bφ_4 − bβ, −aφ_3 + cφ_1 − cβ, aφ_4 − cφ_2 − aβ, a² + bc). Moreover A is a Cohen–Macaulay domain of dimension 4.
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. I checked by direct expansion that the seven displayed generators are exactly the entries of mn = βm (with m = (a b; c −a), n = φ−1), m² = (a²+bc)·1, det(1+n) = 1 and P_φ(1+β) = β² − (φ_1+φ_4)β − (φ_1+φ_4). The claim that A is a Cohen–Macaulay domain of dimension 4 is quoted from Snowden [41] Theorem 3.4.1. External input: Snowden [41] (method of Snowden; 'A is a domain': [41] Theorem 3.4.1)

items.name: Hilbert series of a complete local k-algebra and its partial order
items.statement: For a complete local Noetherian k-algebra (R, m) with residue field k, H_R(t) := Σ_{n≥0} dim_k(m^n/m^{n+1}) t^n ∈ Z⟦t⟧. Order Z⟦t⟧ coefficientwise: Σ a_n t^n ≥ Σ b_n t^n iff a_n ≥ b_n for all n.
items.note: Neither library defines the Hilbert function or series of a complete local ring, or the associated graded ring of the m-adic filtration. Mathlib has only Polynomial.hilbertPoly (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/HilbertPoly.lean, the formal polynomial attached to p/(1−X)^d) and Ideal.Filtration. Tau Ceti's associated graded rings are only for PBW/word filtrations. No atlas stage or decomposition node mentions Hilbert series, Hilbert functions or Hilbert–Samuel theory; PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/multiplicity found the same.

items.name: Lemma 4.4, first part (Hilbert series inequality), corrected
items.statement: Let (R, m) be a complete local Noetherian k-algebra with residue field k, d ≥ 1, and x ∈ m^d. Then H_{R/x}(t)/(1−t) ≥ H_R(t)·(1−t^d)/(1−t) coefficientwise. [Correction: the paper says 'and equality holds if and only if x is a regular element'; in general only the implication 'equality ⇒ x is a regular element' holds, i.e. if x is a zero-divisor the inequality is strict.]
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. The proof's ingredient, Krull's intersection theorem, is in Mathlib (Ideal.iInf_pow_eq_bot_of_isLocalRing, Mathlib/RingTheory/Filtration.lean). The corrected statement (only 'equality ⇒ x regular') is the one to plan. The paper's own example on p. 358 shows that 'regular ⇒ equality' fails. See sourceIssues E75 (only 'equality ⇒ regular' holds).

items.name: Lemma 4.4, second part (graded case)
items.statement: If moreover R is isomorphic to the m-adic completion of its associated graded ring gr(R) = ⊕_n m^n/m^{n+1} (the paper writes R ≃ gr(R)), and x is pure (homogeneous) of degree d, then H_{R/x}(t)/(1−t) = H_R(t)(1−t^d)/(1−t), i.e. H_{R/x}(t) = H_R(t)(1−t^d), holds if and only if x is a regular element.
items.note: Not in either library (no associated graded ring of a local ring, no Hilbert series). Planned nowhere.

items.name: Example: regular element with strict Hilbert inequality (R = k⟦φ^6, φ^7, φ^15⟧)
items.statement: Let R = k⟦φ^6, φ^7, φ^15⟧ ⊂ k⟦φ⟧ and x = φ^6 (degree one). Then x is regular, but H_{R/x}(t)/(1−t) = (1 + 2t + 2t² + t³)/(1−t) > (1 + 2t + t² + t³ + t⁵)/(1−t) = H_R(t). R is a Cohen–Macaulay domain but gr(R) has depth 0, and x is not regular in gr(R).
items.locator: §4.1, after the proof of Lemma 4.4, pp. 357–358
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. I verified the numbers by a monomial computation in the semigroup ⟨6,7,15⟩: (1−t)H_R(t) = 1+2t+t²+t³+t⁵, and H_{R/x}(t) = 1+2t+2t²+t³ (Apéry set {0,7,14,15,22,29}). So H_{R/x}/(1−t) > H_R holds coefficientwise, strictly at t². The example is from Rossi [47].

items.name: The graded ring B = A/β
items.statement: β is non-zero in m/m² of the domain A, hence A-regular, so B := A/βA is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 3. In B the relation β² − (φ_1+φ_4)β − (φ_1+φ_4) becomes φ_1 + φ_4 = 0, and B ≅ k⟦a, b, c, φ_1, φ_2, φ_3⟧/(−φ_1² − φ_2φ_3, aφ_1 + bφ_3, aφ_2 − bφ_1, −aφ_3 + cφ_1, −aφ_1 − cφ_2, a² + bc). All six relations are homogeneous of degree two, so B is isomorphic to the completion of gr(B).
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. I checked that setting β = 0 in A gives exactly the six displayed quadratic relations (φ_4 = −φ_1 from the P_φ relation). The claim that B is Cohen–Macaulay of dimension 3 uses Snowden's theorem that A is a Cohen–Macaulay domain.

items.name: Lemma 4.5 (first terms of H_B)
items.note: An explicit computation (dim m/m² = 6; six independent quadratic relations among 21 monomials, via a 6×6 minor of determinant 1). It is in neither library and planned nowhere. It is checkable by linear algebra over k.

items.name: Graded Cohen–Macaulay rings have regular sequences of linear forms after extending k
items.statement: Let R be a complete local Noetherian Cohen–Macaulay k-algebra with residue field k that is graded (the completion of gr(R)). After replacing k by a finite (sufficiently large) extension, or by k̄, which does not change the Hilbert series, R has a regular sequence of length dim R consisting of elements of pure degree one.
items.note: No Cohen–Macaulay predicate or associated graded ring exists in either library. The ingredients are in Mathlib: biUnion_associatedPrimes_eq_compl_regular (Mathlib/RingTheory/Regular/IsSMulRegular.lean:124; zero-divisors are the union of the associated primes), Subspace.biUnion_ne_univ_of_top_notMem (Mathlib/GroupTheory/CosetCover.lean:389; a vector space over an infinite field is not a finite union of proper subspaces), Ideal.subset_union_prime and Nakayama. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 4.6(a) (Hilbert series modulo a linear regular sequence)
items.statement: If I ⊂ B is an ideal generated by a regular sequence of length 3 of elements of pure degree one, then H_{B/I}(t) = 1 + 3t.
items.note: Specific to the ring B, with H_B = 1+6t+15t²+⋯. It needs graded-cm-linear-regular-sequence and Lemma 4.4 (graded case), all of which are missing. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 4.6(b) (Hilbert series criterion for regularity)
items.statement: If I ⊂ B is any ideal generated by three elements of pure degree one such that H_{B/I}(t) = 1 + 3t, then the three generators of I form a regular sequence.
items.note: Specific to B. It is the converse direction of Lemma 4.4 in the graded case, which is missing. Planned nowhere.

items.name: Lemma 4.7 (an explicit regular sequence in R̃† ⊗ k)
items.statement: {β, a, φ_2 + φ_3, b + c + φ_1} is a regular sequence in A = R̃† ⊗ k. The quotient C = A/(β, a, φ_2+φ_3, b+c+φ_1) = B/(a, φ_2+φ_3, b+c+φ_1) is isomorphic to k⟦x, y, z⟧/(x, y, z)² = k[x,y,z]/(x², y², z², xy, xz, yz), with H_C(t) = 1 + 3t.
items.note: Planned nowhere. I verified the quotient: with a = 0, φ_3 = −φ_2 and φ_1 = −(b+c), the six relations of B become −(b+c)²+φ_2², bφ_2, b(b+c), c(b+c), cφ_2 and bc. With x = b, y = c, z = φ_2 these give C = k[x,y,z]/(x,y,z)², with H_C = 1+3t and a socle of dimension 3.

items.name: Theorem 4.3, second part: dim_k ω_{R̃†}/m = 3
items.statement: Let ω_{R̃†} be the canonical module of R̃†. Then dim_k ω_{R̃†}/m ω_{R̃†} = 3. Thus R̃† is Cohen–Macaulay of type 3 and in particular not Gorenstein.
items.note: The type of R̃† (dim_k ω/mω = 3, not Gorenstein) is in neither library and planned nowhere. It combines the missing canonical-module theory (R03.3) with the explicit Snowden computations (Lemmas 4.5–4.7).

items.name: Setup for Theorem 4.8: ρ̄, N, N*, T and m
items.statement: Let p ≥ 3 and let ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) be absolutely irreducible and modular (= odd), with Serre conductor N = N(ρ̄) and Serre weight k(ρ̄), 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p+1. Assume ρ̄ has minimal conductor amongst all its twists at all primes other than p (this can always be arranged by twisting). Put N* = N if k(ρ̄) = 2 and N* = Np otherwise; ρ̄ is the mod-p reduction of a modular form of weight 2 and level N*. T is the ring of endomorphisms of J_1(N*)/Q generated by the Hecke operators T_l for all primes l (including l = p), and m ⊂ T is the maximal ideal corresponding to ρ̄.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries: Mathlib has no Jacobian of X_1(N) (its 'Jacobian' files are Weierstrass/Jacobian coordinates of elliptic curves), and Tau Ceti has only abelian-variety basics and abstract Hecke rings. The data are planned. The Serre invariants N(ρ̄) and k(ρ̄) are R15.4/R15.6. The Hecke ring T generated by the T_l inside End(J_1(N*)) is ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2. The maximal ideal m attached to ρ̄ is R19.6. 'Modular (= odd)' with odd ⇒ absolutely irreducible is R01.4. Serre's theorem at level N(ρ̄) and weight k(ρ̄) is ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6. Caveat: the paper's 'One knows' step, passing from weight 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p+1 at level N to weight 2 at level Np, is not stated in any layer (closest are SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3/R20.4). External input: The fact that ρ̄ arises in weight 2 and level N* is quoted as known ('One knows'): Serre's conjecture, Khare–Wintenberger [24], with the level and weight results of Ribet and Edixhoven [31]

items.name: Multiplicity of m in J_1(N*)
items.statement: J_1(N*)[m] = {x ∈ J_1(N*)(Q̄) : tx = 0 for all t ∈ m}, a finite-dimensional T/m-vector space with a G_Q-action. m has multiplicity μ if J_1(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄^{⊕μ} as T/m[G_Q]-modules.
items.note: Not in either library. ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2 plans Jacobians with their Hecke action and Tate modules, but no layer defines J[m] as a T/m[G_Q]-module or its multiplicity. Mazur-style multiplicity statements appear nowhere in the atlas.

items.name: Theorem 4.8, first part: multiplicity one (known cases)
items.statement: In setup-4-1-rhobar-level-hecke: if ρ̄ is ramified at p, or ρ̄ is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is not scalar, then J_1(N*)[m] ≃ ρ̄, i.e. m has multiplicity one.
items.note: Not in either library and not planned. The nearest text is ModularCurvesPartII:R14.6, 'Supply … the finite-level freeness statements needed for Taylor–Wiles modules', which does not state multiplicity one. R14.6 also precedes the Katz-form layers R15.2–R15.3 on which Gross's and Edixhoven's proofs rest. The result is a union of cited theorems: Mazur [48] 14.2, Mazur–Ribet [49], Gross [28] 12.10, Edixhoven [31] 9.2, Buzzard (appendix to [50]) and Wiese [51] 4.2. External input: Mazur [48] Prop. 14.2; Mazur–Ribet [49] Main Theorem; Gross [28] Prop. 12.10; Edixhoven [31] Thm 9.2; Buzzard (appendix to Ribet–Stein [50]); Wiese [51] Cor. 4.2

items.name: Wiese: multiplicity at least two in the scalar case
items.statement: If ρ̄ (as in setup-4-1-rhobar-level-hecke) is unramified at p and ρ̄(Frob_p) is scalar, then the multiplicity of m in J_1(N*) is at least two.
items.note: Not in either library and not planned. SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.5 and ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.4 mention 'Wiese's assigned weight-one theorem' as an input to the dyadic Serre argument, but neither states the multiplicity bound of Wiese [51] (Algebra Number Theory 1 (2007)). Its proof uses Katz weight-one forms.

items.name: Gross: the ordinary exact sequence of Tate modules and freeness of T_pG^0
items.statement: Let G be the part of the p-divisible group of J_1(N*) associated to m. There is an exact sequence 0 → T_pG^0 → T_pG → T_pG^e → 0 stable under T_m, with T_pG^0 free of rank one over T_m and T_pG^e = Hom(T_pG^0, Z_p) (so T_pG^e ≅ Hom_{Z_p}(T_m, Z_p)).
items.note: Not in either library: there are no p-divisible groups of Jacobians and no Jacobian of X_1(N). The general tools are planned: FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.1 ('Cartier duality, connected–étale sequences … Construct its Tate module') and ModularCurvesPartII:R14.2 (Tate modules with Hecke action). The m-part statement, with T_pG^0 free of rank one over T_m and T_pG^e = Hom(T_pG^0, Z_p), is planned nowhere. Gross [28] proves it with q-expansion duality. External input: Gross [28], Prop. 12.9 and the proof of Prop. 12.10

items.name: Harmless primes, M, the group Φ, the characters φ ∈ Φ̂ and χ_φ
items.statement: (ρ̄ unramified at p with ρ̄(Frob_p) scalar, so N* = Np.) A prime v is harmless if v ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄|G_v is absolutely irreducible (then v | N). M is the largest divisor of N divisible only by harmless primes. Φ := Z_p ⊗ ∏_{x | M, x prime} (Z/xZ)^×, the p-part of the harmless tame quotients, viewed both as a quotient and as a subgroup of (Z/NpZ)^× ⊗ Z_p. Φ̂ := Hom(Φ, Q̄_p^×), and O is enlarged so that every φ ∈ Φ̂ is O^×-valued. For φ ∈ Φ̂, χ_φ := ε · ⟨det(ρ̄) · ε̄^{-1}⟩ · φ, a character of G_Q, where ⟨·⟩ is the Teichmüller lift and φ is viewed as a Dirichlet character. [Correction: the paper prints ε·⟨ρ̄ε^{-1}⟩φ.]
items.note: A device specific to this paper: harmless primes, M, Φ, Φ̂ and χ_φ = ε·⟨det ρ̄·ε̄^{-1}⟩·φ (the paper prints ε·⟨ρ̄ε^{-1}⟩φ; checked on the page image of p. 362). It is in neither library and planned nowhere. The general operations it uses are planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations:R04.4 ('twisting by characters', 'changing determinant') and tauceti ModularForms layer 0 (diamond characters). See sourceIssues E85 (exceptional set also includes Lemma 4.11 case (3)).

items.name: Local deformation rings R_v = R_{v,φ}
items.statement: For v | N* (N* = Np), R_v = R_{v,φ} is the following quotient of the universal framed deformation ring of ρ̄|G_v with determinant χ_φ|G_v: (1) for v = p, R_p is the ordinary framed deformation ring R† of §3.7 with n = 2; (2) for v ≠ p, R_v is the unrestricted framed deformation ring of ρ̄|G_v with determinant χ_φ|G_v. The isomorphism types of these rings do not depend on φ.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. For v ≠ p the unrestricted framed ring with fixed determinant is R08.1; for v = p the ring R† is as in item R-tilde-dagger (L7/R08.3). Independence of φ up to isomorphism is twisting by a character congruent to 1, which R08.1 and R04.4 cover.

items.name: Global deformation rings R_φ and R_φ^□
items.statement: R = R_φ is the universal deformation ring of ρ̄: G_Q → GL_2(k) for deformations with determinant χ_φ that are unramified outside N* and whose restrictions to G_v, after a choice of framing, are classified by R_v for each v | N*. R^□ is the framed version, with framings at each place v | N*. R^□ is (non-canonically) a power series ring over R.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. Global deformation functors with fixed determinant and prescribed local conditions, their representability, and the framed ring as a power series ring over the unframed one are planned in GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.1–R04.3. The paper's ring is an instance.

items.name: The variant R̃_φ (with Frobenius eigenvalue α at p) and R_loc
items.statement: R̃ = R̃_φ is the global deformation ring classifying deformations of ρ̄ as in R_φ together with an eigenvalue α of Frobenius at p, i.e. with local condition R̃† at p; R̃^□ is its framed version. R_loc := R̃† ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v|N} R_v), and there are surjections R_loc⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ → R̃^□ → R̃ → R̃/ϖ. R̃ maps onto the full Hecke algebra T_{φ,m}, which contains U_p (α ↦ U_p).
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. The completed tensor product R_loc is R03.1, and the presentation R_loc⟦x⟧ ↠ R̃^□ ↠ R̃ is R04.3. The deformation-to-Hecke map, surjective with α ↦ U_p, is R22.1. It needs the ordinary local structure at p over the Hecke algebra, which is R21.3. The paper's variant with a Frobenius eigenvalue α is an instance.

items.name: S_φ, the anaemic ordinary Hecke algebra T^an_φ, the full Hecke algebras T_{φ,m} and T_m
items.statement: S_φ := ⊕_χ S_2^ord(Γ_1(N*), χ, O), where χ runs over the characters of (Z/NpZ)^× with χ|_Φ = φ. Then S_2^ord(Γ_1(N*), O) ⊗ Q = ⊕_{φ∈Φ̂} S_φ ⊗ Q. T^an_φ is the anaemic weight 2, level Γ_1(N*) ordinary Hecke algebra acting on S_φ (it does not contain U_p), and T^an_{φ,m} is its localization at the maximal ideal of ρ̄. T_{φ,m} is the Hecke algebra (the 'adorned' one, including U_p) acting on S_{φ,m} ⊗ K. T_m is the Hecke ring at full level Γ_1(N*), localized at m.
items.note: Neither library has O-integral ordinary weight-2 forms or ordinary Hecke algebras. Mathlib and Tau Ceti have complex modular forms and abstract Hecke rings. S_φ is a sum of nebentypus eigenspaces, and T^an_φ, T_{φ,m} and T_m are Hecke algebras acting on them, all instances of planned constructions. The ordinary projector and diamond action are PadicFamilies:L0, integral forms and Hecke theory R15.2, the Hecke algebra on the Jacobian R14.2, and forms with character and the Hecke algebra tauceti ModularForms layers 0 and 2. The ModularCurvesPartII conventions require 'Distinguish the full Hecke algebra from its away-from-level-and-p subalgebra' (anaemic versus full).

items.name: Twisted Galois representation valued in T^an_{φ,m}
items.statement: Let ρ: G_Q → GL_2(T^an_{φ,m}) be the Galois representation associated to the eigenforms in S_φ. The character ε^{-1} det ρ can be regarded as a character χ: (Z/NpZ)^× → (T^an_{φ,m})^× with χ|_Φ = φ. Let ψ be the restriction of χ to Z_p ⊗ ∏_{x | N, x prime, x ∤ M}(Z/xZ)^× [printed ∏_{x∤M}; sourceIssues E84], regarded as a character of G_Q. It has p-power order and values in 1 + m, so ψ^{-1/2} exists since p is odd (this justification is implicit in the paper). Twisting ρ by ψ^{-1/2} gives a Galois representation G_Q → GL_2(T^an_{φ,m}) with determinant χ_φ = ε·⟨det ρ̄·ε̄^{-1}⟩·φ that is classified by R = R_φ. This gives an O-algebra map R_φ → T^an_{φ,m}.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. The representation over the localised Hecke algebra with determinant and local-type compatibility is R19.6, its ordinary local structure R21.3, twisting and change of determinant R04.4, and the resulting map R_φ → T^an_{φ,m} R22.1. The twist by ψ^{-1/2}, which exists because p is odd and ψ takes values in 1+m, is an instance. The determinant formula printed on p. 363 carries the misprint recorded in harmless-primes-Phi-chi-phi (sourceIssues E83).

items.name: Kisin's method: R_φ[1/p] ≅ T^an_{φ,m}[1/p]
items.statement: Under the hypotheses above, R_φ[1/p] ≅ T^an_{φ,m}[1/p]. The proof uses the patching results Proposition 3.3.1 and Lemma 3.3.4 of Kisin [52], as in the proof of [52] Theorem 3.4.11, except that the local rings (denoted B and D in [52]) need not be integral domains, although their generic fibres are formally smooth over K (Lemma 4.11). The only use in [52] of the domain hypothesis is in the first paragraph of the proof of Lemma 3.3.4; here it suffices that every irreducible component of each R_{v,φ} lies in the support of S_φ.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. Kisin's criterion (Proposition 3.3.1 with Lemma 3.3.4) is a reviewed R03.5 node, which assumes B is a domain. CG's modification (B not a domain, but every component of R_{v,φ} in the support of S_φ) is the R03.6 node's conclusion (3): 'H is nearly faithful over R provided every irreducible component of Spec R_∞[1/p] lies in the support'. The arithmetic application for GL₂ over totally real fields, with component matching, is R22.3–R22.4. The input that every component is in the support is item components-in-support-of-S-phi. See sourceIssues E85 (case-(3) primes need separate treatment). External input: Kisin, Ann. Math. 170 (2009) [52]: Prop. 3.3.1, Lemma 3.3.4, proof of Thm 3.4.11

items.name: Every component of R_{v,φ} is in the support of S_φ
items.statement: For each prime v | N (so v ≠ p), each irreducible component of R_{v,φ} lies in the support of S_φ. This is all that is needed to replace the integral-domain hypothesis on the rings B and D in the first paragraph of the proof of [52, Lemma 3.3.4]. The paper states that it 'follows from now standard results on the existence of modular deformations with prescribed local inertial types' and gives no further argument or reference.
items.note: Not in either library. CG give no citation ('now standard results'). Existence of modular lifts with prescribed local inertial types (for example Gee, Automorphic lifts of prescribed types) is planned in R24.3, and the component-matching use in R22.4. Ordering caveat: R24.3 comes after R22, so a consumer at R22.4 level must take this as a supplied input or be placed after R24. External input: 'now standard results on the existence of modular deformations with prescribed local inertial types' (no specific citation given)

items.name: R_φ (hence R̃_φ) is finite over O
items.statement: The global deformation ring R = R_φ is finite over O. Hence R̃ = R̃_φ, which is finite over R since α satisfies the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius, is finite over O, and R̃/ϖ is Artinian.
items.note: Asserted in the paper, with Thorne [53] Theorem 10.2 cited for the general result. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.1 plans only 'the global deformation-ring finiteness statement of KW II Theorem 10.1'. KW II 10.1 allows only the local rings of KW II Theorem 3.1: types (A)/(B)/(C) at p, and inertia-rigid or semistable away from p. It covers neither the unrestricted R_{v,φ} nor the ordinary R† (a single domain containing both crystalline and semistable points). The R03.4 node (finite-image criterion; finiteness after patching) and the R03.5 Kisin node, which assumes B a domain, give the method but not this instance. External input: Asserted as a fact. For general finiteness of deformation rings over O the paper points to Thorne [53] Theorem 10.2

items.name: The presentation kernels are generated by systems of parameters
items.statement: R^□ is a quotient of (R† ⊗̂ ⊗̂_{v|N} R_v)⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ by a sequence of elements that can be extended to a system of parameters. The kernel of the composite R_loc⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ → R̃^□ → R̃ → R̃/ϖ is generated by a system of parameters, one of which is ϖ.
items.note: Nothing is in the libraries. The presentation of the framed global ring over R_loc⟦x⟧, with the relation bound, is R04.3 and a reviewed R03.2 node. That node's acceptance clause is exactly the step used here: once the local rings are Cohen–Macaulay and R is finite over O, the variables, relations and p form a regular sequence (KW II, Remarks after Proposition 4.5). R03.3's coverage lists these 'CM/CI criteria used in patching' as still to be read. The finiteness input is item R-finite-over-O. External input: Proof of Snowden [41] Prop. 5.1.1; Kisin [54] Prop. 4.1.5

items.name: Lemma 4.11, first part: R_{v,φ} (v ≠ p) are complete intersections
items.statement: For every prime v | N with v ≠ p, the ring R_v = R_{v,φ} is a complete intersection.
items.note: Not in either library. R08.2 plans 'dimensions, smoothness and irreducible components' for unramified, fixed-inertial-type, Steinberg and minimally ramified conditions (KW II Theorem 3.1: flat, relative dimension 3, regular generic fibre). No layer states that the unrestricted fixed-determinant framed ring at v ≠ p is a complete intersection (Shotton's theorem). PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/local-framed-rings records the same gap. See sourceIssues E89 (non-smooth case v ≡ −1 mod p omitted).

items.name: Lemma 4.11, second part: generic fibres formally smooth
items.statement: For every prime v | N with v ≠ p, R_v[1/p] = R_{v,φ}[1/p] is formally smooth over K.
items.note: Not in either library. Formal smoothness of R_v[1/p] for the unrestricted fixed-determinant ring at v ≠ p is planned nowhere: R08.2 plans smoothness only for its named conditions. The proof uses Kisin's Proposition 2.3.5 (a separate item) and H² vanishing at characteristic-zero points. See sourceIssues E89 (non-smooth case v ≡ −1 mod p omitted).

items.name: Lemma 4.11, cases (1) and (2): R_v is a power series ring over O[Δ]
items.statement: (1) If v ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v is reducible and ρ̄|I_v ≃ χ ⊕ 1 for some ramified χ, then after an unramified twist ρ̄|G_v ≅ χ ⊕ 1. All R_v-deformations of ρ̄ have the form (⟨χ⟩ψ ⊕ ψ^{-1}) ⊗ (χ_φ⟨χ^{-1}⟩)^{1/2} with ψ ≡ 1 mod ϖ. Hence ψ is tamely ramified and decomposes as an unramified character times a character of F_v^× of p-power order. Writing down the universal framed deformation identifies R_v with a power series ring over O[Δ], Δ the maximal p-quotient of F_v^×. (2) If v is vexing (v ≡ −1 mod p, ρ̄|G_v absolutely irreducible and induced from a character ξ), any conductor-minimal deformation of ρ̄ is induced from a character ⟨ξ⟩ψ of G_{Q_{v²}} (Q_{v²} the unramified quadratic extension of Q_v) with ψ mod ϖ trivial. Hence ψ is tamely ramified and, up to unramified twist, a character of F_{v²}^× of p-power order. Writing down the universal deformation identifies R_v with a power series ring over O[Δ], Δ the maximal p-quotient of F_{v²}^×. [Implicit in the paper: at a vexing prime every lift of ρ̄|G_v is conductor-minimal, so this covers all R_v-deformations.] In both cases Δ is a finite cyclic p-group. Since O[Δ] is a complete intersection with formally smooth generic fibre, R_v is a complete intersection with formally smooth generic fibre.
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. It gives explicit universal framed deformations over O[Δ] (Δ the p-part of F_v^× or F_{v²}^×) for the principal-series case v ≡ 1 mod p and the vexing case. R08.2 plans minimally ramified and fixed-type conditions but not these unrestricted rings as power series rings over O[Δ].

items.name: Presentation of R_{v,φ} by Z¹ generators and H² relations
items.statement: For v ≠ p, R_{v,φ} is a quotient of a power series ring over O in dim_k Z¹(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) variables by at most dim_k H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) relations. It is formally smooth over O when H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) = 0.
items.note: Not in either library (the audit reports no deformation rings). Framed local representability with tangent space Z¹ and obstructions in H² for fixed determinant is R08.1, and the relation between presentation relations and obstruction spaces is R03.2. The presentation O⟦Z¹⟧/(≤ h² relations), with formal smoothness when H² = 0, is the standard consequence. External input: standard framed deformation theory (e.g. Kisin [52] §2)

items.name: Completed local rings of the generic fibre of a local deformation ring
items.statement: The completion of R_v[1/p] at a closed point is the characteristic-0 (framed, fixed determinant) deformation ring of the corresponding lift ρ: G_v → GL_2(E). When H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ) = 0, it is a power series ring over E in dim Z¹(G_v, ad⁰ρ) = 3 variables.
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. No layer states that the completion of R[1/p] at a closed point pro-represents the characteristic-zero framed deformations of the corresponding lift (Kisin, Ann. Math. 170 (2009), Prop. 2.3.5). R08.3 and L7 plan characteristic-zero point criteria and 'the required smoothness results', and their smoothness proofs need this lemma. External input: Kisin [52] Proposition 2.3.5

items.name: Lemma 4.11, case (3): R_v ≅ O⟦x_1,…,x_4⟧/(r)
items.statement: Suppose ρ̄^{I_v} is 1-dimensional and ρ̄^{ss}|G_v is unramified, with v ≡ 1 mod p (the paper's case (3)) [correction: the same argument and conclusion apply when v ≡ −1 mod p, a case the paper omits]. Then dim Z¹(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) = 4 and dim H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ̄) = 1. The closed points of the generic fibre are lifts that are unramified twists of the Steinberg representation, or (for v ≡ 1 mod p) lifts that decompose after inverting p as χ_φψ ⊕ ψ^{-1} with ψ|I_v of p-power order, or (for v ≡ −1 mod p) lifts induced from characters of G_{Q_{v²}} whose restriction to inertia has p-power order. At each such point H²(G_v, ad⁰ρ) = 0. Hence R_v ≅ O⟦x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4⟧/(r) for some r ≠ 0, and R_v[1/p] is formally smooth over K.
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. R08.2 plans Steinberg conditions with monodromy, but not the unrestricted ring in the unipotent-inertia case as O⟦x_1..x_4⟧/(r) with formally smooth generic fibre. The item records the v ≡ −1 mod p case omitted by the paper (sourceIssues E89); for ρ̄ ≅ (ω ∗; 0 1) the line ω² ⊂ ad⁰ρ̄(1) is trivial exactly when v ≡ ±1 mod p, so H² can be nonzero in that case too.

items.name: Footnote 5: the relation r and the components in case (3)
items.statement: In case (3) one may take r = C(T) − T, where C is the Chebyshev-type polynomial determined by C(t + t^{-1}) = t^v + t^{-v} and T is the trace of a generator of tame inertia (T − 2 ∈ m_{R_v}). The generic fibre of R_v has (q+1)/2 geometric components, where q is the largest power of p dividing v − 1. One component (T = 2) consists of lifts on which inertia acts unipotently [printed 'nilpotent']. The remaining (q−1)/2 components consist of representations finitely ramified of order dividing q, on which T = ζ + ζ^{-1} for some q-th root of unity ζ ≠ 1 [printed 'primitive q-th root of unity'].
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. It gives the explicit relation r = C(T) − T and the (q+1)/2 geometric components, with the wording corrections ('unipotent', 'ζ ≠ 1 a q-th root of unity') recorded in the item (sourceIssues E92, E93). Reduzzi [55] Theorem 1.0.1(A2.2) and Shotton are comparison sources. See sourceIssues E89 (case list omits v ≡ −1 mod p). External input: compare Reduzzi [55] Theorem 1.0.1(A2.2)

items.name: R̃_φ is Cohen–Macaulay, ϖ-torsion free, with μ(ω_{R̃}) = 3
items.statement: R_loc⟦x_1, …, x_n⟧ is Cohen–Macaulay, so the system of parameters whose quotient is R̃/ϖ is a regular sequence. Consequently R̃ = R̃_φ is Cohen–Macaulay and ϖ-torsion free (O-flat), and the canonical modules of R_loc⟦x_1,…,x_n⟧ and of R̃ have the same number of generators as that of R̃†, namely 3.
items.note: Split status. The Cohen–Macaulay and O-flat part is planned: the R03.2 node's acceptance ('If the local rings are Cohen–Macaulay and R̄ … finite over O … regular sequence … flat, CM') with R03.3. The conclusion μ(ω_{R̃}) = μ(ω_{R̃†}) = 3 needs canonical modules (Lemma 4.2), which are planned nowhere, so the item is missing.

items.name: R̃_φ ≅ T_{φ,m}; T_{φ,m} is Cohen–Macaulay of type 3
items.statement: Patching also applies to the adorned Hecke algebras (with U_p), and Kisin's method gives R̃_φ[1/p] = T_{φ,m}[1/p] (using that R̃† is a domain and R̃†[1/p] is formally smooth). Since R̃_φ is O-flat, R̃_φ ≅ T_{φ,m}. In particular T_{φ,m} is Cohen–Macaulay and dim_k ω_{T_{φ,m}}/m = 3.
items.note: Split status. The algebraic step (R̃ O-flat and R̃[1/p] = T[1/p] ⇒ R̃ ≅ T) is covered by R03.6: 'Provide an explicit algebraic theorem for the torsion-free/reduced quotient at which an R=T argument concludes, and a separate stronger theorem when its additional hypotheses are verified'. The generic-fibre R = T for the adorned algebra is R22.3–R22.4. Neither library has anything. The instance R̃_φ ≅ T_{φ,m} with U_p, and the conclusion that T_{φ,m} is Cohen–Macaulay of type 3, are planned nowhere. External input: Kisin [52] (method), as in kisin-patching-R-phi

items.name: Twisting identifies T_{φ²,m} with T_{1,m} ⊗ O(φ)
items.statement: S_2(Γ_1(N*), O)_m ⊗ K = ⊕_{φ∈Φ̂} S_{φ²,m} ⊗ K, writing each element of Φ̂ uniquely as a square (p odd). Twisting by φ induces an isomorphism T_{φ²,m} ≃ T_{1,m} ⊗_O O(φ), where O(φ) is O with the Φ-action (on diamond operators) twisted by φ.
items.note: Specific to this paper and planned nowhere; neither library has integral Hecke algebras of forms with character. Its inputs are the diamond-character decomposition (tauceti ModularForms layer 0) and twisting of forms by Dirichlet characters, which no stage mentions.

items.name: T_m ≅ T_{1,m} ⊗_O O[Φ]; T_m is Cohen–Macaulay of type 3
items.statement: Restriction gives an injection T_m ↪ ⊕_{φ} T_{φ²,m} ≃ T_{1,m} ⊗ ⊕_φ O(φ), whose image lies in T_{1,m} ⊗ O[Φ] and which becomes an isomorphism onto T_{1,m} ⊗ O[Φ] ⊗ K after tensoring with K. Hence T_m ≃ T_{1,m} ⊗_O O[Φ], and by Lemma 4.2 T_m is Cohen–Macaulay with dim_k ω_{T_m}/m = 3.
items.note: Specific to this paper and planned nowhere. It uses O-torsion-freeness of the spaces of forms, the twisting decomposition and Lemma 4.2 for O[Φ], which is itself missing. See sourceIssues E94 (isomorphism needs an argument on generators).

items.name: From type 3 to multiplicity 2
items.statement: Since T_m is finite (and flat) over Z_p and Cohen–Macaulay, Hom_{Z_p}(T_m, Z_p) is its canonical module (Lemma 4.1), so dim_k Hom(T_m, Z_p)/m = 3. Since Hom(T_m, Z_p) ≅ T_pG^e (gross-ordinary-sequence), dim_k G^0[m] = dim_k T_pG^e/m = 3, and dually dim_k G^e[m] = dim_k T_pG^0/m = dim_k T_m/m = 1. The paper then writes dim J_1(N*)[m] = ½ dim G[m] = ½(dim G^0[m] + dim G^e[m]) = (3+1)/2 = 2, where 'dim J_1(N*)[m]' means the multiplicity μ and G[m] = J_1(N*)[m]. [Gap: the additivity dim G[m] = dim G^0[m] + dim G^e[m] is not justified. Left exactness of m-torsion gives only 3 ≤ dim_k G[m] ≤ 4. Since J_1(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄^{⊕μ} has even k-dimension (boston-lenstra-ribet), or since μ ≥ 2 by Wiese, dim_k G[m] = 4.] Hence J_1(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄ ⊕ ρ̄.
items.note: The final count is planned nowhere. It combines Lemma 4.1 (missing), Gross's sequence (missing) and the Boston–Lenstra–Ribet structure of J[m] (missing). The step dim G^0[m] = dim T_pG^e/m uses the duality between G^0 and G^e, which the paper leaves implicit. See sourceIssues E95 (additivity of m-torsion is unjustified).

items.name: J[m] is a direct sum of copies of ρ̄ (implicit input)
items.statement: If m is a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra T acting on J_1(N*) whose associated ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, then J_1(N*)[m] ≅ ρ̄^{⊕μ} for some μ ≥ 1 as T/m[G_Q]-modules. In particular dim_{T/m} J_1(N*)[m] is even.
items.locator: §4.1, Theorem 4.8 and its proof, pp. 361, 366 (used implicitly)
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere as stated. Its algebraic core is planned in IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants:IHG.1 ('Construct the characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient … generalized matrix algebra decompositions'): the Cayley–Hamilton quotient of k[G] for an absolutely irreducible residual determinant is M_2(k). The input on J[m], the Eichler–Shimura relation, is R19.1. The paper uses it implicitly and does not cite it. External input: Boston–Lenstra–Ribet, C. R. Acad. Sci. Paris 312 (1991) 323–328 (not cited in the paper)

items.name: Remark 4.12 (multiplicity on J_H(N*); sketched)
items.statement: Let X_H(N*) = X_1(N*)/H be the smallest quotient of X_1(N*) where one might expect ρ̄ to occur. Provided p ≠ 3 and ρ̄ is not induced from a character of Q(√−3), J_H(N*)[m] has multiplicity two if ρ̄ is unramified at p with scalar Frobenius, and multiplicity one otherwise.
items.note: Only a sketch in the paper. It is in neither library and planned nowhere. Its extra input is Carayol [56] Prop. 3 (see also Edixhoven [57] Prop. 1.10). External input: The extra ingredient is Carayol [56] Prop. 3 (see also Edixhoven [57] Prop. 1.10)

items.name: Lemma 4.14 (R[1/p] is reduced when the generic fibre has finitely many points with finite image)
items.statement: Let F/Q be a number field, k a finite field, and S a finite set of places of F not containing any v | p. Let G_{F,S} be the Galois group of the maximal extension of F unramified outside S, and let ρ̄: G_{F,S} → GL_2(k) be continuous and absolutely irreducible, with universal deformation ring R. Suppose that the Galois representation associated to every Q̄_p-point of R has finite image, and that R has only finitely many Q̄_p-points. Then R[1/p] is reduced, i.e. R[1/p]^red = R[1/p].
items.note: Not in either library and planned nowhere. It is a structural statement about universal deformation rings over a number field with S prime to p: R[1/p] is reduced when there are finitely many Q̄_p-points, all with finite image. The R03.4 node (finite image ⇔ finiteness, KW 2009 Lemma 3.6) is related but different. The proof uses Mazur's representability, trace generation, the fact that no Z_p-extension is unramified at p, and injectivity of inflation in characteristic 0.

items.name: Mazur: the universal deformation ring is complete local Noetherian
items.statement: For S finite (so G_{F,S} satisfies Mazur's p-finiteness condition) and ρ̄ absolutely irreducible, the universal deformation ring R of ρ̄: G_{F,S} → GL_2(k) exists and is a complete local Noetherian W(k)-algebra.
items.note: Not in either library (no deformation functors or rings). Planned: R04.2 verifies the finiteness hypothesis on G_{F,S} and constructs the universal unframed ring under absolute irreducibility, and Schlessinger's criterion is R03.2. Here S contains no place above p, which R04.2's statement allows. External input: Mazur, Deforming Galois representations [58], §1, p. 387

items.name: Mazur: traces generate the universal deformation ring
items.statement: If ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, R is topologically generated over W(k) by the traces of the images of elements of G_{F,S}. Hence the traces generate R[1/p] and all its quotients over W(k) ⊗ Q.
items.note: Not in either library and not planned. The reviewed DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra decomposition lists it under R03.4's remaining coverage ('Carayol's theorem that traces generate the universal deformation ring … not read'). Its gap note assigns such arithmetic inputs to the supplier roadmaps (GlobalGaloisDeformations), which do not state it. The algebraic input is the reconstruction theorem planned in IHG.1 ('over complete local rings when residual absolute irreducibility supplies an actual representation'). External input: Mazur [58], Proposition 4 in §1.8 (printed 'S1.8')

items.name: No nontrivial Z_p^r-extension is unramified at all primes above p
items.statement: Let L be a number field and S a finite set of places of L containing no place above p. Every abelian extension of L with Galois group a finitely generated free Z_p-module that is unramified outside S (in particular unramified at all v | p) is trivial.
items.note: Not in either library. Tau Ceti has TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.finite_rayClassGroup (TauCeti/NumberTheory/NumberField/Global/RayClass/Finite.lean:154) but no global existence theorem. tauceti ClassFieldTheory layers 12–13 plan global existence and 'The ray class field of 𝔪 is the largest abelian extension of conductor dividing 𝔪'. From that, and tameness at S, the statement follows: every finite layer is tamely ramified at S, so it lies in a fixed ray class field. The statement itself is planned nowhere. IntegralIwasawaTheory:L2 ('the finite set of ramified primes' of an arbitrary Z_p-extension) is the closest. External input: class field theory (standard)

items.name: Remark after Lemma 4.14: modular ρ̄ often satisfy its hypotheses
items.statement: If ρ̄: G_{Q,S} → GL_2(k) as in Lemma 4.14 is modular, the hypotheses of Lemma 4.14 (finitely many Q̄_p-points, all with finite image), and hence its conclusion, can often be deduced from the work of Buzzard–Taylor and Buzzard.
items.note: A remark ('one can often deduce'), with no precise statement. Buzzard–Taylor [22] and Buzzard [23] (modularity, hence finite image, of p-adic lifts unramified at p) are in neither library. ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.1 is only a registry of 'weight-one modularity in proved cases' and names neither source (as PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 noted). External input: Buzzard–Taylor [22]; Buzzard [23]

items.name: Finite flat local representation (imaginary quadratic setting)
items.statement: Setting of §5: F is an imaginary quadratic field, p ≥ 3 is a prime unramified in F, and O is the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p with uniformiser ϖ and residue field k. C_O is the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k. Let v|p be a place of F, G_v = Gal(F̄_v/F_v) with inertia subgroup I_v, and A an Artinian local O-algebra. A continuous representation ρ: G_v → GL2(A) is finite flat if there is a finite flat group scheme 𝓕/O_{F_v} such that ρ ≅ 𝓕(F̄_v) as Z_p[G_v]-modules, and det(ρ|I_v) is the cyclotomic character.
items.note: Neither library has finite flat group schemes or GL2(A)-valued Galois representations; Mathlib has only the ℤ_p^×-valued cyclotomicCharacter (a near miss for the determinant condition). The finite-flat local condition is planned across R07.1 (finite flat group schemes and generic fibres, with Raynaud's e < p−1 theorem, which applies since p is unramified in F) and R07.6/R08.4 (the deformation condition and its components), and R02.5 names it. This matches PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 setup-12, where the flat condition at v|ℓ was also marked planned in R08.4/R07.1.

items.name: Ordinary local representation (imaginary quadratic setting)
items.statement: In the setting of finite-flat-local-rep (v|p, A an Artinian local O-algebra), a continuous ρ: G_v → GL2(A) is ordinary if ρ is conjugate in GL2(A) to a representation of the form (εχ1 ∗; 0 χ2), where ε is the cyclotomic character and χ1, χ2 are unramified characters.
items.locator: §5.1, p. 368; §1, p. 301 (the same condition for ρ: G_F → GL2(O), used in Theorems 1.2(1) and 1.3(1))
items.note: Checked on the page image (p. 368): the displayed form is (εχ1 ∗; 0 χ2) with χ1, χ2 unramified, as the item says. No library carrier exists. L7 plans ordinary conditions in every rank (CG's definition is the image of the flag functor, 'conjugate to' an upper-triangular form), and R21.3 plans the GL2 ordinary deformation rings.

items.name: Standing hypotheses on the residual representation ρ̄ (§5)
items.statement: ρ̄: G_F → GL2(k) is a continuous representation such that the restriction ρ̄: G_{F(ζ_p)} → GL2(k) is absolutely irreducible. S(ρ̄) denotes the set of primes of F not dividing p at which ρ̄ is ramified. Assume: (1) det(ρ̄) is the mod-p reduction of the cyclotomic character; (2) ρ̄ is either ordinary or finite flat at each v|p; (3) if x ∈ S(ρ̄), then one of the following holds: (a) ρ̄|I_x is irreducible; (b) ρ̄|I_x is unipotent; (c) ρ̄|D_x is reducible and ρ̄|I_x is of the form ψ ⊕ ψ^{−1}; (d) ρ̄|D_x is irreducible and ρ̄|I_x is reducible, and in that case N_{F/Q}(x) ≢ −1 mod p.
items.note: These standing hypotheses bundle notions planned elsewhere: continuous residual representations (R01.1), inertia and tame characters (R01.2), absolute irreducibility after restriction to F(ζ_p) (R01.4), and the local residual case split at x ∈ S(ρ̄) (R08.2). The finite-flat and ordinary conditions at p are the items above. The IKM extraction classified its analogous setup-12 the same way. Mathlib's modularCyclotomicCharacter, (L ≃+* L) →* (ZMod n)ˣ, is only a near miss for det ρ̄ = ε̄.

items.name: Local types S, P, M, H at primes of S(ρ̄)
items.statement: For x ∈ S(ρ̄), ρ̄|D_x is said to be of type Special (S), Principal (P), Mixed (M) or Harmless (H) 'if [it] is of the type indicated' in deformation conditions (5)–(8): S if ρ̄|I_x is unipotent; P if ρ̄|I_x ≃ ψ ⊕ ψ^{−1}; M if ρ̄|D_x is irreducible and ρ̄|I_x = ψ1 ⊕ ψ2 is reducible; H if ρ̄|I_x is irreducible. The paper does not separate P from M explicitly. Since det ρ̄|I_x is trivial, M-type primes also satisfy the literal P condition. The intended split, matching standing hypotheses (3)(c)/(d), is ρ̄|D_x reducible for P and irreducible for M. Primes of type M are those Diamond [14] calls vexing. Standing hypothesis (3)(d) eliminates the most troublesome of them, namely those with N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ −1 mod p.
items.note: The S/P/M/H classification is the residual case split behind the minimally ramified conditions that R08.2 plans (DDT/Diamond), so it is planned there. R08.2 does not use the names S/P/M/H or the phrase 'vexing'; AutomorphicCongruences L5 mentions only a 'no-vexing-prime' assumption. The blueprint of R08.2 should record this four-way split, including the exclusion N(x) ≡ −1 mod p for type M.

items.name: Unipotent representation
items.statement: For R in C_O and a group G, a representation ρ: G → GL2(R) is unipotent if, after some change of basis, the image of ρ is a subgroup of the group of matrices of the form (1 ∗; 0 1).
items.note: Tau Ceti has TauCeti.upperUnitriangularGroup m R : Subgroup (GL m R), the upper-unitriangular subgroup, which could serve as the carrier. There is no declaration saying 'the image is conjugate into it', so this is a near miss, not a library item. The unipotent-inertia condition (type S) is R08.2's Steinberg/unipotent condition; IKM's steinberg-unipotent item (R^uni) was likewise marked planned in R08.2/L7.

items.name: Fixed-determinant deformation problem minimal outside Q; rings R_Q and R^min
items.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes of O_F containing no prime above p and no prime at which ρ̄ is ramified. For R in C_O, consider lifts ρ: G_F → GL2(R) of ρ̄ with: (1) det(ρ) = ε; (2) if v|p, then (ρ ⊗_R R/m_R^n)|G_v is finite flat or ordinary for all n ≥ 1; (3) if v|p and ρ̄|G_v is finite flat, then (ρ ⊗_R R/m_R^n)|G_v is finite flat for all n ≥ 1; (4) if x ∉ Q ∪ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p}, then ρ|G_x is unramified; (5) S: if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|I_x is unipotent, then ρ|I_x is unipotent; (6) P: if x ∈ S(ρ̄) and ρ̄|I_x ≃ ψ ⊕ ψ^{−1}, then ρ|I_x ≃ ⟨ψ⟩ ⊕ ⟨ψ⟩^{−1}; (7) M: if x ∈ S(ρ̄), ρ̄|D_x is irreducible and ρ̄|I_x = ψ1 ⊕ ψ2 is reducible, then ρ|I_x = ⟨ψ1⟩ ⊕ ⟨ψ2⟩; (8) H: if (x ∈ S(ρ̄), which the paper omits but clearly intends, and) ρ̄|I_x is irreducible, then ρ(I_x) ⥲ ρ̄(I_x). The paper adds '(This also follows automatically from the determinant condition)'. Here ⟨·⟩ denotes the Teichmüller lift (p. 305). In cases (6) and (7), and (8), reduction gives an isomorphism ρ(I_x) ⥲ ρ̄(I_x). The corresponding deformation functor is represented by R_Q. If Q = ∅, R_Q is also written R^min.
items.note: This is a fixed-determinant global problem with standard local conditions, the same shape as IKM's global-deformation-functors, which was marked planned in R04.1/R04.3/R08.2. The Teichmüller lift ⟨·⟩ in conditions (6)–(7) can use Tau Ceti's TauCeti.teichmuller : 𝓀[K]ˣ →* 𝒪[K]ˣ, applied to K = Frac(O), composed with ψ. Nothing else is in the libraries.

items.name: Representability of the deformation functor by R_Q
items.statement: The deformation functor of lifts of ρ̄ satisfying conditions (1)–(8) of deformation-problem-RQ is represented by a complete Noetherian local O-algebra R_Q (in C_O).
items.note: Representability of an unframed fixed-determinant problem with absolutely irreducible ρ̄ is R04.2. That each local condition (1)–(8) is a deformation condition, as in the proof of DDT Theorem 2.41, is part of R04.3 with R08.x. The library audit records no Schlessinger machinery in either library. External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, 'Fermat's Last Theorem' (in Elliptic curves, modular forms & Fermat's last theorem, Int. Press 1997), proof of Theorem 2.41 — ref. [27]

items.name: Local Selmer condition H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) at v|p
items.statement: For v|p, H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) ⊂ H^1(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) is the subspace 'defined as in Sect. 2.4 of [27]' (DDT). The paper gives no other description. It is the local condition L_{Q,v} at v|p in the Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄). The proof of Proposition 5.1 bounds it via DDT Proposition 2.27 (p split), and via CHT Corollary 2.4.3 with the inclusion H^1(G_{F_p}/I_{F_p}, k) ⊂ H^1_f(F_p, adρ̄) ∩ H^1(F_p, k) (p inert). That it contains the tangent space of the finite flat / ordinary conditions (2)–(3) is implicit in that proof but never stated.
items.note: H¹_f is the tangent space of the finite-flat or ordinary condition at v|p, which R02.5 and R08.6 plan explicitly. Neither library has Galois-cohomological Selmer conditions (library audit, D8). External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], §2.4

items.name: Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄) and dual Selmer group H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄) is the kernel of H^1(F, ad⁰ρ̄) → ⊕_x H^1(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄)/L_{Q,x}, where x runs over all primes of F and: L_{Q,x} = H^1(G_x/I_x, (ad⁰ρ̄)^{I_x}) if x ∉ Q ∪ {v|p}; L_{Q,x} = H^1(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄) if x ∈ Q (x ∤ p); L_{Q,v} = H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) if v|p (v ∉ Q). H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) denotes the corresponding dual Selmer group.
items.note: The Selmer group with relaxed conditions at Q, unramified conditions elsewhere and H¹_f at p, together with its dual Selmer group under the annihilators from Poitou–Tate (R02.4), is exactly what R02.5 and L2 plan. There is nothing in the libraries.

items.name: Greenberg–Wiles Euler characteristic formula (as used)
items.statement: For local conditions L = (L_x)_x on H^1(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄), unramified at almost all x, with dual conditions L^⊥: dim_k H^1_L(F, ad⁰ρ̄) − dim_k H^1_{L^⊥}(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) = dim_k H^0(F, ad⁰ρ̄) − dim_k H^0(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) + Σ_x (dim_k L_x − dim_k H^0(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄)), the sum running over all places of F, including the complex place, where L_∞ = 0 and dim_k H^0(C, ad⁰ρ̄) = 3.
items.note: The Greenberg–Wiles formula over a number field, including the complex-place term (L_∞ = 0, h⁰(C, ad⁰) = 3), is the dimension formula R02.5/R02.6 plan, built on R02.3's global Euler characteristic and R02.4's Poitou–Tate. Neither library has it. External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], Theorem 2.19 and Corollary 2.43 (stated there over Q; the number-field version is Wiles 1995, Prop. 1.6)

items.name: Local bound at p: Σ_{v|p}(dim H^1_f − dim H^0) ≤ 2
items.statement: Σ_{v|p} (dim_k H^1_f(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄) − dim_k H^0(F_v, ad⁰ρ̄)) ≤ 2. If p splits in F (F_v = Q_p for both v|p), this follows from DDT Proposition 2.27. If p is inert, the single term dim_k H^1_f(F_p, ad⁰ρ̄) − dim_k H^0(F_p, ad⁰ρ̄) is at most 2. That uses CHT Corollary 2.4.3 and the inclusion H^1(G_{F_p}/I_{F_p}, k) ⊂ H^1_f(F_p, adρ̄) ∩ H^1(F_p, k), where k is viewed as the scalar matrices in adρ̄.
items.note: The split case is DDT Prop. 2.27 over Q_p (flat and ordinary). The inert case uses the Fontaine–Laffaille count of CHT Cor. 2.4.3 over Q_{p²}, planned in L7, together with the passage from ad to ad⁰ through unramified scalar classes. Possible gap: CHT 2.4.3 covers only the Fontaine–Laffaille (finite flat) condition, and the paper gives no argument for ρ̄ ordinary but not finite flat at an inert p. The L7/R08.6 blueprint should supply the ordinary count over Q_{p²}. External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], Proposition 2.27; Clozel–Harris–Taylor [3] (Publ. IHES 108, 2008), Corollary 2.4.3

items.name: Proposition 5.1 (tangent space bound for R_Q)
items.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes of F containing no prime above p and no prime at which ρ̄ is ramified. The reduced tangent space Hom(R_Q/m_O, k[ε]/ε²) of R_Q has dimension at most dim_k H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) − 1 + Σ_{x∈Q} dim_k H^0(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄(1)).
items.note: The bound tangent dim ≤ h¹_Q(ad⁰(1)) − 1 + Σ_{x∈Q} h⁰(F_x, ad⁰(1)) is the Greenberg–Wiles count with the terms at p (≤ 2) and at ∞ (−3); these are the planned R04.3/R02.6 calculations for F imaginary quadratic. I checked the arithmetic: unramified places contribute 0, x ∈ Q contributes h²(F_x, ad⁰) = h⁰(F_x, ad⁰(1)), p contributes ≤ 2 and ∞ contributes −3.

items.name: Tangent bound for a set of Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Suppose that N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p and ρ̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues for each x ∈ Q (Q as in Proposition 5.1). Then H^0(F_x, ad⁰ρ̄) is one-dimensional for each x ∈ Q, and the reduced tangent space of R_Q has dimension at most dim_k H^1_Q(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) − 1 + #Q.
items.note: This is the corollary of Proposition 5.1 for Taylor–Wiles sets. Since N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, ad⁰ρ̄(1) ≅ ad⁰ρ̄ over G_x, and distinct Frobenius eigenvalues give h⁰ = 1. R04.5/R02.6 plan it; neither library has it.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: No formal definition in the paper. Working reading, from the hypotheses on Q in Conjecture A (p. 374) and the sets of Proposition 5.2: a Taylor–Wiles prime (for ρ̄) is a prime x of F with N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p (hence x ∤ p), ρ̄ unramified at x, and ρ̄(Frob_x) with distinct eigenvalues. The sets Q_N of Proposition 5.2 satisfy in addition N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N. The paper calls such primes 'colloquially' Taylor–Wiles primes (p. 370) and uses the term undefined in Lemma 5.6 (p. 375).
items.locator: §5.1, pp. 370–371; §5.3, Conjecture A and Lemma 5.6, pp. 374–375
items.note: R04.5 plans the Taylor–Wiles prime notion over number fields: ρ̄ unramified, N(x) ≡ 1 mod p (mod p^N in Prop. 5.2), distinct eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_x). Neither library has it; Tau Ceti has only the Chebotarev auxiliary prime NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime, an unrelated rational prime ≡ 1 mod n.

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (existence of Taylor–Wiles sets)
items.statement: Let q = dim_k H^1_∅(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) and suppose that ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible. Then q ≥ 1, and for any integer N ≥ 1 there is a set Q_N of primes of F such that: (1) #Q_N = q; (2) N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N for each x ∈ Q_N; (3) for each x ∈ Q_N, ρ̄ is unramified at x and ρ̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues; (4) H^1_{Q_N}(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) = (0). In particular, the reduced tangent space of R_{Q_N} has dimension at most q − 1, and R_{Q_N} is a quotient of a power series ring over O in q − 1 variables.
items.note: This is the Taylor–Wiles set construction under 'ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} absolutely irreducible', exactly R04.5's scope over a number field. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 prop-15-2, which cites Calegari–Geraghty for Taylor–Wiles primes, was marked planned in R04.5/R04.6. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Existence of Chebotarev elements killing dual Selmer classes
items.statement: Assume the setting of §5.1 (F imaginary quadratic, p ≥ 3 unramified in F) and, as in Proposition 5.2, that ρ̄|G_{F(ζ_p)} is absolutely irreducible. Then for each N ≥ 1 and each non-zero class [γ] ∈ H^1_∅(F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)) there is σ ∈ G_F such that: σ acts trivially on F(ζ_{p^N}); ρ̄(σ) has distinct eigenvalues; γ(σ) ∉ (ρ̄(σ) − 1)(ad⁰ρ̄). The paper does not prove this. It says it 'can be established exactly as in the proof of Theorem 2.49 of [27]' (DDT).
items.note: Constructing σ trivial on F(ζ_{p^N}) with ρ̄(σ) regular semisimple and γ(σ) ∉ (ρ̄(σ)−1)ad⁰ρ̄ is the residual-image and cohomology step of DDT Thm 2.49. R04.5 (with the image lemmas of R01.4) plans it. The paper only says it is established 'exactly as in' DDT, which works over Q; the blueprint must redo it over F, including the vanishing of H¹(Gal(F(ζ_{p^N}, ad⁰ρ̄)/F), ad⁰ρ̄(1)). External input: Darmon–Diamond–Taylor [27], proof of Theorem 2.49 ('established exactly as in the proof of Theorem 2.49 of [27]')

items.name: Chebotarev density theorem
items.statement: For a finite Galois extension L/F of number fields and a conjugacy class C ⊂ Gal(L/F), the set of primes of F unramified in L whose Frobenius class is C has Dirichlet density #C/[L:F]; in particular it is infinite.
items.note: Not yet in the libraries at the pinned commits. Tau Ceti has the carrier NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet C (primes 𝔭 unramified in L with artinSymbol = C) and NumberField.exists_auxiliaryPrime, and Mathlib has NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity (definition only) and Dirichlet's theorem over ℚ (Nat.forall_exists_prime_gt_and_eq_mod). The density theorem hasDirichletDensity_frobeniusPrimeSet is absent. It is planned in the existing Tau Ceti Chebotarev roadmap, Layer 10. External input: Standard (Chebotarev); cited by name only

items.name: Arithmetic orbifold Y(K) for Res_{F/Q} PGL(2)
items.statement: A is the ring of adeles of Q and A^∞ the finite adeles; A_F and A_F^∞ are those of F. G := Res_{F/Q} PGL(2) and G_∞ = G(R) = PGL2(C). K_∞ is a maximal compact subgroup of G_∞, with identity component K_∞^0. For a compact open subgroup K of G(A^∞), the arithmetic orbifold is Y(K) := G(Q)\G(A)/K_∞^0 K.
items.note: Y(K) is ALS's X_K for G = Res_{F/Q}PGL₂, with X∞ = PGL₂(ℂ)/PU(2) = ℍ³ (K∞ is connected here). The library audit for ALS.0 finds no adelic quotient or symmetric space beyond the upper half-plane. IKM's arith-manifolds-13-1 (PGL₂/F) was marked planned in ALS.0–ALS.2.

items.name: Remark 5.3: orbifold (group) (co)homology convention
items.statement: If K is sufficiently small (neat), Y(K) is a manifold and a disjoint union of K(π,1) spaces, since each component is a quotient of a contractible space. For a K(π,1)-manifold M there is a functorial isomorphism H^n(π1(M), ⋆) ≃ H^n(M, ⋆) for all n. For orbifolds M = Γ\H with H contractible, the cohomology of M as an orbifold satisfies the same formula. It may differ from the cohomology of the underlying space. Convention: for every K, the cohomology of Y(K) is taken in the orbifold sense, i.e. the cohomology of each component is the (group) cohomology of the corresponding arithmetic lattice. The remark states this only for cohomology; the paper tacitly uses the same convention for the homology groups H•(Y(K), ·) from §5.2.2 on. With this convention, for every finite-index normal subgroup K′ ⊴ K, the map of orbifolds Y(K′) → Y(K) is a covering map with Galois group K/K′.
items.note: The orbifold convention (homology of Γ\ℍ³ taken as group homology of Γ), the K(π,1) property at neat level, and Y(K′) → Y(K) being a K/K′-covering are planned in ALS.0/ALS.1 and AA.4. Mathlib's groupHomology/groupCohomology of an abstract group is the carrier but not the comparison; Tau Ceti has covering-map quotients for free, properly discontinuous actions (library audit ALS.0/AA.4, a near miss).

items.name: Local level subgroups Γ0(v^c), Γ1(v^c), Γ_p(v^c) of PGL2(O_v)
items.statement: For a finite place v of F (ring of integers O_v, uniformiser π_v) and an integer c ≥ 1: Γ0(v^c) = {g ∈ PGL2(O_v) : g ≡ (1 ∗; 0 ∗) mod π_v^c}; Γ1(v^c) = {g ∈ PGL2(O_v) : g ≡ (1 ∗; 0 1) mod π_v^c}; Γ_p(v^c) = {g ∈ PGL2(O_v) : g ≡ (1 ∗; 0 d) mod π_v^c, where d has p-power order}.
items.note: No layer defines Γ₀(v^c), Γ₁(v^c) or the p-power variant Γ_p(v^c) in PGL₂(O_v). ALS and AA plan arbitrary compact open subgroups but no specific level subgroups. The only library relatives are Mathlib's CongruenceSubgroup.Gamma0/Gamma1 : Subgroup SL(2, ℤ), a near miss (ℚ, SL₂, not local or adelic). This matches IKM's level-subgroups-13-4, which was marked missing.

items.name: Levels K_Q ⊂ L_Q and arithmetic quotients Y1(Q), Y0(Q), Y
items.statement: Let S(ρ̄) and Q be as in §5.1. K_Q = ∏_v K_{Q,v} and L_Q = ∏_v L_{Q,v} are the compact open subgroups of G(A^∞) (printed G(A)) with: (1) if v ∈ Q, K_{Q,v} = Γ1(v); (2) if v ∈ Q, L_{Q,v} = Γ0(v); (3) if v ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p} ∪ Q, K_{Q,v} = L_{Q,v} = PGL2(O_v); (4) if v|p, K_{Q,v} = L_{Q,v} = PGL2(O_v) (printed GL2(O_v)) if ρ̄|D_v is finite flat, and Γ0(v) otherwise; (5) if v ∈ S(ρ̄), K_{Q,v} = L_{Q,v} = Γ0(v) if ρ̄ is of type S at v, and Γ_p(v^c) if ρ̄ is of type P, M or H at v, where c is the conductor of ρ̄|D_v. Define Y0(Q) := Y(L_Q) and Y1(Q) := Y(K_Q). Topologically these are finite disjoint unions of finite-volume arithmetic hyperbolic 3-orbifolds. The symbol Y (H1(Y, O), Lemma 5.8, Theorem 5.11) is used in §5 without definition. Context, and the analogous definition in §9 (p. 412), give Y = Y(K_∅) = Y1(∅) = Y0(∅), since K_∅ = L_∅.
items.note: These are levels K_Q ⊂ L_Q tailored to the types of ρ̄ (Γ₀ at type S, Γ_p(v^c) at types P/M/H, Γ₀ or maximal at p, Γ₁/Γ₀ at Q), with Y₀(Q), Y₁(Q) and Y. No layer defines them. Checked on the page image: (4) prints 'GL₂(O_v)' where PGL₂(O_v) is meant, since G = Res PGL₂; the item uses PGL₂, and arXiv v2 p. 56 has the same misprint (sourceIssues E107). See sourceIssues E106 (Γ_p(v^c) does not cut out the minimal type).

items.name: Hecke operators T(g), T_α and diamond operators ⟨α⟩ on H•(Y(K), O)
items.statement: For g ∈ G(A^∞) and a compact open K ⊂ G(A^∞), T(g) on H•(Y(K), O) is the composite H•(Y(K), O) → H•(Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K), O) → H•(Y(K ∩ g^{−1}Kg), O) → H•(Y(K), O). The first map is corestriction (transfer) for the covering Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K) → Y(K), which is always a covering in the orbifold sense. The second is induced by right multiplication by g on G(A), Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K) → Y(K ∩ g^{−1}Kg). The third is the natural map on homology. Hecke operators act on H•(Y(K), O) but need not preserve the homology of connected components. The group of components is isomorphic via det to F^×\A_F^{∞,×}/(A_F^{∞,×})² det(K), the mod-2 reduction of a ray class group. For α ∈ A_F^{∞,×}, T_α := T(g) with g = (α 0; 0 1). If α is a unit at all finite places, ⟨α⟩ := T_α is called a diamond operator; it acts as an automorphism of Y(K) for all the K considered.
items.note: T(g) as transfer, then translation by g, then pushforward is ALS.3's correspondence (orbifold version through AA.4). The component group F^×\A_F^{∞,×}/(A_F^{∞,×})²det K via det is ALS.0's component map, with the idelic/ray-class side in Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 7. Library near misses: Mathlib's HeckeRing/HeckeCosetModule (abstract double-coset module) and Tau Ceti's convolution product, which have no action on homology. IKM's double-coset-13-2 was classified the same way.

items.name: Definition 5.4: Hecke algebras T^an_Q ⊂ T_Q and T = T_∅
items.statement: T^an_Q is the O-subalgebra of End_O H1(Y1(Q), O) generated by the Hecke endomorphisms T_α for all α ∈ A_F^{∞,×} that are trivial at the primes in Q ∪ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p}. T_Q is the O-algebra generated by the same operators together with T_α for α non-trivial at places in Q. If Q = ∅, write T = T_∅ for T_Q. These rings are commutative. If ε ∈ O_F^× is a global unit, T_ε acts as the identity. If a ⊆ O_F is an ideal prime to the level, the Hecke operator T_a is T_α for any α ∈ A_F^{∞,×} that represents a and is 1 at each component dividing the level. In particular, for a prime x, T_x is uniquely defined when x is prime to the level, but not when x divides the level.
items.note: T^an_Q, T_Q and T_∅ are the O-subalgebras of End_O H₁ generated by specified double-coset operators, an instance of IHG.2's image algebras, with the operators from ALS.3 and the T_v normalisation from IHG.3. IKM's hecke-algebra-13-3 was marked planned the same way. Two caveats: T_Q adds the Taylor–Wiles-level operators (U_x, ⟨α⟩ at x ∈ Q), whose well-definedness modulo m is the separate missing item rmk-5-7-Ux; and IKM marked its fuller TW-level algebra with maximal ideals (hecke-TSigmaQ-13-6) missing. Only the abstract Hecke ring is in the libraries.

items.name: Definition 5.5: Eisenstein and non-Eisenstein maximal ideals
items.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of T_Q, and let T_{Q,m} be the completion, a local ring that is finite (but not necessarily flat) over O. m is Eisenstein if T_λ − 2 ∈ m for all but finitely many primes λ that split completely in some fixed abelian extension of F. m is non-Eisenstein if it is not Eisenstein.
items.note: No layer defines Eisenstein or non-Eisenstein maximal ideals in this sense (T_λ − 2 ∈ m for almost all λ split completely in a fixed abelian extension). ALS.4 only warns that 'the phrase non-Eisenstein alone is not a proof of vanishing for arbitrary groups', and ModularCurvesPartII R14.3 uses the word for modular curves. IKM defines non-Eisenstein through ρ̄_m instead (inside hecke-algebra-13-3).

items.name: Maximal ideal associated to ρ̄
