items.statement: A maximal ideal m of T_Q is associated to ρ̄ if T_λ − Trace(ρ̄(Frob_λ)) ∈ m for each prime λ ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {v|p} of F.
items.note: The condition that m is associated to ρ̄ (T_λ − tr ρ̄(Frob_λ) ∈ m away from S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {v|p}) is planned only for other settings. GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 ('Choose the modular residual representation and construct the localised finite-level Hecke module') is for Hilbert/quaternionic levels over totally real fields, and nothing covers Bianchi homology. Neither library has it.

items.name: Conjecture A (existence of Galois representations; part (1))
items.statement: Conjecture (assumed, not proved). Let Q be a (finite) set of primes v of F such that N(v) ≡ 1 mod p, ρ̄ is unramified at v, and ρ̄(Frob_v) has distinct eigenvalues. Let m be a maximal ideal of T_Q that is non-Eisenstein and associated to ρ̄. Then there exists a continuous Galois representation ρ = ρ_m: G_F → GL2(T_{Q,m}) with the following property, together with properties (2)–(4) (conj-A-2-types-S-P, conj-A-3-TW-primes, conj-A-4-at-p). (1) If λ ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ Q ∪ {v|p} is a prime of F, then ρ is unramified at λ, and the characteristic polynomial of ρ(Frob_λ) is X² − T_λ X + N_{F/Q}(λ) ∈ T_{Q,m}[X].
items.note: Conjecture A, the existence of ρ_m over T_{Q,m} for torsion Bianchi classes, is not stated by any layer. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds Scholze's infrastructure but says it is 'not an additional requirement to formalize its final Galois-representation theorem'; IHG.1 (reconstruction) and IHG.5 (nilpotent descent) are only ingredients. This matches IKM's conj-A, which was marked missing. It must enter as an explicit Prop-valued hypothesis, never as a conclusion.

items.name: Conjecture A(2): local behaviour at primes of S(ρ̄)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Conjecture A, the representation ρ_m satisfies: (2) if v ∈ S(ρ̄), then (a) if ρ̄|D_v is of type S, ρ_m|I_v is unipotent; (b) if ρ̄|D_v is of type P, so that ρ̄|I_v ≅ ψ ⊕ ψ^{−1}, then ρ_m|I_v ≅ ⟨ψ⟩ ⊕ ⟨ψ⟩^{−1}.
items.note: This is part (2) of the missing Conjecture A: local behaviour at types S and P. It covers only types S and P; for types M and H, minimality of ρ_m must come from det = ε (see lemma-5-6). Nothing in the atlas states it.

items.name: Conjecture A(3): local behaviour at Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Conjecture A: (3) if v ∈ Q, the operators T_α for α ∈ F_v^× ⊂ A_F^{∞,×} are invertible. Let φ be the character of D_v = Gal(F̄_v/F_v) that corresponds, by local class field theory, to the homomorphism F_v^× → T_{Q,m}^× sending x to T_x. By assumption, φ mod m is unramified, so it factors through F_v^×/O_v^× ≃ Z and φ(Frob_v) mod m is well defined. Assume that φ(Frob_v) ≢ ±1 mod m. Then ρ_m|D_v ∼ φε ⊕ φ^{−1}.
items.note: This is part (3) of the missing Conjecture A: ρ_m|D_v ∼ φε ⊕ φ⁻¹ at Taylor–Wiles primes, with φ attached by local class field theory to α ↦ T_α. Checked on the page image (p. 375): the conclusion is φε ⊕ φ⁻¹. Local CFT is Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 7 (planned), but the conjecture itself is unplanned.

items.name: Conjecture A(4): local behaviour at p
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Conjecture A: (4) if v|p and ρ̄|D_v is finite flat, then ρ_m|D_v is finite flat (every ρ_m ⊗ T_{Q,m}/m^n is finite flat); and if ρ̄|D_v is ordinary, then ρ_m|D_v is ordinary.
items.note: This is part (4) of the missing Conjecture A: local–global compatibility at p. Misprint (checked on the image, p. 375, and in arXiv v2 p. 58): the first clause is printed 'If v|p, then ρ̄|D_v is finite flat'. The intended statement, used in §5.4 via condition (3) of §5.1, is 'if ρ̄|D_v is finite flat then ρ_m|D_v is finite flat'; the item uses the corrected reading. See sourceIssues E115 (misprinted first clause of (4)).

items.name: Deformation minimal outside Q
items.statement: A deformation ρ_Q of ρ̄ is minimal outside Q if it arises from a quotient of the ring R_Q of §5.1, i.e. it is the pushforward of the universal deformation along some homomorphism R_Q → A.
items.note: 'Minimal outside Q' means that the deformation satisfies conditions (1)–(8), equivalently that it is classified by a map R_Q → A. This is the universal property of R_Q, planned in R04.2 for problems defined in R04.1. It is a named convenience, not new mathematics.

items.name: Lemma 5.6 (Galois representation to T_{Q,m} minimal outside Q)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A. Assume that there exists a maximal ideal m of T_Q associated to ρ̄, and that Q consists entirely of Taylor–Wiles primes. Then there exists a representation ρ_Q: G_F → GL2(T_{Q,m}) whose traces generate T_{Q,m} and which is a minimal deformation of ρ̄ outside Q with cyclotomic determinant.
items.note: This lemma is conditional on the missing Conjecture A. Its proof uses Conjecture A(3) and Hensel's lemma to put the T_α for α | Q in the trace subalgebra. Conjecture A(2) covers only types S and P, so minimality at M and H primes must follow from det = ε: the paper says so for H, and for M the same argument seems to need N(x) ≢ −1 mod p, i.e. hypothesis (3)(d). That step is not written in the paper and I have not verified it. The GL₂/totally-real analogue is R22.1, which does not cover this setting. See sourceIssues E111 (needs U_v ≢ ±1 mod m for v ∈ Q).

items.name: Comparison maps T^an_Q → T_∅ and T^an_Q ↪ T_Q; pulled-back ideal m∅
items.statement: Let m∅ be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_∅. There are natural homomorphisms T^an_Q → T^an = T_∅ and T^an_Q ↪ T_Q. The first is induced by the map H1(Y1(Q), O) → H1(Y, O), the second is the natural inclusion. The paper asserts that H1(Y1(Q), O) → H1(Y, O) is surjective, 'an immediate consequence of the interpretation of these groups in terms of group cohomology [read: group homology, i.e. abelianisations of the arithmetic lattices ⊗ O] and the fact that the abelianization of PSL2(F_x) is trivial for N(x) > 3'. The ideal m∅ pulls back to an ideal of T^an_Q, also denoted m∅. It may give rise to several maximal ideals m of T_Q.
items.note: Change-of-level maps on homology are generic ALS.3/ALS.6 material, but no layer states the surjectivity H₁(Y₁(Q), O) → H₁(Y, O) or the induced T^an_Q → T_∅. The group-theoretic input is in Mathlib as SL2Simple.PSL_commutator_eq_top: commutator PSL(2,F) = ⊤ if some a ≠ 0 has a² ≠ 1, i.e. #F ≥ 4, so N(x) > 3. The paper leaves implicit that the image of Γ in PGL₂(F_x) contains PSL₂(F_x) with abelian quotient of order ≤ 2, which dies with O-coefficients because p is odd.

items.name: Remark 5.7: operators T_x and U_x
items.statement: If x ∉ Q ∪ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p} is prime, there is an operator T_x ∈ T^an_Q. If x ∈ Q, U_x := T_{π_x}, where π_x ∈ A_F^{∞,×} is (by abuse of notation) the adele that is trivial away from x and equals the uniformiser π_x at x. This operator is well defined only up to a diamond operator ⟨α⟩ with α ∈ O_x^× ⊂ A_F^{∞,×}. By Conjecture A, however, its image modulo m is well defined, because the associated character φ is unramified.
items.note: U_x = T_{π_x} is an ALS.3 double-coset operator, but its well-definedness only up to ⟨α⟩, α ∈ O_x^×, and the well-definedness of its image mod m (conditional on Conjecture A) are Taylor–Wiles-level statements that no layer plans. The analogues are planned only in R22.2 (totally real) and PA.4 (CM fields); IKM's analogue hecke-TSigmaQ-13-6 was marked missing.

items.name: Lemma 5.8 (no new classes at Taylor–Wiles level)
items.statement: Let m∅ be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of T_∅. Suppose that for each x ∈ Q, N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p and the polynomial X² − T_x X + N_{F/Q}(x) ∈ T_∅[X] has distinct roots modulo m∅. Let m be the maximal ideal of T_Q containing m∅ and U_x − α_x for each x ∈ Q, where α_x is a chosen root of X² − T_x X + 1 mod m. Then there is an isomorphism of T^an_{Q,m∅}-modules H1(Y0(Q), O)_m ⥲ H1(Y, O)_{m∅}.
items.note: This is the Bianchi 'no new classes at Taylor–Wiles level' isomorphism H₁(Y₀(Q), O)_m ≅ H₁(Y, O)_{m∅}, proved 'as in Lemma 3.5' through H¹(·, K/O) and the universal coefficient theorem. The totally-real analogue is GL2ModularityLifting R22.2 ('prove the required freeness/control statement ... specialisation back to the original level'); nothing plans it for PGL₂ over an imaginary quadratic field.

items.name: Δ_Q-covers, local systems, T^univ and the maximal ideal m
items.statement: The covering Y1(Q) → Y0(Q) is Galois with group Δ_Q := ∏_{x∈Q} (O_F/x)^×. A finitely generated O[Δ_Q]-module μ gives rise to a local system on Y0(Q). T^univ is the polynomial O-algebra, analogous to the one in §3.2.3, generated by symbols for the Hecke endomorphisms T_α (α trivial at the primes in Q ∪ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p}) and U_x (x ∈ Q). It acts on the homology H_i(Y0(Q), μ) and on the Borel–Moore homology H_i^{BM}(Y0(Q), μ). After a choice of eigenvalue mod m for U_x for each x dividing Q, m∅ gives rise to a maximal ideal m of T^univ. For a quotient Δ of Δ_Q, Y_Δ(Q) → Y0(Q) is the corresponding Galois cover. If Δ is a p-power-order quotient, O[Δ] is a local ring, and Shapiro's lemma gives H1(Y0(Q), O[Δ]) ≅ H1(Y_Δ(Q), O).
items.note: The generic pieces are planned: local systems from O[Δ]-modules (ALS.1), Hecke operators and T^univ on H and H^BM (ALS.3, IHG.2), finite covers (AA.4) and finite-cover descent (ALS.6). The specific Galois cover Y₁(Q) → Y₀(Q) with group Δ_Q = ∏(O_F/x)^× depends on the missing Γ₀/Γ₁ levels, and the TW-level ideal m on the missing U_x item. Shapiro's lemma is in Mathlib as groupHomology.indIso (H_n(G, Ind_S^G A) ≅ H_n(S, A)), which gives H₁(Y₀(Q), O[Δ]) ≅ H₁(Y_Δ(Q), O) componentwise under the orbifold convention.

items.name: Lemma 5.9(1) (vanishing of H_0 and H_3 at non-Eisenstein m)
items.statement: Let Δ be a p-power-order quotient of Δ_Q, let m ⊂ T^univ be the maximal ideal determined by a non-Eisenstein m∅ and choices of U_x-eigenvalues, and let μ be a finitely generated O[Δ]-module. Then H_i(Y0(Q), μ)_m = (0) for i = 0, 3.
items.note: No layer states that H₀ and H₃ vanish after localising at a non-Eisenstein m. Gap, recorded as sourceIssues E116: the proof asserts H₃(Y₀(Q), k) = 0, but under the orbifold convention of Remark 5.3 this is group homology of lattices that can contain 3-torsion at non-neat level, so for p = 3 it need not vanish unless one adds neatness or an Eisenstein argument. For p ≥ 5, finite subgroups of PGL₂(F) have order divisible only by 2 and 3, so the claim holds.

items.name: Lemma 5.9(2) (H_2 is p-torsion free)
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 5.9: if μ is a p-torsion-free finitely generated O[Δ]-module, then H_2(Y0(Q), μ)_m is p-torsion free.
items.note: No layer states it. Misprints in the proof (sourceIssues E117; checked on the p. 377 image): it writes 'H²(Y₀(Q), μ)_m[ϖ] = 0' for the homology group H₂, and the vanishing it uses is H₃(Y₀(Q), μ/ϖ)_m (part (1) applied to μ/ϖ), not H₃(Y₀(Q), μ)_m. See sourceIssues E116 (H_3 vanishing needs localisation; p = 3 open).

items.name: Lemma 5.9(3) (interior homology = Borel–Moore homology at m)
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma 5.9: for all i, the natural map H_i(Y0(Q), μ)_m → H_i^{BM}(Y0(Q), μ)_m is an isomorphism.
items.note: The boundary long exact sequence and the vanishing of localized boundary homology are what ALS.4 plans; IKM treated the same step inside prop-13-6 as planned in ALS.4. The Bianchi instance (cusps are tori, and the Hecke action is through algebraic Grössencharacters) is in boundary-hecke-eisenstein, and the non-Eisenstein condition itself is the missing def-5-5-eisenstein. Neither library has the boundary triangle (library audit ALS.4).

items.name: Hecke action on boundary homology is Eisenstein
items.statement: (Proof of Lemma 5.9(3).) The Hecke operators act on the boundary ∂Y0(Q) in the evident topological way (see p. 107 of [63]). The cusps are given by tori, specifically elliptic curves with CM by some order in O_F. Since the cohomology with constant coefficients of tori is torsion free, the case μ = k reduces to μ = O and then to μ = K. The paper claims, citing [64] with Sect. 2.10 of [65] as explicit reference, that the action of T^univ on the homology of the cusps in characteristic zero is given by a sum of algebraic Grössencharacters of F, and that such a representation is Eisenstein by class field theory. Hence H_i(∂Y0(Q), μ)_m = 0 for all i.
items.note: For PGL₂/F the Borel–Serre boundary components are 2-tori (nilmanifold fibres over finite Levi quotients), and the Hecke action on their homology is via parabolic induction from algebraic Grössencharacters. ALS.2/ALS.4 plan this, with the characters from Tau Ceti GlobalNumberFields Layer 10; turning them into Galois characters, which gives 'Eisenstein', uses global CFT (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory Layer 11). The explicit computation is cited to Harder [64] and Berger [65, §2.10]; neither library has any of it. External input: G. Harder, Eisenstein cohomology of arithmetic groups. The case GL2, Invent. Math. 89 (1987) 37–118 [64]; explicit reference: T. Berger, An Eisenstein ideal for imaginary quadratic fields, PhD thesis, Michigan 2005, §2.10 [65]; Hecke action on the boundary: R. Taylor, PhD thesis, Princeton 1988, p. 107 [63]

items.name: Hecke-equivariant Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence for Y_Δ(Q) → Y0(Q)
items.statement: For Δ a p-power-order quotient of Δ_Q and S = O[Δ], there is a Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H_i(Δ, H_j(Y0(Q), S)) = Tor_i^S(H_j(Y0(Q), S), O) ⟹ H_{i+j}(Y0(Q), O). T^univ acts on it compatibly with the differentials, by the argument of Proposition 3.8, so it may be localised at m. The same holds with S ⊗_O K and K coefficients.
items.locator: §5.3.1, proof of Proposition 5.10, p. 378; §5.4, proof of Theorem 5.11(b), p. 380
items.note: The spectral sequence Tor_i^S(H_j(Y₀(Q), S), O) ⇒ H_{i+j}(Y₀(Q), O) for S = O[Δ] is P7's Tor spectral sequence for C ⊗^L_S O, applied to the finite cover (ALS.6). The Hecke-equivariance needed to localise at m is planned through chain-level Hecke actions (ALS.3, IHG.2). Mathlib has group homology but no Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence; the library audit finds only low-degree inflation–restriction.

items.name: Poincaré duality on Y0(Q) with K coefficients
items.statement: dim_K H_2(Y0(Q), K)_m = dim_K H_1^{BM}(Y0(Q), K)_{m*}, where m* is the dual maximal ideal. Since G = PGL(2), m* is identified with m.
items.note: dim H₂(K)_m = dim H₁^BM(K)_{m*} is rational Poincaré–Lefschetz duality with Hecke adjoints. For PGL₂, T(g)* = T(g⁻¹) and g⁻¹ is a scalar multiple of an element of the same double coset, which gives m* = m. With K-coefficients the orbifold stabilisers do not matter. Planned in ALS.5 (Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 6 for manifold duality); not in the libraries. External input: Standard (Poincaré–Lefschetz duality for the Borel–Serre compactification, rational coefficients); not cited

items.name: Proposition 5.10 (the Taylor–Wiles-level homology is balanced)
items.statement: Let Δ be a p-power-order quotient of Δ_Q and let m ⊂ T^univ be as above (from a non-Eisenstein m∅). The O[Δ]-module M := H1(Y0(Q), O[Δ])_m ≅ H1(Y_Δ(Q), O)_m is balanced in the sense of Definition 2.2. That is, with S = O[Δ], d_S(M) = dim_k M ⊗_S k − dim_k Tor_1^S(M, k) ≥ 0.
items.note: The notion 'balanced' (d_S(M) ≥ 0, CG Def. 2.2) is planned in the reviewed node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:R03.5/balanced-modules-and-module-patching. Showing that H₁(Y₀(Q), O[Δ])_m is balanced is the arithmetic input, specific to ℓ₀ = 1 Bianchi homology, and no layer plans it. Its proof combines Lemma 5.9, the Hecke-equivariant Hochschild–Serre and Poincaré duality.

items.name: The maximal ideal m∅ attached to ρ̄ (minimal level, trivial weight)
items.statement: m∅ is the ideal of T_∅ generated by ϖ and T_λ − Trace(ρ̄(Frob_λ)) for all primes λ ∉ S(ρ̄) ∪ {v|p} of F. Hypothesis: m∅ is a proper ideal of T_∅, i.e. ρ̄ is 'modular' of minimal level and trivial weight. Then T_∅/m∅ ↪ k, so m∅ is maximal. Since ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible, m∅ is non-Eisenstein by Chebotarev density.
items.note: The ideal m∅ = (ϖ, T_λ − tr ρ̄(Frob_λ)) and the hypothesis that ρ̄ is 'modular of minimal level and trivial weight' for Bianchi homology are not planned anywhere; R22.1 does the analogous choice only for totally real/quaternionic settings. Non-Eisensteinness follows from absolute irreducibility and Chebotarev (Tau Ceti Chebotarev Layer 10, planned).

items.name: The homomorphism φ: R^min → T_{m∅}
items.statement: Assume Conjecture A for m∅ (Q = ∅). Then there is a continuous ρ_{m∅}: G_F → GL2(T_{m∅}) with the properties of Conjecture A. By the definition of m∅ and Chebotarev density, ρ_{m∅} mod m∅ ≅ ρ̄. Properties (1)–(4) of Conjecture A imply that ρ_{m∅} is a deformation of ρ̄ of the type classified by R^min. This gives a homomorphism φ: R^min → T_{m∅} under which the universal deformation pushes forward to ρ_{m∅}. By Conjecture A(1), φ: R^min → T_{∅,m∅} is surjective.
items.note: The map φ: R^min → T_{m∅}, and its surjectivity from Conjecture A(1), are conditional on the missing Conjecture A. The unconditional analogue is GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 ('construct the deformation-to-Hecke map and prove surjectivity from generation by Frobenius/Hecke data'), which is planned only for Hilbert/quaternionic Hecke modules.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles patching data for Theorem 5.11
items.statement: The data fed into Proposition 2.3. R := R^min and H := H1(Y, O)_{m∅}. q := dim_k H^1_∅(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄(1)), with q ≥ 1 by Proposition 5.2. Δ∞ := Z_p^q, Δ_N := (Z/p^N Z)^q and S_N := O[Δ_N]. R∞ := O⟦x1, …, x_{q−1}⟧. For each N ≥ 1: Q_N is a set of primes satisfying Proposition 5.2, with a fixed surjection φ̃_N: R∞ ↠ R_{Q_N}; φ_N is the composite R∞ ↠ R_{Q_N} ↠ R^min. Δ_{Q_N} := ∏_{x∈Q_N} (O_F/x)^×, with a chosen surjection Δ_{Q_N} ↠ Δ_N and corresponding Galois cover Y_{Δ_N}(Q_N) → Y0(Q_N). H_N := H1(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_N), O)_m, where m is the ideal of T_{Q_N} containing m∅ and U_x − α_x for each x ∈ Q_N, for some choice of α_x. H_N is naturally an O[Δ_N] = S_N-module. It is an R∞-module via φ̃_N and the surjection R_{Q_N} ↠ T_{Q_N,m} given by Conjecture A, hence an R∞ ⊗_O S_N-module.
items.note: The abstract Proposition 2.3 is planned in the reviewed node R03.5/balanced-modules-and-module-patching. Its arithmetic instantiation for Bianchi homology, with the data (R^min, H, Q_N, Δ_N, S_N, H_N) and the checks (5a)–(5c), is not planned (R22.2/R22.3 are totally real). Misprint (checked on the p. 379 image and in arXiv v2 p. 61): 'q := dim_k H¹_∅(G_F, ad⁰ρ̄)' should read ad⁰ρ̄(1), as in Prop. 5.2; the item uses the corrected form. R∞ = O⟦x₁,…,x_{q−1}⟧ is one of the known bracket defects (sourceIssues E15). See sourceIssues E120 (q must use ad⁰ρ̄(1)).

items.name: Theorem 5.11 (minimal R = T for PGL(2) over an imaginary quadratic field, assuming Conjecture A)
items.statement: Let F be an imaginary quadratic field, p ≥ 3 a prime unramified in F, and ρ̄: G_F → GL2(k) satisfying the standing hypotheses of §5.1. Let T_∅ act on H1(Y, O), Y = Y(K_∅), and let m∅ ⊂ T_∅ be the ideal attached to ρ̄. Assume: (1) the ideal m∅ is a proper ideal of T_∅; (2) Conjecture A holds for all Q. Then the map φ: R^min → T_{m∅} = T_{∅,m∅} is an isomorphism, and T_{∅,m∅} acts freely on H1(Y, O)_{m∅}.
items.note: Theorem 5.11, minimal R = T for PGL₂ over imaginary quadratic F conditional on Conjecture A, is planned nowhere. GL2ModularityLifting covers only totally real fields in defect 0 (KW II). The IKM brief records that the positive-defect Hecke side for PGL₂/F overlaps this extraction and should be imported from it.

items.name: Multiplicity one for PGL(2)/F (as used)
items.statement: External input, cited and not proved: multiplicity one for PGL(2)/F. Each cuspidal automorphic representation of PGL2(A_F) occurs with multiplicity one; with strong multiplicity one, distinct such π have distinct Hecke eigensystems. The paper (p. 380) uses it to assert: 'If H1(Y, O)_{m∅} ⊗ Q ≠ 0, then … the multiplicity μ for H as a T_{∅,m∅}-module is one.' Caveat: the rank μ of the free module H1(Y, O)_{m∅} equals dim π_f^{K_∅} for any contributing π. It is 1 only if dim π_v^{K_{∅,v}} = 1 at every v. That holds at S-type, unramified and p-adic places, but fails in general at primes of type P, M or H, where K_{∅,v} = Γ_p(v^c) (see sourceIssues E121). The claim is justified when S(ρ̄) contains no prime of type P, M or H.
items.note: To get μ = 1 one needs global multiplicity one (R16.4), dim π_v^{K_v} ≤ 1 at the chosen levels (R16.2's newvector theorem), and the identification of H₁(Y, ℂ)_m with cuspidal cohomological π (AS.5, ALS.5 comparison). All are planned; the paper invokes them only by name. Library near miss: Tau Ceti HeckeRing.GL2.cuspFormsNewEigenspace_le_span_singleton, classical newform multiplicity one over ℚ. See sourceIssues E121 (μ = 1 fails at type P, M, H primes). External input: Standard (multiplicity one for automorphic representations of PGL(2)/F, with local newform theory at the chosen level); invoked by name only

items.name: §5.5: why PGL rather than GL; class-group twists and the alternative GL construction
items.statement: (§5.5, discussion, not a theorem.) Why PGL rather than GL: suppose p divides the class number of F. For example, suppose ρ̄ is modular of level one, its minimal fixed-determinant deformation ring is O, and Cl(O_F) ≅ Z/pZ. Then the minimal Hecke ring T_m is expected to be O[Z/pZ] rather than O, because the Hecke algebra sees twists by class-group characters of p-power order. So R^min → T_m is not surjective. This cannot be fixed by a choice of level structure, since the level only sees ramification. One fix is to work with PGL. The paper also sketches another fix for GL, not carried out: replace Y, Y0(Q), Y1(Q) by their quotients by Cl_p(O_F) := Cl(O_F) ⊗ Z_p. At Y the diamond operators act via an extension of Cl(O_F) by a group of prime-to-p order, so there is a canonical splitting and a canonical quotient Y/Cl_p(O_F). For p odd, Cl_p(O_F) acts freely on components, so this quotient is a subset of the components of Y. In the example, the Hecke ring there (generated by T_α with the image of (α) in Cl(O_F) of prime-to-p order) is O. This is not canonical enough: on Y1(Q) the diamond operators act through a group with p-Sylow RCl_p(Q) = RCl(Q) ⊗ Z_p, which surjects onto Cl_p(O_F) with no natural section. The Taylor–Wiles method seems to apply if one restricts to Taylor–Wiles primes x for which RCl_p(Q) → Cl_p(O_F) splits, a further Chebotarev condition (x splits completely in a metabelian extension of F). Explicitly, assume p is prime to the order of the unit group of F, and let a ∈ Cl_p(O_F) have p-power order h with a^h = (α). A necessary condition on x is α^{(N(x)−1)/p} ≡ 1 mod x, equivalently x splits completely in F(α^{1/p}, ζ_p). The paper instead imposes det(ρ̄) cyclotomic, natural for elliptic curves.
items.note: §5.5 is an expository sketch, not a theorem: why PGL is used, the expected T_m ≅ O[ℤ/p] for GL when p | h_F, and a heuristic ('It seems that the Taylor–Wiles method still applies') with the metabelian splitting condition α^{(N(x)−1)/p} ≡ 1 mod x. Nothing plans it. The Kummer-theoretic equivalence with x splitting completely in F(α^{1/p}, ζ_p) would use Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layer 9 (Kummer theory). See sourceIssues E124 (the exponent should use h, not p).

items.name: Remark 5.14: l0 for PGL(2) over a number field; no solvable base change when l0 = 1
items.statement: Remark 5.14. Solvable base change is a tool 'conspicuously absent when l0 = 1'. For GL(2) over totally real fields one may pass to a finite solvable extension to avoid issues such as level lowering ([67]). But if F is imaginary quadratic, every non-trivial extension H/F has at least two complex places ('two pairs of complex places'). The invariant l0 = rank(G) − rank(K) for PGL(2)/H is then at least 2, and more precisely equals the number of complex places of H. Hence, when l0 = 1, the techniques are 'mostly confined' to the approach of Wiles, Taylor–Wiles and Diamond [1, 2, 26].
items.note: No layer defines ℓ₀ = rank G − rank K or computes it for PGL₂/H. The elementary half follows from Mathlib: NumberField.isTotallyComplex_of_algebra, NumberField.IsTotallyComplex.nrRealPlaces_eq_zero and NumberField.InfinitePlace.card_add_two_mul_card_eq_rank give r₂(H) = [H:ℚ]/2 ≥ 2 for H ⊋ F with F imaginary quadratic. The ℓ₀ formula and the 'no solvable base change when ℓ₀ = 1' consequence are the missing parts.

items.name: Theorem 5.16 (conditional modularity lifting for GL_n over an arbitrary number field)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let F/Q be an arbitrary number field and n a positive integer. Let p > n be a prime unramified in F. Let O be the ring of integers of a finite extension of Q_p, with uniformiser ϖ and residue field k. Let r: G_F → GL_n(O) be a continuous Galois representation unramified outside a finite set of primes, and let r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) be its reduction mod ϖ. Suppose that: (1) if v|p, r|D_v is crystalline; (2) if v|p, then gr^i(r ⊗_{Z_p} B_DR)^{D_v} = 0 unless i ∈ {0, 1, …, n − 1}, in which case it is free of rank 1 over O ⊗_{Z_p} F_v; (3) the restriction of r̄ to F(ζ_p) is absolutely irreducible, and the field F(ad⁰(r̄)) does not contain F(ζ_p); (4) r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big in the sense of [CHT, Definition 2.5.1]; (5) if v|∞ is a real place of F, then r|G_{F_v} is odd; (6) if r is ramified at a prime x ∤ p, then r|I_x is unipotent, and if moreover r̄ is unramified at x, then N(x) ≡ 1 mod p; (7) det(r) = ε^{n(n−1)/2}; (8) either (a) there is a cuspidal automorphic representation π0 of GL_n(A_F) such that π_{0,v} has trivial infinitesimal character for all v|∞, π0 has good reduction at all v|p, and the p-adic Galois representation r_p(π0) satisfies condition (6) and r̄_p(π0) = r̄; or (b) r̄ is Serre modular of minimal level N(r̄), and r is ramified only at primes at which r̄ is ramified. Then r is modular: there exists a regular algebraic cusp form π for GL_n(A_F) with trivial infinitesimal character such that L(r, s) = L(π, s).
items.locator: Part 2, Theorem 5.16, pp. 383–384; deduced from Theorem 9.19, §9.5, p. 424 (no deduction written)
items.note: No layer states a GL_n modularity lifting theorem over an arbitrary number field conditional on Conjecture B. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure builds infrastructure for CM fields (its README names Calegari–Geraghty as 'primary supporting source' but says ACC+ 'supplies its unconditional specialized arithmetic inputs rather than making the general CG conjectures true'), and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.2 assembles ACC+'s unconditional potential automorphy. This cluster only sees the statement; the proof is §9 (Theorem 9.19). The paper writes no deduction of Theorem 5.16 from Theorem 9.19 ('This theorem will follow immediately from Theorem 9.19'). The design job must supply three steps: produce the maximal ideal m with r̄_m ≅ r̄ from (8a) or (8b), check that r is a deformation of type S, and pass from the point of R_S given by r to a cuspidal π using near faithfulness and the boundary vanishing of Conjecture B(4)(b). See sourceIssues E125 and E126 (misprints in hypotheses (6) and (4)) and E203 (hypotheses weaker than Theorem 9.19 uses).

items.name: Group rings S_N, S∞ and the quotient conventions of §6
items.statement: Fix an integer q ≥ 0. For N ≥ 0 put Δ_N := (Z/p^N Z)^q and S_N := O[Δ_N], the group ring of the finite p-group Δ_N. It is a local, finite free O-algebra with maximal ideal m_{S_N} and residue field k. Put S∞ := O⟦(Z_p)^q⟧, the completed group ring. For M ≥ N ≥ 0 and each ideal I of O, S_N/I (in particular O/I = S_0/I) is regarded as a quotient of S_M via the quotient map Δ_M ↠ Δ_N and reduction modulo I. S∞ ↠ S_N is the natural surjection, and a_N := ker(S∞ ↠ S_N). The augmentation ideal of S_N (resp. S∞) is the kernel of the O-algebra map to O that sends every group element to 1.
items.locator: §6 introduction, p. 384; §6.1, Theorem 6.3 and its proof, pp. 386–387
items.note: The finite group rings and their augmentation ideals exist in the libraries (Mathlib MonoidAlgebra; Tau Ceti's augmentation with kernel spanned by g − 1). The completed group ring S∞, the quotient conventions S_M ↠ S_N/I and a_N are planned in P8 (whose reviewed node uses exactly S_∞ = O[[(Z_p)^q]], S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q]); completed group rings in general are planned in PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1. See sourceIssues E14 (S_N is reduced, not 'non-reduced').

items.name: Codimension of a module over a Noetherian local ring
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring of Krull dimension n and M a finitely generated S-module. Define codim(M) := n − dim(M), where dim(M) = dim Supp(M) = dim S/Ann_S(M). For a bounded complex P of S-modules, H*(P) := ⊕_i H^i(P), so codim(H*(P)) = n − max_i dim H^i(P). A module ‘of codimension l0’ (§6 introduction) is one with codim = l0.
items.locator: §6 introduction, p. 384; proof of Lemma 6.2, p. 385; Notation, p. 306 (for H*(P))
items.note: No library declaration defines codim(M) = dim S − dim M; Mathlib has the two ingredients (Module.supportDim, equal to dim S/Ann(M) for finite M, and ringKrullDim). P9 plans codimension of support over a regular local base and its node states CG Lemma 6.2 with codim H*(P). Note that with Mathlib's convention supportDim(0) = ⊥ the codimension of the zero module is +∞, so every use needs M ≠ 0.

items.name: Perfect complexes (paper's conventions)
items.statement: Notation (p. 306): for a ring R, a perfect complex of R-modules is a bounded complex of finitely generated projective R-modules. For a bounded complex P, H*(P) := ⊕_i H^i(P), and every map H*(P) → H*(P) is assumed to preserve degrees. §7.1 (p. 392), with R = O[Δ]: ‘Recall that by a perfect complex of R-modules, we mean a bounded complex of finite free R-modules.’ The two conventions agree when R is local (e.g. S_N/ϖ^N, S∞, S∞^□, or O[Δ] with Δ a finite p-group), because finitely generated projective modules over a local ring are free.
items.note: Perfect complexes are absent from both libraries and planned in P7. The remark that 'finite projective' and 'finite free' agree over local rings is covered by Mathlib's Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing (finite flat modules over a local ring are free).

items.name: Depth is bounded by dim S/p for associated primes
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring and N a nonzero finitely generated S-module. Then depth(N) ≤ dim S/p for every p ∈ Ass_S(N). In particular depth(N) ≤ min_{p ∈ Ass(N)} dim S/p.
items.note: Mathlib has associated primes and Rees' Ext characterisation of regular sequences, but no depth invariant, so the inequality is not in the library. The reviewed R03.3 node names exactly this inequality (Stacks 0BK4, Matsumura 17.2). External input: H. Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory (Cambridge Stud. Adv. Math. 8), Theorem 17.2, cited as [69], Theorem 17.2

items.name: Lemma 6.1 (submodules have dimension at least the depth)
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring. If N is a [finitely generated] S-module with depth n, and M is a submodule with 0 ≠ M ⊆ N, then dim(M) ≥ n.
items.note: Stated verbatim in the reviewed R03.3 node, with CG's proof. Not in either library, since depth is undefined there. See sourceIssues E129 (N must be finitely generated).

items.name: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula
items.statement: Let S be a Noetherian local ring and M ≠ 0 a finitely generated S-module of finite projective dimension. Then proj.dim_S(M) + depth(M) = depth(S). In particular, if S is regular local of dimension n, every finitely generated M ≠ 0 has proj.dim(M) = n − depth(M), and M is free iff depth(M) = n.
items.locator: §6, proof of Lemma 6.2, p. 385; proof of Theorem 6.4(1), p. 389; §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 310 (applied to X∞ over S∞ and over R∞)
items.note: Absent from both libraries (AUDIT-17); Mathlib has projective dimension and regular local rings but not depth. R03.3 plans the formula and, in its node, the finite global dimension of regular local rings needed for the 'S regular' corollary. External input: Auslander–Buchsbaum formula, invoked by name without a reference (e.g. Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory, Theorem 19.1)

items.name: Lemma 6.2 (codimension bound for cohomology of a short perfect complex)
items.statement: Let l0 ≥ 0 be an integer and let S be a Noetherian regular local ring of dimension n ≥ l0. Let P be a perfect complex of S-modules concentrated in degrees 0,…,l0, with differentials δ^i: P^i → P^{i+1}, and [implicitly] H*(P) ≠ 0. Then codim(H*(P)) ≤ l0. More precisely, let m ≤ l0 be the smallest integer with H^m(P) ≠ 0 and put K^m := P^m/Im(δ^{m−1}). Then P^0 → P^1 → … → P^m is a projective resolution of K^m, and codim(H^m(P)) = n − dim H^m(P) ≤ n − depth(K^m) = proj.dim(K^m) ≤ m.
items.note: The reviewed P9 node states Lemma 6.2 and reproduces its proof. The node omits the hypothesis H*(P) ≠ 0 that this item makes explicit: for acyclic P, codim(0) is +∞ under Mathlib's supportDim(0) = ⊥, so the inequality fails. The blueprint should add the hypothesis. See sourceIssues E130 (Lemma 6.2 needs H*(P) ≠ 0).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(1) (equality case: P resolves its top cohomology)
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 6.2 (S Noetherian regular local of dimension n ≥ l0; P perfect, concentrated in degrees 0,…,l0, with H*(P) ≠ 0), suppose codim(H*(P)) = l0. Then H^i(P) = 0 for all i < l0, so P is a projective resolution of H^{l0}(P): the sequence 0 → P^0 → P^1 → … → P^{l0} → H^{l0}(P) → 0 is exact. Moreover codim(H^{l0}(P)) = l0.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.2(1) and last paragraph of proof, p. 385
items.note: Stated in the reviewed P9 node, including the vanishing of H^i(P) for i < l0, and not in either library. The same caveat applies: H*(P) ≠ 0 is needed. See sourceIssues E130 (Lemma 6.2 needs H*(P) ≠ 0).

items.name: Lemma 6.2(2) (equality case: depth n − l0 and projective dimension l0)
items.statement: In the situation of Lemma 6.2, suppose codim(H*(P)) = l0. Then H^{l0}(P) has depth n − l0 and projective dimension l0. In particular P is a projective resolution of H^{l0}(P) of minimal length.
items.note: Stated in the reviewed P9 node. It uses Auslander–Buchsbaum and depth (R03.3), neither of which is in the libraries.

items.name: Framing variables: O^□, M^□, S∞^□ and the ideal a
items.statement: Let j ≥ 0. Put O^□ := O⟦z_1,…,z_j⟧. For each O-module or O-algebra M, put M^□ := M ⊗_O O^□. For finitely generated O-modules, such as S_N, S_N/ϖ^n and the terms of D_N, this equals M⟦z_1,…,z_j⟧. For S∞ it must be read as the completed tensor product S∞^□ = S∞ ⊗̂_O O^□ = O⟦(Z_p)^q⟧⟦z_1,…,z_j⟧, a regular local ring of dimension 1+q+j. Any O-algebra A is regarded as a quotient of A^□ via z_i ↦ 0. Let a ⊂ S∞^□ be the kernel of the O-algebra map S∞^□ → O that sends each element of (Z_p)^q to 1 and each z_i to 0. The augmentation ideal of S_N^□ is the kernel of S_N^□ → O (group elements ↦ 1, z_i ↦ 0).
items.note: O^□ exists as MvPowerSeries, but the completed tensor product S∞ ⊗̂_O O^□ and the ideal a do not. P8's node fixes the framing variables and R03.1 plans completed tensor products over O. The item's warning that S∞^□ must be the completed tensor product (not the plain one) should be carried into P8.

items.name: Patching system of complexes (hypotheses of Theorem 6.3)
items.statement: Let l0 ≥ 0, and let q, j be non-negative integers with q + j ≥ l0. Let S∞, S_N, Δ_N, O^□, (−)^□ and a be as above. A patching system consists of the following data. (1) R∞, an object of C_O of Krull dimension 1 + j + q − l0. (2) R, an object of C_O, and an R-module H [H must be a nonzero finitely generated R-module; see sourceIssues E134]. (3) A complex T of finite-dimensional k-vector spaces concentrated in degrees 0,…,l0, with differential d = 0, and an isomorphism of k-modules H^{l0}(T) ≅ H/ϖH. (4) For each integer N ≥ 1, a perfect complex D_N of S_N/ϖ^N-modules and a surjective map φ_N : R∞ → R. These satisfy: (a) there is an isomorphism D_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/m_{S_N} ≅ T; (b) for each M ≥ N ≥ 0 with M ≥ 1 and each n ≥ 1 there is an action of R∞ on the cohomology of D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^n commuting with the action of S_M^□, and for N ≥ N' ≥ 0 and n ≥ n' ≥ 1 the natural map H*(D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^n) → H*(D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_{N'}/ϖ^{n'}) is compatible with the R∞-actions; (c) for each N ≥ 1 and each n with 1 ≤ n ≤ N [printed: ‘for each n ≥ 1’] there is an isomorphism of R∞-modules H^{l0}(D_N^□ ⊗_{S_N^□} O/ϖ^n) = H^{l0}(D_N ⊗_{S_N} O/ϖ^n) ≅ H/ϖ^n H, where R∞ acts on the left through (b) (with M = N and N = 0) and on H/ϖ^n H via φ_N, and these isomorphisms are compatible for fixed N and varying n; (d) for M, N, n as in (b), the image of S_M^□ in End_O(H*(D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^n)) is contained in the image of R∞, and the image of the augmentation ideal of S_N^□ (the kernel of S_N^□ → O) is contained in the image of ker(φ_M) [printed: ker(φ_N)].
items.note: The hypotheses of Theorem 6.3 are planned in the reviewed P8 node. That node follows the printed text: it has 'ker φ_N' in (d), no restriction n ≤ N in (c), and 'H an R-module' with no nonvanishing or finiteness condition. The corrections recorded for this item (sourceIssues E132, E133, E134) need to be carried into P8.

items.name: Auxiliary open ideals d_N of R
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 6.3, choose open ideals (d_N)_{N≥1} of R such that d_N ⊃ d_{N+1} for all N ≥ 1, ∩_{N≥1} d_N = (0), and ϖ^N R ⊂ d_N ⊂ ϖ^N R + Ann_R(H) for all N. For example, d_N can be the ideal generated by ϖ^N and Ann_R(H)^N.
items.locator: §6.1, proof of Theorem 6.3, p. 387 (referring to the proof of Proposition 2.3, p. 308)
items.note: Planned word for word in the R03.5 node (CG Prop. 2.3), and the P8 node reuses it. The Krull intersection step (∩ d_N = 0) uses Mathlib's adic separatedness of Noetherian local rings.

items.name: Patching datum of level N (for complexes)
items.statement: Fix N ≥ 1. A patching datum of level N is a triple (φ, ψ, P) where: (1) φ : R∞ ↠ R/d_N is a surjection in C_O; (2) P is a perfect complex of S∞/(a_N + ϖ^N)-modules (note S∞/(a_N + ϖ^N) = S_N/ϖ^N) such that P ⊗ S∞/m_{S∞} ≅ T; (3) for each N ≥ N' ≥ 0, each N ≥ n' ≥ 1 and each ideal I of O^□ with (z_1^N,…,z_j^N) ⊂ I ⊂ (z_1,…,z_j) [this family of I must be restricted, e.g. to I = (z_1^m,…,z_j^m) with 1 ≤ m ≤ N together with I = (z_1,…,z_j); see sourceIssues E137], the groups H^i(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S^□_{N'}/(I + ϖ^{n'})) carry an action of R∞ that commutes with the action of S∞^□, and these actions are compatible for varying N', n' and I; (4) ψ : H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S∞^□/(a + ϖ^N)) ≅ H/ϖ^N H is an isomorphism of R∞-modules, with R∞ acting on H/ϖ^N H via φ. ψ then induces isomorphisms H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗ S∞^□/(a + ϖ^{n'})) ≅ H/ϖ^{n'} H for N ≥ n' ≥ 1. Two triples (φ, ψ, P) and (φ', ψ', P') are isomorphic if φ = φ' and there is an isomorphism of complexes P ≅ P' of S∞-modules that induces isomorphisms of R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞^□-modules on cohomology compatible with ψ and ψ' in degree l0. Up to isomorphism there are finitely many patching data of level N. For 1 ≤ N' ≤ N, a datum D of level N gives a datum D mod N' of level N' ‘in an obvious fashion’: reduce φ modulo d_{N'} and P modulo a_{N'} + ϖ^{N'}, and restrict the actions and ψ.
items.note: Planned in the P8 node, with the finiteness of isomorphism classes. The ideals I in condition (3) must be restricted, as the item records (sourceIssues E137). The node does not mention this, so the P8 blueprint has to fix the family of I.

items.name: The patching data D_{M,N}
items.statement: For M ≥ N ≥ 1, define the patching datum D_{M,N} of level N as follows. φ is the composite R∞ →(φ_M) R ↠ R/d_N. P := D_M ⊗_{S∞} S∞/(a_N + ϖ^N) = D_M ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^N. ψ : H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S∞^□/(a + ϖ^N)) = H^{l0}(D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M^□} O/ϖ^N) ≅ H/ϖ^N is the isomorphism given by hypothesis (c) for D_M with n = N ≤ M. The R∞-actions come from hypothesis (b) through the identification H^i(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S^□_{N'}/(I + ϖ^{n'})) = H^i(D_M^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_{N'}/ϖ^{n'}) ⊗_{O^□} O^□/I, for 1 ≤ n' ≤ N and 0 ≤ N' ≤ N.
items.note: The P8 node plans this construction as the input of the diagonal-subsequence step; R03.5's node treats the module analogue (CG Prop. 2.3) explicitly. Neither library has patching data. See sourceIssues E137 (identification needs O^□/I flat over O).

items.name: The patched complex P∞ and the maps φ∞, ψ∞, ı
items.statement: Since each level has only finitely many patching data up to isomorphism, there is a sequence of pairs (M_i, N_i)_{i≥1} with M_i ≥ N_i, M_{i+1} ≥ M_i and N_{i+1} > N_i [printed: N_{i+1} ≥ N_i] such that D_{M_{i+1},N_{i+1}} mod N_i ≅ D_{M_i,N_i} for all i ≥ 1. Write D_{M_i,N_i} = (φ_i, ψ_i, P_i) and fix such isomorphisms. Define: φ∞ : R∞ ↠ R as the inverse limit of the φ_i; P∞ := lim_i P_i, where each transition map is P_{i+1} ↠ P_{i+1}/(ϖ^{N_i} + a_{N_i}) ≅ P_i; and ψ∞ : H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a = H^{l0}(P∞^□/a) ≅ H as the isomorphism of R∞-modules induced by the ψ_i, with R∞ acting on H via φ∞. Then the following hold. P∞ is a perfect complex of S∞-modules concentrated in degrees 0,…,l0. H*(P∞^□) carries an action of R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞^□ extending that of S∞^□. The image of S∞^□ in End_O(H*(P∞^□)) is contained in the image of R∞, by (d) and because the image of R∞ is closed in End_O(H*(P∞^□)) for its profinite topology; hence each H^i(P∞^□) is a finite R∞-module. Since S∞^□ is formally smooth over O, there is a homomorphism ı : S∞^□ → R∞ in C_O compatible with the actions of S∞^□ and R∞ on H*(P∞^□).
items.note: Every step is planned in the P8 node. The item's N_{i+1} > N_i (printed ≥) must be used so that the inverse limit is over a cofinal system. The map ı can use Mathlib's evaluation maps out of MvPowerSeries once S∞^□ ≅ O⟦y_1,…,y_{q+j}⟧ is established (absent). See sourceIssues E139 (N_{i+1} > N_i is needed).

items.name: Theorem 6.3 (patching of complexes)
items.statement: Let (q, j, R∞, R, H, T, (D_N, φ_N)_{N≥1}) satisfy hypotheses (1)–(3) and (a)–(d) of Theorem 6.3 (see cg-patching-system, with the corrections noted there). Let a ⊂ S∞^□ be the kernel of the map S∞^□ → O sending each element of (Z_p)^q to 1 and each z_i to 0. Then there is a perfect complex P∞ of finitely generated S∞-modules, concentrated in degrees 0,…,l0, such that, with P∞^□ := P∞ ⊗_{S∞} S∞^□: (i) P∞^□ is a projective resolution, of minimal length, of its top degree cohomology H^{l0}(P∞^□); (ii) there is an action of R∞ ⊗̂_O S∞^□ on H^{l0}(P∞^□) extending the action of S∞^□, and H^{l0}(P∞^□) is a finite R∞-module; (iii) the R∞-depth of H^{l0}(P∞^□) [printed: H^{l0}(P∞)] equals 1 + j + q − l0 (= dim R∞); (iv) there is a surjection φ∞ : R∞ ↠ R and an isomorphism ψ∞ : H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a ≅ H of R∞-modules, where R∞ acts on H via φ∞; moreover, the image of a in End(H^{l0}(P∞^□)) is contained in the image of ker(φ∞).
items.note: The reviewed P8 node states Theorem 6.3, with (iii) already for the framed complex (P′_∞), and uses P9's Lemma 6.2 in its last step. The corrections to the hypotheses (ker φ_M, n ≤ N, H ≠ 0 and finitely generated; sourceIssues E133, E132, E134) are not in the node yet. See sourceIssues E138 ((iii) concerns H^{l0}(P∞^□)).

items.name: Nearly faithful module
items.statement: Let A be a ring and M an A-module. M is nearly faithful over A if Ann_A(M) is a nilpotent ideal. For A Noetherian and M finitely generated this is equivalent to Supp_A(M) = Spec(A), i.e. to every minimal prime of A lying in the support of M.
items.note: Near faithfulness is not in either library. It is planned in R03.6 and P9, and the R03.6 node records the definition. The equivalence with Supp_A(M) = Spec A for finite M follows from Mathlib's Module.support_eq_zeroLocus and nilradical lemmas. External input: R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations. II, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), 183–239, cited as [11]

items.name: Theorem 6.4(1) (freeness when R∞ is formally smooth)
items.statement: Keep the notation and hypotheses of Theorem 6.3, with P∞, φ∞, ψ∞ and ı : S∞^□ → R∞ as constructed in its proof, and suppose in addition that R∞ is p-torsion free. If R∞ is formally smooth over O, so that R∞ [printed: R] ≅ O⟦x_1,…,x_{q+j−l0}⟧, then H is a free R-module. More precisely, H^{l0}(P∞^□) is free over R∞ and ker(φ∞) = ı(a)R∞, so that R ≅ R∞/ı(a)R∞.
items.note: Planned in the reviewed R03.6 node, including ker φ∞ = ı(a)R∞. The printed 'R ≅ O⟦x_1,…⟧' is the misprint for R∞ that the item corrects (sourceIssues E141).

items.name: Reduction of near faithfulness from R∞ to R (step in proof of Theorem 6.4)
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 6.3, with ı as in its proof, suppose H^{l0}(P∞^□) is a nearly faithful R∞-module. Let 𝔑 be the ideal of nilpotent elements of R∞. Then H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a ≅ H is nearly faithful over R∞/ı(a)R∞, and the R∞-action on it factors through R∞/ker(φ∞) = R, which gives a natural surjection R^red ↠ (R∞/ı(a)R∞)^red. Because the image of a in End(H^{l0}(P∞^□)) lies in that of ker(φ∞), we have ı(a) + 𝔑 ⊂ ker(φ∞) + 𝔑. Hence this surjection is an isomorphism, and H is a nearly faithful R-module.
items.note: This reduction step is written out in the reviewed R03.6 node; the libraries have radicals and nilradicals but no near-faithfulness.

items.name: Near faithfulness over a p-torsion-free ring via the generic fibre
items.statement: Let R∞ be an object of C_O that is p-torsion free, so that all its minimal primes have characteristic 0. Let M be a finitely generated R∞-module. Then M is nearly faithful over R∞ if and only if every irreducible component of Spec(R∞[1/p]) lies in the support of M[1/p].
items.note: Planned as a proof step of the R03.6 node. P9 also plans keeping 'integral support' apart from 'support after inverting p'.

items.name: Support of a module of maximal depth
items.statement: Let A be a Noetherian local ring and M ≠ 0 a finitely generated A-module with depth_A(M) = dim A. Then every associated prime p of M satisfies dim A/p = dim A. Hence Supp(M) is a nonempty union of irreducible components of Spec(A) of maximal dimension.
items.locator: §6.1, proof of Theorem 6.4(2), p. 390; Remark 6.5, p. 390
items.note: The general lemma (depth = dim A forces dim A/p = dim A for every associated prime, by Matsumura 17.2) belongs to R03.3's associated-prime and support lemmas, and R03.6 states its patching use. Neither library has it, since depth is missing.

items.name: Theorem 6.4(2) (near faithfulness when R∞[1/p] is irreducible)
items.statement: Keep the notation and hypotheses of Theorem 6.3 [with H ≠ 0], and suppose R∞ is p-torsion free. If R∞[1/p] is irreducible, then H is a nearly faithful R-module.
items.note: Stated in the reviewed R03.6 node. The proof uses H^{l0}(P∞^□) ≠ 0, i.e. H ≠ 0, which the node does not state; the blueprint should add it. See sourceIssues E134 (H must be non-zero and finite).

items.name: Theorem 6.4(3) (near faithfulness under a support condition)
items.statement: Keep the notation and hypotheses of Theorem 6.3, and suppose R∞ is p-torsion free. If every irreducible component of Spec(R∞[1/p]) lies in the support of H^{l0}(P∞^□)[1/p] [printed: H^{l0}(P∞)[1/p]], then H is a nearly faithful R-module.
items.note: Planned in the R03.6 node. The node keeps the printed H^{l0}(P∞)[1/p]; it should read H^{l0}(P∞^□)[1/p], since only the framed module is an R∞-module in the theorem. See sourceIssues E140 (support condition concerns H^{l0}(P∞^□)).

items.name: Remark 6.5 (equidimensionality is necessary)
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 6.3, where depth_{R∞} H^{l0}(P∞^□) = dim R∞, if H^{l0}(P∞^□) is nearly faithful as an R∞-module then R∞ is equidimensional.
items.note: Recorded in the reviewed R03.6 node. Equidimensionality itself is an R03.3 target that is not in Mathlib.

items.name: Proposition 6.6 (simultaneous patching of two data sets congruent mod ϖ)
items.statement: Let S_N and O^□ be as in Theorem 6.3. Suppose we are given two sets of data (R∞^i, R^i, H^i, T^i, (D_N^i)_{N≥1}, (φ_N^i)_{N≥1}), i = 1, 2, each satisfying assumptions (1)–(3) and (a)–(d) of Theorem 6.3 (same q, j, l0). Suppose we are also given: (1) isomorphisms of k-algebras R∞^1/ϖ ≅ R∞^2/ϖ and R^1/ϖ ≅ R^2/ϖ; (2) an isomorphism H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ of modules over R^1/ϖ ≅ R^2/ϖ; (3) for each M ≥ N ≥ 0, an isomorphism of S_N/ϖ-modules H^{l0}(D_M^1 ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) ≅ H^{l0}(D_M^2 ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) which, after tensoring over O with O^□, induces an isomorphism H^{l0}((D_M^1)^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) ≅ H^{l0}((D_M^2)^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) of modules over R∞^1 ⊗_O S_N^□/ϖ ≅ R∞^2 ⊗_O S_N^□/ϖ. Assume that for each M ≥ 1 the following square commutes: its top row is the given isomorphism H^{l0}(D_M^1 ⊗_{S_M} O/ϖ) → H^{l0}(D_M^2 ⊗_{S_M} O/ϖ) (the case N = 0); its vertical maps are the isomorphisms of (c) with n = 1 onto H^1/ϖ and H^2/ϖ; its bottom row is H^1/ϖ → H^2/ϖ. [An additional compatibility of the (M,N)-isomorphisms under the reductions S_N → S_{N'} appears to be needed; see sourceIssues E142.] Then one can find complexes P∞^{i,□}, i = 1, 2, satisfying conclusions (i)–(iv) of Theorem 6.3, together with an isomorphism of R∞^1/ϖ ≅ R∞^2/ϖ-modules H^{l0}(P∞^{1,□})/ϖ ≅ H^{l0}(P∞^{2,□})/ϖ such that the following square commutes: top row H^{l0}(P∞^{1,□})/(a + ϖ) → H^{l0}(P∞^{2,□})/(a + ϖ) (induced); vertical maps ψ∞^i mod ϖ onto H^i/ϖ; bottom row the given H^1/ϖ → H^2/ϖ.
items.note: Planned in the R03.6 node, whose gaps list the omitted proof ('we omit the details') as an obligation; P8 plans the comparison of two patched systems. The item's warning about an extra compatibility of the (M,N)-isomorphisms under S_N → S_{N'} must be settled when that proof is written. See sourceIssues E142 (missing compatibility of the (M,N)-isomorphisms).

items.name: Betti setting of §7.1: the Δ-cover X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q)
items.statement: Let G be a reductive group over a number field F. Let K_0(Q) ⊂ G(A_F^∞) be a compact open subgroup, and K_Δ(Q) ⊂ K_0(Q) a normal subgroup with finite abelian quotient Δ. Let X_0(Q) and X_Δ(Q) be the associated locally symmetric spaces; X_Δ(Q) → X_0(Q) is a covering map with group Δ. (In practice Q is a set of Taylor–Wiles primes, and §9 fixes the subgroups for G = PGL(n).) Put R := O[Δ], with augmentation ideal a. For a topological space Y, C(Y) is the complex of O-valued singular chains on Y; C(X_Δ(Q)) is a complex of R-modules via the deck action. In both the Betti and coherent cases, the cohomology localized at a maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra T is assumed to vanish outside a range of length l0.
items.note: The spaces X_K, their finite-level covers and the chain complexes are planned in ALS.0/ALS.1/ALS.6. Tau Ceti's AlgebraicTopology Stage 5 plans the deck-group structure of the chains of a regular finite cover. Mathlib has singular chain complexes. The standing assumption that the m-localised cohomology vanishes outside a range of length l0 is a hypothesis, not a construction.

items.name: Mumford's lemma: finite replacement of complexes
items.statement: As the paper uses it: let A be a Noetherian ring and K• a bounded complex of A-modules with finitely generated cohomology. Then there is a bounded complex K'• of finitely generated A-modules in the same range of degrees, with a quasi-isomorphism K'• → K•, such that all terms of K'• are free except possibly the extreme one, which is flat if the terms of K• are flat. If A is local, that flat, finitely generated term is also free.
items.locator: §7.1, proofs of Lemmas 7.1 and 7.4, pp. 392, 394; §7.2, p. 398
items.note: The P7 node plans Mumford's argument (finite free resolution, truncation, flat finitely presented last term). The input that a bounded complex with finitely generated cohomology over a Noetherian ring is pseudo-coherent is not stated in the node, and the P7 blueprint should add it. The 'last term free because R is local' step is Mathlib's Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing. External input: D. Mumford, Abelian Varieties, §II.5, Lemma 1, cited as [43, Sect. II.5 Lemma 1] (‘Lemma 1 of Mumford ([43], Chap. II.5)’)

items.name: Quasi-isomorphisms of flat complexes are preserved by base change
items.statement: As the paper uses it ([43, §II.5, Lemma 2]): let φ : C → C′ be a morphism of complexes of flat R-modules that are bounded above in cohomological indexing (for chain complexes, C_i = 0 for i ≪ 0, e.g. singular chain complexes with C_i = 0 for i < 0), and suppose φ is a quasi-isomorphism. Then φ ⊗ 1 : C ⊗_R A → C′ ⊗_R A is a quasi-isomorphism for every R-module A. In particular H_*(C ⊗_R A) ≅ H_*(C′ ⊗_R A) for every R-algebra A.
items.note: That bounded-above complexes of flat modules compute ⊗^L, so quasi-isomorphisms between them survive any base change, is the basic lemma behind P7's 'derived tensor products' and 'derived coefficient change'. Neither library has it, and the P7 node does not state it; the blueprint should make it explicit. External input: D. Mumford, Abelian Varieties, §II.5, Lemma 2, cited as [43, Sect. II.5 Lemma 2]

items.name: Lemma 7.1 (perfect complex computing the homology of the Δ-cover)
items.statement: In the setting of §7.1, there exist a perfect complex C of R-modules (a bounded complex of finite free R-modules) and a quasi-isomorphism C → C(X_Δ(Q)) of complexes of R-modules. In particular, for all integers N [≥ 1]: H_*(C ⊗_O O/ϖ^N) = H_*(X_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^N) and H_*(C ⊗_R R/(a + ϖ^N)) = H_*(X_0(Q), O/ϖ^N).
items.note: The unlocalised O[Δ]-perfect model of C(X_Δ(Q)) is planned: ALS.1 (finite projective models over the coefficient ring O[Δ], with base change), ALS.6 (finite-cover descent) and Tau Ceti AT Stage 5 (C_*(E)_G ≅ C_*(B)). This agrees with PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24's note on its Prop. 13.9. P8 assigns 'group-algebra freeness at auxiliary level' to ALS, but no ALS stage states it for O[Δ]; the ALS blueprint should. See sourceIssues E144 (singular chains are unbounded; Mumford's lemma needs care).

items.name: Hecke operators T_γ on homology and on singular chains
items.statement: Let γ ∈ G(A_F^{∞,p}) and K := K_Δ(Q), so X_K = X_Δ(Q). Put K' := γKγ^{-1} ∩ K and K'' := K ∩ γ^{-1}Kγ. Right multiplication by γ gives an isomorphism γ : X_{K'} → X_{K''}. For A = O/ϖ^N with N ≤ ∞ (O/ϖ^∞ := O), the Hecke operator T_γ on H_i(X_K, A) equals, up to an invertible scalar, the composite H_i(X_K, A) →(tr) H_i(X_{K'}, A) →(γ_*) H_i(X_{K''}, A) → H_i(X_K, A). Here tr is the transfer (corestriction) for the finite covering X_{K'} → X_K, and the last map is induced by the covering X_{K''} → X_K. After ⊗_O A, T_γ is induced by the chain-level composite T̃_γ : C(X_K) →(tr) C(X_{K'}) →(γ_*) C(X_{K''}) → C(X_K) [printed with K' and K'' interchanged].
items.locator: §7.1, p. 392 and proof of Lemma 7.2, p. 393
items.note: Planned in ALS.3 (the two maps through K ∩ gKg^{-1}, trace, chain maps) with chain-level transfer from Tau Ceti AT Stage 5. The printed chain-level composite has K′ and K″ interchanged (p. 393), a misprint the item corrects (sourceIssues E146).

items.name: Lifting chain maps out of a bounded complex of projectives through a quasi-isomorphism
items.statement: As the paper needs it: let C be a bounded (above) complex of projective R-modules and s : C → L a quasi-isomorphism of complexes of R-modules. Then every morphism of complexes f : C → L lifts to a morphism of complexes g : C → C with s∘g homotopic to f. Equivalently, morphisms out of C in the derived category D(R) are represented by chain maps, and Hom_{K(R)}(C, C) → Hom_{K(R)}(C, L) is bijective.
items.note: Mathlib proves that a bounded-above cochain complex of projectives is K-projective. For such a complex it also proves that homotopy classes of maps into any L biject with morphisms in the derived category. Applied to L = C and L = C(X_K), with the quasi-isomorphism s invertible in D, this is exactly the lifting statement, up to reindexing chain complexes as ℤ-graded cochain complexes; for ModuleCat R the derived category exists via HasDerivedCategory.standard. The lift commutes only up to homotopy, which is all that CG's 'making the diagram commute' can mean. External input: The Stacks Project, Tag 08FQ, cited as [70, Tag 08FQ]

items.name: Lemma 7.2 (Hecke operators lift to the perfect complex)
items.statement: Let C be as in Lemma 7.1 and γ ∈ G(A^{∞,p}) [the paper allows any such γ; R-linearity needs T_γ to commute with Δ = K_0(Q)/K_Δ(Q), i.e. K_Δ(Q)δ^{-1}γδK_Δ(Q) = K_Δ(Q)γK_Δ(Q) for δ ∈ K_0(Q). This holds, e.g., for γ trivial at the places where K_Δ(Q) ≠ K_0(Q), or for the U_x, x ∈ Q, which the paper asserts commute with the diamond operators; see sourceIssues E143]. Then the action of T_γ on homology lifts to a map T_γ : C → C of complexes of R-modules: a chain map whose composite with the quasi-isomorphism s : C → C(X_Δ(Q)) is homotopic [printed: equal, 'making the diagram commute'] to T̃_γ ∘ s. It induces T_γ on H_*(C ⊗_O A) = H_*(X_Δ(Q), A) for A = O/ϖ^N, N ≤ ∞.
items.note: The Hecke correspondence on chains is ALS.3, and moving it to the perfect model C is the chain versus derived comparison that IHG.2 plans. The homotopy-lifting step is in Mathlib (K-projectivity and Qh_map_bijective). See sourceIssues E143 (T_γ must commute with Δ) and E147 (lift commutes only up to homotopy).

items.name: Lifting elements of the Hecke algebra T to C
items.statement: Let T be a Hecke algebra generated over O by a collection of operators T_γ. Every T ∈ T can be written as a polynomial in the T_γ. Substituting the lifts of Lemma 7.2 gives an endomorphism T : C → C of complexes of R-modules that lifts the action of T on homology.
items.note: Planned in IHG.2. The lifts T_γ commute and satisfy the Hecke relations only up to homotopy, so a polynomial in them depends on the choices and lifts T only on homology, which is exactly what CG claims. IHG.2's chain, derived and cohomology distinction covers this. See sourceIssues E143 (R-linear lifts need the Δ-stability hypothesis).

items.name: Lemma 7.3 (ordinary part of a perfect complex)
items.statement: For T ∈ T acting R-linearly on C through a lift, let e_T := lim_{n→∞} T^{n!}, the idempotent in the finite O-algebra generated by T in End_R(C^i). It projects onto the part on which T is invertible; the complementary factor is the part on which T is topologically nilpotent. Equivalently, e_T M = ∩_n T^n M. Put C_T := e_T C [printed: C_T := lim→_n T^n C. Here lim→ denotes the limit as n → ∞ of the decreasing chain T^n C, i.e. ∩_n T^n C = e_T C, as in e_α := lim→ Q(V)^{n!} on p. 422; it is not a direct limit along T, which would be a localisation]. Then C_T is a perfect complex of R-modules, termwise a direct summand of C (so with finitely generated projective terms), and its homology is e_T H_*(C) [printed: lim→ T^n H_*(C)].
items.note: L0a plans exactly this (the U^{n!} projector for finite modules over complete Noetherian local rings with finite residue field, applied degreewise to perfect complexes), and O[Δ] qualifies. CG's 'lim→ T^n C' must be read as e_T C, as the item does: the literal colimit along T is a localisation (for M = O, T = ϖ it is K), not a direct summand.

items.name: Lemma 7.4 (Nakayama's lemma for perfect complexes: minimal complexes)
items.statement: Assume Δ has p-power order, so that R = O[Δ] is local with maximal ideal m_R. Let T ∈ T. Then there is a perfect complex D of R-modules, quasi-isomorphic to C_T, such that for all n: dim_k D_n/m_R D_n = dim_k H_n(C_T ⊗_R R/m_R) = dim_k lim→_m T^m H_n(X_0(Q), k). Equivalently, D ⊗_R R/m_R has zero differentials.
items.note: P7 plans the minimal complex and its ranks. The second equality (with lim→ T^m H_n(X_0(Q), k)) combines Lemma 7.1's base change (ALS.1) with exactness of e_T (PadicFamilies L0a). The proof's 'differential d on D' should read K.

items.name: Lemma 7.4, length bound (corrected form)
items.statement: Corrected form: in Lemma 7.4, if H_n(C_T ⊗_R R/m_R) = lim→_m T^m H_n(X_0(Q), k) vanishes for n outside an interval [q0, q0 + l0], then D_n = 0 for n ∉ [q0, q0 + l0], so D has length at most l0. [Printed: ‘Moreover, the length of D is at most l0, where l0 is the range of cohomology groups such that lim→ T^n H^*(C) is non-zero.’]
items.note: In corrected form, D_n = 0 exactly when H_n(C_T ⊗ R/m_R) = 0. This is a property of minimal complexes planned in P7, and P7 insists on the same distinction between cohomological range and Tor-amplitude. The printed statement uses the degrees where lim→ T^n H*(C) is nonzero, which bounds cohomology rather than Tor-amplitude and does not give the conclusion. See sourceIssues E148 (printed length bound does not follow).

items.name: The Hecke algebra T = T^an[U_x : x ∈ Q]; maximal ideals with the same Galois representation
items.statement: In practice the Hecke algebra is T = T^an[U_x : x ∈ Q], where T^an is the O-subalgebra generated by the good Hecke operators away from Q and p. Two maximal ideals of T give rise to the same Galois representation if they have the same contraction to T^an. m denotes a maximal ideal of T with residue field k, at which the homology groups H_*(X_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^N) are to be localized.
items.note: No layer defines, for a general reductive G (PGL(n) over an arbitrary F in CG §9), the Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebra T = T^an[U_x : x ∈ Q] and the relation 'same Galois representation' (equal contraction to T^an). The analogues are planned only for GL_n over CM fields (PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure PA.4) and for totally real GL_2 (GL2ModularityLifting R22.1–R22.2). PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked its PGL_2/F analogue (hecke-TSigmaQ-13-6) missing. The generic ingredients are ALS.3 (operators) and IHG.2 (image algebras).

items.name: The localizing Hecke operator T = ∏_{x∈Q} P_x ∘ ∏_{i∈Ω} P_i
items.statement: For each of the finitely many maximal ideals n of T occurring in H_*(X_Δ(Q), k), choose an O-algebra homomorphism φ_n : T → k̄ with kernel n. Let Ω index the maximal ideals n that give rise to a Galois representation distinct from that of m; equivalently, φ_n and φ_m differ on T^an. For i ∈ Ω corresponding to n, choose a good Hecke operator T_i ∈ T^an with φ_n(T_i) ≠ φ_m(T_i). Let F_i(T) be the minimal polynomial over K [printed: E] of the Teichmüller lift of φ_n(T_i) to K̄. Then φ_m(T_i) ∈ k is not a root of F_i modulo ϖ, so P_i := F_i(T_i) lies in n but not in m. For x ∈ Q, let P_x be a projector that commutes with the diamond operators and cuts out the localization at m among the maximal ideals with the same Galois representation as m. For example, for G = GL(2), P_x = lim_n (U_x − β_x)^{n!}, where U_x − α_x ∈ m and α_x, β_x are lifts to O of the (distinct) eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x). Put T := ∏_{x∈Q} P_x ∘ ∏_{i∈Ω} P_i. Then lim→_n T^n H_*(X_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^N) = H_*(X_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^N)_m [printed with Γ_Δ(Q_N) in place of X_Δ(Q)].
items.note: The generic part is close to planned layers. IHG.2 plans 'localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings' and L0a the U^{n!} projector. However, no layer plans CG's explicit construction: P_i = F_i(T_i) from minimal polynomials of Teichmüller lifts, and TW-prime projectors P_x commuting with diamond operators (for GL(2), lim (U_x − β_x)^{n!}). P_x is an arithmetic input at Taylor–Wiles primes, planned only for CM GL_n (PA.4) and totally real GL_2 (R22.2). The printed 'minimal polynomial over E' should read K (E is undefined; Notation p. 306 fixes K), and 'Γ_Δ(Q_N)' should read X_Δ(Q).

items.name: Output of §7.1: bounded minimal complex computing the localized homology
items.statement: Assume Δ has p-power order and let m and T be as above. Let D be the complex of Lemma 7.4 for this T. Then D is a perfect complex of (finite free) R-modules such that: (1) D_n ≠ 0 if and only if H_n(X_0(Q), k)_m ≠ {0}; (2) H_n(D ⊗_O O/ϖ^N) ≅ H_n(X_Δ(Q), O/ϖ^N)_m for all n and N; (3) H_n(D ⊗_R R/(a + ϖ^N)) ≅ H_n(X_0(Q), O/ϖ^N)_m for all n and N. Moreover D ⊗_R R/m_R has zero differentials.
items.note: Each ingredient is planned: the O[Δ]-perfect model with base change (ALS.1/ALS.6), localisation of a Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex at m as a direct summand (IHG.2), and the minimal complex over the local ring O[Δ] (P7). Bullet (3) compares with X_0(Q) at the same level Q, so no Iwahori-versus-spherical comparison is involved. With IHG.2's idempotent e_m in place of CG's explicit T, the statement is their direct combination. The ALS blueprint should state the assembled O[Δ]-version, which P8 expects from ALS.

items.name: Betti duality: Pontryagin dual of lowest-degree cohomology is top-degree homology
items.statement: In Betti cohomology, when m is chosen so that the cohomology of the boundary vanishes after localization at m, the patched module H^{q0}(X, K/O)^∨_m [printed: H^{q0}(X, 𝓔/O)^∨_m] can be identified in two ways. By Poincaré duality (the boundary contributions die after localization) followed by universal coefficients, it is H^{q0+l0}(X, O)_m, the non-zero cohomology group of highest degree with O-coefficients. By universal coefficients alone, it is H_{q0}(X, O)_m, the homology group of lowest degree. Both identifications transpose the Hecke action, m ↔ m*. [Printed: 'the non-zero homology group of highest degree with coefficients in O, namely H_{q0+l0}(X, O)_m … essentially a consequence of Poincaré duality'. That group is O-torsion free and differs from H^{q0}(X, K/O)^∨_m whenever H_{q0}(X, O)_m has torsion; see sourceIssues E153.]
items.note: Finite-level Poincaré–Lefschetz duality with orientation twists is planned in ALS.5:finite-level-duality, and boundary vanishing after localisation in ALS.4 (which rightly asks for an actual eigenvalue argument). The paper states this identification informally ('essentially a consequence of Poincaré duality'). The blueprint must add the dimension 2q0 + l0 of X and the Pontryagin-duality/universal-coefficient step (ALS.1). See sourceIssues E153 (top-degree cohomology, not homology).

items.name: Coherent setting of §7.2
items.statement: f : Y = X_Δ(Q) → X = X_0(Q) is an étale map with Galois group Δ, a finite abelian p-group. X and Y are proper and smooth over Spec(O) and arise as integral models of the Shimura varieties attached to a reductive group G over a number field F and compact open subgroups K_Δ(Q) ⊂ K_0(Q) ⊂ G(A_F^∞). When these Shimura varieties are not compact, X and Y are arithmetic toroidal compactifications as constructed in [71]. An automorphic vector bundle 𝓔 is given on X [printed: ‘on Y … which pulls back to a bundle also denoted by 𝓔 on X’], a canonical or subcanonical extension in the toroidal case, with pullback also denoted 𝓔 on Y. R := O[Δ]. m is a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra generated by the good Hecke operators at unramified primes together with certain operators at the primes of the Taylor–Wiles set Q. The goal is a perfect complex of R/ϖ^n-modules computing H_i(Y, 𝓔 ⊗ O/ϖ^n)_m.
items.note: Parts of the setting are planned: integral PEL toroidal compactifications (ShimuraCompactifications C5), prime-to-p level changes of integral models (PELModuli M4) and characteristic-zero canonical/subcanonical extensions (AutomorphicBundles B3, whose reviewed node is complex-analytic). Integral automorphic vector bundles over O, with integral canonical/subcanonical extensions on the smooth proper models and their pullback along the étale Δ-cover Y → X, are planned nowhere. The printed direction ('bundle on Y which pulls back to X') is reversed, as the item corrects (sourceIssues E152). External input: K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties (PhD thesis), cited as [71]

items.name: Coherent homology
items.statement: H_i(Y, 𝓔 ⊗ O/ϖ^n) := H^i(Y, 𝓔^* ⊗_{O_Y} ω_Y ⊗_O O/ϖ^n)^∨, where ω_Y is the determinant of Ω^1_{Y/O} and ∨ denotes the Pontryagin dual. By the duality recalled on p. 398, this is H^{d−i}(Y, 𝓔 ⊗ O/ϖ^n), where d is the relative dimension.
items.note: No layer defines Pontryagin-dual 'coherent homology' H_i(Y, E ⊗ O/ϖ^n) := H^i(Y, E^* ⊗ ω_Y ⊗ O/ϖ^n)^∨ on integral models, or its identification with H^{d−i}(Y, E ⊗ O/ϖ^n) by duality. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked its weight-one instance (weight-one-sheaf, 'as in [17, §7.2]') missing too.

items.name: Lemma 7.5 (ϖ-torsion-free modules are free modulo ϖ^n)
items.statement: Let P be an O-module that is ϖ-torsion free. Then P/ϖ^n P is free over O/ϖ^n for each n ≥ 1. In fact, lifts x_α ∈ P of any k-basis of P/ϖP map to an O/ϖ^n-basis of P/ϖ^n P.
items.note: Mathlib gets ϖ-torsion-free ⇒ flat over O ⇒ P/ϖ^n flat over O/ϖ^n, but 'flat ⇒ free' over the Artinian local ring O/ϖ^n only for finite modules. CG applies Lemma 7.5 to non-finitely-generated modules (sections of coherent sheaves over affine opens), so the statement is not in the library. The referee's argument is Stacks 051G (flat over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal ⇒ free), which is also absent. No layer plans it.

items.name: Lemma 7.6 (freeness over R/ϖ^n from freeness over O/ϖ^n and R/ϖ)
items.statement: Let Δ be any finite abelian group and R = O[Δ]. If M is an R-module that is free over O/ϖ^n and M/ϖM is free over R/ϖ = k[Δ], then M is free over R/ϖ^n. In fact, lifts y_α ∈ M of a k[Δ]-basis of M/ϖM form an R/ϖ^n-basis.
items.note: The freeness criterion over (O/ϖ^n)[Δ] (free over O/ϖ^n and free modulo ϖ over k[Δ] implies free) is in neither library and no layer plans it. It is a case of the local flatness criterion for the nilpotent ideal (ϖ), followed by flat ⇒ free over an Artinian local ring. P8 names group-algebra freeness as an arithmetic input, not this algebraic criterion.

items.name: Nakajima's Čech complex for the Δ-cover
items.statement: Let f : Y → X be as in §7.2 (étale, Galois group Δ an abelian p-group, X and Y smooth and proper over O), and let 𝓕 be a ϖ-torsion-free coherent O_X-module. Following Nakajima [72], take a finite affine open cover {U_α} of X; the U_α are flat over O. The Čech complex D of the pulled-back cover of Y, with coefficients in f^*𝓕, is a bounded complex of O-flat O[Δ]-modules computing H^i(Y, f^*𝓕). Its terms are direct sums of modules N ⊗_A B, where Spec(A) ⊂ X is an intersection of U_α's, Spec(B) ⊂ Y is its preimage and N = Γ(Spec A, 𝓕). Moreover D ⊗ O/ϖ^n computes H^i(Y, f^*𝓕 ⊗ O/ϖ^n) for every n. By Lemma 7.7, D ⊗ O/ϖ^n is a bounded complex of free (in particular projective) R/ϖ^n-modules.
items.note: The generic Čech comparison is planned in Tau Ceti (JacobianChallenge Layer B: 'Čech ≃ derived on a separated scheme'; StableReduction Layer 2 over locally Noetherian bases). No layer plans the Δ-equivariant Čech complex of an étale Galois cover of smooth proper O-schemes as a complex of O-flat O[Δ]-modules that computes H^i(Y, f^*F ⊗ O/ϖ^n) for every n. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 found the same gap for its Prop. 14.1 ('The Δ-equivariant construction on the Shimura curve is planned nowhere'). External input: S. Nakajima, On Galois module structure of the cohomology groups of an algebraic variety, Invent. Math. 75 (1984), cited as [72]

items.name: Nakajima: projectivity over k[Δ] for Galois étale covers
items.statement: As the paper uses it: if Spec(B/ϖ) → Spec(A/ϖ) is finite Galois étale with group Δ and N' is an A/ϖ-module, then N' ⊗_{A/ϖ} B/ϖ is a projective k[Δ]-module.
items.note: If A → B is finite Galois étale with group Δ, then B is a projective A[Δ]-module, so N′ ⊗_{A/ϖ} B/ϖ is projective over k[Δ]. Neither library has this and no layer plans it for general rings. The nearest layer is ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.7 ('normal-basis maps ... tame normal-integral-basis'), whose scope is rings of integers. External input: S. Nakajima, Invent. Math. 75 (1984), Lemma 1, cited as [72] (‘Lemma 1 of [72]’)

items.name: Kaplansky: projective modules over local rings are free
items.statement: Every projective module, not necessarily finitely generated, over a local ring is free.
items.note: Kaplansky's theorem (every projective module over a local ring is free) is absent: Mathlib has only the finitely generated case. CG needs it for the non-finitely-generated k[Δ]-module (N ⊗_A B)/ϖ. The weaker Stacks 051G (projective, even flat, modules over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal are free) suffices, because k[Δ] is Artinian local. No layer plans either. External input: I. Kaplansky, Projective modules, Ann. of Math. (2) 68 (1958), 372–377, cited as [73]

items.name: Lemma 7.7 (freeness of N ⊗_A B modulo ϖ^n over R/ϖ^n)
items.statement: Let Spec(B) → Spec(A) be a finite Galois étale morphism of flat O-algebras with Galois group Δ, a finite abelian p-group, and let R denote the local ring O[Δ]. Then for any A-module N that is flat over O, (N ⊗_A B)/ϖ^n is a free R/ϖ^n-module for each n ≥ 1.
items.note: Combines nakajima-lemma-1, kaplansky/Stacks 051G, lemma-7-5 and lemma-7-6, all missing; no layer plans the freeness of (N ⊗_A B)/ϖ^n over (O/ϖ^n)[Δ] for Galois étale covers.

items.name: The perfect complexes C_n^∨ and C_n computing coherent (co)homology
items.statement: Take 𝓕 := 𝓔^* ⊗_{O_X} ω_X in nakajima-cech-complex. Then D ⊗ O/ϖ^n is a bounded complex of projective R/ϖ^n-modules computing H^i(Y, f^*(𝓕)/ϖ^n) = H^i(Y, 𝓔^* ⊗ ω_Y ⊗ O/ϖ^n). By [43, Ch. II.5, Lemma 1] it may be replaced by a quasi-isomorphic perfect complex C_n^∨ of R/ϖ^n-modules. Dualizing C_n^∨ gives a (chain) complex C_n whose homology groups are H_i(Y, 𝓔 ⊗ O/ϖ^n).
items.note: No layer builds perfect (O/ϖ^n)[Δ]-complexes C_n^∨ computing H^i(Y, E^* ⊗ ω ⊗ O/ϖ^n), with their duals C_n computing coherent homology. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked its weight-one version (Prop. 14.1) missing and planned its assembly over O through Khare–Thorne in P7. The step replacing a bounded projective complex by a perfect one (Mumford II.5 Lemma 1) is P7.

items.name: Toroidal compactifications of Hecke correspondences
items.statement: For γ ∈ G(A_F^{∞,p}), let L := K_Δ(Q) ⊂ G(A^∞) be the level of Y and L^γ := γLγ^{-1} ∩ L. By choosing suitable polyhedral cone decomposition data, there is an arithmetic toroidal compactification Y^γ, proper and smooth over O, of the Shimura variety of level L^γ, together with maps π_1, π_2 : Y^γ → Y. Here π_1 is associated to the inclusion L^γ → L and π_2 to right multiplication by γ on complex points.
items.note: Planned by C3 (Hecke translations extended to toroidal compactifications with compatible fans) together with C5 (integral good-prime PEL toroidal compactifications, which depend on C3). Neither description says explicitly that the Hecke extension is built on the integral models with Y^γ smooth and proper over O, as Lan §6.4.3 does. The C5 blueprint should state it; otherwise this is a gap. External input: K.-W. Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties, cited as [71, Sect. 6.4.3]

items.name: Hecke-equivariance of automorphic vector bundles on toroidal compactifications
items.statement: In the situation of lan-toroidal-hecke-correspondence there is an isomorphism φ : π_2^*𝓔 ≅ π_1^*𝓔 of sheaves on Y^γ, for the canonical or subcanonical extension 𝓔.
items.note: AutomorphicBundles B5 plans 'pullback, coefficient identification, and trace along Hecke correspondences' and B3 the canonical/subcanonical extensions, both over characteristic-zero canonical models (B3's reviewed node is complex-analytic). The isomorphism φ: π2^*E ≅ π1^*E of integral canonical/subcanonical extensions on Y^γ over O (Lan's Kuga-family Thm. 2.15(4)(c), with Lan–Suh's reduction to the Hodge bundle) is planned nowhere. External input: K.-W. Lan, Toroidal compactifications of PEL-type Kuga families, Algebra Number Theory, cited as [74, Thm. 2.15(4)(c)], together with ‘the fact that all automorphic vector bundles are constructed from the Hodge bundle’, Lan–Suh, Adv. Math. 242 (2013), cited as [18, Sect. 4.2]

items.name: Grothendieck–Serre (‘Verdier’) duality over O/ϖ^n with trace
items.statement: Let A = O/ϖ^n and π : Y_A := Y ×_O A → Spec A (proper smooth of relative dimension d) with dualizing sheaf ω_{Y_A}. For a (Δ-equivariant) locally free 𝒢 of finite rank: RHom(RHom(O_{Y_A}, 𝒢), A[0]) = RHom(𝒢, ω_{Y_A}[d]), compatibly with the trace morphism RΓ(Y_A, ω_{Y_A}[d]) → A[0] (on H^d: tr : H^d(Y_A, ω_{Y_A}) → A). Consequently H^i(Y, (f^*𝓕)_A) is Pontryagin dual to H^{d−i}(Y, Hom_{O_Y}(f^*𝓕, ω_Y)_A) = H^{d−i}(Y, (f^*𝓔)_A).
items.note: Coherent duality is planned only for curves: Tau Ceti JacobianChallenge Layer B (Serre duality over a field k) and StableReduction Layer 2 (relative dualizing sheaf of Cohen–Macaulay curves). SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3 only integrates those. Grothendieck–Serre duality with trace for smooth proper morphisms of any relative dimension d over O/ϖ^n, in the derived form CG uses, is planned nowhere. CG calls it 'Verdier duality' without a reference. External input: Grothendieck–Serre duality, invoked as ‘Verdier duality’ without a specific reference

items.name: Coherent Hecke operators T_γ via a duality pairing
items.statement: Let A = O/ϖ^n, 𝓕 = 𝓔^* ⊗ ω_X, M_A := M ⊗_O A for an O-module or sheaf M, and d = dim Y. Using verdier-serre-duality, define T_γ on H^i(Y, (f^*𝓕)_A) as the endomorphism corresponding to the pairing H^i(Y, (f^*𝓕)_A) ⊗_A H^{d−i}(Y, (f^*𝓔)_A) → A given by x ⊗ y ↦ tr(π_1^*(x) ∪ φπ_2^*(y)). Here π_1^*(x) ∪ φπ_2^*(y) is the image of the cup product of π_1^*(x) and φπ_2^*(y) under the natural map H^d(Y^γ, (𝓔^* ⊗ ω_{Y^γ} ⊗ 𝓔)_A) → H^d(Y^γ, (ω_{Y^γ})_A), and tr : H^d(Y^γ, (ω_{Y^γ})_A) → A is the trace.
items.note: No layer defines Hecke operators on integral coherent cohomology over O/ϖ^n through the Faltings–Chai pairing tr(π1^*(x) ∪ φπ2^*(y)). B5 is characteristic zero, and the IKM analogue (hecke-14) was marked missing. See sourceIssues E154 (tr is a trace map, not an isomorphism). External input: Approach of Faltings–Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties, cited as [75, p. 256], which avoids defining a trace for π_1 on cohomology

items.name: Lifting coherent Hecke operators to the perfect complex C_n^∨
items.statement: Let Y_A = Y ×_O A, π : Y_A → Spec A the structure map, and 𝒢 := (f^*𝓕)_A, a Δ-equivariant sheaf. Regard Rπ_*(𝒢) = RHom(O_{Y_A}, 𝒢) as an object of D^b(R) with R = A[Δ]. Verdier duality identifies Hom(RHom(O_{Y_A}, 𝒢), RHom(O_{Y_A}, 𝒢)) with Hom(RHom(O_{Y_A}, 𝒢) ⊗^L RHom(𝒢, ω_{Y_A}[d]), A[0]). T̃_γ is the element of the right-hand side obtained by composing three maps: (1) the pullback π_1^* ⊗ (φ ∘ π_2^*), into RHom(O_{Y^γ_A}, π_1^*𝒢) ⊗^L RHom(π_1^*𝒢, ω_{Y^γ_A}[d]); (2) the composition morphism to RHom(O_{Y^γ_A}, ω_{Y^γ_A}[d]); (3) the duality (trace) morphism to A[0]. Then T̃_γ induces the Hecke operator T_γ on H^i(Y_A, 𝒢). Since C_n^∨ ≅ Rπ_*(𝒢) in D^b(R) and C_n^∨ is perfect, T̃_γ lifts to a morphism of complexes T_γ : C_n^∨ → C_n^∨ inducing T_γ on cohomology [70, Tag 08FQ], and dually to C_n.
items.note: The derived-category morphism T̃_γ (pullback, composition, trace) on Rπ_*G ∈ D^b(A[Δ]) and its identification with T_γ on cohomology are planned nowhere. Only the final lift to the perfect complex C_n^∨ follows from Mathlib's K-projective API. IHG.2 would handle the Hecke image algebras once the action exists. See sourceIssues E143 (Δ-equivariance hypothesis on γ) and E154 (trace is a morphism, not an isomorphism).

items.name: Output of §7.2: localized perfect complexes in the coherent case
items.statement: Given a maximal ideal m of the Hecke algebra, for a judicious choice of Hecke operator T (as in §7.1), the complex lim→_m T^m C_n is a perfect complex of R-modules (R = A[Δ], A = O/ϖ^n) with homology H_i(Y, 𝓔_A)_m.
items.note: This depends on the missing coherent Hecke action. Once that exists, localisation is PadicFamilies L0a (U^{n!} projector on the finite (O/ϖ^n)[Δ]-modules of C_n) plus IHG.2. The paper only says the argument goes 'exactly as in the previous section'.

items.name: The invariant l0 for G = GL(1)/F
items.statement: For G = GL(1)/F, with F a number field of signature (r1, r2) not containing ζ_p, the invariant l0 equals r1 + r2 − 1.
items.note: The value r1 + r2 − 1 is Mathlib's unit rank.
