The CG invariant l0 = rank G(F∞) − rank K∞ − rank A∞ (p. 297), with q0, is defined in no library and planned in no layer: ALS.0 builds the symmetric space but names no l0, and AF.4 has cohomological representations but not the range [q0, q0 + l0]. The general definition sits in another cluster and should be routed with it.

items.name: Strategy for Theorem 5.16: minimal case by TWK patching, non-minimal case by Taylor's Ihara avoidance
items.statement: Given the patching theorem (Theorem 6.3) and complexes satisfying its boundedness condition (a), the proof of Theorem 5.16 runs as follows. (i) Minimal case: there is no prime x ∤ p at which ρ|D_x is ramified while r̄|D_x is unramified. For every N one builds a set Q_N of q primes x with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N. The Hecke rings T_{Q_N} are all quotients of one patched global deformation ring R∞, and R∞[1/p] is irreducible of the appropriate dimension. The sets Q_N come from the usual Taylor–Wiles–Kisin method, with modifications due to Thorne. R∞ is naturally a power series ring over R_loc, and its dimension is l0 less than in the classical case. Assume (a) cohomology vanishes outside the expected range and (b) the Hecke action on cohomology in that range comes from Galois representations with the expected properties. Then one builds complexes with R∞-actions, and Theorem 6.3 gives the conclusion. (ii) Non-minimal case: there are primes x with ρ|I_x unipotent, N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and r̄|D_x unramified. Here one uses Taylor's trick [11] to avoid Ihara's lemma. It needs only (a) control of the depth of the patched module on which R∞ acts and (b) the structure mod ϖ of the local deformation rings. Compared with the classical case, the dimension of R∞ and the depth of H^{l0}(P∞) are both exactly l0 smaller, so the argument goes through.
items.note: No layer plans the assembled conditional positive-defect lifting argument for Theorem 5.16 (GL2 over an imaginary quadratic field, l0 = 1) or for its GL_n form. The ingredients are planned: CG Theorem 6.3 is the reviewed node DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P8/patched-perfect-complexes-in-a-range-of-degrees ('R_∞ ∈ C_O of Krull dimension 1 + j + q − l₀'), Taylor–Wiles primes are GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5, and the Ihara-avoidance comparison is P9/R03.6. GL2ModularityLifting follows KW II with l0 = 0, and PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure covers only the unconditional ACC+ CM setting. Neither library has deformation theory or patching.

items.name: Taylor's Ihara-avoidance argument
items.statement: (External input. §8.1 invokes only the idea; it is applied in the proof of Theorem 9.19, p. 428, together with Lemma 8.2.) Taylor [11, Def. 2.1]: a finitely generated module M over a noetherian local ring A is nearly faithful if Ann_A(M) is nilpotent, i.e. every minimal prime of A lies in Supp M. [11, Lemma 2.2]: (1) if M is nearly faithful over A and I is an ideal, then M/IM is nearly faithful over A/I. (2) Suppose A is a catenary (e.g. excellent) local O-algebra, equidimensional, with all generic points of characteristic 0, and every prime of A minimal over ϖA contains a unique minimal prime of A. If M is an O-torsion-free A-module and M/ϖM is nearly faithful over A/ϖA, then M is nearly faithful over A. [11, Lemma 2.3]: if the m_A-depth of M is ≥ dim A, then Supp M is a union of irreducible components of Spec A; in particular M is nearly faithful if Spec A is irreducible. Application in the paper: put R^1_∞ = R^1_loc⟦x_1,…,x_g⟧ and R^2_∞ = R^χ_loc⟦x_1,…,x_g⟧, with R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ compatible with H^{l0}(P^1_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l0}(P^2_∞)/ϖ. Since Spec R^2_∞ is irreducible, H^{l0}(P^2_∞) is nearly faithful over R^2_∞ (the paper cites Theorem 6.4; the depth equality of Theorem 6.3(iii) together with [11, Lemma 2.3] also gives it). Reducing mod ϖ and transporting shows that H^{l0}(P^1_∞)/ϖ is nearly faithful over R^1_∞/ϖ. Then [11, Lemma 2.2(2)], with the hypotheses on R^1_∞ from Lemma 8.2(1),(4), shows H^{l0}(P^1_∞) is nearly faithful over R^1_∞, provided H^{l0}(P^1_∞) is p-torsion free. The paper deduces that from the fact that its associated primes are minimal primes of R^1_∞, all of characteristic 0.
items.locator: §8.1, p. 401 (applied in the proof of Theorem 9.19 with Lemma 8.2)
items.note: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra plans this algebra in two forms: the module form with near-faithfulness in R03.6, and the derived form in P9 (reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara, after ACC+ Prop 6.3.8). PA.3 is the ACC+ arithmetic analogue. The paper and Taylor [11] are sources for P9/R03.6. I did not check the item's lemma number '[11, Lemma 2.2]' against Taylor's paper; neither library has anything here. External input: R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations II, Publ. IHES 108 (2008) 183–239 ([11]); in particular Lemma 2.2 and Proposition 3.1

items.name: GL(1) example: trivial residual character, Selmer and dual Selmer groups
items.statement: Let F be a number field of signature (r1, r2), p an odd prime and ζ_p ∉ F. Take G = GL(1)/F. Up to twist the only residual representation is the trivial character r̄: G_F → F_p^×. Its minimal deformations are the everywhere unramified ones. Here ad(r̄) = F_p and ad(r̄)(1) = μ_p. Define the Selmer condition L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, F_p) as follows: for finite v (including v | p), L_v is the set of classes unramified on inertia; for v | ∞, L_v = H^1(F_v, F_p) = 0. The Selmer group H^1_L(F, F_p) is the group of global classes lying in L_v at every v, i.e. the everywhere-unramified classes. The dual Selmer group H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) is cut out by the annihilators L*_v = L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, μ_p) under local Tate duality. The invariant for this example is ℓ0 = r1 + r2 − 1.
items.note: These are the instance M = F_p, M^∨(1) = μ_p with unramified local conditions of the planned generic Selmer construction. SelmerIwasawaCohomology L2 owns the generic Selmer kernel (the unreviewed RS-08 proposal says so), R02.5 its deformation use, R02.4 and CFT layer 5 the local duality defining L_v^⊥. The value ℓ0 = r1 + r2 − 1 is only a number here. Near miss: Mathlib's IsDedekindDomain.selmerGroup is the valuative group K(S,n) ⊂ K^×/(K^×)^n, not a Galois-cohomological Selmer group (the library audit records the latter as absent).

items.name: GL(1): dim H^1_L(F,F_p) − dim H^1_{L*}(F,μ_p) = −(r1+r2−1)
items.statement: Assume p odd and ζ_p ∉ F, with F of signature (r1, r2). Then dim H^1_L(F, F_p) − dim H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) = −(r1 + r2 − 1). The Greenberg–Wiles count gives this as follows. (1) The global term |H^0(F,F_p)|/|H^0(F,μ_p)| = p, because ζ_p ∉ F; this contributes +1. (2) Each archimedean v has H^0(F_v, F_p) one-dimensional and L_v = 0, so the infinite places contribute −r1 − r2. (3) Each v | p has H^0(F_v, F_p) one-dimensional and L_v = H^1(Gal(k̄_v/k_v), F_p) one-dimensional, by inflation–restriction 0 → H^1(Gal(k̄_v/k_v), F_p) → H^1(F_v, F_p) → H^1(I_v, F_p); this contributes 1 − 1 = 0. (4) Finite v ∤ p contribute 0. The same equality also follows from class field theory. First, dim H^1_L(F, F_p) = dim Cl(F)/p. Second, H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) = H^1_fppf(O_F, μ_p), whose dimension is dim Cl(F)[p] + dim O_F^×/O_F^{×p}, and dim O_F^×/O_F^{×p} = r1 + r2 − 1.
items.note: Not named in any layer. It specializes the planned R02.5 dimension formula to M = F_p with unramified conditions, and adds a class-field-theory cross-check. The library supplies parts of the cross-check: Mathlib's unit theorem gives ℤ-rank r1 + r2 − 1, and Tau Ceti proves 1 → O^×/(O^×)^n → K(∅,n) → Cl[n] → 1 (valuative Selmer group). The step dim H¹_L(F,F_p) = dim Cl(F)/p needs the Hilbert class field, planned but unbuilt in tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 13. See sourceIssues E156 (L_v^* has codimension one, not dimension one).

items.name: Flat Kummer sequence: H^1_fppf(O_F, μ_p) as an extension of Cl(F)[p] by units mod p-th powers
items.statement: For a number field F and a prime p there is an exact sequence 0 → O_F^×/O_F^{×p} → H^1_fppf(Spec O_F, μ_p) → Cl(F)[p] → 0. It comes from the fppf Kummer sequence 1 → μ_p → G_m →(·p) G_m → 1 on Spec O_F together with Hilbert 90: H^1_fppf(O_F, G_m) = H^1_et(O_F, G_m) = Pic(O_F) = Cl(F) [33, III Prop 4.9]. If ζ_p ∉ F, Dirichlet's unit theorem gives dim_{F_p} O_F^×/O_F^{×p} = r1 + r2 − 1. Moreover H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) = H^1_fppf(O_F, μ_p) ⊂ H^1(F, μ_p) = F^×/F^{×p} (the last equality is classical Hilbert 90 / Kummer theory).
items.note: Neither library has flat cohomology of Spec O_F. SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2 plans fppf sheaf cohomology in general, but not this sequence. Near miss: Tau Ceti proves the same sequence for any Dedekind domain with the valuative Selmer group K(∅,n) in place of H¹_fppf(O_F, μ_n); Mathlib has Cl ≃ Pic and the unit theorem; Tau Ceti has the injection F^×/(F^×)^n ↪ H¹(G_F, μ_n), but not its surjectivity (Hilbert 90). The identification H¹_fppf(O_F, μ_p) ≅ K(∅,p) is in neither library. External input: J.S. Milne, Étale Cohomology, Princeton 1980 ([33]), Ch. III, Prop. 4.9 (Hilbert 90 for G_m in the flat topology); Dirichlet's unit theorem

items.name: GL(1) arithmetic spaces Y, Y_Q, X_Q
items.statement: Notation: U = ∏_v O_v^× is the maximal compact subgroup of the finite ideles, and K∞ is the identity component of the maximal compact subgroup of (F ⊗ R)^×, so K∞ ≅ (S^1)^{r2}. Set Y := F^×\A_F^×/U K∞ (the paper writes 'J_F/F^×'). Let Q be a set of auxiliary primes v with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n. Define U_Q by replacing O_v^× with O_v^{×p^n}, its unique subgroup of index p^n, for each v ∈ Q, and set Y_Q := F^×\A_F^×/U_Q K∞. Let A^0_∞ be the identity component of the R-points of the maximal Q-split torus in the centre, and set X_Q := F^×\A_F^×/U_Q K∞ A^0_∞. In GL(n) notation, Y = Y_0(Q) and Y_Q = Y_1(Q). Y_Q is an R-bundle over X_Q, so the two have the same cohomology.
items.note: Y, Y_Q and X_Q are the GL₁ case of the planned adelic quotients, with the split-centre quotient A⁰_∞; AA.5 names the GL₁ comparison explicitly. The library has carriers only: Mathlib's NumberField.IdeleGroup and IdeleClassGroup, without the quotients by U_Q K∞ or A⁰_∞.

items.name: GL(1): geometry and cohomology of X_Q, Hecke and diamond operators
items.statement: (a) The fibres of Y_Q are the connected components of coker(O_F^× → R^{×r1} × C^{×r2}/K∞), which is (S^1)^{r1+r2−1} × R. So each connected component of X_Q is a torus (S^1)^{r1+r2−1}, of dimension ℓ0 = r1 + r2 − 1. The paper describes π_0(X_Q) as 'the maximal quotient of the ray class group of conductor Q and exponent p^n'. Correctly, π_0(X_Q) = F^×\A_F^×/U_Q (F⊗R)^{×,0}: an extension of the narrow class group by a quotient of ∏_{v∈Q} O_v^×/O_v^{×p^n} (see sourceIssues E160). (b) H^0(X_Q, Z_p) ≅ Z_p[π_0(X_Q)] (printed Z_p[RCl(Q)/p^n]), by class field theory. (c) For v prime to Q with uniformizer π_v, the Hecke operator T_{π_v} acts on the component group through the class of [π_v]. For v | Q there are diamond operators ⟨α⟩, α ∈ O_v^×. (d) The action of T_Q on the higher cohomology is propagated from H^0 by the Künneth formula, so T_Q acts the same way on all cohomology groups.
items.note: No layer names the explicit description: components are tori of dimension r1 + r2 − 1, the correct π₀(X_Q), H⁰ = Z_p[π₀], Hecke operators through [π_v], diamond operators, and Künneth propagation. The pieces are planned: compactness and identity component of the norm-one idele class group (tauceti GlobalNumberFields layers 6–7), the GL₁ validation AA.5, Hecke correspondences ALS.3, and TC.4's 'GL_1 class-field … normalization examples'. The libraries have only the idele carriers and Dirichlet's unit theorem (Mathlib). See sourceIssues E160 (π_0(X_Q) is not RCl(Q)/p^n).

items.name: GL(1): Galois representation to T_Q and surjection R_Q ↠ T_{Q,m}
items.statement: By class field theory there is a Galois representation ρ_Q: G_F → T_Q^×. Via the local Artin map, the diamond operators correspond to the action of the inertia subgroups at v | Q. Localising at the maximal ideal m of T_Q corresponding to r̄ gives a deformation of r̄ ramified only at Q. If R_Q is the deformation ring of r̄ unramified outside Q, there is a surjection R_Q ↠ T_{Q,m}. Both rings are naturally modules over the ring of diamond operators Z_p[Δ_Q] = Z_p[U/U_Q]: on R_Q via Yoneda's lemma and local class field theory, on T_{Q,m} via the Hecke operators. The two actions agree.
items.note: Not planned as stated. TC.4 plans 'GL_1 class-field … normalization examples' of the Hecke-to-Galois construction, and GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/R04.5 plan universal rings and the diamond structure at Taylor–Wiles primes. No layer builds the rank-one ring R_Q, the surjection R_Q ↠ T_{Q,m}, or the agreement of the two Z_p[Δ_Q]-actions. Global and local Artin maps are planned in tauceti ClassFieldTheory layers 7 and 11–12. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: GL(1): existence of Taylor–Wiles primes annihilating the dual Selmer group iff ζ_p ∉ F
items.statement: In the GL(1) setting, a Taylor–Wiles prime is a prime v with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n that satisfies two conditions. The automorphic condition (no extra cohomology from X to X_0(Q)) holds automatically, since X = X_0(Q). The Galois condition is that one can choose |Q| = dim H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) = dim H^1_L(F, F_p) + ℓ0 primes that exactly annihilate the dual Selmer group H^1_{L*}(F, μ_p) = H^1_fppf(O_F, μ_p) ⊂ H^1(F, μ_p) = F^×/F^{×p}. Allowing ramification at v in the Selmer condition forces dual Selmer classes to split completely at v. So a class [α] is killed by v when its image in H^1(F_v, μ_p) = H^1(F_v, F_p) is non-trivial (here μ_p ≅ F_p as a G_{F_v}-module because N(v) ≡ 1 mod p). This happens exactly when Frob_v is non-trivial in Gal(F(α^{1/p}, ζ_p)/F) and N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^n. By Chebotarev such v exist unless F(α^{1/p}) ⊂ F(ζ_{p^n}). Since F(ζ_{p^n})/F is abelian, that containment would make F(α^{1/p})/F Galois and abelian, hence F(ζ_p) ⊂ F(α^{1/p}), and comparing degrees gives ζ_p ∈ F. Hence, if ζ_p ∉ F, suitable primes annihilating the dual Selmer group can be chosen.
items.note: R04.5 plans Taylor–Wiles primes via 'Chebotarev, residual-image lemmas and dual Selmer calculations'. The rank-one argument is not named: there ζ_p ∉ F replaces the residual-image hypothesis, and Kummer theory, F(α^{1/p}) ⊄ F(ζ_{p^n}), supplies the Chebotarev condition. Its inputs are planned or partial: Chebotarev (tauceti Chebotarev layer 10, unbuilt; Tau Ceti has Frobenius prime sets but not the density theorem) and Kummer theory (tauceti ProfiniteCohomology layer 9; the Kummer injection is built, surjectivity is not). External input: Kummer theory; Chebotarev density theorem

items.name: GL(1): R^unr ≅ Z_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ Z_p] (circular illustration)
items.statement: Assume p odd and ζ_p ∉ F. Let R^unr be the universal deformation ring (O = Z_p) of the trivial character r̄: G_F → F_p^× for everywhere-unramified deformations. The patching result gives an isomorphism R^unr ≅ Z_p[Cl(O_F) ⊗ Z_p]. Hence the Galois group of the maximal unramified abelian p-power extension of F is isomorphic to Cl(F) ⊗ Z_p. (Printed as 'the class group of F'; see sourceIssues E163.)
items.note: The Galois-side consequence, Gal(F^{ur,ab}(p)/F) ≅ Cl(F) ⊗ Z_p, is planned in tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 13 ('gal_hilbertClassField_equiv_classGroup … Prove also the maximal unramified properties'). No layer, including GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2, names the identification of the unramified deformation ring of a character with the completed group ring of that Galois group. The paper's patching proof is circular (Remark 8.1), so only the statement needs an owner. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: The invariant l0 for Res_{F/Q}PGL(n)
items.statement: For a number field F of signature (r1, r2) and an integer n ≥ 1: l0 := r1·(rank SL_n(R) − rank SO_n(R)) + r2·(rank SL_n(C) − rank SU_n(C)). Here 'rank' is the absolute rank of the real Lie group, i.e. the dimension of a Cartan subalgebra; the paper's 'rank over R' means this, not the R-split rank. Explicitly, l0 = r1·(n−1)/2 + r2(n−1) for n odd, and l0 = r1·(n−2)/2 + r2(n−1) for n even.
items.note: No layer defines l0 = rank G(R) − rank K∞ for Res_{F/Q}PGL_n; the patching layers P8/P9 use l₀ only as an integer parameter. PAPER-VENKATESH-19/1 marked the analogous δ as planned at ALS.0/ALS.1, but neither stage's text mentions it. Near miss: Mathlib's LieAlgebra.rank is the absolute rank via the characteristic polynomial of ad, but nothing computes it for sl_n(R), so_n, sl_n(C) or su_n, and no rank of a real Lie group exists. I checked that the absolute-rank reading gives the printed closed formulas for both parities of n.

items.name: The invariant q0 (via 2q0 + l0)
items.statement: 2q0 + l0 := r1·(dim SL_n(R) − dim SO_n(R)) + r2·(dim SL_n(C) − dim SU_n(C)) = r1·(n² − 1 − n(n−1)/2) + r2·(2(n² − 1) − (n² − 1)), where dim means real dimension. Equivalently, q0 := ((2q0 + l0) − l0)/2.
items.note: Not defined in any layer, like l0 (see def-l0). It needs the real dimensions of SL_n(R), SO_n(R), SL_n(C) and SU_n(C), i.e. of the symmetric spaces that ALS.0 builds, but the invariant q0 itself is not planned. Mathlib has no dimension formula for these real Lie groups.

items.name: Meaning of q0 and l0: dimension and cuspidal cohomology range
items.statement: Let G := Res_{F/Q}(PGL(n)). Then 2q0 + l0 is the real dimension of the associated locally symmetric space. The degrees in which cuspidal automorphic representations π of G that are tempered at ∞ contribute to cuspidal cohomology are exactly [q0, …, q0 + l0]. In particular q0 is an integer.
items.note: The dimension statement follows once ALS.0 builds the symmetric space and q0 is defined. The tempered cuspidal range [q0, q0 + l0] (Borel–Wallach VII Thm 6.7) is planned nowhere: AF.1 defines relative Lie algebra cochains and AF.4 cohomological representations, but no layer computes the (g,K)-cohomology of tempered representations. PAPER-VENKATESH-19/2 (the same fact, with multiplicities) is also missing and was routed to its proposed ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpacesPartII. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: A. Borel, N. Wallach, Continuous cohomology, discrete subgroups, and representations of reductive groups, 2nd ed., AMS 2000 ([9]), Ch. VII, Theorem 6.7, p. 226

items.name: Odd representation at the archimedean places
items.statement: Let V be an n-dimensional representation of G_F over a field of characteristic ≠ 2. V is odd at v | ∞ if the action of G_{F_v} is odd. At complex places this is no condition. At a real place v it means that complex conjugation c_v ∈ G_{F_v} satisfies Trace(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1}. [Since char ≠ 2, c_v is diagonalisable with eigenvalues ±1. The intended condition, and the one needed for equation (1), is that the ±1-eigenspaces of c_v have dimensions differing by at most one. The printed trace criterion, computed in the coefficient field, is equivalent to this in characteristic 0, and in characteristic ℓ exactly when ℓ > n + 1 (n even) or ℓ > n (n odd); see sourceIssues E164.]
items.locator: §8.4, p. 406; Part 2 introduction, p. 383 (recalled before Theorem 5.16 for Gal(C/R) → GL_n(O); hypothesis (5))
items.note: ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.4 plans rank-two oddness, and G7 plans only polarized oddness. The paper's unpolarized condition Tr(c_v) ∈ {−1, 0, 1} in arbitrary rank is not planned. For n = 2 in characteristic ≠ 2 it is equivalent to det(c_v) = −1, so the R01.4 case is recovered. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E164 (trace criterion fails in small characteristic).

items.name: Equation (1): Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad^0 V) = [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 + l0
items.statement: Let V be a representation of G_F of dimension n over a field of characteristic ≠ 2 that is odd at every v | ∞. [Here 'odd' must mean that at each real v the ±1-eigenspaces of c_v have dimensions differing by at most one. The printed criterion Trace(c_v) ∈ {−1,0,1} is equivalent to this only in characteristic 0 or characteristic ℓ with ℓ > n+1 (n even) or ℓ > n (n odd). Under §8.5 (p > n) it can fail only for n even and p = n + 1; see sourceIssues E164.] Then Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad^0(V)) = r1·((n²+1)/2 − 1) + r2(n² − 1) if n is odd, and r1·(n²/2 − 1) + r2(n² − 1) if n is even. In both cases, (1): Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad^0(V)) = [F:Q]·n(n−1)/2 + l0.
items.note: R02.6 plans the KW II rank-two inequalities 'with infinity and p=2 contributions visible'; no layer computes the rank-n archimedean invariants. I checked the formula: if c_v has eigenvalue multiplicities a, b with a + b = n and |a − b| ≤ 1, then h⁰ = a² + b² − 1. That is (n² − 1)/2 or n²/2 − 1 at real places and n² − 1 at complex places, and in both parities the sum is [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 + l0. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E164 (trace criterion fails in small characteristic).

items.name: Standing hypotheses of §8.5 on p, F, k and r̄
items.statement: Global notation: O is the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Q_p, with uniformizer ϖ and residue field k (p ≥ 3). C_O is the category of complete Noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k, with continuous O-algebra maps. Let p > n be a prime unramified in F, and assume Frac W(k) contains the image of every embedding F ↪ Q̄_p. Fix a continuous absolutely irreducible representation r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) such that: (i) for each v | p, r̄|G_{F_v} is Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0, 1, …, n−1] for each τ: O_F → k factoring through O_{F_v}; (ii) for each v ∤ p, r̄|G_{F_v} has at worst unipotent ramification, and N_{F/Q}(v) ≡ 1 mod p if r̄ is ramified at v; (iii) r̄|G_{F_v} is odd for each v | ∞.
items.note: Every clause is planned except oddness at real places in rank n, which is missing (see odd-representation). The planned clauses are the coefficient conventions (R03.1), continuous absolutely irreducible r̄ (R01.1), the Fontaine–Laffaille condition at v | p (L7, R07.3), and unipotent ramification away from p (R08.2/L7). This follows the precedent of PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/setup-12. The libraries have only generic ingredients such as the absolute Galois group.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille representation with weights [0,…,n−1] (residual and framed-lift versions)
items.statement: For v | p, with F_v/Q_p unramified and p > n: a representation of G_{F_v} on a finite O-module is Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0, 1, …, n−1] for each τ if it lies in the essential image of the Fontaine–Laffaille functor on (O ⊗ O_{F_v})-Fontaine–Laffaille modules. For each embedding τ: O_{F_v} → W(k) (equivalently O_{F_v} → k), the τ-part of the associated filtered module must have its jumps exactly at 0, 1, …, n−1, each with multiplicity one.
items.note: Planned: the essential-image condition with τ-labelled jumps 0, …, n−1 is L7's Fontaine–Laffaille condition, built on R07.3's functor over an absolutely unramified base. Since p > n, the weights lie in R07.3's range [0, p−2]. PA.1 consumes the condition for ACC+. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations, Publ. IHES 108 (2008) ([3]), §2.4.1

items.name: The fixed determinant character ξ
items.statement: Fix a continuous character ξ: G_F → O^× lifting det(r̄) such that ξ|I_v = ε^{n(n−1)/2} for all v | p and ξ|I_v = 1 for all v ∤ p. Here ε is the p-adic cyclotomic character. (Printed example: 'we can simply take ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}'. That is valid only when det r̄ = ε̄^{n(n−1)/2}, as holds under Theorem 5.16(7). In general take ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}·[det(r̄)ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2}]^~, using the Teichmüller lift of an everywhere-unramified character.)
items.note: Choosing the fixed determinant is part of the planned deformation datum (as in PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/setup-12). The library has ingredients only: Mathlib's cyclotomicCharacter and Tau Ceti's local Teichmüller map on residue-field units; there is no Teichmüller lift of global characters. The printed example ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2} is valid only when det r̄ = ε̄^{n(n−1)/2}. The general ξ in the item works because det r̄ · ε̄^{−n(n−1)/2} is unramified everywhere, by the Fontaine–Laffaille and unipotent hypotheses. See sourceIssues E170 (printed ξ needs det r̄ = ε̄^{n(n−1)/2}).

items.name: Prime sets S_p, R, Q, S, S_Q, T
items.statement: S_p is the set of primes of F above p. R is a finite set of primes of F disjoint from S_p that contains every prime at which r̄ ramifies and satisfies N_{F/Q}(v) ≡ 1 mod p for each v ∈ R; these are the primes away from p where ramification is allowed. Q is a finite set of primes of F disjoint from R ∪ S_p (the Taylor–Wiles primes). Put S = S_p ⊔ R, S_Q = S ⊔ Q and T = S_p ∪ R (the framing set).
items.note: These are the bookkeeping data of the planned global deformation problems: ramification set, framed places T, and auxiliary set Q. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E169 (Lemma 8.2 needs r̄|G_{F_v} trivial on R).

items.name: Framed Fontaine–Laffaille deformation ring R_v (v | p)
items.statement: For v | p, R_v is the framed Fontaine–Laffaille O-deformation ring of r̄|G_{F_v}: it represents framed lifts to objects of C_O with determinant ξ|G_{F_v} that are Fontaine–Laffaille with τ-weights [0, 1, …, n−1] for each τ: O_{F_v} ↪ W(k). (Printed as 'for each τ: O_F ↪ W(k)'.)
items.note: Planned: this is ACC+ Prop 6.2.14's R_v^FL, which L7 exports, with the determinant fixed via R08.1. The printed 'τ: O_F ↪ W(k)' should read τ: O_{F_v} ↪ W(k), as the item already records (sourceIssues E167). Nothing is in the libraries; the audit lists framed representability as absent.

items.name: Formal smoothness of the Fontaine–Laffaille framed deformation ring
items.statement: For v | p (F_v/Q_p unramified, p > n, r̄|G_{F_v} Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0,…,n−1] for each τ), the ring R_v is formally smooth over O of relative dimension n² − 1 + [F_v : Q_p]·n(n−1)/2.
items.note: Planned at L7. The variable-determinant version is ACC+ Prop 6.2.14(3), formally smooth of dimension 1 + n² + [F_v:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 (read in arXiv:1812.09999); the fixed-determinant count n² − 1 + [F_v:Q_p]n(n−1)/2 must be recomputed at L7. I did not check the CHT numbering 'Proposition 2.4.3'. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor [3], Proposition 2.4.3 (stated there in the unitary-group setting; the paper applies it with GL_n and fixed determinant)

items.name: Level-raising characters χ_v (v ∈ R)
items.statement: For each v ∈ R choose a tuple χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}) of pairwise distinct characters χ_{v,i}: I_v → 1 + m_O ⊂ O^× with ∏_i χ_{v,i} trivial. Needed in addition (implicit in the paper): each χ_{v,i} = χ'_{v,i} ∘ Art_{F_v}^{-1}|_{I_v} for a character χ'_{v,i}: O_{F_v}^× → 1 + m_O. Equivalently, χ'_{v,i} factors through k_v^× and has p-power order, as in [11, §3].
items.note: These are the data of the ACC+ §6.2.15 level-raising deformation problem, which L7 exports. The unreviewed RS-08 proposal makes R08.2 the owner of away-from-p local types in the required rank. ACC+ defines the χ_i on O_{F_v}^× through Art_{F_v}, which is the implicit requirement the item records (sourceIssues E168). Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Unipotent-type framed local deformation ring R_v^1 (v ∈ R)
items.statement: For v ∈ R, R_v^1 is the universal framed O-deformation ring of r̄|G_{F_v} for lifts with determinant ξ such that every σ ∈ I_v has characteristic polynomial (X − 1)^n. D_v^1 denotes the corresponding local deformation problem.
items.note: Planned: this is ACC+ §6.2.15 with all χ_i = 1 (R_v^1, Prop 6.2.16), exported by L7, with R08.2 owning away-from-p types. ACC+ and Taylor assume r̄|G_{F_v} trivial and do not fix the determinant. CG fixes ξ and states no triviality hypothesis, so the layer must carry both variants. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: χ-type framed local deformation ring R_v^{χ_v} (v ∈ R)
items.statement: For v ∈ R, R_v^{χ_v} is the universal framed O-deformation ring of r̄|G_{F_v} for lifts with determinant ξ such that every σ ∈ I_v has characteristic polynomial ∏_i (X − χ_{v,i}(σ)). D_v^χ denotes the corresponding local deformation problem.
items.note: Planned: this is ACC+ §6.2.15's D_v^χ with pairwise distinct χ_i (Prop 6.2.17), exported by L7, and a fixed inertial type in R08.2's sense. The same caveats apply as for R_v^1: the determinant is fixed here, and triviality of r̄|G_{F_v} is needed for the component statements. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E168 (χ_{v,i} must come from O_{F_v}^×) and E169 (component statements need r̄|G_{F_v} trivial).

items.name: Local deformation rings R^1_loc and R^χ_loc
items.statement: R^1_loc := (⊗̂_{v∈S_p} R_v) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v∈R} R_v^1) and R^χ_loc := (⊗̂_{v∈S_p} R_v) ⊗̂ (⊗̂_{v∈R} R_v^{χ_v}). All completed tensor products are over O.
items.note: Planned: the completed tensor product over O (R03.1) of the planned local rings, as in ACC+ §6.2.22's R^{T,loc}_S (L7 export) and R04.3's presentation base. Neither library has completed tensor products of complete local O-algebras.

items.name: Lemma 8.2(1): R^1_loc and R^χ_loc are p-torsion free and equidimensional
items.statement: [Hypotheses as in §8.5. The cited proof also needs r̄|G_{F_v} trivial for every v ∈ R and the characters χ_{v,i} of the form in level-raising-characters-chi-v; see sourceIssues E169, E168. Moreover the cited results ([11, Prop 3.1], [76, Lemma 3.3]) give only that all generic points have characteristic 0, not p-torsion-freeness of the non-reduced rings; see sourceIssues E165.] Each of R^1_loc and R^χ_loc is p-torsion free and equidimensional of dimension 1 + |S_p ∪ R|(n² − 1) + [F:Q]·n(n−1)/2.
items.note: Planned at L7 as the fixed-determinant analogue of ACC+ Lemma 6.2.25(1). The dimension changes by one per place (n² − 1 instead of n²), and ACC+ asserts characteristic-zero generic points rather than p-torsion-freeness. The hypothesis r̄|G_{F_v} trivial for v ∈ R, missing from CG, must be kept. Its input BLGHT Lemma 3.3 is itself unplanned (see blght-lemma-3-3-completed-tensor). Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E165 (only characteristic-0 minimal primes), E168 (form of the χ_{v,i}) and E169 (needs r̄|G_{F_v} trivial on R).

items.name: Lemma 8.2(2): R^1_loc/ϖ ≅ R^χ_loc/ϖ
items.statement: There is a natural isomorphism R^1_loc/ϖ ≅ R^χ_loc/ϖ.
items.note: The isomorphism holds because each χ_{v,i} ≡ 1 mod ϖ. It is the 'common residual specialization' that P9's reviewed node P9/support-transport-avoiding-ihara takes as a hypothesis (R_∞/ϖ ≅ R′_∞/ϖ), supplied by L7's local comparisons. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Lemma 8.2(3): Spec R^χ_loc is irreducible
items.statement: [Needs r̄|G_{F_v} trivial for each v ∈ R, as in [11, Prop 3.1]; it is false in the stated generality, see sourceIssues E169.] The topological space Spec R^χ_loc is irreducible.
items.note: Planned at L7 as the fixed-determinant analogue of ACC+ Lemma 6.2.25(2). ACC+ assumes r̄|G_{F_v} trivial for v ∈ R, and CG's statement without it is recorded as sourceIssues E169. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Lemma 8.2(4): components of Spec R^1_loc/ϖ lie in unique components of Spec R^1_loc
items.statement: [Hypotheses as in lemma-8-2-1.] Every irreducible component of Spec R^1_loc/ϖ is contained in a unique irreducible component of Spec R^1_loc.
items.note: Planned at L7 as the analogue of the last sentence of ACC+ Lemma 6.2.25(1), under the same hypotheses as lemma-8-2-1. Nothing is in the libraries. See sourceIssues E169 (needs r̄|G_{F_v} trivial for v ∈ R).

items.name: Taylor's local deformation rings at level-raising primes (Tay08, Prop 3.1)
items.statement: Setting of [11, §3]: n ≥ 1, a prime p > n, v ∤ p with #k(v) ≡ 1 mod p, and r̄|G_{F_v} trivial. Let χ_{v,1},…,χ_{v,n}: G_{F_v} → 1 + m_O be continuous characters, so that each χ_{v,i}|I_v has order dividing #k(v) − 1; equivalently, via Art, characters of O_{F_v}^× trivial mod ϖ. Let I^χ be the ideal of the universal lifting ring R^loc_v cut out by char_{ρ(σ)}(X) = ∏_j (X − χ_{v,j}(σ)) for all σ ∈ I_v, and write I^1 = I^{(1,…,1)}. (1) If the χ_{v,i}|I_v are pairwise distinct, then Spec R^loc_v/I^χ is irreducible, its generic point has characteristic 0, and R^loc_v/I^χ has Krull dimension n² + 1. (2) R^loc_v/(ϖ, I^χ) = R^loc_v/(ϖ, I^1). (3) Every irreducible component of Spec R^loc_v/I^1 has dimension n² + 1, all its generic points have characteristic 0, and every prime of R^loc_v/I^1 minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime. (4) An analogous statement holds for a 'Steinberg' quotient, which is O-flat by construction. No O-flatness is asserted for R^loc_v/I^χ or R^loc_v/I^1; the proof shows only that (R^loc_v/I^χ)_red is O-flat. (With the determinant fixed, p ∤ n, the Krull dimensions become n²; this is an inference, not stated in [11].)
items.note: Planned: ACC+ Props 6.2.16–6.2.17 restate Taylor's Prop 3.1 and are part of the ACC+ §6.2 input that L7 exports; R08.2 owns dimensions and components of away-from-p types. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations II, Publ. IHES 108 (2008), Proposition 3.1 ([11]); statement as paraphrased in Allen et al., arXiv:1812.09999, §6.2.15–6.2.17

items.name: Completed tensor products of local deformation rings (BLGHT11, Lemma 3.3)
items.statement: [76, Lemma 3.3] (BLGHT11, stated to fill a gap in [11, p. 218]). Let C^noeth_O be the category of complete noetherian local O-algebras with residue field k. Call A geometrically integral (resp. geometrically irreducible) if A ⊗_O O_{L'} is a domain (resp. has irreducible Spec) for every finite extension L'/L = Frac O. (2) If A, B are O-flat domains in C^noeth_O, then dim(A ⊗̂_O B) = dim A + dim B − 1. (3) If A, B are O-flat and geometrically integral (resp. irreducible), then A ⊗̂_O B is O-flat and geometrically integral (resp. irreducible). (5) Suppose A has minimal primes p_1,…,p_r and B has minimal primes q_1,…,q_s, with every A/p_i and B/q_j O-flat and geometrically integral. Then the minimal primes of A ⊗̂_O B are exactly the distinct ideals p_i(A ⊗̂ B) + q_j(A ⊗̂ B). (7) Suppose in addition that for every prime q of A (resp. B) minimal over ϖ, A/q (resp. B/q) is geometrically integral and q contains a unique minimal prime. Then every prime of A ⊗̂_O B minimal over ϖ contains a unique minimal prime. (8) If X/Spec O is flat of finite type and x is a closed point with residue field k, then after a finite extension L'/L every minimal prime p of Ô_{X,x} ⊗ O_{L'} has (Ô_{X,x} ⊗ O_{L'})/p O_{L'}-flat and geometrically integral. (Parts (1), (4), (6), (9) are auxiliary or the k-analogues.) The paper applies this in the proof of Lemma 8.2 to the factors R_v (formally smooth), R_v^1 and R_v^{χ_v}.
items.note: Not named in any layer. It is a proof input of ACC+ Lemma 6.2.25, which L7 exports, but it is pure commutative algebra. R03.1 plans only when completed tensor products stay Noetherian and local, and R03.3 plans 'equidimensionality, associated-prime and support lemmas for finite modules', not the components of a completed tensor product. BLGHT11 was not available to me, so I did not check its exact hypotheses; the published lemma may also require geometric irreducibility of the components' generic fibres. Neither library has completed tensor products of complete local O-algebras. External input: T. Barnet-Lamb, D. Geraghty, M. Harris, R. Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy II, Publ. RIMS 47 (2011) 29–98 ([76]), Lemma 3.3

items.name: Residual condition at Taylor–Wiles primes v ∈ Q
items.statement: For each v ∈ Q assume r̄|G_{F_v} ≅ s̄_v ⊕ ψ̄_v, where ψ̄_v is a generalized eigenspace of Frobenius of dimension 1. (r̄ is unramified at v, since v ∉ R.)
items.note: Planned. CG needs only one one-dimensional generalized eigenspace ψ̄_v, not n distinct eigenvalues as in ACC+ §6.2.18, so R04.5 must state this eigenline form. The unreviewed RS-08 proposal makes R04.5 the owner of 'Actual Taylor–Wiles auxiliary-prime selection with prescribed congruences and eigenlines'. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Taylor–Wiles local deformation problem D_v (v ∈ Q)
items.statement: For v ∈ Q, D_v is the deformation problem, in the sense of [3, Defn 2.2.2], consisting of lifts ρ of r̄|G_{F_v} with determinant ξ of the form ρ ≅ s_v ⊕ ψ_v. Here s_v (resp. ψ_v) lifts s̄_v (resp. ψ̄_v), and I_v acts on s_v and on ψ_v by (possibly different) scalars.
items.note: Planned: this is the Taylor–Wiles local condition of R04.5's handoff. CG's block form, s_v ⊕ ψ_v with inertia acting by scalars on each block, differs from ACC+ §6.2.18 (n distinct eigenvalues, lifts ≅ γ1 ⊕ … ⊕ γn), so R04.5 must record it separately. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Selmer condition L_v at v ∈ Q
items.statement: L_v ⊂ H^1(G_{F_v}, ad^0(r̄)) is the subspace determined by all deformations of r̄|G_{F_v} to k[ε]/ε² of type D_v. L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(G_{F_v}, ad^0(r̄)(1)) is its annihilator under local Tate duality.
items.note: Planned: the tangent subspace of D_v in H¹(G_v, ad⁰r̄) belongs to R02.5's tangent-condition identifications, and L_v^⊥ comes from local duality (R02.4, tauceti ClassFieldTheory layer 5). Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: dim_k L_v − h^0(G_v, ad^0 r̄) = 1 for v ∈ Q
items.statement: Let v ∈ Q be as in tw-prime-residual-splitting with N_{F/Q}(v) ≡ 1 mod p. (This congruence is needed but omitted in §8.5.1; it holds for the Q of Prop 8.5.) Then dim_k L_v − h^0(G_{F_v}, ad^0(r̄)) = 1.
items.locator: §8.5.1, p. 408 (restated in the proof of Prop 8.5, p. 411)
items.note: Planned; the unreviewed RS-08 proposal makes R02.5 the owner of 'Deformation-specific local tangent Selmer dimensions'. I checked the count. The tangent space is the unramified block-diagonal classes, of dimension h⁰ since Hom(s̄_v, ψ̄_v) has no G_v-invariants, plus one ramified direction: inertia acting by scalars a and b on the two blocks with (n−1)a + b = 0. That direction exists only when N(v) ≡ 1 mod p, so the congruence is needed, as the item says. See sourceIssues E172 (needs N(v) ≡ 1 mod p).

items.name: Deformation problems and T-framed deformations of a given type (CHT)
items.statement: The paper follows [3, §2.2] with GL_n in place of G_n. A local deformation problem [3, Defn 2.2.2] is a collection D of lifts of r̄|G_{F_v} to objects of C_O with six properties: (1) it contains r̄|G_{F_v} itself; (2) it is closed under push-forward along morphisms in C_O; (3) it is closed under the fibre-product construction R_1 ×_{R_1/I_1 ≅ R_2/I_2} R_2; (4) it is closed under inverse limits; (5) it is closed under equivalence, i.e. conjugation by 1 + M_n(m_R); (6) if R ↪ S is injective and the push-forward of a lift to S lies in D, then the lift lies in D. By [3, Lemma 2.2.3] such problems correspond exactly to (1_n + M_n(m))-invariant ideals I of the universal lifting ring R^loc_v: D consists of the lifts whose classifying map kills I, so D is represented by R^loc_v/I. Its Selmer condition L_v ⊂ H^1(G_v, ad) is the image of the tangent space of R^loc_v/I [3, Defn 2.2.4]. By [3, Defn 2.2.1], a T-framed lift is a tuple (ρ; (α_v)_{v∈T}) with ρ a lift of r̄ and α_v ∈ 1_n + M_n(m_A). Two such are equivalent if (ρ'; α'_v) = (βρβ^{-1}; βα_v) for some β ∈ 1_n + M_n(m_A), and a T-framed deformation is an equivalence class. By [3, Defn 2.2.7], a T-framed deformation is of type S if ρ|G_v ∈ D_v for all v in the index set (equivalently α_v^{-1}ρ|G_vα_v ∈ D_v for v ∈ T). The global data S_Q, S^χ_Q, with fixed determinant ξ, are defined by the paper itself (p. 408) on this model.
items.note: Planned: framed and unframed deformation functors, local deformation problems as quotient-representable conjugation-stable subfunctors, and T-framings, with GL_n in place of CHT's group G_n. The library audit lists all of these as absent. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor [3], Definitions 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.7

items.name: Global deformation data S_Q and S^χ_Q; deformations of type S_Q
items.statement: S_Q = (r̄, O, S_Q, ξ, (D_v)_{v∈S_p∪Q}, (D_v^1)_{v∈R}) and S^χ_Q = (r̄, O, S_Q, ξ, (D_v)_{v∈S_p∪Q}, (D_v^χ)_{v∈R}). For v ∈ S_p, D_v is the problem determined by R_v. For v ∈ R, D_v^1 and D_v^χ are determined by R_v^1 and R_v^{χ_v}. For v ∈ Q, D_v is the Taylor–Wiles problem. A deformation of r̄ to an object of C_O is of type S_Q (resp. S^χ_Q) if: (1) it is unramified outside S_Q; (2) it has determinant ξ; (3) for each v ∈ S_p ∪ Q its restriction is of type D_v, and for v ∈ R it is of type D_v^1 (resp. D_v^χ). For Q = ∅ write S and S^χ.
items.note: Planned: global fixed-determinant problems in arbitrary rank with prescribed local conditions. CG's data (D_v at S_p ∪ Q, D_v^1 or D_v^χ at R) are an instance. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Universal deformation rings R_{S_Q}, R_{S^χ_Q}
items.statement: The functor from C_O to Sets sending A to the set of deformations of r̄ of type S_Q (resp. S^χ_Q) is represented by an object R_{S_Q} (resp. R_{S^χ_Q}) of C_O. For Q = ∅ these are R_S and R_{S^χ}.
items.note: Planned: representability of the unframed rings under absolute irreducibility of r̄. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: T-framed global deformation rings R^{□_T}_{S_Q}, R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q} and their structure maps
items.statement: Let T = S_p ∪ R. R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}) is the object of C_O representing the functor sending A in C_O to the set of deformations of r̄ of type S_Q (resp. S^χ_Q) framed at each v ∈ T, in the sense of [3, Defns 2.2.1, 2.2.7] with GL_n in place of G_n. The forgetful maps on deformation functors give natural maps R_{S_Q} → R^{□_T}_{S_Q} and R^1_loc → R^{□_T}_{S_Q}. The χ-versions are analogous: R_{S^χ_Q} → R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q} and R^χ_loc → R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}.
items.note: Planned: T-framed rings and the maps from R_{S_Q} and R^1_loc. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Lemma 8.3: R_{S_Q} → R^{□_T}_{S_Q} is formally smooth of relative dimension n²|T| − 1
items.statement: The map R_{S_Q} → R^{□_T}_{S_Q} is formally smooth of relative dimension n²|T| − 1. The same holds for the corresponding rings of type S^χ_Q.
items.note: Planned. The relative dimension n²|T| − 1 is unchanged by fixing the determinant: framings range over (1 + M_n(m_A))^T, and the diagonal scalars act trivially. This needs T ≠ ∅, which holds since S_p ⊆ T. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Selmer group H^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄)
items.statement: H^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄) := ker( H^1(G_{F,S_Q}, ad^0 r̄) → ⊕_{x∈T} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄) ⊕ ⊕_{x∈Q} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄)/L_x ). That is: unramified outside S_Q, trivial at T, and in L_x at x ∈ Q. Write h^1_{L(Q),T} for its k-dimension. For Q = ∅ it is written H^1_{L,T}.
items.note: Planned: the relative tangent Selmer group with trivial conditions at T and L_x at x ∈ Q (ACC+'s h¹_{S,T}). Nothing is in the libraries; the audit marks Galois Selmer groups absent.

items.name: Dual Selmer group H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1))
items.statement: H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) := ker( H^1(G_{F,S_Q}, ad^0 r̄(1)) → ⊕_{x∈Q} H^1(G_x, ad^0 r̄(1))/L_x^⊥ ). There is no condition at x ∈ T; the dual of 'trivial' is 'everything'. For Q = ∅ it is written H^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)), and it equals H^1(G_{F,S}, ad^0 r̄(1)).
items.note: Planned: the dual Selmer group with no condition at T and L_x^⊥ at x ∈ Q. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Proposition 8.4(1): presentation of R^{□_T}_{S_Q} over R^1_loc
items.statement: The ring R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}) is a quotient of a power series ring over R^1_loc (resp. R^χ_loc) in h^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄) + Σ_{v∈T} h^0(G_v, ad r̄) − h^0(G_F, ad r̄) variables. (Printed subscript: 'L,T'.)
items.note: Planned. The planned sources are KW II (fixed determinant, rank 2) and ACC+ Prop 6.2.25 (variable determinant, g = h¹_{S,T}(ad)). CG's mixed count, h¹ of ad⁰ plus Σ_T h⁰(ad) − h⁰(G_F, ad), is the fixed-determinant rank-n form that R04.3 and G8 must record. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Proposition 8.4(2): Euler characteristic formula for h^1_{L(Q),T}
items.statement: h^1_{L(Q),T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄) = h^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) + h^0(G_F, ad^0 r̄) − h^0(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) + Σ_{v∈Q} (dim_k L_v − h^0(G_v, ad^0 r̄)) − Σ_{v∈T∪{v|∞}} h^0(G_v, ad^0 r̄). (Printed subscripts: 'L,T' and 'L^⊥,T'.)
items.note: Planned: this is the Greenberg–Wiles formula (see greenberg-wiles-formula) with L_v = 0 at v ∈ T and at v | ∞; for p odd, H¹(G_v, ad⁰r̄) = 0 at archimedean v. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Kisin's presentation of framed global deformation rings over local ones
items.statement: (The argument of [52, Lemma 3.2.2].) The T-framed global deformation ring is a quotient of a power series ring over the completed tensor product of the local framed deformation rings at v ∈ T. The number of variables equals the dimension of the relative tangent space: dim H^1 of the Selmer group with trivial conditions at T and the given conditions elsewhere, plus Σ_{v∈T} h^0(G_v, ad) − h^0(G_F, ad).
items.note: Planned: the presentation over the local rings, with the relative tangent-space count, is the reviewed R03.2 node (KW II Lemma 4.6 and ACC+ Prop 6.2.25), used in R04.3 and G7. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: M. Kisin, Moduli of finite flat group schemes, and modularity, Ann. of Math. 170 (2009) 1085–1180 ([52]), Lemma 3.2.2 and (proof of) Proposition 3.2.5

items.name: Big subgroup of GL_n(k) (CHT Definition 2.5.1)
items.statement: (CHT [3], Definition 2.5.1, GL_n version.) A subgroup H ⊂ GL_n(k) is big if: (a) H has no non-trivial quotient of p-power order; (b) H^0(H, ad^0) = 0 and H^1(H, ad^0) = 0, where ad^0 = g_n^0(k) is the trace-zero subspace of M_n(k); (c) for every irreducible k[H]-submodule W ⊂ ad^0 there are h ∈ H and α ∈ k such that the α-generalized eigenspace V_{h,α} of h on k^n is one-dimensional and π_{h,α} ∘ W ∘ i_{h,α} ≠ 0. Here π_{h,α}: k^n → V_{h,α} is the h-equivariant projection and i_{h,α}: V_{h,α} → k^n the h-equivariant inclusion. The paper applies this to H = r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) (Prop 8.5, p. 410; cf. Theorem 5.16(4), p. 383).
items.note: Planned as one of G7's 'strengthened image conditions', but G7 names only adequacy and ACC+'s 'enormous', and its reviewed node covers only 'enormous'. CHT bigness must be added there as its own definition. Its condition (c) asks for h and α with a one-dimensional generalized eigenspace and π_{h,α}∘W∘i_{h,α} ≠ 0, not for a regular semisimple h with W^h ≠ 0. Nothing is in the libraries. External input: Clozel–Harris–Taylor [3], Definition 2.5.1

items.name: Proposition 8.5: Taylor–Wiles primes and the numerical coincidence (defect l0)
items.statement: In the setting of §8.5, assume r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big, and let q ≥ h^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) be an integer (the Q = ∅ dual Selmer group). Then for every N ≥ 1 there is a tuple (Q, (ψ̄_v)_{v∈Q}) such that: (1) Q is a finite set of primes of F disjoint from S with |Q| = q; (2) for each v ∈ Q, r̄|G_{F_v} ≅ s̄_v ⊕ ψ̄_v with ψ̄_v a generalized eigenspace of Frobenius of dimension 1; (3) N_{F/Q}(v) ≡ 1 mod p^N for each v ∈ Q; (4) R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S^χ_Q}) is a quotient of a power series ring over R^1_loc (resp. R^χ_loc) in q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]·n(n−1)/2 − l0 variables. Moreover the proof gives H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) = 0.
items.note: Planned, consistent with PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/prop-15-2 (CG Prop 5.2) at R04.5/R04.6. The layers are written for KW II (l0 = 0) and polarized ACC+, so the blueprint must record this unpolarized fixed-determinant form over an arbitrary F, with bigness and the defect −l0. I checked the count: with the dual Selmer group killed and h⁰(G_F, ad⁰r̄) = h⁰(G_F, ad⁰r̄(1)) = 0 (both follow from bigness of r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)})), Prop 8.4 and equation (1) give q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 − l0. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Effect of Taylor–Wiles primes on the dual Selmer group
items.statement: Let (Q, (ψ̄_v)_{v∈Q}) satisfy (1)–(3) of Prop 8.5. Let e_v ∈ ad r̄ be the G_{F_v}-equivariant projection onto ψ̄_v. Then there is an exact sequence 0 → H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) → H^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) → ⊕_{v∈Q} k, where the last map is [φ] ↦ (tr(e_v φ(Frob_v)))_{v∈Q}.
items.note: Planned: this is the change of dual Selmer group when primes of Q are added, with the map [φ] ↦ tr(e_v φ(Frob_v)). The unreviewed RS-08 proposal makes R02.6 the owner of 'Conditional dual-Selmer rank-drop calculations'. Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Arithmetic orbifold Y(K)
items.statement: For a compact open subgroup K ⊂ G(A^∞), Y(K) := G(Q)\G(A)/K∞^0 K. It is an arithmetic orbifold of real dimension 2q0 + l0. Its cohomology means orbifold cohomology in the sense of Remark 5.3. Take S = S_p ∪ R and S_Q = S ∪ Q as in §8.
items.note: Planned, as for PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/arith-manifolds-13-1; the quotient uses the identity component K⁰_∞. Its dimension 2q0 + l0 depends on q0 and l0, which are unplanned (def-q0, def-l0). Nothing is in the libraries.

items.name: Level subgroups K_Q = ∏K_{Q,v} and L_Q = ∏L_{Q,v}
items.statement: K_Q = ∏_v K_{Q,v} and L_Q = ∏_v L_{Q,v} are open compact subgroups of G(A^∞) (printed 'G(A)') with: (1) for v ∈ Q, K_{Q,v} is the image in PGL_n(O_v) of {g ∈ GL_n(O_v) : g stabilises ℓ mod π_v}, for a fixed line ℓ ⊂ k_v^n; (2) for v ∈ Q, L_{Q,v} ⊂ K_{Q,v} is the normal subgroup with quotient k_v^×; explicitly K_{Q,v} = (1 *; 0 GL_{n−1}(O_v)) mod π_v and L_{Q,v} = (1 *; 0 SL_{n−1}(O_v)) mod π_v (printed GL_{N−1}, SL_{N−1}); (3) for v ∉ S_Q, K_{Q,v} = L_{Q,v} = PGL_n(O_v) (presumably also for v ∈ S_p, which the printed text omits); (4) for v ∈ R, K_{Q,v} = L_{Q,v} is the Iwahori subgroup Iw(v) of PGL_n(O_v) associated to the upper-triangular unipotent subgroup.
items.note: Not planned, like PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24/level-subgroups-13-4. ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans parahorics in general, which covers Iw(v) and the (1, n−1)-parahoric K_{Q,v}. No layer defines L_{Q,v}, the kernel of K_{Q,v} → k_v^×, or these particular levels. Printing issues: 'G(A)' should be G(A^∞), GL_{N−1}/SL_{N−1} should be GL_{n−1}/SL_{n−1}, and clause (3) omits v ∈ S_p. Neither library has these levels.

items.name: End of the proof of Proposition 8.5: the dual Selmer exact sequence and the choice of Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Setting of §8.5–8.6. r̄: G_F → GL_n(k) is absolutely irreducible, r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big, T = S_p ∪ R, and q ≥ h^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)). Let (Q, (ψ̄_v)_{v∈Q}) satisfy properties (1)–(3) of Proposition 8.5. For v ∈ Q let e_v ∈ ad r̄ be the G_v-equivariant projection onto the one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace ψ̄_v. Then there is an exact sequence 0 → H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) → H^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) → ⊕_{v∈Q} k whose last map is [φ] ↦ (tr(e_v φ(Frob_v)))_{v∈Q}. The argument of [3, Prop. 2.5.9] then shows that one can choose (Q, (ψ̄_v)) satisfying (1)–(3) with H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) = {0}. Property (4) follows from three inputs: Proposition 8.4; equation (1) of §8.4, Σ_{v|∞} dim H^0(F_v, ad^0 r̄) = [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 + l0; and dim_k L_v − h^0(G_v, ad^0 r̄) = 1 for v ∈ Q.
items.note: R02.5 plans the exact sequence comparing H^1_{L(Q)^⊥,T} with H^1_{L^⊥,T}, which is a change of local conditions at the added primes. R04.5 plans the choice of Q that kills the dual Selmer group; GlobalGaloisDeformations G7's 'arbitrary-n auxiliary-prime lemma … control of dual Selmer' is the rank-n model. The variable count in (4) comes from the D8/G8 dimension calculation for CG's unpolarized, fixed-determinant problem over an arbitrary F. G7 itself warns that fixed-determinant variants 'must recompute their tangent dimensions rather than borrow' ACC+'s count g = qn − n²[F⁺:Q].

items.name: Clozel–Harris–Taylor, Proposition 2.5.9 (existence of Taylor–Wiles primes that kill the dual Selmer group)
items.statement:
Clozel–Harris–Taylor [3], Proposition 2.5.9, is stated in the unitary-group setting of [3, §2.3]: F/F^+ is CM and r̄: G_{F^+} → G_n(k), with l the residue characteristic.

Hypotheses: q0 ∈ Z_{≥0}; r̄ is Schur; r̄(G_{F^+(ζ_l)}) is big; and for v ∈ S − T, dim_k L_v − dim_k H^0(G_{F_v}, ad r̄) = [F_v^+ : Q_l]n(n−1)/2 if v | l, and 0 if v ∤ l. Put q := max(dim_k H^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_{F^+,S}, ad r̄(1)), q0).

Conclusion: for every N ≥ 1 there is (Q, Q̃, {ψ̄_v}_{v∈Q}) as in [3, Def. 2.5.7] such that #Q = q, Nv ≡ 1 mod l^N for v ∈ Q, and R^T_{S(Q)} is topologically generated over R^loc_T by #Q − Σ_{v∈T, v|l}[F_v^+ : Q_l]n(n−1)/2 − nΣ_{v|∞}(1 + χ(c_v))/2 elements. In Def. 2.5.7, Q is a set of primes of F^+ outside S that split in F, and r̄|_{G_{F_ṽ}} = ψ̄_v ⊕ s̄_v with dim ψ̄_v = 1 and s̄_v not containing ψ̄_v as a subquotient.

Proof: Q is chosen, using Chebotarev and bigness, so that H^1_{L^⊥}(G_{F^+,S}, ad r̄(1)) → ⊕_{v∈Q} H^1(G_{F_ṽ}/I_{F_ṽ}, ad ψ̄_v(1)) = ⊕_{v∈Q} k is injective, i.e. H^1_{L(Q)^⊥} = 0. The map is [φ] ↦ (π_{Frob_v,ψ̄_v(Frob_v)} ∘ φ(Frob_v) ∘ i_{Frob_v,ψ̄_v(Frob_v)})_v. For each cocycle φ with [φ] ≠ 0, the proof finds σ ∈ G_{F(ζ_{l^N})} such that r̄(σ) has an eigenvalue α with one-dimensional generalized eigenspace and π_{σ,α}∘φ(σ)∘i_{σ,α} ≠ 0.

Use in §8.6: CG apply 'the argument' to GL_n over F with ad^0 r̄(1), their local problems D_v at v ∈ Q, q ≥ h^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)), and the map [φ] ↦ (tr(e_v φ(Frob_v)))_v. For a one-dimensional eigenspace, π∘φ∘i is the scalar tr(e_v φ).
items.locator: invoked in §8.6, proof of Proposition 8.5, pp. 410–411; CHT [3], Proposition 2.5.9, pp. 60–62 (Definition 2.5.7, pp. 59–60)
items.note: The Taylor–Wiles prime lemma in arbitrary rank is planned in R04.5 and GlobalGaloisDeformations G7, which is the owner for the polarized rank-n case; CHT works in the polarized G_n setting. CHT's hypothesis is bigness (CHT Def. 2.5.1), and no atlas layer names it. R04.5 requires each construction to use its own source's image hypothesis, and ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations G7 plans the residual-image criteria, so bigness belongs there as a separate condition. It must not be replaced by ACC+ enormity. External input: L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), 1–181, Proposition 2.5.9 (ref. [3])

items.name: Adelic set-up for G = Res_{F/Q} PGL(n)
items.statement: Let F be a number field of signature (r1, r2) and let n ≥ 1. Write A for the adeles of Q and A^∞ for the finite adeles; A_F and A_F^∞ are the adeles and finite adeles of F. Put G := Res_{F/Q} PGL(n) and G_∞ := G(R) = PGL_n(R)^{r1} × PGL_n(C)^{r2}. K_∞ is a maximal compact subgroup of G_∞, with identity component K_∞^0.
items.note: The adeles A, A^∞, A_F and A_F^∞ already exist in Mathlib. The topological group G(A) = PGL_n(A_F), G_∞ = PGL_n(R)^{r1} × PGL_n(C)^{r2} and a maximal compact subgroup K_∞ with its identity component are missing. The reviewed audit finds 'maximal compact' absent from both trees. AA.1 plans G(A) with restriction of scalars, and ALS.0 plans K_∞ and the symmetric space.

items.name: Arithmetic quotients Y, Y_0(Q), Y_1(Q)
items.statement:
Y := Y(K_∅), whose level is PGL_n(O_v) at v ∉ R and Iw(v) at v ∈ R. For Q ≠ ∅, put Y_0(Q) := Y(K_Q) and Y_1(Q) := Y(L_Q); these are the (PGL-)analogues of the modular curves for Γ_0(Q) and Γ_1(Q).

[Implicit in the paper:] K_Q ⊂ K_∅ gives the natural projection Y_0(Q) → Y (pr in Conjecture B(5)).

By §9.1(2) and the orbifold convention of Remark 5.3, Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q) is a Galois covering with group K_Q/L_Q ≅ ∏_{x∈Q} k_x^× = ∏_{x∈Q}(O_F/x)^×. §9.5 (p. 425) states this and calls the group Δ̃; §5.3 (p. 376) writes Δ_Q for the analogous group.
items.locator: §9.1, p. 412 (Galois group: §9.5, p. 425; cf. Remark 5.3, p. 372)
items.note: Y, Y_0(Q) and Y_1(Q) are ALS.0's X_K at K_∅, K_Q and L_Q. For L_Q normal in K_Q, the orbifold Galois covering Y_1(Q) → Y_0(Q) with group K_Q/L_Q is AA.4's covering of nested levels, which retains groupoids at non-neat level. The item is planned only as these instances: the subgroups K_Q and L_Q themselves are the missing item level-subgroups-KQ-LQ.

items.name: Rank-one local systems O(ψ) and the cohomology H^i_ψ
items.statement: For v ∈ R, let Iw_1(v) ⊂ Iw(v) be the pro-v Iwahori subgroup, so that Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ (k_v^×)^n/(k_v^×). Fix characters ψ_v = ψ_{v,1} × ··· × ψ_{v,n}: Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ (k_v^×)^n/(k_v^×) → 1 + m_O ⊂ O^×. Thus each ψ_{v,i}: k_v^× → 1 + m_O and ∏_i ψ_{v,i} = 1. Put ψ = (ψ_v)_{v∈R}. Let Y′ be Y, Y_0(Q) or Y_1(Q). Let π: Ỹ′ → Y′ be the arithmetic quotient obtained by replacing Iw(v) with Iw_1(v) for each v ∈ R. Define the local system O(ψ) of free rank-one O-modules on Y′ as follows: a section over an open U ⊂ Y′ is a locally constant f: π^{−1}(U) → O with f(γu) = ψ(γ)f(u) for all γ ∈ ∏_{v∈R} Iw(v)/Iw_1(v). Set H^i_ψ(Y′, O) := H^i(Y′, O(ψ)) and H_{i,ψ}(Y′, O) := H_i(Y′, O(ψ)), and define the O/ϖ^m versions, the boundary versions and the compactly supported versions in the same way. If ψ = 1 then O(ψ) ≅ O, so H^i_ψ(Y′, O) ≅ H^i(Y′, O).
items.note: O(ψ) is the rank-one local system on X_K attached to the discrete O-module O(ψ), on which K acts through ∏_{v∈R} Iw(v)/Iw_1(v). ALS.1 plans this, with ordinary, compactly supported and relative cochains, and ALS.4 plans the boundary versions. RG2.3 supplies the pro-v Iwahori Iw_1(v) and the identification Iw(v)/Iw_1(v) ≅ T(k_v) = (k_v^×)^n/k_v^×. The printed 'O(ψ) on Y_i(Q) for i = 1, 2' should read i = 0, 1; the item extends the definition to Y as well.

items.name: Hecke operator T(g) on H_{•,ψ}(Y(K), O) and H^•_ψ(Y(K), O)
items.statement: Let g ∈ G(A^∞) with g_v = 1 for every v ∈ R, and let K be K_Q or L_Q. Define T(g) on H_{•,ψ}(Y(K), O) as the composite H_{•,ψ}(Y(K), O) → H_{•,ψ}(Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K), O) → H_{•,ψ}(Y(K ∩ g^{−1}Kg), O) → H_{•,ψ}(Y(K), O). The first map is corestriction, meaning the transfer for the finite covering Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K) → Y(K) (§5.2.2 writes 'corestriction (= transfer)'). The second is induced by right multiplication by g on G(A), which carries G(Q)\G(A)/K_∞^0(gKg^{−1} ∩ K) onto G(Q)\G(A)/K_∞^0(K ∩ g^{−1}Kg). The third is the natural push-forward on homology. T(g) on H^•_ψ(Y(K), O) is defined in the same way, and so are the versions with O/ϖ^m coefficients. The operators T(g) do not preserve the (co)homology of individual connected components.
items.note: T(g) is ALS.3's correspondence through K ∩ gKg^{−1}: the transfer, then right translation by g, then push-forward. The transfer for finite covers is in Tau Ceti AlgebraicTopology Stage 5. The first printed display has 'Y(gKg^{−1} ∩ K_Q)', which should read ∩ K; this matters for K = L_Q.

items.name: Hecke operators T_{α,k}
items.statement: For α ∈ A_F^{∞,×} with α_v = 1 at v ∈ R, and 1 ≤ k ≤ n, set T_{α,k} := T(g) with g = diag(α, …, α, 1, …, 1) ∈ G(A^∞) = PGL_n(A_F^∞), where α appears k times and 1 appears n − k times. It acts on H_{•,ψ}(Y(K), O) and H^•_ψ(Y(K), O), and on their O/ϖ^m versions, for K = K_Q or L_Q. Since diag(α, …, α) is central, hence trivial in PGL_n, T_{α,n} = id.
items.note: T_{α,k} is ALS.3's T(g) for g = diag(α^(k), 1^(n−k)). For α a uniformizer at one place it is exactly IHG.3's T_{v,k}. T_{α,n} = id because diag(α, …, α) is central, hence trivial in PGL_n.

items.name: Hecke operators T_{a,k} attached to ideals; T_{λ,i}, V_x
items.statement: Let a ⊆ O_F be an ideal prime to the level, and let α ∈ A_F^{×,∞} represent a with α_v = 1 at every component dividing the level. Set T_{a,k} := T_{α,k}. [Corrected. Printed: T_{a,k} := (1/N_{F/Q}(a)^k)T_{α,k}. That normalization can be kept only if the exponent i(i−1)/2 in Conjecture B is changed to i(i+1)/2; see sourceIssues E180.] For a prime λ ∉ S_Q this defines T_{λ,i}. For a prime x, T_{x,k} is uniquely defined when x is prime to the level. It is not uniquely defined when x divides the level: then it depends on the choice of uniformizer at x, up to diamond operators. For x ∈ Q, V_x := T_{x,1} is well defined modulo m (Conjecture B(5)).
items.note: The corrected, unnormalized T_{a,k} := T_{α,k} and T_{λ,i} match IHG.3's normalization exactly, including the exponent i(i−1)/2. The printed factor 1/N(a)^k would force the exponent i(i+1)/2. The clauses on x dividing the level and on V_x := T_{x,1} for x ∈ Q are not planned; they belong to def-9-1-hecke-algebra-TQ (missing). See sourceIssues E180 (normalisation clashes with Conjecture B's exponent).

items.name: Definition 9.1: the anemic Hecke algebra T^an_{Q,ψ}
items.statement:
Definition 9.1. T^an_{Q,ψ} is the subring of End(⊕_{j≥0, m≥1} H^j_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)) generated by the Hecke endomorphisms T_{α,k}, 1 ≤ k ≤ n, for all α ∈ A_F^{∞,×} that are units at every prime of S_Q. The construction of §9.2 needs α_v = 1 at v ∈ R. By construction T^an_{Q,ψ} acts on every H^j_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m).

As printed, α may be a non-trivial unit at x ∈ Q. The corresponding T_{α,k} act on H^*_ψ(Y_1(Q), ·) through K_Q/L_Q (diamond operators), so they lie in T^an_{Q,ψ].

[Editorial: the paper also localizes H^*_ψ(Y, ·), H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), ·) and H^*_ψ(∂Y_1(Q), ·) at maximal ideals m of T^an_{Q,ψ} (Conjecture B(4)(b), (5)) without comment. The same operators T_{α,k} act on these groups, so this localization is to be read via the preimage of m in the abstract Hecke algebra generated by the T_{α,k}.]
items.note: T^an_{Q,ψ} is the image of the unramified operators T_{α,k} in the endomorphisms of ⊕_{j,m} H^j_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m). IHG.2 plans this image algebra and compares it with the chain and derived images, which is how finiteness over O follows. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked the analogous T^S(K) (hecke-algebra-13-3) planned against ALS.3 and IHG.2. The same operators act on Y, Y_0(Q) and the boundary through ALS.3's change-of-level and boundary compatibility.

items.name: Definition 9.1: the Hecke algebra T_{Q,ψ} (with operators at Q) and T_ψ
items.statement:
T_{Q,ψ} is the O-algebra generated by the operators of Definition 9.1 together with the T_{α,k} for α non-trivial at places of Q (printed 'T_α'). In particular it contains V_x = T_{x,1} for x ∈ Q (α a uniformizer at x). If Q = ∅, T_ψ := T_{∅,ψ}, which equals T^an_{∅,ψ}. §9.5 uses T := T_{∅,1} (p. 425) and T_χ := T_{∅,χ} (p. 426).

[Editorial, not stated in the paper: for α ∈ ∏_{x∈Q} O_x^× the operators T_{α,k} act on H^*_ψ(Y_1(Q), ·) through the covering group K_Q/L_Q ≅ ∏_{x∈Q} k_x^× (Δ̃ in §9.5); under the printed Definition 9.1 these already lie in T^an_{Q,ψ}.]
items.note: No layer plans the Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebra for PGL_n over an arbitrary number field. That algebra includes V_x = T_{x,1} at x ∈ Q, which depends on the choice of uniformizer up to diamond operators, and the diamond operators through K_Q/L_Q ≅ Δ_Q, which make it an O[Δ_Q]-algebra. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 recorded its PGL₂ analogue (hecke-TSigmaQ-13-6) as missing.

items.name: Localized/completed Hecke algebra T^an_{Q,ψ,m}
items.statement: Let m be a maximal ideal of T^an_{Q,ψ}. T^an_{Q,ψ,m} denotes the completion at m. It is a local ring, finite over O but not necessarily flat. The cases ψ = 1 and ψ = χ are written T^an_{Q,1,m} and T^an_{Q,χ,m}.
items.note: Since T^an_{Q,ψ} is finite over the complete ring O, it is the product of its completions T^an_{Q,ψ,m}, each local and finite but not necessarily flat over O. This is IHG.2's localization decomposition.

items.name: Conjecture B, first assertion: residual Galois representations r̄_m
items.statement: Conjecture. For every maximal ideal m of T^an_{Q,ψ} there is a semisimple continuous representation r̄_m: G_F → GL_n(T^an_{Q,ψ}/m) with the following property. For every prime λ ∉ S_Q of F, r̄_m is unramified at λ, and the characteristic polynomial of r̄_m(Frob_λ) is X^n − T_{λ,1}X^{n−1} + ··· + (−1)^i N_{F/Q}(λ)^{i(i−1)/2} T_{λ,i} X^{n−i} + ··· + (−1)^n N_{F/Q}(λ)^{n(n−1)/2} T_{λ,n} in (T^an_{Q,ψ}/m)[X]. Here T_{λ,i} = T_{α,i}, with α a uniformizer at λ and 1 elsewhere (the unnormalized operator). With the printed normalization T_{λ,i} = N(λ)^{−i}T_{α,i}, the exponent must be i(i+1)/2. By Chebotarev density (and Brauer–Nesbitt), this property determines r̄_m up to isomorphism.
items.note: The existence of r̄_m for torsion Hecke eigenclasses of PGL_n over a general F is an open conjecture, and no layer states it. For F CM it follows from Scholze (ext-scholze-torsion-galois-reps), which is also missing. TorsionCohomologyInfrastructure builds that argument's inputs but explicitly excludes its final theorem. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 recorded the n = 2 analogue (conj-A) as missing. See sourceIssues E180 (normalisation of T_{λ,i} versus exponent i(i−1)/2).

items.name: Non-Eisenstein maximal ideal (GL(n) setting)
items.statement: A maximal ideal m of T^an_{Q,ψ} is non-Eisenstein if the representation r̄_m of Conjecture B is absolutely irreducible.
items.note: The definition 'r̄_m absolutely irreducible' relies on r̄_m from Conjecture B, which is missing. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 made the same observation for its Conjecture A.

items.name: Conjecture B: integral lift r_m to T^an_{Q,ψ,m}
items.statement: Conjecture. If m is non-Eisenstein, there is a continuous deformation r_m: G_F → GL_n(T^an_{Q,ψ,m}) of r̄_m, unramified outside S_Q, such that for every prime λ ∉ S_Q the characteristic polynomial of r_m(Frob_λ) is given by the same formula as for r̄_m, now in T^an_{Q,ψ,m}[X].
items.note: The deformation r_m over T^an_{Q,ψ,m} is conjectural. Scholze's method gives determinants only modulo a nilpotent ideal, which IHG.2 and IHG.5 plan as tools, and its removal is not planned anywhere. Once a determinant over T^an_m exists, IHG.1 would give the representation under residual absolute irreducibility.

items.name: Set of Taylor–Wiles primes (for Conjecture B)
items.statement:
A set of Taylor–Wiles primes, for r̄ and an integer N ≥ 1, is a set Q with data (ψ̄_x)_{x∈Q} as constructed in Proposition 8.5:
(1) Q is a finite set of q primes of F disjoint from S.
(2) For x ∈ Q, r̄|_{G_x} ≅ s̄_x ⊕ ψ̄_x, where ψ̄_x is a one-dimensional generalized eigenspace of Frobenius.
(3) N_{F/Q}(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N.
(4) R^{□_T}_{S_Q} (resp. R^{□_T}_{S_Q^χ}) is a quotient of a power series ring over R^1_loc (resp. R^χ_loc) in q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 − l0 variables.
For x ∈ Q put α_x := ψ̄_x(Frob_x). Q = ∅ is allowed, and then the condition is empty.
items.locator: §9.3, Conjecture B, p. 414 (referring to §8.6, Proposition 8.5, p. 410)
items.note: A set of Taylor–Wiles primes is exactly the output datum of R04.5 for the arbitrary-rank, fixed-determinant problems of G8. Property (4), the count q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 − l0, is the D8/G8 variable count. GlobalGaloisDeformations G7 plans the rank-n local condition with 'chosen eigenspaces'. The count itself is not written in any layer, and G7 says fixed-determinant counts must be recomputed.

items.name: Conjecture B(1): Fontaine–Laffaille at p
items.statement: Conjecture. Assume m is non-Eisenstein, r̄_m ≅ r̄ (r̄ as in §8.5; printed 'r_m ≅ r̄'), and Q is a set of Taylor–Wiles primes. Then for every v | p, r_m|_{G_v} is Fontaine–Laffaille with all weights equal to [0, 1, …, n − 1], for every embedding τ, as in the definition of R_v in §8.5.1.
items.note: This is conjectural local–global compatibility at v | p for r_m over T^an_m and a general F, and no layer states it. ACC+ proves a version over CM fields modulo a nilpotent ideal (PA.1), which is not the statement here. The printed hypothesis 'r_m ≅ r̄' should read r̄_m ≅ r̄.

items.name: Conjecture B(2): type D_v at Taylor–Wiles primes
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypotheses of Conjecture B(1), for every v ∈ Q, r_m|_{G_v} is a lifting of type D_v, the local deformation problem of §8.5.1. That is, r_m|_{G_v} ≅ s_v ⊕ ψ_v, where s_v lifts s̄_v and ψ_v lifts ψ̄_v, I_v acts through (possibly different) scalars on s_v and on ψ_v, and the determinant is ξ|_{G_v}.
items.note: The condition that r_m|G_v has type D_v at Taylor–Wiles primes is conjectural for a general F, and no layer states it.

items.name: Conjecture B(3): inertial types at v ∈ R
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypotheses of Conjecture B(1), for every v ∈ R and every σ ∈ I_v, the characteristic polynomial of r_m(σ) is (X − ψ_{v,1}(Art_v^{−1}(σ))) ··· (X − ψ_{v,n}(Art_v^{−1}(σ))). Here Art_v: F_v^× → G_v^ab is the local Artin map; Art_v^{−1}(σ) ∈ O_v^×, and ψ_{v,i} is evaluated through O_v^× → k_v^×.
items.note: This is conjectural local–global compatibility at v ∈ R for torsion classes with ψ-twisted coefficients, and no layer states it.

items.name: Conjecture B(4)(a): vanishing outside [q0, q0 + l0]
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypotheses of Conjecture B(1), for all m ≥ 1 the localizations H^i_ψ(Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m vanish unless i ∈ [q0, q0 + l0].
items.note: Vanishing of non-Eisenstein mod-ϖ^m cohomology outside [q0, q0 + l0] for PGL_n over a general F is open, and no layer plans it. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked the PGL₂ analogue (conj-C) missing. PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure's README notes that ACC+ 'does not establish the general expected mod-p cohomology vanishing conjecture'.

items.name: Conjecture B(4)(b): vanishing of localized boundary cohomology
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypotheses of Conjecture B(1), for all i and all m ≥ 1, H^i_ψ(∂Y_1(Q), O/ϖ^m)_m = 0, where ∂Y_1(Q) is the boundary of the Borel–Serre compactification of Y_1(Q).
items.note: For a general F this needs Galois representations for the Levi cohomology, so it is conjectural. ALS.4 plans only the boundary triangle and an eigenvalue criterion, not this vanishing.

items.name: Conjecture B(5): no new cohomology at Taylor–Wiles level
items.statement: Conjecture. Under the hypotheses of Conjecture B(1), for x ∈ Q let P_x(X) = (X − α_x)Q_x(X) be the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_x), where α_x = ψ̄_x(Frob_x). Let m_Q be the maximal ideal of T_{Q,ψ} containing m and V_x − α_x for all x ∈ Q, where V_x := T_{x,1} is well defined modulo m. Then for every m ≥ 1 the map lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q} Q_x(V_x)^{k!} ∘ pr^*: H^*_ψ(Y, O/ϖ^m)_m → H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), O/ϖ^m)_{m_Q} is an isomorphism. Here pr: Y_0(Q) → Y is the natural projection, and Q_x(V_x) is formed with any lifts of the coefficients of Q_x to O.
items.note: This is an Ihara/level-raising type statement at Taylor–Wiles level for PGL_n over a general F. It is conjectural apart from n = 2, which is Lemma 9.6, and no layer states it.

items.name: Consequence of Conjecture B: r_m has type S_Q (resp. S_Q^χ), giving R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an_{Q,1,m} (resp. R_{S_Q^χ} ↠ T^an_{Q,χ,m})
items.statement:
Assume Conjecture B, with m non-Eisenstein, r̄_m ≅ r̄, and Q a set of Taylor–Wiles primes. Suppose ψ_v = 1 for all v ∈ R (resp. ψ_v = χ_v for all v ∈ R, i.e. ψ_{v,i}(Art_v^{−1}(σ)) = χ_{v,i}(σ) for σ ∈ I_v). Suppose also ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2}; the paper leaves this implicit.

Then r_m is a deformation of r̄ of type S_Q (resp. S_Q^χ) in the sense of §8.5.2. The paper concludes that there is a surjection R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an_{Q,1,m} (resp. R_{S_Q^χ} ↠ T^an_{Q,χ,m}).

[Caveat: the image of R_{S_Q} is the closed O-subalgebra generated by the T_{λ,i}, λ ∉ S_Q. Surjectivity onto T^an_{Q,ψ,m} as printed also needs the diamond operators at x ∈ Q (T_{α,k} with α_x ∈ O_x^×) to lie in that image. This needs local–global compatibility at Q, which Conjecture B does not include (contrast Conjecture A(3) and Lemma 5.6).]
items.note: The consequence R_{S_Q} ↠ T^an_{Q,1,m} (and its χ-version) is conditional on Conjecture B, and no layer states it. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked its PGL₂ analogue (conj-B) missing. The determinant condition ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2} that the item adds was not checked here and does not affect the status. See sourceIssues E181 (no local–global compatibility at Q) and E186 (surjection needs ξ = ε^{n(n−1)/2} or a twist).

items.name: Dévissage for conditions (4) and (5) of Conjecture B
items.statement: Conditions (4) and (5) of Conjecture B hold for all coefficients O/ϖ^m (m ≥ 1) if and only if they hold for m = 1, i.e. with coefficients in the residue field k = O/ϖ.
items.note: This is a short lemma: induct on m using 0 → O/ϖ^{m−1} → O/ϖ^m → k → 0, exactness of localization, and the five lemma for condition (5), which is natural in the coefficients. No layer states it, because it concerns the conjectural conditions.

items.name: Dual maximal ideal m^*
items.statement:
The paper does not define m^*. It is used in §5.3 (p. 378: 'Because we are working with PGL, the dual maximal ideal m^* is identified with m'), in Remarks 9.3 and 9.5, and in §9.5.

Standard interpretation: m^* is the image of m under the anti-involution T(g) ↦ T(g^{−1}). This gives the adjoint of T(g) for the Poincaré duality pairing H^i(Y, k) × H_c^{d−i}(Y, k) → k, with d = 2q0 + l0.

For the operators T_{α,k} of §9.2 with α_x = 1 at x ∈ Q (e.g. on Y = Y(K_∅)): at v ∉ S_Q the permutation matrices lie in K_v = PGL_n(O_v), and g^{−1} ≡ diag(1^{(k)}, α^{(n−k)}) modulo the centre, so the involution sends T_{α,k} to T_{α,n−k}. For n = 2 it fixes T_{α,1}, consistent with §5.3.

On Y_1(Q), if α_x = u is a non-trivial unit at x ∈ Q, the two operators differ by the diamond operator attached to u^n.
items.locator: not defined in the paper; used in §5.3, p. 378, §9.3, Remarks 9.3 and 9.5, pp. 415–416, and §9.5, p. 425
items.note: m* is the pull-back of m under the involution T(g) ↦ T(g^{−1}), which is the adjoint for Poincaré duality. Both are planned in ALS.5:finite-level-duality and SR.1. T_{α,k} ↦ T_{α,n−k} is a double-coset computation: invert, multiply by the central α, then conjugate by a Weyl element in K_v.

items.name: Remark 9.3: Conjecture B(4)(a) in small rank via the congruence subgroup property
items.statement:
Remark 9.3. Part (4)(a) of Conjecture B may be verified directly in a number of small rank cases, in particular for GL(2)/F with F a CM field of degree 2 or 4, and for GL(3)/Q.

In the latter two cases, (q0, l0) = (2, 2) and (2, 1) respectively; put d = 2q0 + l0. The key point is that the lattices in question satisfy the congruence subgroup property [77]. This gives (H^1)_m = 0 for every non-Eisenstein m. By Poincaré duality, applied to both m and m^*, (H_c^{d−1})_m = 0. Since boundary cohomology vanishes after localization at m, (H^{d−1})_m = 0. The printed text has q0 − 1 where d − 1 appears here.

In these cases enough is known about the boundary to also resolve Part (4)(b).

[Editorial: the paper gives no separate argument for the imaginary quadratic case, where d = 3 and the range is [1, 2]; Bianchi groups do not have the congruence subgroup property.]
items.note: This verifies Conjecture B(4)(a) for GL(2) over CM fields of degree 2 or 4 and for GL(3)/ℚ, using the congruence subgroup property and duality. No layer plans it. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked its imaginary-quadratic analogue missing. The printed (H_c^{q0−1})_m should be (H_c^{d−1})_m with d = 2q0 + l0. See sourceIssues E185 (Serre's 1970 SL_2 paper is not cited).

items.name: Congruence subgroup property (Bass–Milnor–Serre; Serre for SL_2)
items.statement: As used here: SL_3(Z), and more generally SL_n(O_F) for n ≥ 3, has the congruence subgroup property: the congruence kernel is finite, and trivial when F has a real place (Bass–Milnor–Serre [77]). For F with infinitely many units, e.g. a CM quartic field, SL_2(O_F) has finite congruence kernel (Serre 1970). What the paper uses: for the relevant lattices Γ, the classes in H^1(Γ, k) = Hom(Γ, k) come from congruence quotients, so they vanish after localization at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal.
items.note: The congruence subgroup property is not planned. KTheoryLowDegrees U.4 plans only the SK₁ part of Bass–Milnor–Serre. PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25 routed the SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) case to ModularCurvesPartII R14.4 as a source. SL_3(ℤ) (Bass–Milnor–Serre) and SL_2(O_F) for a CM quartic F (Serre 1970) are missing. See sourceIssues E185 (the paper does not cite Serre 1970). External input: H. Bass, J. Milnor, J.-P. Serre, Solution of the congruence subgroup problem for SL_n (n ≥ 3) and Sp_2n (n ≥ 2), Publ. Math. IHÉS 33 (1967), 59–137 (ref. [77]); for SL_2: J.-P. Serre, Le problème des groupes de congruence pour SL2, Ann. of Math. 92 (1970), 489–527 (not cited in the paper)

items.name: Remark 9.5: the patched complexes compute localized homology
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B(4)(b). Then H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^∨_m ≅ H_c^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^∨_m ≅ H_*(Y, O/ϖ^m)_{m*}, where m^* is the dual maximal ideal (printed 'for the dual maximal ideal m'). The complexes patched in §9.5 compute these groups. In a homological formulation of Conjecture B no hypothesis on the localized boundary would be needed. The paper also says that, after Scholze [8], the real difficulty in Conjecture B is proving non-vanishing of (co)homology in the required range after localization at m, and local–global compatibility, especially at v | p.
items.note: Given B(4)(b), the identifications H^* ≅ H_c^* after localization, Poincaré duality with m ↔ m*, and Pontryagin/universal-coefficient duality are assembled from ALS.4, ALS.5 and ALS.1. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 treated its prop-13-6 the same way. The remarks about Scholze and where the difficulty lies are commentary. The printed 'for the dual maximal ideal m' should read m*.

items.name: Lemma 9.6: condition (5) of Conjecture B for n = 2
items.statement:
Lemma 9.6. If n = 2, then condition (5) of Conjecture B holds for all Taylor–Wiles primes.

Standing assumptions: p > n, so p is odd; m is as in Conjecture B, i.e. non-Eisenstein with r̄_m ≅ r̄; ψ is dropped from the notation in the proof.

Explicitly: for every set Q of Taylor–Wiles primes (Prop. 8.5) and every m ≥ 1, the map (lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q}(V_x − β_x)^{k!}) ∘ pr^*: H^*_ψ(Y, O/ϖ^m)_m → H^*_ψ(Y_0(Q), O/ϖ^m)_{m_Q} is an isomorphism. Here α_x = ψ̄_x(Frob_x), β_x is the other eigenvalue of r̄(Frob_x), and Q_x(X) = X − β_x.

The proof reduces by induction to Q = {x}. It uses only N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and α_x ≠ β_x; for n = 2 the latter follows from ψ̄_x being a one-dimensional generalized eigenspace. For notational convenience it assumes x is trivial in the ray class group of the component group of Y.
items.note: This is Conjecture B(5) for PGL₂ over an arbitrary F, proved through the amalgam G = Γ¹ ∗ Γ¹ and U_{x²} = 1. No layer plans it. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24's Ihara items for PGL₂/F (conj-D, thm-13-12) are also missing. See sourceIssues E189 (Lyndon-sequence argument needs further justification).

items.name: Degeneracy maps φ, φ^∨ at level Γ_0(x) and the old-space splitting
items.statement:
Let n = 2 and Q = {x}. The two natural degeneracy maps Y_0(x) → Y induce φ: H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^2 → H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m) (the sum of the two pull-backs) and φ^∨: H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m) → H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^2 (the two push-forwards). The composite is φ^∨∘φ = (N(x)+1, T_x ; T_x, N(x)+1), with T_x the unnormalized Hecke operator. Its determinant is (1 + N(x))^2 − T_x^2 (printed with the opposite sign).

If α_x, β_x are the eigenvalues of r̄(Frob_x), then α_xβ_x ≡ N(x) ≡ 1 mod p. For a Taylor–Wiles prime, α_x ≠ β_x, equivalently α_x ≢ ±1 mod p. Hence T_x^2 − (1 + N(x))^2 ∉ m, and φ^∨∘φ is invertible after localizing at m.

φ and φ^∨ then induce splittings H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m)_m ≃ H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)^2_m ⊕ W and H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m)_{m̃} ≃ H^*(Y, O/ϖ^m)_{m̃} ⊕ W_{m̃}. Here W ⊂ H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m) is a T^an_{Q,m}-module, m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x), and α_x also denotes any lift to O/ϖ^m.

The paper then says: 'It suffices to prove that W is trivial.' [Editorial: W_{m̃} = 0 would already suffice for condition (5).]
items.note: The two degeneracy maps at Γ_0(x) for PGL₂/F and the identity φ^∨∘φ = (N(x)+1, T_x; T_x, N(x)+1) are planned nowhere. The determinant is printed with the opposite sign. PAPER-IYENGAR-KHARE-MANNING-24 marked the analogous level-lowering maps (level-lowering-13-5) missing.

items.name: The amalgam G = Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1 ⊂ PSL_2(O_F[1/x])
items.statement: Write Y ≃ ⊔_i Γ_i\H, with Γ_i congruence subgroups commensurable with PGL_2(O_F) and H the symmetric space. The components form a torsor under a ray class group attached to the level of Y. For one such Γ, let Γ^1 := Γ ∩ PSL_2(O_F).
