Then Φ := Γ/Γ^1 is an elementary abelian 2-group, and since p is odd, Hochschild–Serre gives H^*(Γ, O/ϖ^m) ≃ H^*(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)^Φ. Let x be a Taylor–Wiles prime; the level of Y at x is maximal. Assume also that x is trivial in the ray class group of the component group of Y. Put Γ^1_0(x) := Γ_0(x) ∩ Γ^1 and G := Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1, the amalgam of Γ^1 with itself along Γ^1_0(x). Then G is a congruence subgroup of the S-arithmetic group PSL_2(O_F[1/x]), with the same level structure as Γ^1 at primes away from x.
items.note: The formation of Γ¹ ∗_{Γ¹_0(x)} Γ¹ as a congruence subgroup of PSL₂(O_F[1/x]) rests on Ihara's theorem and is planned nowhere. PAPER-CALEGARI-DIMITROV-TANG-25's analogue for SL₂(ℤ[1/p]) (amalgam-sl2-z1p) is missing and routed to R14.4. The step H^*(Γ) ≅ H^*(Γ¹)^Φ for p odd and Φ an elementary abelian 2-group is covered by the planned Hochschild–Serre layers.

items.name: Lyndon (Mayer–Vietoris) long exact sequence for an amalgam
items.statement: For an amalgam G = G_1 ∗_A G_2 and a G-module M there is a long exact sequence ··· → H^{i−1}(A, M) → H^i(G, M) → H^i(G_1, M) ⊕ H^i(G_2, M) → H^i(A, M) → H^{i+1}(G, M) → ···. It comes from the exact sequence 0 → Z[G/A] → Z[G/G_1] ⊕ Z[G/G_2] → Z → 0 given by the tree of G. Applied here to G = Γ^1 ∗_{Γ^1_0(x)} Γ^1 and M = O/ϖ^m: ··· → H^i(G, O/ϖ^m) → H^i(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)^2 → H^i(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m) → H^{i+1}(G, O/ϖ^m) → ···.
items.locator: invoked in §9.3, proof of Lemma 9.6, p. 418
items.note: The long exact sequence of an amalgam is missing. It follows from the tree's short exact sequence 0 → ℤ[G/A] → ℤ[G/G₁] ⊕ ℤ[G/G₂] → ℤ → 0 and Shapiro's lemma. Exactness of that sequence is the Bass–Serre tree property, which Mathlib's PushoutI normal forms should give. External input: J.-P. Serre, Arbres, amalgames, SL2, Astérisque 46 (1977), p. 169 as cited (ref. [78])

items.name: Ihara/Serre: PSL_2(F_x) is an amalgam; PGL_2(F_x) is not (Remark 9.7)
items.statement: As noted in [6], PSL_2(F_x) (and SL_2(F_x)) decomposes as an amalgam of two maximal compact subgroups along an Iwahori subgroup Γ_0(x): these are the stabilizers of two adjacent vertices of the Bruhat–Tits tree and of the edge between them. PGL_2(F_x) does not decompose this way. This is why the proof of Lemma 9.6 reduces to PSL_2. One could use PGL_2 instead, but then the amalgams are more naturally subgroups of PGL_2(O_F[1/x])^{(ev)} ⊂ PGL_2(O_F[1/x]), the matrices whose determinant has even valuation at x ([6, Ch. 4]). In either case U_{x^2} acts by +1 on H^*(G, O/ϖ^m).
items.note: The decomposition of SL₂(F_x) or PSL₂(F_x) as the amalgam of two vertex stabilizers along the Iwahori, the failure for PGL₂(F_x), and the even-valuation subgroup PGL₂^{(ev)} are not planned. They are the Bass–Serre consequence of the planned SL₂ tree action, which has an edge as strict fundamental domain. External input: F. Calegari, A. Venkatesh, Towards a torsion Jacquet–Langlands correspondence (ref. [6]), Ch. 4; J.-P. Serre, Arbres, amalgames, SL2 (ref. [78]), Ch. II (Ihara's theorem)

items.name: The operator U_{x^2} and its action on H^*(G)
items.statement:
U_{x^2} is defined as 1/N(x)^2 times the double-coset operator for Γ^1_0(x) given by the matrix (π_x^2 0 ; 0 1). The operator depends on the matrix only up to scalars, so one may use g := (π_x 0 ; 0 π_x^{−1}), and g ∈ G. [Implicit: π_x is a global generator of x, which exists by the assumption that x is trivial in the ray class group.]

The paper states that the induced map on H^*(G, O/ϖ^m) is multiplication by the degree of the operator on Γ^1_0(x), which is N(x)^2. Hence U_{x^2} acts on H^*(G, O/ϖ^m) by 1. The paper also claims, without proof, that the Lyndon sequence is U_{x^2}-equivariant.

On H^*(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m), U_x^2 = U_{x^2} when U_x is normalized as 1/N(x) times the double coset of (π_x 0 ; 0 1), as with the printed T_{x,1} = N(x)^{−1}T_{α,1}. For the unnormalized U_x = T_{x,1} one has U_x^2 = N(x)^2 U_{x^2} ≡ U_{x^2} mod p, which does not affect the argument.
items.note: The normalised operator U_{x²} = N(x)^{−2}[Γ¹_0(x) diag(π_x², 1) Γ¹_0(x)] and its action by 1 on H^*(G) are specific to the proof of Lemma 9.6 and are not planned. That action holds because g = diag(π_x, π_x^{−1}) lies in G, and the degree is N(x)². So are the Hecke-equivariance of the Lyndon sequence and U_x² = U_{x²} on Y_0(x). See sourceIssues E189 (Lyndon equivariance; U_{x²} acts by N(x)^{−2}).

items.name: Key step of Lemma 9.6: H^i(Y)^2_m ≅ H^i(Y_0(x))_m and the U_x-projections
items.statement:
If one localizes the Lyndon sequence at an ideal m at which U_{x^2} − 1 is invertible, then H^i(Γ^1, O/ϖ^m)^2_m ≃ H^i(Γ^1_0(x), O/ϖ^m)_m. This is because U_{x^2} acts by 1 on H^*(G), so the localized H^*(G)-terms vanish.

To recover the statement for Y, repeat this for each lattice Γ_i, using H^*(Γ) ≃ H^*(Γ^1)^Φ.

On H^*(Y_0(x)), U_x^2 = U_{x^2}. With the unnormalized U_x one has instead U_x^2 = N(x)^2U_{x^2} ≡ U_{x^2} mod p. Since neither α_x nor β_x is ±1, U_{x^2} − 1 is invertible after localization. This gives H^i(Y, O/ϖ^m)^2_m ≃ H^i(Y_0(x), O/ϖ^m)_m for the maximal ideal of interest.

Taking m̃ = (m, U_x − α_x) and applying the projections lim_{k→∞}(U_x − β_x)^{k!} and lim_{k→∞}(U_x − α_x)^{k!} gives the isomorphism required by Conjecture B(5) for Q = {x}. The paper prints these limits with exponent n (sourceIssues E191).
items.note: The step H^i(Y)²_m ≅ H^i(Y_0(x))_m, followed by the projections with (U_x − β_x)^{k!} and (U_x − α_x)^{k!}, is part of the proof of Lemma 9.6 and is planned nowhere. The paper prints these limits with exponent n. See sourceIssues E189 (U_{x²} acts on H^*(G) by N(x)^{−2}, harmlessly).

items.name: Enormous image (§9.4)
items.statement: r̄ has enormous image if r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big and, in addition, suitable Taylor–Wiles primes x exist such that r̄(Frob_x) has distinct eigenvalues.
items.note: CG's notion is informal: bigness plus Taylor–Wiles primes whose Frobenius has distinct eigenvalues. The atlas plans its precise form, ACC+ Def. 6.2.29, where a regular semisimple h plays the role of a Frobenius with distinct eigenvalues. The two definitions are not literally identical, since ACC+ condition (3) replaces the CHT bigness condition, so the formal item should adopt ACC+'s definition and record CG's wording as motivation.

items.name: Irreducible mod-p representation associated to ρ̄
items.statement: Let ρ̄: G_x → GL_n(k) be continuous and semisimple, with x ∤ p. An irreducible admissible mod-p representation π of G = GL_n(F_x) is associated to ρ̄ if rec(π) = WD(ρ̄) under the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Vignéras [79].
items.note: The definition rec(π) = WD(ρ̄) needs Vignéras's semisimple mod-ℓ correspondence, which is not planned.

items.name: Vignéras: semisimple mod-ℓ local Langlands correspondence for GL(n)
items.statement: Vignéras [79] (Invent. Math. 144 (2001), 177–223): let F_x be a non-archimedean local field whose residue characteristic differs from the coefficient prime p; here x ∤ p, automatic since N(x) ≡ 1 mod p. There is a semisimple Langlands correspondence modulo p, compatible with reduction mod p of the characteristic-zero correspondence. It is a bijection between supercuspidal supports of irreducible smooth F̄_p-representations of GL_n(F_x) and semisimple n-dimensional F̄_p-representations of the Weil group W_{F_x}. For irreducible π, rec(π) is the semisimple representation attached to the supercuspidal support of π, so π ↦ rec(π) is not injective. §9.4.1 uses it to define 'π associated to ρ̄' by rec(π) = WD(ρ̄).
items.note: The classification of mod-ℓ (ℓ ≠ p) smooth representations of GL_n(F) and Vignéras's semisimple correspondence compatible with reduction are planned nowhere. External input: M.-F. Vignéras, Correspondance de Langlands semi-simple pour GL(n, F) modulo ℓ ≠ p, Invent. Math. 144 (2001), 177–223 (ref. [79])

items.name: Local setting at a Taylor–Wiles prime (§9.4.1)
items.statement: Let F/Q be a number field and x a prime of F with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p (so the residue characteristic ℓ of x is different from p). Put G = GL_n(F_x). Let B ⊂ G be the Borel subgroup, P ⊃ B the parabolic subgroup with Levi factor L := GL_{n−1}(F_x) × F_x^×, and D ≅ (F_x^×)^n the Levi (diagonal torus) of B, so D ⊂ B ⊂ P ⊂ G. Let G(O_x) = GL_n(O_x); U(x) ⊂ G(O_x) the full congruence subgroup of level x (kernel of GL_n(O_x) → GL_n(O_x/ϖ_x)); U_0(x) ⊂ G(O_x) the largest subgroup containing U(x) whose image in GL_n(O_x/ϖ_x) stabilizes a line, the line chosen compatibly with P (so U_0(x)/U(x) is the corresponding maximal parabolic subgroup of GL_n(O_x/ϖ_x)). Put G(k) := G(O_x)/U(x) ≅ GL_n(k), with images B(k) and D(k) = (k^×)^n; in these expressions k denotes the residue field O_x/ϖ_x. Separately, ρ̄ : G_x = Gal(F̄_x/F_x) → GL_n(k) denotes a continuous semisimple representation, where k is the coefficient field (residue field of O).
items.note: D ⊂ B ⊂ P, with Levi GL_{n−1} × F_x^×, comes from Tau Ceti Layer 7. U(x) is the principal congruence subgroup and U_0(x) the parahoric of the facet stabilizing a line (the preimage of a maximal parabolic of GL_n(k_x)); both are RG2.3 constructions. In RG2.3 'pro-p' refers to the residue characteristic of E, which here is ℓ, so U(x) is pro-ℓ. The item's two uses of k (the coefficient field and O_x/ϖ_x) must be kept apart. This agrees with cluster K9's local-setup-9-4-1.

items.name: Lemma 9.9 (unramified ρ̄ with distinct eigenvalues)
items.statement: Let ρ̄ : G_x → GL_n(k) be unramified with distinct eigenvalues (of ρ̄(Frob_x)), with N(x) ≡ 1 mod p. Then rec(π) = ρ̄ (i.e. π is associated to ρ̄) if and only if π is the irreducible unramified mod-p principal series π = n-ind_B^G(χ), where χ = (χ_1, …, χ_n) : (F_x^×)^n → k^× factors through (F_x^×/O_x^×)^n and sends each uniformizer (in the i-th factor) to a distinct eigenvalue of ρ̄(Frob_x).
items.note: Not planned. SR.2 plans parabolic induction and SR.4 the Satake identification of unramified Hecke eigencharacters, but only in characteristic zero or integrally. Nothing plans irreducibility of the mod-p principal series n-ind_B^G(χ), or its identification with the representation associated to unramified ρ̄ with distinct eigenvalues. Irreducibility uses N(x) ≡ 1 mod p: |·| is trivial mod p, so χ_i ≠ χ_j·|·|^{±1} reduces to the χ_i being distinct.

items.name: Ext^1 between irreducibles forces equal supercuspidal support (Emerton–Helm, Theorem 3.2.13, as invoked)
items.statement: As invoked in the proof of Lemma 9.10: let π, π′ be irreducible admissible smooth mod-p representations of GL_n(F_x) (residue characteristic of x different from p). If Ext^1_G(π, π′) ≠ 0 or Ext^1_G(π′, π) ≠ 0, then π and π′ have the same supercuspidal support.
items.note: I checked the statement in the arXiv draft of Emerton–Helm (1104.0321, 'Draft: April 1, 2011', §3.2). There K is a field of characteristic different from the residue characteristic of E, and Theorem 3.2.13 reads: "Let π, π′ be irreducible admissible representations of G over K, or more generally of a Levi subgroup M of G, and suppose that for some i, Ext^i(π, π′) is nonzero. Then π and π′ have the same supercuspidal support." This is stronger than the Ext¹ form the item uses. SR.3 plans supercuspidal support and the Bernstein decomposition for complex representations only. SR.5 plans Helm's integral blocks but no Ext-vanishing statement between irreducible mod-ℓ representations. Not in either library. External input: M. Emerton, D. Helm, The local Langlands correspondence for GL_n in families, Ann. Sci. Éc. Norm. Supér. (4) 47 (2014), 655–722 [80], Theorem 3.2.13

items.name: Lemma 9.10 (Ext^1 vanishing)
items.statement: Let π = n-ind_B^G(χ) be the unramified principal series of Lemma 9.9 (ρ̄ unramified with distinct eigenvalues, N(x) ≡ 1 mod p), and let π′ be any irreducible admissible representation of G such that π′ ≄ π. Then Ext^1(π, π′) = Ext^1(π′, π) = 0 (Ext in the category of smooth G-representations).
items.note: Not planned. The proof combines Emerton–Helm Theorem 3.2.13 (missing) with Lemma 9.9 (missing): the characters χ_i are distinct, so the supercuspidal support determines π.

items.name: Definition 9.11 (the category 𝒞)
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be unramified with distinct eigenvalues and π the associated unramified principal series (Lemma 9.9). Let 𝒞 denote the category of locally admissible G-modules over A := O/ϖ^a (a ≥ 1; printed O/ϖ^k) such that every irreducible subquotient of every M ∈ 𝒞 is associated to ρ̄, equivalently (Lemma 9.9) is isomorphic to π (printed: 'is associated to π').
items.note: SR.0 plans smooth modules and admissibility ('Define admissibility by finite generation of every compact-open invariant module'). It plans neither locally admissible G-modules over A = O/ϖ^a nor the full subcategory whose irreducible subquotients are all ≅ π. The printed 'associated to π' should read 'associated to ρ̄', and 'O/ϖ^k' reuses k; the item already corrects both (sourceIssues E195, E196).

items.name: Lemma 9.12 (finite length objects of 𝒞 are parabolically induced)
items.statement: Assume ρ̄ unramified with distinct eigenvalues and let π = n-ind_B^G(χ). Suppose M ∈ 𝒞 has finite length as a G-module. Then there exist a finite length A-module M_B and a character χ̃ : B → Aut(M_B) (a smooth action of B on M_B, through D) whose irreducible constituents correspond to the character χ, such that M ≃ n-ind_B^G(M_B). More precisely: the parabolic restriction res_G^B(M) decomposes as ⊕_{w∈W} M_B^w, where the irreducible constituents of M_B^w are the characters χ^w (pairwise distinct, W the Weyl group), length_A(M_B^w) = length_G(M) for every w, M_B := M_B^{id}, and the composite M → n-ind_B^G res_G^B(M) = ⊕_W n-ind_B^G M_B^w → n-ind_B^G M_B is an isomorphism.
items.note: SR.2 plans the tools: normalized induction, Jacquet functors, 'exactness in the valid coefficient regime' (here p ≠ ℓ, so pro-ℓ unipotent coinvariants are exact) and 'the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing', which gives the W-indexed decomposition of res∘ind. The lemma itself is planned nowhere: finite-length objects of 𝒞 are n-ind_B^G(M_B), with length_A(M_B^w) = length_G(M). See sourceIssues E198 (the printed length-comparison reduction is false).

items.name: Deformations of the unramified character χ of D(F_x)
items.statement: Let χ : D(F_x) = (F_x^×)^n → k^× be the character of Lemma 9.9 (trivial on D(O_x)). A finite deformation χ̃ of χ (a character of D(F_x) with values in a finite local A-algebra, lifting χ) has pro-p image on D(O_x); more precisely χ̃·[χ]^{-1} ([χ] the Teichmüller lift) has pro-p image and factors through (lim← F_x^×/(F_x^×)^{p^m})^n ≅ (Z_p ⊕ lim← k^×/(k^×)^{p^m})^n = (Z_p ⊕ (k^× ⊗ Z_p))^n, where k = O_x/ϖ_x, the factor Z_p corresponding to a uniformizer and k^× ⊗ Z_p ≅ Z/q (q = |k^× ⊗ Z_p|, the p-part of N(x) − 1) to O_x^×. Hence the universal deformation of χ over A takes values in the completed group ring A⟦(Z/q × Z_p)^n⟧ ≅ ⊗_{i=1}^n (A[T_i]/(T_i^q − 1) ⊗ A⟦X_i⟧).
items.note: Some ingredients are planned: completed group rings R⟦G⟧ (PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1) and maximal pro-p quotients (Tau Ceti ProfiniteProPGroups Layer 3). No layer plans the deformation theory of a character of D(F_x) = (F_x^×)^n, the factorisation of χ̃·[χ]^{-1} through (Z_p ⊕ k_x^× ⊗ Z_p)^n, or the identification of the universal ring with A⟦(Z/q × Z_p)^n⟧ ≅ ⊗(A[T_i]/(T_i^q − 1) ⊗ A⟦X_i⟧). The printed display omits the exponent n on the right and the Teichmüller twist; the item corrects both (sourceIssues E199). The bracket A⟦X⟧ is Correction item 11 (sourceIssues E197).

items.name: Corollary 9.13 (𝒞 as modules over an explicit deformation ring)
items.statement: Assume ρ̄ unramified with distinct eigenvalues, N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, A = O/ϖ^a. Let q = |k^× ⊗ Z_p|, where k = O_x/ϖ_x. Then n-ind_B^G induces an equivalence of categories between the category of direct limits of finite length modules over the ring R := ⊗_{i=1}^n (A[T]/(T^q − 1) ⊗_O A⟦X⟧) (n copies with independent variables T_i, X_i; R ≅ A⟦(Z/q × Z_p)^n⟧ is the universal deformation ring of χ) and 𝒞. Here an R-module M_B is made into a B-module via the universal deformation of χ, inflated from D to B.
items.note: This is a block equivalence for the regular unramified principal-series block: 𝒞 is equivalent to direct limits of finite-length modules over R ≅ A⟦(Z/q × Z_p)^n⟧, via n-ind_B^G. No layer plans it. The nearest planned material is SR.5 (Helm's integral Bernstein centre and blocks, ℓ ≠ p), which does not state it. The only genuine polynomial ring here is A[T]/(T^q − 1); A⟦X⟧ is Correction item 11 (sourceIssues E197).

items.name: Lemma 9.14 (enough injectives; U(x)-invariants of injectives are acyclic)
items.statement: The category 𝒞 has enough injectives. The functor M ↦ M^{U(x)} from 𝒞 to the category of G(k) := G(O_x)/U(x) ≅ GL_n(k)-modules (k = O_x/ϖ_x) takes injectives to acyclic modules. (In the proof: for a deformation χ̃ of χ, which factors through (k^× × Z)^n, one has (n-ind_B^G χ̃)^{U(x)} ≃ Ind_{B(k)}^{G(k)}(χ̃|_{D(k)}); since finitely generated injective A[T]/(T^q − 1)-modules are free, the image of an injective has a filtration with graded pieces Φ := Ind_{B(k)}^{G(k)}(ψ), ψ the universal deformation of D(k) to the group algebra of the p-part of D(k); Φ is a direct summand of Ind_{B(k)}^{G(k)} k[D(k)] and hence of k[G(k)], so Φ is injective and acyclic.)
items.note: Not planned. The acyclicity of M ↦ M^{U(x)} on injectives of 𝒞 is specific to 𝒞. Its proof passes through (n-ind χ̃)^{U(x)} ≅ Ind_{B(k_x)}^{G(k_x)}(χ̃|D(k_x)) and injectivity of k[G(k_x)]. G(k) := G(O_x)/U(x) means GL_n(O_x/ϖ_x), not GL_n of the coefficient field.

items.name: Remark 9.15 (derived functors of invariants on 𝒞 are group cohomology)
items.statement: Since U(x) is pro-ℓ with ℓ ≠ p (printed: pro-p), H^i(U(x), M) = 0 for i > 0 and all M ∈ 𝒞. Hence for any subgroup U(x) ⊂ Γ ⊂ G(O_x), Hochschild–Serre gives H^i(Γ, M) ≅ H^i(Γ/U(x), M^{U(x)}). Any injective G(k)-module is injective as a Γ/U(x)-module (Γ/U(x) ⊂ G(k)). Hence, by Lemma 9.14, the right derived functors of M ↦ M^Γ on 𝒞 are well defined and coincide with H^i(Γ, M) (continuous cohomology).
items.note: The group-cohomological inputs are planned. Vanishing of H^i(U(x), M), i > 0, for pro-ℓ U(x) and p-primary M is in Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology Layers 10–11 ('a class of Hⁱ(G, M) annihilated by restriction to an open U is annihilated by (G : U)'; cd_p, with the edge case 'p not dividing the order of any G ⧸ U'). Hochschild–Serre is ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.2. The conclusion itself, that the right derived functors of M ↦ M^Γ on 𝒞 are H^i(Γ, M), rests on Lemma 9.14 (missing) and is specific to 𝒞. The printed 'U(x) is pro-p' must read pro-ℓ.

items.name: The operator V = V_{ϖ_x} and the ordinary projector e_α
items.statement: Let P(T) = (T − α)Q(T) be the polynomial whose roots are the Satake parameters of π (equivalently the eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_x), which are distinct, so Q(α) ≠ 0). The Hecke algebra of U_0(x) contains the operator V = V_{ϖ_x} given by the double coset of the diagonal matrix diag(1, …, 1, ϖ_x) (n − 1 entries 1, final entry ϖ_x). P(V) is zero on π^{U_0(x)} and hence acts nilpotently on M^{U_0(x)} for M ∈ 𝒞. Define e_α := lim_{m→∞} Q(V)^{m!} (printed lim_→ Q(V)^{n!}), with Q lifted to O[T]; e_α is an idempotent projecting M^{U_0(x)} onto the localization of M^{U_0(x)} at the ideal (V − α), for any lift of α to O.
items.note: The generic pieces are planned. SR.1 plans integral double-coset operators ('construct integral double-coset operators by finite correspondences where averaging is unavailable'), and PadicFamilies L0a the factorial-power projector ('U^(n!) is eventually constant with value the projector e onto the invertible summand'). Not planned: the computation that V acts on the n-dimensional π^{U_0(x)} through the Satake parameters, so that P(V) = 0 there and P(V) is nilpotent on M^{U_0(x)} for M ∈ 𝒞. The printed exponent n! clashes with the rank n.

items.name: The functors F, G and the natural transformation ι
items.statement: Define functors on 𝒞 by F(M) := M^{G(O_x)} and G(M) := e_α M^{U_0(x)}, and ι : F → G as the composite of the inclusion M^{G(O_x)} ↪ M^{U_0(x)} with e_α. F and G are left exact; as 𝒞 has enough injectives (Lemma 9.14) they have right derived functors R^kF, R^kG, and since e_α is exact, Remark 9.15 gives R^kF(M) ≃ H^k(G(O_x), M) and R^kG(M) ≃ e_α H^k(U_0(x), M).
items.note: The general derived-functor machinery exists in Mathlib. The functors F(M) = M^{G(O_x)}, G(M) = e_α M^{U_0(x)}, the transformation ι, and the identifications R^kF ≅ H^k(G(O_x), −), R^kG ≅ e_α H^k(U_0(x), −) on 𝒞 depend on Lemma 9.14 and Remark 9.15, both missing.

items.name: Theorem 9.16 (level raising isomorphism at a prime with distinct eigenvalues)
items.statement: In the setting of §9.4.1 (N(x) ≡ 1 mod p; ρ̄ : G_x → GL_n(k) unramified with distinct eigenvalues of ρ̄(Frob_x); π the associated unramified principal series; α one of the eigenvalues; 𝒞, F, G, ι as defined), the natural transformation ι : F → G is an isomorphism of functors on 𝒞. In particular, for every M ∈ 𝒞 and every k ≥ 0 there is an isomorphism ι_* : H^k(G(O_x), M) → e_α H^k(U_0(x), M).
items.note: Planned nowhere. ACC+ needs the analogous local input for CM fields: KT17 Lemmas 5.3–5.4, used in the proofs of ACC+ Lemmas 6.5.8–6.5.9 (Iwahori level, all eigenvalues distinct). No layer names that input either; PA.4 says only 'identify its specialization with the original complex'. Theorem 9.16 is purely local: parahoric invariants of the unramified principal-series block.

items.name: Clozel–Harris–Taylor Lemma 3.2.2 (degree 0 comparison), as recalled in Remark 9.17
items.statement: As recalled in Remark 9.17: [3, Lemma 3.2.2] implies that ι_* is an isomorphism for k = 0 for modules M ∈ 𝒞 of the form N ⊗ O/ϖ^n where N is an admissible O[GL_n(F_x)]-module, flat over O, with N ⊗_O K̄ semisimple; its implicit hypothesis on ρ̄ is only that the particular eigenvalue α of ρ̄(Frob_x) has multiplicity one, and M need not lie in 𝒞 (for the module M of [3, §3] one can deduce M ∈ 𝒞 from local–global compatibility). Thorne [53, Proposition 5.9] generalizes [3, Lemma 3.2.2].
items.note: No layer plans CHT §3.2 or Thorne's Proposition 5.9; an atlas search for CHT or Clozel–Harris–Taylor finds only unrelated matches. I did not check the statement against CHT or Thorne; it follows Remark 9.17. It is recorded as the degree-0 comparison under the weaker hypothesis that α has multiplicity one. External input: L. Clozel, M. Harris, R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), Lemma 3.2.2 [3]; J. Thorne, On the automorphy of l-adic Galois representations with small residual image, J. Inst. Math. Jussieu (2012), Proposition 5.9 [53]

items.name: Remark 9.8 (injectivity of pull-back in the lowest degree)
items.statement: (Remark to Lemma 9.6: n = 2, x a Taylor–Wiles prime.) The proof of Lemma 9.6 is related to those of Lemmas 3.5 and 5.8, where only the lowest degree was needed, which is more elementary. Let q0 be the lowest degree in which H^{q0}(Y, O/ϖ)_m ≠ 0. By Hochschild–Serre, the kernel of H^{q0}(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n) → H^{q0}(X_1(x), O/ϖ^n) has a filtration by (subquotients of) terms H^i(Δ, H^j(X_1(x), O/ϖ^n)) with j < q0. By assumption these coefficients vanish after localization at m for j < q0, so the localized kernel vanishes and the map is injective. Hence the argument in the proof of Lemma 9.6 using the representation Π generated by w ∈ W applies in this lowest degree. Analysis of this spectral sequence suggests that the localized map is not in general injective in degrees > q0 when l0 > 0. The paper does not define X_0(x), X_1(x), Δ or the vanishing assumption. X_0(x) is the level-x quotient Y_0(x), and X_1(x) → X_0(x) is a Galois cover with group Δ; Δ is not the group Γ/Γ^1 of the proof of Lemma 9.6. See sourceIssues E193.
items.note: The kernel of H^{q0}(X_0(x)) → H^{q0}(X_1(x)) is filtered by H^i(Δ, H^j(X_1(x))) with j < q0. This is the Hecke-equivariant finite-cover Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (ALS.6), localised at m (IHG.2). The vanishing hypothesis for j < q0 is of Conjecture B(4)(a) type and enters as a hypothesis. The closing claim that injectivity fails for i > q0 when l0 > 0 is a heuristic, not a theorem. Cluster K9 marked the same item planned, citing ALS.6 and ALS.4; I cite IHG.2 for the localisation, because ALS.4's localisation clause concerns boundary strata.

items.name: The G-modules M_j at a Taylor–Wiles prime (§9.4.2)
items.statement: (GL(n) setting of §9.4.2.) Let X, X_0(x) and X(x^m) be the arithmetic quotients with the fixed level away from x and level G(O_x), U_0(x), and the full congruence subgroup of level x^m at x, respectively; let m (also written m_∅) be the maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra away from x attached to r̄, with r̄|G_x unramified with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues. For j ≥ 0 and n ≥ 1 put M_j := lim_{m→∞} H^j(X(x^m), O/ϖ^n)_m (direct limit over the level at x), a smooth G = GL_n(F_x)-module over O/ϖ^n.
items.note: M_j = lim_m H^j(X(x^m), O/ϖ^n)_m is a direct limit over level at x ∤ p, i.e. tame level. GL_n(F_x) acts smoothly on it by right translation, and it is localised at a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra away from x. All of this is an instance of ALS.6, SR.0 and IHG.2. Attaching m to r̄ uses r̄_m from Conjecture B, which is missing (cluster K9's conj-B-residual-galois-rep).

items.name: M_j lies in 𝒞
items.statement: Assume (local–global compatibility at x) that every irreducible G-subrepresentation π′ ⊂ M_j[m] lies in 𝒞, i.e. π′ ≅ π. Then M_j ∈ 𝒞. (M_j is filtered as a G-module by the admissible module M_j[m], and Lemma 9.10 propagates the condition to every irreducible subquotient.)
items.note: This is a global statement: M_j ∈ 𝒞, assuming local–global compatibility at x for the irreducible subrepresentations of M_j[m]. The paper says only 'By assumption'. It uses Lemma 9.10 and the category 𝒞, both missing. No layer plans it.

items.name: Conjecture B part 5 at a prime with distinct eigenvalues (GL(n), informal)
items.statement: Under the assumptions of §9.4.2, Hochschild–Serre gives spectral sequences H^i(G(O_x), M_j) ⇒ H^{i+j}(X, O/ϖ^n)_{m_∅} and e_α H^i(U_0(x), M_j) ⇒ e_α H^{i+j}(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n)_{m_∅} = H^{i+j}(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n)_m, where m = (m_∅, V − α). The maps ι_* form a morphism of spectral sequences which is an isomorphism on E_2 by Theorem 9.16. Hence e_α : H^*(X, O/ϖ^n)_{m_∅} → H^*(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n)_m is an isomorphism, which is the GL(n)-analogue of Conjecture B part (5) for Q = {x}.
items.note: The Hochschild–Serre spectral sequences of the tower X(x^m) → X are planned (ALS.6). The morphism of spectral sequences given by ι_*, and the conclusion that e_α identifies H^*(X, O/ϖ^n)_{m∅} with H^*(X_0(x), O/ϖ^n)_m, are not planned. This is an informal GL(n) discharge of Conjecture B(5) at primes with distinct Frobenius eigenvalues; the paper only asserts that the PGL(n) case follows. Cluster K9 routed Conjecture B(5) as a hypothesis, discharged for n = 2 by Lemma 9.6. See sourceIssues E194 (GL spaces are torus, not circle, bundles).

items.name: Standing hypotheses of §9.5 (modularity lifting)
items.statement: Notation of §§8.4–8.5 and 9.1–9.3. F is a number field, n ≥ 1, and p > n is a prime unramified in F. O is the ring of integers of a finite extension K/Q_p, with uniformizer ϖ and residue field k, and Frac W(k) contains the image of every embedding F ↪ Q̄_p. r̄ : G_F → GL_n(k) is continuous and absolutely irreducible, and: Fontaine–Laffaille with weights [0, 1, …, n − 1] at each v | p (for each τ); at worst unipotently ramified at each v ∤ p, with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p wherever r̄ ramifies; odd at each v | ∞. ξ : G_F → O^× lifts det r̄, with ξ|I_v = ε^{n(n−1)/2} for v | p and ξ|I_v = 1 for v ∤ p. R is a finite set of primes, disjoint from S_p and containing the ramification primes of r̄, with N(v) ≡ 1 mod p for v ∈ R. S = S_p ⊔ R and T = S_p ∪ R. χ = (χ_v)_{v∈R}, where χ_v = (χ_{v,1}, …, χ_{v,n}) are distinct characters I_v → 1 + m_O with trivial product; they define the local system O(χ) of §9.1 via ψ_v = χ_v∘Art_v. q0 and l0 are as in §8.4. Y = Y(K_∅), Y_0(Q) and Y_1(Q) are the arithmetic quotients of Res_{F/Q} PGL(n) of §9.1 (Iwahori level at R), and T := T_{∅,1} (Definition 9.1 with Q = ∅, ψ = 1). Assume: (i) there is a maximal ideal m of T with r̄_m ≅ r̄; (ii) r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) is big; (iii) an integer q ≥ h^1_{L^⊥,T}(G_F, ad^0 r̄(1)) is fixed, and for each N ≥ 1 the set Q_N (with (ψ̄_v)_{v∈Q_N}) satisfies the conclusions of Proposition 8.5. Namely: |Q_N| = q; Q_N ∩ S = ∅; N(v) ≡ 1 mod p^N; r̄|G_v ≅ s̄_v ⊕ ψ̄_v with ψ̄_v a one-dimensional generalized Frobenius eigenspace; and R^{□_T}_{S_{Q_N}}, R^{□_T}_{S^χ_{Q_N}} are quotients of power series rings over R^1_loc, R^χ_loc in g = q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 − l0 variables. (iv) Conjecture B holds for each set Q_N (as stated on p. 425) and also for Q = ∅, in each case for ψ = 1 and for ψ = χ. The proof uses Q = ∅ for the surjections R_S ↠ T_m and R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m}, and for the vanishing statements on Y.
items.note: Most clauses are planned elsewhere: Fontaine–Laffaille at v | p (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7), unipotent ramification and the χ_v (R08.2/L7), Taylor–Wiles sets satisfying Proposition 8.5 (R04.5/G8, per clusters K8 and K9), the Hecke algebra T_{∅,1} (IHG.2/ALS.3), and bigness (G7, though CHT bigness is not yet named there). Two parts are unplanned: rank-n trace oddness at real places (missing, per cluster K8's odd-representation) and the Conjecture B clauses, namely r̄_m ≅ r̄ in (i) and Conjecture B for every Q_N in (iv). The package is therefore conditional and unplanned as a whole. See sourceIssues E203 (Theorem 5.16 omits hypotheses assumed here).

items.name: The Taylor–Wiles covers Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) and S_N
items.statement: For each N ≥ 1 the natural covering Y_1(Q_N) → Y_0(Q_N) has Galois group Δ̃ := ∏_{x∈Q_N} (O_F/x)^×. Choose a surjection Δ̃ ↠ Δ_N := (Z/p^N Z)^q (possible since N(x) ≡ 1 mod p^N) and let Y_{Δ_N}(Q_N) → Y_0(Q_N) be the corresponding subcover. For 0 ≤ M ≤ N regard Δ_M as a quotient of Δ_N in the natural way; this gives subcovers Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) → Y_0(Q_N) with group Δ_M (Y_{Δ_0}(Q_N) = Y_0(Q_N)). Put S_N := O[Δ_N] (group ring of the finite group Δ_N), a local ring with maximal ideal m_{S_N}.
items.note: Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) → Y_0(Q_N) is the Galois subcover of the level L_Q ⊂ K_Q attached to the quotient Δ̃ ↠ Δ_M. It is an instance of AA.4's nested-level coverings over ALS.0's arithmetic quotients. The levels K_Q ⊃ L_Q themselves are the separate missing item level-subgroups-KQ-LQ, routed to ALS.0/ALS.3 by clusters K8 and K9. The printed product should run over x ∈ Q_N.

items.name: Minimal perfect complexes D̃_N computing localized homology
items.statement: By Conjecture B (for Q_N) and the results of §7.1 (Lemmas 7.1–7.4), there is a perfect complex D̃_N of free S_N-modules (a homological complex) such that: (1) D̃_N is concentrated in degrees q0, …, q0 + l0; (2) the complex D̃_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/m_{S_N} has trivial differentials; (3) for each i, each n ≥ 1 and each 0 ≤ M ≤ N there is an isomorphism of S_N-modules H_i(D̃_N ⊗_{S_N} S_M/ϖ^n) ≅ (lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q_N} Q_x(V_x)^{k!}) H_i(Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m*}, where (as in Conjecture B(5)) P_x(X) = (X − α_x)Q_x(X) is the characteristic polynomial of r̄(Frob_x), α_x = ψ̄_x(Frob_x), V_x = T_{x,1}, and m* is the dual maximal ideal (Remark 9.5).
items.note: The generic §7.1 construction is planned (ALS.1, ALS.6, IHG.2, with P7 minimal complexes; cluster K7's betti-localized-complex-D). Two parts are missing. Concentration in degrees q0, …, q0 + l0 needs Conjecture B(4)(a). The projector ∏_x Q_x(V_x)^{k!} needs the Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebra containing V_x, which cluster K9 marked missing (def-9-1-hecke-algebra-TQ). The IKM analogue, Proposition 13.9, is missing too. The printed limit variable n clashes with O/ϖ^n.

items.name: The χ-twisted complexes D̃^χ_N
items.statement: Working with the local system O(χ) on the Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N) attached to χ = (χ_v)_{v∈R} (§9.1), there is a perfect complex D̃^χ_N of free S_N-modules concentrated in degrees q0, …, q0 + l0, with D̃^χ_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/m_{S_N} having trivial differentials, and such that for each i, each n ≥ 1 and 0 ≤ M ≤ N there is an isomorphism of S_N-modules H_i(D̃^χ_N ⊗_{S_N} S_M/ϖ^n) ≅ (lim_{k→∞} ∏_{x∈Q_N} Q_x(V_x)^{k!}) H_{i,χ}(Y_{Δ_M}(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m*}.
items.note: Same status as complex-D-tilde-N, for the local system O(χ). The χ-twisted local systems are planned (ALS.1; cluster K9's local-system-O-psi). The concentration statement and the Taylor–Wiles projector are conditional on Conjecture B and on the missing Taylor–Wiles-level Hecke algebra. See sourceIssues E207 (should use the dual local system O(χ^{-1})).

items.name: Duals of localized cohomology are localized homology
items.statement: For each N and n ≥ 1, H^*(Y_1(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)^∨_m ≃ H_*(Y_1(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m*} and H^*_χ(Y_1(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)^∨_m ≃ H_{*,χ}(Y_1(Q_N), O/ϖ^n)_{m*} (degree by degree; ∨ the Pontryagin dual, m* the dual maximal ideal). The paper attributes this to the assumed vanishing of the cohomology of the boundary after localization at m (Conjecture B part (4)).
items.note: The identification is assembled from the boundary triangle (ALS.4), finite-level duality with Hecke adjoints (ALS.5) and universal-coefficient/Pontryagin duality (ALS.1), with the boundary vanishing B(4)(b) as an explicit hypothesis, as the paper says. The dual ideal m* is planned (cluster K9's dual-maximal-ideal-m-star). This matches cluster K9's rmk-9-5-homological-formulation and IKM's prop-13-6. See sourceIssues E207 (χ-twisted identity needs χ^{-1} on homology).

items.name: T_χ, the maximal ideal m of T_χ, and the surjections R_S ↠ T_m, R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m}
items.statement: Since the χ_v are trivial modulo ϖ, H^*(Y, O/ϖ) ≅ H^*_χ(Y, O/ϖ) compatibly with Hecke operators; hence m induces a maximal ideal of T_χ := T_{∅,χ}, also denoted m. By Conjecture B (Q = ∅, ψ = 1 and ψ = χ) there are surjections R_S ↠ T_m and R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m}, where R_S, R_{S^χ} are the universal deformation rings of type S and S^χ of §8.5.2.
items.note: Two parts are planned: H^*(Y, O/ϖ) ≅ H^*_χ(Y, O/ϖ) (O(χ)/ϖ = O/ϖ as local systems, ALS.1) and T_χ as an image algebra (IHG.2). The surjections R_S ↠ T_m and R_{S^χ} ↠ T_{χ,m} are consequences of Conjecture B, which cluster K9 marked missing (conj-B-type-SQ-and-R-to-T-surjection); IKM's conj-B is also missing.

items.name: Theorem 9.19 (main modularity lifting theorem: R^red = T^red)
items.statement: Assume the standing hypotheses of §9.5 (setup-sec-9-5): in particular Conjecture B (for Q = ∅ and for the Taylor–Wiles sets Q_N, with ψ = 1 and ψ = χ), a maximal ideal m of T = T_{∅,1} with r̄_m ≅ r̄, and r̄(G_{F(ζ_p)}) big. Regard H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m as an R_S-module via the surjection R_S ↠ T_m. Then H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m is a nearly faithful R_S-module.
items.note: No layer states a GL(n) modularity lifting theorem over an arbitrary number field conditional on Conjecture B. The abstract patching and support theory is planned (P8, P9, R03.6), and PA.3/PA.4 plan the unconditional ACC+ analogue over CM fields. The arithmetic input (Conjecture B, the Taylor–Wiles-level complexes and the verification of the patching hypotheses) is not planned. sourceIssues E181 records a gap: condition (d) of Theorem 6.3 needs local–global compatibility of diamond operators at Taylor–Wiles primes, which Conjecture B does not state.

items.name: Patching rings and modules in the proof of Theorem 9.19
items.statement: Input to Proposition 6.6 (two data i = 1, 2, each satisfying the hypotheses of Theorem 6.3): g := q + |T| − 1 − [F:Q]·n(n − 1)/2 − l0, the number of variables in Proposition 8.5(4). S_∞ := O⟦(Z_p)^q⟧ and S_N := O[Δ_N]. j := n²|T| − 1 and O^□ := O⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧, with M^□ := M ⊗_O O^□ as in Theorem 6.3; for the complete local rings R_{S_{Q_N}} this is used in the form R⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧. R^1_∞ := R^1_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧ and R^2_∞ := R^χ_loc⟦x_1, …, x_g⟧. (R^1, H^1) := (R_S, H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m) and (R^2, H^2) := (R_{S^χ}, H^{q0}_χ(Y, K/O)^∨_m). T := T^1 = T^2 is the complex of finite-dimensional k-vector spaces in degrees 0, …, l0 with T^i = H^{q0+l0−i}(Y, O/ϖ)^∨_m (printed: T^i = H^{i−l0}(Y, O/ϖ)^∨_m) and all differentials zero. Hence H^{l0}(T) = H^{q0}(Y, O/ϖ)^∨_m ≅ H^1/ϖ, using H^{q0−1}(Y, K/O)_m = 0.
items.note: The shape of the data is planned. The reviewed P8 node takes 'S_∞ = O[[(Z_p)^q]], S_N = O[(Z/p^N)^q], O′ = O[[z₁,…,z_j]] ... R_∞ ∈ C_O of Krull dimension 1 + j + q − l₀ ... T a complex ... with H^{l₀}(T) ≅ H/ϖ'. R^i_loc is planned at L7 (cluster K8) and g at R04.5/G8. The instantiation needs H^1 = H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m to be an R_S-module, which comes from Conjecture B (missing); this is the same reason IKM's patched-rings-15 is missing. T is misprinted (sourceIssues E208): it should be T^i = H^{q0+l0−i}(Y, O/ϖ)^∨_m. The ⟦ ⟧ for S_∞, O^□ and R^i_∞ are Correction items 1 and 12 (sourceIssues E12, E205).

items.name: Properties of R^i_∞, R^i, H^i
items.statement: Each R^i_∞ (i = 1, 2) is p-torsion free and equidimensional of Krull dimension 1 + q + j − l0; there is a natural isomorphism R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ; and there are natural compatible isomorphisms R^1/ϖ ≅ R^2/ϖ and H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ.
items.note: The ring statements are planned. Each R^i_∞ is p-torsion free and equidimensional (Lemma 8.2, at L7 per cluster K8), and R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ is L7's comparison, which P9 takes as the 'common residual specialization'. R_S/ϖ ≅ R_{S^χ}/ϖ follows from the local rings mod ϖ (R04.3). I checked the dimension: 1 + (n²−1)|T| + [F:Q]n(n−1)/2 + g = 1 + j + q − l0. The clause H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ, compatible with the R^i-actions, needs Conjecture B for the actions and B(4)(a) to identify H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m/ϖ with H^{q0}(Y, O/ϖ)^∨_m; this is unplanned, so the item as a whole is missing. See sourceIssues E165 (p-torsion-freeness of R^i_∞ is unsupported).

items.name: Patching complexes D^1_N, D^2_N
items.statement: Regard the homological complexes D̃_N, D̃^χ_N (degrees q0, …, q0 + l0) as cohomological complexes concentrated in degrees 0, …, l0 (cohomological degree c corresponding to homological degree q0 + l0 − c). Let D^1_N := D̃_N/ϖ^N and D^2_N := D̃^χ_N/ϖ^N, perfect complexes of S_N/ϖ^N-modules. Then H^c(D^1_N) ≅ (lim_k ∏_{x∈Q_N} Q_x(V_x)^{k!}) H^{q0+l0−c}(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_N), O/ϖ^N)^∨_m, and similarly H^c(D^2_N) with H^*_χ (printed: 'computes H^*(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_N), O/ϖ^N)^∨_m … after a shift in degree by q0'). One may and does assume D^i_N ⊗_{S_N} S_N/m_{S_N} ≅ T for i = 1, 2.
items.note: P8 plans the abstract input: 'D_N perfect complexes of S_N/ϖ^N-modules with D_N ⊗ S_N/m ≃ T'. The instance D^i_N = D̃_N/ϖ^N depends on the missing D̃_N. The identification D^i_N ⊗ S_N/m ≅ T needs Conjecture B(5) at Q_N to compare with the level of Y. The printed 'shift in degree by q0' should be the reversal c ↦ q0 + l0 − c.

items.name: Framed global deformation rings and the surjections φ^i_N
items.statement: Choose representatives for the universal deformations of type S_{Q_N} and S^χ_{Q_N} which agree modulo ϖ. This gives isomorphisms R^{□_T}_{S_{Q_N}} ≅ R_{S_{Q_N}}⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧ and R^{□_T}_{S^χ_{Q_N}} ≅ R_{S^χ_{Q_N}}⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧ (Lemma 8.3). These are the rings R^□_{S_{Q_N}} and R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}} in the notation of Theorem 6.3, and R^□_{S_{Q_N}}/ϖ ≅ R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}}/ϖ. By Proposition 8.5(4), choose surjections R^1_∞ ↠ R^□_{S_{Q_N}} and R^2_∞ ↠ R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}}. They must be chosen compatibly modulo ϖ: under R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ and R^□_{S_{Q_N}}/ϖ ≅ R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}}/ϖ they reduce to the same map, which is possible by sending the x_i to elements with equal reductions. The paper omits this requirement. Composing with the natural maps R^□_{S_{Q_N}} ↠ R_{S_{Q_N}} ↠ R_S = R^1 and R^□_{S^χ_{Q_N}} ↠ R_{S^χ_{Q_N}} ↠ R_{S^χ} = R^2 gives surjections φ^1_N : R^1_∞ ↠ R^1 and φ^2_N : R^2_∞ ↠ R^2.
items.note: R^{□_T} ≅ R⟦z_1, …, z_j⟧ with j = n²|T| − 1 is Lemma 8.3, and the surjections R^i_∞ ↠ R^□ come from Proposition 8.5(4); clusters K8 and K9 found both planned. The composites φ^i_N are formal. The blueprint of R04.x/G8 should record the choice of universal representatives that agree mod ϖ, the unframed version of what ACC+ gets from its canonical isomorphisms R_N/ϖ ≅ R′_N/ϖ. The brackets ⟦z⟧ are Correction item 12 (sourceIssues E205). See sourceIssues E209 (surjections must agree modulo ϖ).

items.name: Verification of the hypotheses of Theorem 6.3 and Proposition 6.6
items.statement: (b) For each M ≥ N ≥ 0 with M ≥ 1 and each n ≥ 1, Conjecture B (for Q_M) gives an action of R_{S_{Q_M}} (resp. R_{S^χ_{Q_M}}) on H^*(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_M), O/ϖ^n)_m (resp. H^*_χ(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_M), O/ϖ^n)_m) (printed with Q_N); applying X ↦ X^□ and the surjection R^1_∞ ↠ R^□_{S_{Q_M}} (resp. R^2_∞ ↠ R^□_{S^χ_{Q_M}}) gives an action of R^1_∞ (resp. R^2_∞) on H^*(D^{1,□}_M ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^n) (resp. H^*(D^{2,□}_M ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ^n)), so condition (b) of Theorem 6.3 holds for both data; condition (d) is claimed to follow from Conjecture B and condition (c) to be clear. Finally, for all M ≥ N ≥ 0 with M ≥ 1 there are isomorphisms H^{l0}((D^1_M)^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) ≅ (projected) H^{q0}(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_M), O/ϖ)^{∨,□}_m ≅ H^{q0}_χ(Y_{Δ_N}(Q_M), O/ϖ)^{∨,□}_m ≅ H^{l0}((D^2_M)^□ ⊗_{S_M} S_N/ϖ) (printed with H^{l0}(Y…)), compatible with the actions of R^i_∞, giving the commutative square required by Proposition 6.6.
items.note: This is the arithmetic verification of Theorem 6.3's conditions (b), (c) and (d), and of the commutative square of Proposition 6.6, all conditional on Conjecture B for Q_M. PA.4 plans the analogous verification only for the ACC+ tower over CM fields ('Prove that the system of finite-level complexes satisfies the boundedness and compatibility hypotheses of ultrapatching'). sourceIssues E181 records that (d) needs local–global compatibility of diamond operators, which Conjecture B lacks, and sourceIssues E211 records the misprint Q_N for Q_M. See sourceIssues E132 (condition (c) holds only for n ≤ N).

items.name: Existence of the patched complexes P^{1,□}_∞, P^{2,□}_∞
items.statement: Proposition 6.6 yields complexes P^{1,□}_∞ and P^{2,□}_∞ of finitely generated S^□_∞-modules, concentrated in degrees 0, …, l0, satisfying conclusions (i)–(iv) of Theorem 6.3 for i = 1, 2: (i) P^{i,□}_∞ is a projective resolution, of minimal length, of H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞); (ii) R^i_∞ ⊗̂_O S^□_∞ acts on H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞), extending the action of S^□_∞, and H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞) is a finite R^i_∞-module; (iii) its R^i_∞-depth is 1 + j + q − l0 = dim R^i_∞; (iv) there are a surjection φ^i_∞ : R^i_∞ ↠ R^i and an isomorphism H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞)/a ≅ H^i of R^i_∞-modules, and the image of a in End(H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞)) is contained in that of ker φ^i_∞. In addition there is an isomorphism of R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ-modules H^{l0}(P^{1,□}_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l0}(P^{2,□}_∞)/ϖ, compatible with H^1/ϖ ≅ H^2/ϖ: the square through H^{l0}(P^{i,□}_∞)/(a + ϖ) commutes.
items.note: The abstract Proposition 6.6 is planned: the R03.6 node records it and its omitted proof as an obligation, and P8 plans the 'comparison of two patched systems'. This item is Proposition 6.6 applied to the Conjecture B data of §9.5, which is unplanned; the same reason made IKM's lemma-15-3 missing.

items.name: H^{l0}(P^{2,□}_∞) is nearly faithful over R^2_∞
items.statement: Spec R^2_∞ is irreducible (Lemma 8.2(3): Spec R^χ_loc is irreducible), so by Theorem 6.4 (case (2), as established in its proof) H^{l0}(P^{2,□}_∞) is a nearly faithful R^2_∞-module. Consequently H^{l0}(P^{1,□}_∞)/ϖ ≅ H^{l0}(P^{2,□}_∞)/ϖ is nearly faithful over R^1_∞/ϖ ≅ R^2_∞/ϖ.
items.note: The algebra is planned. The R03.6 node states '(2) if R_∞[1/p] is irreducible then H is a nearly faithful R-module', and its proof shows 'maximal depth makes the support a union of top-dimensional components, which for irreducible R_∞[1/p] is everything'. Irreducibility of Spec R^χ_loc (Lemma 8.2(3)) is at L7. The item concerns the unplanned patched object H^{l0}(P^{2,□}_∞) of §9.5. The paper cites Theorem 6.4 for the R_∞-level statement, which is proved only inside that theorem's proof.

items.name: Taylor's lemma: nearly faithful modulo ϖ implies nearly faithful (Ihara avoidance)
items.statement: As used in the proof of Theorem 9.19: let R be a complete local noetherian O-algebra which is p-torsion free and equidimensional, such that every irreducible component of Spec(R/ϖ) is contained in a unique irreducible component of Spec(R), and let M be a finitely generated R-module on which p is not a zero divisor. If M/ϖM is a nearly faithful R/ϖR-module, then M is a nearly faithful R-module.
items.note: Taylor's module-level Ihara-avoidance lemma is planned in P9 and R03.6, in agreement with cluster K8. I did not check the statement or numbering against Taylor [11]; it is given in the form CG use. External input: R. Taylor, Automorphy for some l-adic lifts of automorphic mod l Galois representations. II, Publ. Math. IHÉS 108 (2008), 183–239 [11], Lemma 2.2

items.name: Transfer to the unipotent data and conclusion of Theorem 9.19
items.statement: H^{l0}(P^{1,□}_∞) is p-torsion free: by Theorem 6.3(iii) its R^1_∞-depth equals dim R^1_∞, so every associated prime is a minimal prime of R^1_∞, and these have characteristic 0 by Lemma 8.2. Hence, by Lemma 8.2(4) and [11, Lemma 2.2], H^{l0}(P^{1,□}_∞) is nearly faithful over R^1_∞, and by conclusion (iv) of Theorem 6.3 (as in the proof of Theorem 6.4) H^1 = H^{q0}(Y, K/O)^∨_m is nearly faithful over R^1 = R_S.
items.note: Every algebraic step is planned. Depth = dim forces associated primes to be minimal (R03.3's associated-prime lemmas; cluster K7's max-depth-support-components). Minimal primes have characteristic 0 by Lemma 8.2 (L7). Taylor's lemma is P9/R03.6. The transfer by conclusion (iv) is the R03.6 node step 'Reduce near-faithfulness of H over R to that of H^{l₀}(P_∞) over R_∞'. The item applies these to the unplanned §9.5 objects and ends in the conclusion of Theorem 9.19.

items.name: Modular and potentially modular Galois representations
items.statement: The paper uses 'modular' only in the sense of the conclusions of Theorem 1.2 (p. 301) and Theorem 5.16 (p. 384): r : G_F → GL_n(O) is modular if there exists a regular algebraic cusp form π for GL_n(A_F) such that L(r, s) = L(π, s). In Theorem 5.16, π also has trivial infinitesimal character, matching Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, n − 1. 'Potentially modular' (Theorem 1.1(1), §10) is not defined in the paper; in §10 it means that r|G_L is modular for some finite extension L/K, obtained there by Moret-Bailly's theorem. Modularity of an elliptic curve E is likewise not defined; it is read as modularity of ρ_{E,p}, equivalently of the compatible system. For CM curves it is read in the usual sense, which allows isobaric, non-cuspidal automorphic representations (L(E, s) is then a product of two Hecke L-functions).
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 301; Theorem 5.16, p. 384; Theorem 1.1(1), p. 300; §10, pp. 428–429 (terms used; 'potentially modular' not defined)
items.note: 'Modular' (a regular algebraic cuspidal π with trivial infinitesimal character and L(r, s) = L(π, s)) and 'potentially modular' (modular after restriction to some finite L/K) are the endpoint notions of ML.0/ML.2, with AG2.0's regular algebraic cuspidal representations and R01.6's ρ_{E,p}. The trivial-infinitesimal-character normalization must be fixed in ML.0.

items.name: Sato–Tate conjecture for an elliptic curve
items.statement: (Standard statement, not given in the paper.) Let E be an elliptic curve over a number field F. For primes v of F where E has good reduction, write N(v) + 1 − #Ẽ(k_v) = 2√N(v)·cos θ_v with θ_v ∈ [0, π]. If E has no CM, the Sato–Tate conjecture asserts that the θ_v, with v ordered by norm, are equidistributed in [0, π] with respect to (2/π) sin²θ dθ. If E has CM by an imaginary quadratic field M, the corresponding (known) law is equidistribution with respect to (1/π) dθ when M ⊆ F, and with respect to ½δ_{π/2} + (1/(2π)) dθ when M ⊄ F.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1(2), p. 300 (term used, not defined in the paper; standard formulation)
items.note: The statement of the Sato–Tate law for non-CM E over a number field (and the CM law) is ML.3's endpoint. ACC+ Corollary 7.1.14, Sato–Tate over CM fields, is the case the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure README hands to ML.3.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(1) (conditional potential modularity of elliptic curves over any number field)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let F be any number field and E an elliptic curve over F. Then E is potentially modular.
items.note: This is conditional on Conjecture B. ML.2 plans potential automorphy only in proved cases, and ML.1's acceptance forbids to 'claim all elliptic curves over arbitrary number fields are covered'. ML.0 does allow endpoints with 'an explicit known/conditional/conjectural status'. No layer states this conditional theorem.

items.name: Theorem 1.1(2) (conditional Sato–Tate over any number field)
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let F be any number field and E an elliptic curve over F. Then the Sato–Tate conjecture is true for E.
items.note: This is conditional on Conjecture B. ML.3 plans Sato–Tate only in proved cases (Newton–Thorne; ACC+ Corollary 7.1.14 over CM fields). The deduction from the conditional potential modularity of odd symmetric powers is planned in ML.3 (hsbt-thm-4-2), but the conditional theorem over an arbitrary number field is stated nowhere.

items.name: CM elliptic curves (input 'well known')
items.statement: The paper states: 'If A has CM, then the result is well known' (no reference). Standard justification, not in the paper: suppose E/F has CM by an imaginary quadratic field M. Then V_pE is free of rank one over M ⊗ Q_p, and G_{FM} acts through the p-adic avatar of an algebraic Grössencharacter ψ of FM (Deuring, Shimura–Taniyama). So ρ_{E,p}|G_{FM} ⊗ Q̄_p is a sum of two characters. If M ⊄ F, ρ_{E,p} ≅ Ind_{G_{FM}}^{G_F} ψ_λ corresponds to the cuspidal automorphic induction of ψ, and E is modular over F. If M ⊆ F, ρ_{E,p} ⊗ Q̄_p is a sum of two characters and corresponds to an isobaric sum of Hecke characters, which is not cuspidal. The CM analogue of the Sato–Tate law follows from Hecke's equidistribution theorem for Grössencharacters.
items.note: Potential modularity of CM curves comes from the Hecke characters of CM.4 and monomial automorphic induction (R17.5); the CM equidistribution law comes from Hecke L-functions (AN.4) in ML.3's CM branch. CG give no argument ('well known'). When the CM field lies in F, ρ_{E,p} is a sum of two characters, so 'modular' must be read as isobaric: no cuspidal π on GL_2 matches it. External input: Deuring, Hecke (classical; not cited in the paper, which says 'the result is well known')

items.name: Reduction of Sato–Tate to potential modularity of symmetric powers (Harris–Shepherd-Barron–Taylor)
items.statement: As invoked on p. 428: 'To prove Theorem 1.1, it suffices (following, for example, the proof of Theorem 4.2 of [81]) to prove that for each n, there exists a p such that r [= Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{A,p}] is potentially modular.' That is, for a non-CM elliptic curve A over a number field K: if for every n ≥ 1 some prime p makes Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{A,p} potentially modular (over extensions of the kind produced in §10), then both parts of Theorem 1.1 hold for A. Part (1) is the case n = 1. The paper gives no further argument; [81] works over totally real fields.
items.note: The deduction of Sato–Tate from potential automorphy of symmetric powers is ML.3's endpoint argument. ACC+ Corollary 7.1.13, owned by ML.3 through the PotentialAutomorphyInfrastructure README, uses exactly 'the usual Brauer's theorem argument (together with known non-vanishing properties of automorphic L-functions as in [JS77]) as in [HSBT10, Thm. 4.2]'. Brauer induction is planned in Tau Ceti and Rankin–Selberg in AL.3. I did not check the statement against HSBT. See sourceIssues E214 (reduction needs simultaneous modularity over soluble subextensions). External input: M. Harris, N. Shepherd-Barron, R. Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy, Ann. Math. 171 (2010), 779–813 [81], proof of Theorem 4.2

items.name: Reduction of Theorem 1.1 to potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}
items.statement: Let A be an elliptic curve over a number field K with End_C(A) = Z. To prove Theorem 1.1 for A it suffices to show that for each n ≥ 1 there exists a prime p such that r = Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{A,p} : G_K → GL_{2n}(Q_p), the representation on the (2n−1)-th symmetric power of the p-adic Tate module of A, is potentially modular.
items.note: This is the HSBT Theorem 4.2 reduction applied to A; ML.3 plans it and G7 the symmetric-power representations. HSBT needs only the odd powers Sym^{2n−1}, because the even powers are reached by Rankin–Selberg (AL.3 retains nonvanishing 'only in their proved regions'). ML.3 is written around Newton–Thorne, where all symmetric powers are automorphic, so its blueprint must record this odd-only, potential variant. See sourceIssues E214 (reduction needs simultaneous modularity over soluble subextensions).

items.name: Extra hypothesis on (A, p) in §10
items.statement: For a non-CM elliptic curve A over a number field K and n ≥ 1: there exists a prime p which is totally split in K such that p + 1 is divisible by an integer N_2 > n + 1 (printed here: 'greater than n') prime to the conductor of A; moreover the mod-p representation ρ̄_A : G_K → GL_2(F_p) on A[p] is surjective, A has good reduction at all v | p, and for all v | p, ρ̄_A|G_{K_v} ≃ Ind_{G_{Q_{p^2}}}^{G_{Q_p}} ω_2 (K_v = Q_p since p splits), ω_2 a fundamental character of level 2 (so A has supersingular reduction at v).
items.note: The hypothesis is a conjunction of planned predicates: p totally split in K, N_2 | p + 1 with N_2 > n + 1 prime to the conductor, ρ̄_A surjective, good reduction at v | p, and ρ̄_A|G_{K_v} ≅ Ind ω_2 (supersingular). I classify it planned, following cluster K8's treatment of the §8.5 hypothesis package. The printed 'greater than n' is 'N_2 > n + 1' where it is used, and 'G_{Q_p}' means G_{K_v} with K_v = Q_p. See sourceIssues E213 (bound should be N_2 > 2n + 1).

items.name: The Dwork family and its λ-adic representations (BLGHT II)
items.statement: The Dwork family of [76]: a family of hypersurfaces over the open subscheme T_0 of the parameter line, with an action giving, for each number field L, t ∈ T_0(L) and prime λ of Q(ζ_N)^+ (N the parameter of the family), a λ-adic representation V_{λ,t} of G_L (here of dimension 2n, with Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, 2n − 1) with residual representation V[λ]_t; the V_{λ,t} for varying λ form a compatible system, so modularity of one member gives modularity of all.
items.note: An atlas-wide search for 'Dwork', 'Calabi', BLGHT, BLGGT and HSBT finds no plan for the Dwork family: its hypersurfaces, group action, invariant piece V_{λ,t}, compatible systems and residual monodromy. The same object is needed by ML.2's ACC+ route: ACC+ Proposition 7.2.3 is a variant of BLGGT Theorem 3.1.2, whose proof uses V_n[λ] of the Dwork family. That gap already exists in the atlas. External input: T. Barnet-Lamb, D. Geraghty, M. Harris, R. Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy II, Publ. Res. Inst. Math. Sci. 47 (2011), 29–98 [76]

items.name: Moret-Bailly's theorem in the form of [76, Proposition 6.2]
items.statement: Cited as [76, Proposition 6.2] (p. 429) and not stated in the paper. Standard form of Moret-Bailly's theorem: let K be a number field, S a finite set of places of K, M/K a finite extension, and X/K a smooth geometrically connected variety. For each v ∈ S let L_v/K_v be a finite Galois extension and Ω_v ⊂ X(L_v) a non-empty open Gal(L_v/K_v)-invariant subset for the v-adic topology. Then there are a finite Galois extension L/K, linearly disjoint from M over K, and a point P ∈ X(L) such that for every v ∈ S and every place w | v of L, L_w ≅ L_v over K_v and P ∈ Ω_v ⊂ X(L_w). Taking L_v = K_v makes v split completely in L, as §10 needs for p (conditions (3)).
items.note: Planned at R23.1 in the generality CG use: an arbitrary smooth geometrically irreducible variety, local opens, prescribed splitting and linear disjointness. I did not check the exact form of [76, Proposition 6.2]. Neither library has it. External input: [76] Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, PRIMS 47 (2011), Proposition 6.2 (after L. Moret-Bailly)

items.name: Potential automorphy argument of [76, Theorem 6.4]
items.statement: §10 follows the proof of [76, Theorem 6.4], a potential automorphy theorem of Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor proved via the Dwork family. Its statement is not given in the paper. The automorphy lifting steps are replaced by two applications of Theorem 5.16: one to the λ′-adic representation of the Dwork fibre V, one to Sym^{2n−1}(A)|G_L. The paper follows Theorem 6.4 rather than Theorem 6.3 of [76] because the latter 'proceeds via compatible families arising from the Dwork family such that V[λ]_t is ordinary but not crystalline, which would necessitate a different version of Theorem 5.16'; Theorem 5.16 requires crystalline representations at p. Data taken from the statement of [76, Theorem 6.4]: integers N_1, N_2 with p + 1 = N_1N_2 and N_2 > n + 1.
items.note: BLGHT's potential automorphy theorem, with its method (the Dwork family, crystalline specialisations, auxiliary N_1N_2 = p + 1 with N_2 > n + 1, and two applications of a lifting theorem), is planned nowhere. PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23 plans only Taylor's rank-two potential modularity via Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli. I did not check its statement against [76]. External input: [76] Barnet-Lamb–Geraghty–Harris–Taylor, A family of Calabi–Yau varieties and potential automorphy II, PRIMS 47 (2011), Theorem 6.4 (and its proof)

items.name: Residual modularity of inductions of Grössencharacters
items.statement: As used on p. 429: r′ is 'an ordinary weight 0 representation which [is] induced from G_{LM} for some suitable CM field M/Q of degree 2n'. Its residual representation r̄′ is residually modular 'coming from the induction of a Grossencharacter': r′ is induced from the λ′-adic character of an algebraic Grössencharacter θ of LM and is automorphic by automorphic induction. This gives the residual modularity (Theorem 5.16(8a)) for the application of Theorem 5.16 to V_{λ′,t}. The paper gives no details. Automorphic induction (Arthur–Clozel) needs LM/L cyclic (or solvable Galois), and a cusp form needs the induced representation to be irreducible. As in [76], M and θ are chosen so that these hold and r′ has Hodge–Tate weights 0, …, 2n − 1.
items.note: Automorphic induction is registered at ML.5 with its exact hypotheses, and the λ-adic avatars θ_λ of algebraic Grössencharacters are at AG2.0/CM.4. It is known (Arthur–Clozel) when LM/L is cyclic, so M must be chosen cyclic over Q, as in BLGHT; CG do not say this. Getting residual modularity in the sense of Theorem 5.16(8a) also needs π to be compared with the torsion Betti cohomology of Y (ALS.5/AS.5), which the paper leaves implicit. External input: Automorphic induction (Arthur–Clozel); not cited in the paper, which says 'the residual modularity coming from the induction of a Grossencharacter'

items.name: Existence of a Dwork-family point linking r̄ to an induced representation
items.statement: Assume the extra hypothesis for A, n and a sufficiently large p, and let r = Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{A,p}. Then there exist a sufficiently large prime l, a finite extension L/K, an integer N_2 > n + 1 with p + 1 = N_1N_2 (as in [76, Theorem 6.4]), primes λ | p and λ′ | l of Q(ζ_N)^+ and a point t ∈ T_0(L) of the Dwork family such that: (1) V[λ]_t ≃ r̄|G_L; (2) V[λ′]_t ≃ r̄′|G_L, where r′ is an ordinary weight 0 representation induced from G_{LM} for some suitable CM field M/Q of degree 2n; (3) p splits completely in L; (4) A and V (the fibre at t) are semistable over L; (5) r|G_L and the λ′-adic representation V_{λ′,t} (printed: 'r̄|G_L and r̄′|G_L') satisfy all the hypotheses of Theorem 5.16 with the possible exception of residual modularity.
items.note: This is the existence of t ∈ T_0(L) with properties (1)–(5), obtained by Moret–Bailly (R23.1, planned) on Dwork-family moduli (missing). Clause (5) checks the hypotheses of the conditional Theorem 5.16. No layer plans it. The printed 'r̄|G_L and r̄′|G_L' in (5) should refer to the characteristic-zero representations. See sourceIssues E213 (bound should be N_2 > 2n + 1) and E214 ((5) concerns the p-adic representations).

items.name: Potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1} under the extra hypothesis
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let A/K be a non-CM elliptic curve and n ≥ 1, and suppose the extra hypothesis holds for a sufficiently large prime p. Then r = Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{A,p} is potentially modular: with L as in sec10-dwork-point, r|G_L is modular.
items.note: This is potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}ρ_{A,p} under the extra hypothesis, by two applications of the conditional Theorem 5.16. It is conditional on Conjecture B and planned nowhere.

items.name: Auxiliary elliptic curve lemma (general case)
items.statement: Let E/K be a non-CM elliptic curve and n ≥ 1. The paper asserts, as following 'easily from Proposition 6.2 of [76], now applied to twists of a modular curve', that there exist a second elliptic curve A, a number field L/K and primes p and q such that: (1) the q-adic representation (Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{E,q})|G_L, whose residual representation is r̄ = (Sym^{2n−1} ρ̄_{E,q})|G_L, satisfies all the hypotheses of Theorem 5.16 (with q in place of p) except possibly residual modularity (printed: 'The mod-p representation r̄ = (Sym^{2n−1}ρ̄_E)|G_L'); (2) A and E are semistable over L and have good reduction at all primes dividing p and q; (3) p and q split completely in L; (4) p + 1 is divisible by an integer N_2 > n + 1 prime to the conductor of A; (5) E[q] ≃ A[q] as G_L-modules, and the corresponding mod-q representation G_L → GL_2(F_q) is surjective (printed: 'mod-p'); (6) the mod-p representation ρ̄_A : G_L → GL_2(F_p) is surjective, and ρ̄_A|G_{L_w} ≃ Ind_{G_{Q_{p^2}}}^{G_{Q_p}} ω_2 for each place w | p of L (L_w = Q_p by (3)).
items.note: The paper derives it from [76, Proposition 6.2] applied to twists of a modular curve, i.e. Moret–Bailly (R23.1, planned) on the twisted modular curve parametrizing A with A[q] ≅ E[q] and the local conditions at p. The rank-two twisted moduli step is planned only for Hilbert–Blumenthal moduli (R23.2), not for twisted modular curves over an arbitrary K. Clause (1) refers to the conditional Theorem 5.16. The printed 'mod-p' in (1) and (5) should read mod-q. See sourceIssues E213 (bound should be N_2 > 2n + 1) and E215, E216 (inconsistent roles of p and q).

items.name: Potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}(E) in general
items.statement: Assume Conjecture B. Let E/K be a non-CM elliptic curve and n ≥ 1, and choose (A, L, p, q) as in sec10-auxiliary-curve-lemma. By sec10-special-case (for A at p), Sym^{2n−1}(A) is potentially modular over some extension L′/L unramified at q (printed: 'using the mod-q representation … unramified at p'); since E[q] ≃ A[q], Theorem 5.16 applied at q (printed: 'at the prime at p') to (Sym^{2n−1} ρ_{E,q})|G_{L′} shows that Sym^{2n−1}(E) is modular over L′, i.e. potentially modular (printed: 'is modular').
items.note: This is the p–q switch: from potential modularity of Sym^{2n−1}(A) and E[q] ≅ A[q], it applies Theorem 5.16 at q. It is conditional on Conjecture B and planned nowhere. The published text swaps p and q (sourceIssues E216), and the item records the corrections. Its final 'is modular' means modular over L′, i.e. potentially modular.

items.name: Greenberg–Wiles (Poitou–Tate) Selmer group Euler characteristic formula
items.statement: Let F be a number field, p odd, and S a finite set of places of F containing all places above p and ∞. Let M be a finite G_{F,S}-module of p-power order with Cartier dual M* = Hom(M, μ_{p^∞}). For each v ∈ S let L_v ⊂ H^1(F_v, M) be a subgroup, and let L_v^⊥ ⊂ H^1(F_v, M*) be its annihilator under local Tate duality. Put H^1_L(F, M) = ker(H^1(G_{F,S}, M) → ⊕_{v∈S} H^1(F_v, M)/L_v), and define H^1_{L^⊥}(F, M*) likewise. Then |H^1_L(F, M)| / |H^1_{L^⊥}(F, M*)| = (|H^0(F, M)| / |H^0(F, M*)|) · ∏_{v∈S} |L_v| / |H^0(F_v, M)|.
items.locator: §8.2, p. 402 (displayed formula, with M = F_p); also Prop 8.4(2), p. 410 ('Poitou–Tate duality and the global Euler characteristic formula')
items.note: Planned at ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.5, on top of R02.3 (Tate's global Euler characteristic) and R02.4 (Poitou–Tate). The reviewed library audit lists this exact target as absent. Neither library has G_{F,S}, Galois-cohomological Selmer groups, global Euler characteristics or Poitou–Tate duality. External input: Standard (Wiles 1995 Prop. 1.6; e.g. Darmon–Diamond–Taylor, 'Fermat's Last Theorem', Thm 2.19). The paper cites no reference for it in §8.2; for Prop 8.4(2) it points to the proof of [52, Prop 3.2.5].

items.name: Top-degree cohomology commutes with base change
items.statement: Let P be a complex of S-modules with P^i = 0 for i > l0. Then for every S-module B, H^{l0}(P ⊗_S B) = H^{l0}(P) ⊗_S B, since H^{l0}(P) = coker(P^{l0−1} → P^{l0}) and ⊗ is right exact. The paper uses this implicitly in two places: for 'ψ then gives rise to an isomorphism … between H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗ S∞^□/(a + ϖ^{n′})) and H/ϖ^{n′}H for each N ≥ n′ ≥ 1' (p. 387), and for 'H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a = H^{l0}(P∞^□/a)' (p. 388).
items.note: Keep this as an implicitly used standard lemma, like ext-depth-dim-finite-map and mumford-lemma-2. No existing item states it. Both uses check out on the rendered pages. p. 387 (PDF 91): '(Note that ψ then gives rise to an isomorphism of R∞-modules between H^{l0}(P^□ ⊗_{S∞^□} S∞^□/(a + ϖ^{n′})) and H/ϖ^{n′}H for each N ≥ n′ ≥ 1)'. p. 388 (PDF 92): 'ψ∞ … H^{l0}(P∞^□)/a = H^{l0}(P∞^□/a) ≅ H'. Theorem 6.4's proof (p. 389) uses the same identification. In both cases P^{l0+1} = 0, and P has projective terms, so P ⊗ B also computes the derived tensor product. The lemma is a direct application of Mathlib declarations, all read at the pinned commit. (1) CategoryTheory.Functor.preservesLeftHomology_of_zero_g (Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/PreservesHomology.lean:886): a functor that preserves the cokernel of S.f preserves the homology of a short complex S with S.g = 0. (2) CategoryTheory.ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso (same file, :455) gives (S.map F).homology ≅ F.obj S.homology. (3) Base change F = ModuleCat.extendScalars is a left adjoint: ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj (Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/ChangeOfRings.lean:885), with an IsLeftAdjoint instance at :925. So F preserves colimits by CategoryTheory.Adjunction.leftAdjoint_preservesColimits (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Adjunction/Limits.lean:90). (4) At module level, rTensor_exact and rTensor.equiv (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/TensorProduct/RightExactness.lean:399, 393) give the cokernel form directly. No single declaration states 'H^{top}(P ⊗ B) = H^{top}(P) ⊗ B', but the lemma is a one-step instance of (1)–(3), with S = P.sc l0, whose g is zero because P^{l0+1} = 0. The derived version (the edge of the Tor spectral sequence) is also in the scope of DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7: 'Prove the spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^(j−i)(C⊗ᴸ_A B)'.

items.name: Admissible and locally admissible smooth representations over A
items.statement: Let A = O/ϖ^a and G = GL_n(F_x). A smooth representation M of G on an A-module (every vector fixed by an open subgroup) is admissible if M^K is a finitely generated A-module for every compact open subgroup K ⊂ G. It is locally admissible if every v ∈ M lies in an admissible G-subrepresentation of M, equivalently if the G-subrepresentation generated by v is admissible. The category 𝒞 of Definition 9.11 consists of locally admissible modules, and M_j[m] in §9.4.2 is called admissible.
items.note: Checked on pp. 420 and 424 (PDF pp. 124, 128). Definition 9.11 reads 'the category of locally admissible G-modules over A := O/ϖ^k', and §9.4.2 says M_j is filtered 'by the admissible module M_j[m]'. Neither notion is defined in the paper, so the item is kept: it is a definition 𝒞 depends on. Existing items record it only in def-9-11-category-C's xnote ('Locally admissible: every vector generates an admissible subrepresentation'). The equivalence of the item's two formulations uses that A = O/ϖ^a is noetherian, so that a subrepresentation of an admissible representation is admissible. Atlas: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0 plans admissibility, 'Define admissibility by finite generation of every compact-open invariant module, with stronger finiteness conditions explicitly separated', over the README's 'commutative coefficient rings A', and plans 'closure under subobjects'. Local admissibility is a weaker condition and is named nowhere: a grep for 'locally admissible' over data/atlas.json, research/blueprint/roadmaps and data/decompositions finds nothing. So the item as a whole is not planned. Libraries: there is no admissible or smooth-representation category. Near miss: Tau Ceti TauCeti.IsSmoothDiscrete (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/SmoothDiscrete.lean:254), smoothness (open stabilizers) of a discrete TopRep, with no admissibility.

items.name: Normalized parabolic induction n-ind_B^G and parabolic restriction res_G^B
items.statement: Let B = D·N be the Borel subgroup of G = GL_n(F_x), with unipotent radical N. For a smooth A-representation σ of B trivial on N, n-ind_B^G(σ) is the space of locally constant f : G → σ with f(bg) = δ_B(b)^{1/2} σ(b) f(g), with G acting by right translation. The square root of δ_B exists since √N(x) ∈ Z_p, as N(x) ≡ 1 mod p and p > n ≥ 2. The parabolic restriction res_G^B(M) is the normalized Jacquet module M_N ⊗ δ_B^{−1/2}. It is exact and left adjoint to n-ind_B^G (Frobenius reciprocity Hom_G(M, n-ind_B^G σ) = Hom_B(res_G^B M, σ)), which gives the natural map M → n-ind_B^G res_G^B(M) of Lemma 9.12. For π = n-ind_B^G(χ) as in Lemma 9.9, res_G^B(π) has as constituents the n! distinct characters χ^w, w ∈ W.
items.locator: §9.4.1, Lemmas 9.9 and 9.12, Corollary 9.13, Theorem 9.16, pp. 420–423 (used without definition)
items.note: Checked on pp. 420–423 (PDF pp. 124–127). n-ind_B^G and res_G^B are used in Lemma 9.9, Lemma 9.12 (the natural map M → n-ind_B^G res_G^B(M) and the decomposition res_G^B(M) ≃ ⊕_W M_B^w), Corollary 9.13 and the proof of Theorem 9.16, without definition. They are genuine definitions the section depends on, and no existing item defines them (lem-9-12's note only names SR.2 as the source of tools). Kept. Planned: SR.2 says 'Prove Frobenius reciprocity with correct adjoint direction and hypotheses, induction in stages and Mackey filtrations. For P=MN define unnormalized induction and N-coinvariants, then normalized induction/Jacquet functors using a specified square root of the modulus character. Prove exactness in the valid coefficient regime … and the geometric lemma with double-coset indexing.' The roadmap README says 'Basic categorical constructions use commutative coefficient rings A'. Here A = O/ϖ^a with ℓ ≠ p, so ℓ is a unit in A and N-coinvariants are exact: this is the valid regime. The geometric lemma plus distinctness of the eigenvalues gives the n! distinct constituents χ^w of res_G^B(π). The item's remark that √N(x) ∈ Z_p (N(x) ≡ 1 mod p, p odd, Hensel) is editorial, not in the paper. SR.2's 'specified square root' covers it. Library near misses only: Tau Ceti TauCeti.coind (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Coinduced.lean:82), the unnormalized smooth coinduction {f locally constant, f(ug) = u·f(g)} with right translation; Mathlib ContRepresentation.coind (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Continuous/Basic.lean:547), continuous functions without smoothness or normalization. Neither library has a Jacquet functor or normalized induction.

items.name: Supercuspidal support (mod p, ℓ ≠ p)
items.statement: Let π be an irreducible smooth representation of GL_n(F_x) over F̄_p, where the residue characteristic ℓ of x differs from p. Its supercuspidal support is the multiset {σ_1, …, σ_r} of irreducible supercuspidal representations σ_i of GL_{n_i}(F_x), with Σ n_i = n, such that π is a subquotient of the parabolic induction of σ_1 ⊗ … ⊗ σ_r. It is unique up to permutation (Vignéras). For π = n-ind_B^G(χ) with χ = (χ_1, …, χ_n) it is {χ_1, …, χ_n}.
items.locator: §9.4.1, proof of Lemma 9.10, p. 420 (used without definition)
items.note: Checked on p. 420 (PDF p. 124). The proof of Lemma 9.10 reads: 'The supercuspidal support of π consists of the distinct characters χ_i. If either extension group is non-zero, then, by Theorem 3.2.13 of [80], it follows that π′ has the same supercuspidal support as π.' The notion is used without definition, and no item defines it: emerton-helm-3-2-13 and lem-9-10 use it. Kept as a definition. Atlas: SR.3 plans 'the subquotient description by supercuspidal support' only under 'Admissible complex representations'. The SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups README says: 'Complex Bernstein theory, integral ℓ-adic theory (ℓ≠p) and characteristic-p smooth theory have separate theorem hypotheses. No transfer of admissibility or semisimplicity between them is implicit.' SR.5 (Helm's integral families) plans no mod-ℓ supercuspidal support. So the F̄_p-coefficient notion (ℓ ≠ p) and its uniqueness are not planned. The uniqueness attribution to Vignéras is standard for GL_n but I did not re-check it against the source. Not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti.

items.name: Splitting over a finite-index subgroup implies splitting (characteristic 0)
items.statement: Let L/F be finite with L ⊂ F_S, and let H = Gal(F_S/L) = G_{L,S}, an open normal subgroup of finite index in G_{F,S} after passing to the Galois closure. If an extension 0 → V → W → V → 0 of continuous E[G_{F,S}]-modules (E of characteristic 0) splits over H, then it splits over G_{F,S}. By inflation–restriction, the kernel of H¹(G_{F,S}, End_E V) → H¹(H, End_E V) is H¹(Gal(L/F), End_E V) = 0.
items.note:
Kept. This is the fourth input of Lemma 4.14, alongside the itemised mazur-def-ring-noetherian, mazur-traces-generate and cft-no-Zp-extension-unramified-at-p. The xnote of lem-4-14-reducedness mentions it but no item states it. Printed on p. 368 (checked on the image, PDF p. 72; arXiv v2 has the same wording): 'because G_{L,S} has finite image in G_{F,S}, the extension also splits over G_{F,S}, because the inflation map is injective (the kernel is computed by H^1 of a finite group acting in characteristic zero)'. The intended meaning is finite index and restriction, not inflation; this is recorded as sourceIssues E99 and E100.
Library, read at the pin: Tau Ceti has continuous H¹ for any topological group G and topological coefficients M. It has restriction explicitRes1 (TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/ExplicitFunctoriality.lean:497). It has explicitCor1_comp_res1 (Corestriction.lean:496), 'cor¹ ∘ res¹ = (G : U) • id' on H¹(G, M) for open U of finite index. It has explicitInfRes_exact (Inflation.lean:336), range(infl) = ker(res) in degree 1.
Consequence: ker(res) is killed by the index. For M = End_E V, a Q_p-vector space, H¹ is torsion-free (if n·c = d0(m) then c = d0(m/n)), so res is injective. This is a few-line corollary, not a single declaration.
In the paper's situation, G_{L,S} acts trivially on V, and so also on W once the extension splits over it. The conclusion is then Maschke for the finite group Gal(L/F) over E (char 0): Mathlib MonoidAlgebra.Submodule.exists_isCompl (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Maschke.lean:162, hypotheses [Finite G] [NeZero (Nat.card G : k)]). This route avoids the extension ↔ H¹(G, End V) dictionary, which neither library has.
